P0001.title: Fuel Volume Regulator A Control Circuit/Open
P0001.description: The fuel volume regulator (also called metering unit or suction control valve) is a solenoid valve on the inlet side of the high-pressure pump, used mainly on common-rail diesel engines. The engine control module pulses it to set how much fuel the pump draws in and delivers to the rail, and in this way controls rail pressure. P0001 is set when the control module detects that the control circuit of this valve is open, i.e. no plausible current flows when the valve is driven. Rail pressure can then no longer be controlled as intended. Whether the valve is open or closed without current depends on the design, so the same fault can cause excess pressure in one system and no pressure in another.

causes.label: Connector at the regulator loose, corroded or unplugged
Solenoid coil of the regulator open
Broken wire in the harness, e.g. chafing or rodent damage
Output driver in the engine control module faulty

symptoms: Engine cranks but does not start, or stalls (normally closed valve)
Loss of power or limp mode (normally open valve)

P0002.title: Fuel Volume Regulator A Control Circuit Range/Performance
P0002.description: The fuel volume regulator (also called metering unit or suction control valve) is a solenoid valve on the inlet side of the high-pressure pump, used mainly on common-rail diesel engines. The engine control module pulses it to set how much fuel the pump draws in and delivers to the rail, and in this way controls rail pressure. With P0002 the circuit is electrically intact, but command and effect do not match: the measured current does not fit the duty cycle, or rail pressure does not follow the regulator position plausibly. The cause is often mechanical, for example a sticking valve, rather than the wiring.

causes.label: Regulator sticking or worn due to dirt, debris or water in the fuel
High resistance at connector or wiring causing wrong current
Low-pressure supply problem: clogged filter or air in the fuel
Rail pressure sensor reading wrong values

symptoms: Loss of power or limp mode

P0003.title: Fuel Volume Regulator A Control Circuit Low
P0003.description: The fuel volume regulator (also called metering unit or suction control valve) is a solenoid valve on the inlet side of the high-pressure pump, used mainly on common-rail diesel engines. The engine control module pulses it to set how much fuel the pump draws in and delivers to the rail, and in this way controls rail pressure. P0003 means the control module measures a voltage or current below the expected range on the control circuit, typically because of a short to ground. On some output stages an open circuit is also reported as low. A short on the switched ground side can keep the valve permanently energised.

causes.label: Harness chafed through, short to ground
Shorted turns in the regulator coil (resistance too low)
Water or corrosion in the connector
Output driver in the engine control module faulty

symptoms: Loss of power or limp mode

P0004.title: Fuel Volume Regulator A Control Circuit High
P0004.description: The fuel volume regulator (also called metering unit or suction control valve) is a solenoid valve on the inlet side of the high-pressure pump, used mainly on common-rail diesel engines. The engine control module pulses it to set how much fuel the pump draws in and delivers to the rail, and in this way controls rail pressure. P0004 means the voltage on the control circuit stays too high for the commanded duty cycle, typically because of a short to battery voltage, or, with a switched ground side, an open circuit. The valve can then not be energised; a normally open design delivers maximum fuel and rail pressure rises.

causes.label: Short to battery voltage in the harness
Open coil or wire, reported as high with ground-side switching
Connector fault at the regulator
Output driver in the engine control module faulty

symptoms: Loss of power or limp mode
Rough running or diesel knock possible

P0005.title: Fuel Shutoff Valve A Control Circuit/Open
P0005.description: The fuel shutoff valve is a solenoid valve that opens or blocks the fuel supply. On diesel engines it is usually closed without current, so that the engine stops reliably when switched off. The engine control module energises it to let fuel flow and monitors its control circuit continuously. P0005 is set when this control circuit is open. A normally closed valve then cannot open, so the engine does not start or cuts out while driving. Which vehicles use this valve and code varies by manufacturer.

causes.label: Wire or connector interrupted or corroded
Valve coil open
Fuse or relay in the valve supply faulty
Output driver in the engine control module faulty

symptoms: Engine cranks but does not start

P0006.title: Fuel Shutoff Valve A Control Circuit Low
P0006.description: The fuel shutoff valve is a solenoid valve that opens or blocks the fuel supply. On diesel engines it is usually closed without current, so that the engine stops reliably when switched off. The engine control module energises it to let fuel flow and monitors its control circuit continuously. P0006 means voltage or current in the control circuit is below the expected range, typically because of a short to ground; depending on the output stage an open circuit can also show up this way. The valve is then not energised correctly, which can prevent starting or make the engine stall.

causes.label: Short to ground in the harness
Shorted turns in the valve coil
Corroded connector
Output driver in the engine control module faulty

P0007.title: Fuel Shutoff Valve A Control Circuit High
P0007.description: The fuel shutoff valve is a solenoid valve that opens or blocks the fuel supply. On diesel engines it is usually closed without current, so that the engine stops reliably when switched off. The engine control module energises it to let fuel flow and monitors its control circuit continuously. P0007 means the voltage in the control circuit stays too high, because the control module expects the line to be pulled to ground. Typical causes are a short to battery voltage or, with ground-side switching, an open circuit. The valve cannot be switched, which leads to starting problems or stalling.

causes.label: Control wire open or shorted to battery voltage
Valve coil open
Connector fault at the valve
Output driver in the engine control module faulty

P0008.title: Engine Position System Performance Bank 1
P0008.description: The engine control module learns how far each camshaft of bank 1 is offset from the crankshaft and compares this with a reference. P0008 is set when both camshafts of this bank are shifted in the same direction beyond a threshold. That points to the drive shared by the bank: a stretched primary timing chain, a worn tensioner, an idler gear or a crankshaft reluctor wheel that has slipped. A single faulty camshaft phaser does not set this code, because it affects only one camshaft.

causes.label: Primary or timing chain stretched
Chain tensioner worn or loose
Timing drive fitted incorrectly after an engine repair
Crankshaft reluctor wheel slipped

symptoms: Timing chain rattle, especially at cold start
Loss of power or rough running
Often stored together with P0016 to P0019

P0009.title: Engine Position System Performance Bank 2
P0009.description: The engine control module learns how far each camshaft of bank 2 is offset from the crankshaft and compares this with a reference. P0009 is set when both camshafts of this bank are shifted in the same direction beyond a threshold. That points to the drive shared by the bank: a stretched primary timing chain, a worn tensioner, an idler gear or a crankshaft reluctor wheel that has slipped. A single faulty camshaft phaser does not set this code, because it affects only one camshaft. Bank 2 exists only on V and boxer engines.

causes.label: Primary or timing chain stretched
Chain tensioner worn or loose
Timing drive fitted incorrectly after an engine repair
Crankshaft reluctor wheel slipped

symptoms: Timing chain rattle, especially at cold start
Loss of power or rough running
Often stored together with P0016 to P0019

P000A.title: A Camshaft Position Slow Response Bank 1
P000A.description: This monitor does not judge the end position of the intake camshaft on bank 1 but how fast it follows a change of the commanded angle. The code is set when the actual angle lags behind the target for too long during several adjustments. The adjustment speed depends directly on oil flow, so worn or wrong oil and a partly clogged screen are the usual causes. Drivability is often hardly affected; the fault is an early warning before the camshaft misses its target position altogether. Bank 1 is the cylinder bank that contains cylinder 1.

causes.label: Oil too thick or too thin, sludged, or oil level low
Screen at the oil control valve partly clogged
Oil control valve sluggish
Cam phaser leaking internally or worn
Generally weak oil pressure, e.g. worn oil pump or bearings

P000E.title: Fuel Volume Regulator Control Exceeded Learning Limit
P000E.description: The fuel volume regulator (also called metering unit or suction control valve) is a solenoid valve on the inlet side of the high-pressure pump, used mainly on common-rail diesel engines. The engine control module pulses it to set how much fuel the pump draws in and delivers to the rail, and in this way controls rail pressure. To compensate for tolerances and wear, the control module learns a long-term correction of the regulator control. P000E is set when this correction leaves its calibrated range. The regulator is electrically fine, but the system needs an unusually large correction all the time, which points to wear or contamination of regulator or pump, a weak low-pressure supply, or a missing calibration after a pump replacement.

causes.label: Fuel volume regulator worn or contaminated
High-pressure pump worn, delivering less
Low-pressure side: clogged filter, weak lift pump or air in the fuel
Not calibrated after pump or regulator replacement
Rail pressure sensor drifting

symptoms: Often hardly noticeable at first, later loss of power
Hard starting if rail pressure is wrong

P000F.title: Fuel System Over Pressure Relief Valve Activated
P000F.description: On common-rail diesel and some gasoline direct-injection systems a spring-loaded pressure relief valve protects the rail and injectors: if pressure rises too far, it opens and returns fuel to the tank, often holding a reduced pressure for limp-home operation. The control module recognises the opening from the rail pressure signal and stores P000F. The code reports an event, not a defect of the relief valve itself; the actual cause usually lies in pressure control, for example a regulator that delivers too much fuel.

causes.label: Fuel volume regulator stuck open or without current, pump over-delivers
Rail pressure sensor reading wrong, control runs into overpressure
Pressure control valve faulty, where fitted
Fuel return line blocked or kinked
Relief valve itself leaking or fatigued

symptoms: Sudden loss of power or limp mode

P0010.title: "A" Camshaft Position Actuator Circuit (Bank 1)
P0010.description: The engine control module drives the oil control valve (a pulse-width modulated solenoid) of the variable valve timing on the intake camshaft on bank 1. It checks the electrical state of this output and sets the code when the circuit is open, or when the measured state does not match the command, for example because of a short. Camshaft adjustment is then disabled and the phaser stays in its locked rest position: the engine keeps running, but with less torque and higher consumption. Bank 1 is the cylinder bank that contains cylinder 1.

causes.label: Solenoid coil of the oil control valve open or shorted
Connector corroded, loose or soaked with engine oil wicking through the valve
Wiring harness chafed through or broken
Supply voltage missing, e.g. blown fuse
Output driver in the engine control module faulty

symptoms: Less pulling power at low and medium engine speed

P0011.title: "A" Camshaft Position - Timing Over-Advanced or System Performance (Bank 1)
P0011.description: The engine control module compares the commanded position of the intake camshaft on bank 1 with the actual position it calculates from the camshaft and crankshaft sensors. This code is set when the camshaft sits further advanced than commanded for longer than a calibrated time, or, depending on the manufacturer, when the target is missed in either direction ("system performance"). Typical cause is a phaser that does not return to its rest position, for example because the oil control valve sticks open or its screen is clogged. Bank 1 is the cylinder bank that contains cylinder 1.

causes.label: Oil level too low, oil sludged or wrong viscosity
Screen at the oil control valve clogged with debris
Oil control valve mechanically sticking
Cam phaser worn or its locking pin sticking
Timing chain worn or fitted incorrectly after a repair

symptoms: Rough or unstable idle, as valve overlap is too large
Rattling from the timing drive at cold start

P0012.title: "A" Camshaft Position - Timing Over-Retarded (Bank 1)
P0012.description: The engine control module compares the commanded position of the intake camshaft on bank 1 with the actual position from the camshaft and crankshaft sensors. This code is set when the camshaft stays further retarded than commanded for longer than a calibrated time. Usually the phaser does not move far enough out of its rest position, because oil pressure is too low to release the locking pin, the oil control valve does not open, or the oil screen is blocked. A stretched timing chain also shifts the camshaft towards retarded. Bank 1 is the cylinder bank that contains cylinder 1.

causes.label: Oil pressure or oil level too low, oil worn out
Oil control valve sticking closed or its screen blocked
Cam phaser defective or seized in its rest position
Timing chain stretched or jumped a tooth
Wear debris in the oil circuit, e.g. from a thrust bearing

symptoms: Noticeably less torque and pulling power
Rattle from the timing drive if the chain is stretched

P0013.title: "B" Camshaft Position Actuator Circuit (Bank 1)
P0013.description: The engine control module drives the oil control valve (a pulse-width modulated solenoid) of the variable valve timing on the exhaust camshaft on bank 1. It checks the electrical state of this output and sets the code when the circuit is open, or when the measured state does not match the command, for example because of a short. symptoms: Less pulling power at low and medium engine speed

P0015.title: "B" Camshaft Position - Timing Over-Retarded (Bank 1)
P0015.description: The engine control module compares the commanded position of the exhaust camshaft on bank 1 with the actual position from the camshaft and crankshaft sensors. P0016.title: Crankshaft Position - Camshaft Position Correlation (Bank 1 Sensor A)
P0016.description: The engine control module checks whether the signal of the intake camshaft on bank 1 (sensor A) arrives at the expected crankshaft position, usually while the camshaft phaser is in its rest position. P0016 is set when the deviation stays outside a calibrated window. The camshaft is then out of step with the crankshaft: a timing belt or chain has jumped a tooth, the chain is stretched, the phaser is stuck at an end stop, or a reluctor wheel has slipped. On engines with a single camshaft, sensor A is simply the only camshaft sensor.

causes.label: Timing chain stretched, or belt or chain jumped a tooth
Camshaft phaser stuck at an end stop, oil control valve or oil pressure faulty
Incorrect assembly after a belt or chain replacement
Camshaft or crankshaft sensor signal disturbed
Reluctor wheel on crankshaft or camshaft slipped

symptoms: Rough idle and loss of power
Chain rattle at cold start on chain-driven engines
Risk of valve damage on interference engines if the timing has jumped

P0017.title: Crankshaft Position - Camshaft Position Correlation (Bank 1 Sensor B)
P0017.description: The engine control module checks whether the signal of the exhaust camshaft on bank 1 (sensor B) arrives at the expected crankshaft position, usually while the camshaft phaser is in its rest position. P001A.title: A Camshaft Profile Actuator A Control Circuit/Open Bank 1
P001A.description: A camshaft profile actuator switches the intake camshaft (camshaft A) on bank 1 between two or more fixed cam profiles with different valve lift and duration, for example by shifting a cam piece axially or by locking rocker arms or tappets with oil pressure. Unlike a camshaft phaser it does not shift the timing continuously. The second letter "A" in the title numbers the actuator on this camshaft. This code is set when the control circuit of the actuator is open: no current flows when it is driven, because of a broken wire, an unplugged connector or an open coil. The engine usually stays on one profile, typically the base profile with low lift. Some manufacturers report these faults with their own codes instead.

causes.label: Connector at the actuator corroded, oil-soaked or loose
Wire broken, e.g. at the valve cover
Actuator coil open
Output driver in the engine control module faulty

symptoms: Less power at high engine speed because the profile does not switch
Higher consumption or uneven part-load running, depending on the profile

P001B.title: A Camshaft Profile Actuator A Control Circuit Low Bank 1
P001B.description: A camshaft profile actuator switches the intake camshaft (camshaft A) on bank 1 between two or more fixed cam profiles with different valve lift and duration, for example by shifting a cam piece axially or by locking rocker arms or tappets with oil pressure. causes.label: Oil pressure or oil level too low, oil worn out
Oil control valve sticking closed or its screen blocked
Cam phaser defective or seized in its rest position
Timing chain stretched or jumped a tooth
Wear debris in the oil circuit, e.g. from a thrust bearing

symptoms: Noticeably less torque and pulling power
Rattle from the timing drive if the chain is stretched

P0023.title: "B" Camshaft Position Actuator Circuit (Bank 2)
P0023.description: The engine control module drives the oil control valve (a pulse-width modulated solenoid) of the variable valve timing on the exhaust camshaft on bank 2. It checks the electrical state of this output and sets the code when the circuit is open, or when the measured state does not match the command, for example because of a short. Camshaft adjustment is then disabled and the phaser stays in its locked rest position: the engine keeps running, but with less torque and higher consumption. Bank 2 exists only on V and boxer engines; it is the cylinder bank without cylinder 1.

causes.label: Solenoid coil of the oil control valve open or shorted
Connector corroded, loose or soaked with engine oil wicking through the valve
Wiring harness chafed through or broken
Supply voltage missing, e.g. blown fuse
Output driver in the engine control module faulty

symptoms: Less pulling power at low and medium engine speed

P0024.title: "B" Camshaft Position - Timing Over-Advanced or System Performance (Bank 2)
P0024.description: The engine control module compares the commanded position of the exhaust camshaft on bank 2 with the actual position it calculates from the camshaft and crankshaft sensors. This code is set when the camshaft sits further advanced than commanded for longer than a calibrated time, or, depending on the manufacturer, when the target is missed in either direction ("system performance"). Typical cause is a phaser that does not return to its rest position, for example because the oil control valve sticks open or its screen is clogged. Bank 2 exists only on V and boxer engines; it is the cylinder bank without cylinder 1.

causes.label: Oil level too low, oil sludged or wrong viscosity
Screen at the oil control valve clogged with debris
Oil control valve mechanically sticking
Cam phaser worn or its locking pin sticking
Timing chain worn or fitted incorrectly after a repair

symptoms: Rattling from the timing drive at cold start

P0025.title: "B" Camshaft Position - Timing Over-Retarded (Bank 2)
P0025.description: The engine control module compares the commanded position of the exhaust camshaft on bank 2 with the actual position from the camshaft and crankshaft sensors. This code is set when the camshaft stays further retarded than commanded for longer than a calibrated time. Usually the phaser does not move far enough out of its rest position, because oil pressure is too low to release the locking pin, the oil control valve does not open, or the oil screen is blocked. A stretched timing chain also shifts the camshaft towards retarded. Bank 2 exists only on V and boxer engines; it is the cylinder bank without cylinder 1.

causes.label: Oil pressure or oil level too low, oil worn out
Oil control valve sticking closed or its screen blocked
Cam phaser defective or seized in its rest position
Timing chain stretched or jumped a tooth
Wear debris in the oil circuit, e.g. from a thrust bearing

symptoms: Noticeably less torque and pulling power
Rattle from the timing drive if the chain is stretched

P0026.title: Intake Valve Control Solenoid Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 1)
P0026.description: A solenoid valve routes engine oil to a valve control element on the intake side of bank 1. Depending on the manufacturer this is a valve lift changeover or a camshaft phaser. P0026 is a plausibility fault: the electrical control is in order, but the expected effect does not occur or comes too late. The control module recognises this from feedback such as an oil pressure switch or the camshaft sensor. Pure circuit faults of the same solenoid have their own codes. The engine usually remains drivable, but with less power and higher consumption.

Feedback oil pressure switch faulty or leaking (systems with switch)
Screen in front of the solenoid clogged, or solenoid sticking
Mechanical fault in the valve train, e.g. locking pin or phaser sticking
Contact resistance in wiring or connector

symptoms: Loss of power, no extra pull at higher engine speed
Rough idle possible if a phaser is affected

P002A.title: B Camshaft Profile Actuator A Control Circuit/Open Bank 1
P002A.description: A camshaft profile actuator switches the exhaust camshaft (camshaft B) on bank 1 between two or more fixed cam profiles with different valve lift and duration, for example by shifting a cam piece axially or by locking rocker arms or tappets with oil pressure. Unlike a camshaft phaser it does not shift the timing continuously. The second letter "A" in the title numbers the actuator on this camshaft. This code is set when the control circuit of the actuator is open: no current flows when it is driven, because of a broken wire, an unplugged connector or an open coil. The engine usually stays on one profile, typically the base profile with low lift. Some manufacturers report these faults with their own codes instead.

causes.label: Connector at the actuator corroded, oil-soaked or loose
Wire broken, e.g. at the valve cover
Actuator coil open
Output driver in the engine control module faulty

symptoms: Less power at high engine speed because the profile does not switch
Higher consumption or uneven part-load running, depending on the profile

P002B.title: B Camshaft Profile Actuator A Control Circuit Low Bank 1
P002B.description: A camshaft profile actuator switches the exhaust camshaft (camshaft B) on bank 1 between two or more fixed cam profiles with different valve lift and duration, for example by shifting a cam piece axially or by locking rocker arms or tappets with oil pressure. Unlike a camshaft phaser it does not shift the timing continuously. The second letter "A" in the title numbers the actuator on this camshaft. This code is set when the control circuit reads too low, typically because the control wire is shorted to ground. The engine usually stays on one profile, typically the base profile with low lift. Some manufacturers report these faults with their own codes instead.

causes.label: Control wire chafed through and shorted to ground
Connector corroded or contaminated with oil
Shorted turns in the actuator coil
Output driver in the engine control module faulty

symptoms: Less power at high engine speed because the profile does not switch
Higher consumption or uneven part-load running, depending on the profile

P002C.title: B Camshaft Profile Actuator A Control Circuit High Bank 1
P002C.description: A camshaft profile actuator switches the exhaust camshaft (camshaft B) on bank 1 between two or more fixed cam profiles with different valve lift and duration, for example by shifting a cam piece axially or by locking rocker arms or tappets with oil pressure. P002E.description: A camshaft profile actuator switches the exhaust camshaft (camshaft B) on bank 2 between two or more fixed cam profiles with different valve lift and duration, for example by shifting a cam piece axially or by locking rocker arms or tappets with oil pressure. P002F.title: B Camshaft Profile Actuator A Control Circuit High Bank 2
P002F.description: A camshaft profile actuator switches the exhaust camshaft (camshaft B) on bank 2 between two or more fixed cam profiles with different valve lift and duration, for example by shifting a cam piece axially or by locking rocker arms or tappets with oil pressure. P0030.title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P0030.description: The upstream oxygen sensor on bank 1 (sensor 1, before the catalytic converter) only delivers a usable signal once its ceramic element is hot. A heating element inside the sensor gets it there quickly after a cold start. Typically the heater receives battery voltage via a fuse or relay, and the engine control module switches the ground side with a pulsed signal while comparing the commanded state with the measured voltage or current. P0030 is the general circuit fault: the measured state does not fit the command, most often because the circuit is interrupted. Which physical fault sets P0030, P0031 or P0032 is defined by each manufacturer. Without heating, closed-loop mixture control starts late and cold-start emissions rise.

causes.label: Heater circuit interrupted, e.g. broken or chafed wire near the exhaust
Heating element inside the sensor burnt out
Connector corroded or terminal pushed back
Heater supply fuse or relay faulty
Output driver in the engine control module faulty

symptoms: Closed-loop control starts late after a cold start
Emissions test or readiness check failed

P0031.title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit Low (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P0031.description: The upstream oxygen sensor on bank 1 (sensor 1, before the catalytic converter) only delivers a usable signal once its ceramic element is hot. A heating element inside the sensor gets it there quickly after a cold start. Typically the heater receives battery voltage via a fuse or relay, and the engine control module switches the ground side with a pulsed signal while comparing the commanded state with the measured voltage or current. P0031 means the control module measures too little voltage or current while the heater is switched on. Depending on the system this points to a burnt-out element, a missing supply or an interrupted control wire. The sensor then warms up late, so mixture control starts late and cold-start emissions rise.

causes.label: Heating element burnt out or high resistance (too little current)
Supply wire interrupted or fuse blown
Control wire to the engine control module interrupted
Corroded connector with high contact resistance
Output driver in the engine control module faulty

symptoms: Closed-loop control starts late after a cold start
Further heater codes if a shared fuse has blown
Emissions test or readiness check failed

P0032.title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit High (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P0032.description: The upstream oxygen sensor on bank 1 (sensor 1, before the catalytic converter) only delivers a usable signal once its ceramic element is hot. A heating element inside the sensor gets it there quickly after a cold start. Typically the heater receives battery voltage via a fuse or relay, and the engine control module switches the ground side with a pulsed signal while comparing the commanded state with the measured voltage or current. P0032 means the control module sees too high a voltage on the heater control circuit, typically because the switched ground wire is shorted to battery voltage. Systems that measure current may also report an internal short in the heating element this way. The control module usually switches the heater off to protect its output, so the sensor warms up late.

causes.label: Heater control wire shorted to battery voltage, e.g. chafed harness
Heating element shorted internally (resistance too low)
Water or corrosion in the connector causing leakage between pins
Output driver in the engine control module faulty

symptoms: Closed-loop control starts late after a cold start
Emissions test or readiness check failed

P0033.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Bypass Valve A Control Circuit
P0033.description: The turbocharger bypass valve A is the compressor recirculation (diverter) valve: it connects the pressure side of the compressor with the intake side upstream of the turbocharger. It opens when the throttle closes quickly at high boost, so the compressor does not surge and the compressor wheel keeps its speed for the next acceleration. It is not the wastegate, which bypasses exhaust gas around the turbine and has its own codes. The valve is either electric or a vacuum unit controlled by a solenoid. P0033 is the general circuit fault, usually an open circuit: the voltage at the control output does not match the command.

causes.label: Wire or connector interrupted, corroded or chafed
Solenoid coil or electric bypass valve faulty
Supply missing, e.g. fuse or main relay
Output driver in the engine control module faulty

symptoms: Fluttering or hissing when lifting off the throttle if the valve stays closed
Too little boost if the valve stays open

P0034.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Bypass Valve A Control Circuit Low
P0034.description: The turbocharger bypass valve A is the compressor recirculation (diverter) valve: it connects the pressure side of the compressor with the intake side upstream of the turbocharger. It opens when the throttle closes quickly at high boost, so the compressor does not surge and the compressor wheel keeps its speed for the next acceleration. It is not the wastegate, which bypasses exhaust gas around the turbine and has its own codes. The valve is either electric or a vacuum unit controlled by a solenoid. P0034 means the voltage at the control output is too low, typically because the control wire is shorted to ground; on some control modules an open circuit also sets this code.

causes.label: Control wire shorted to ground
Valve shorted internally
Supply missing, e.g. fuse or main relay
Output driver in the engine control module faulty

symptoms: Fluttering or hissing when lifting off the throttle if the valve stays closed
Too little boost if the valve stays open

P0035.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Bypass Valve A Control Circuit High
P0035.description: The turbocharger bypass valve A is the compressor recirculation (diverter) valve: it connects the pressure side of the compressor with the intake side upstream of the turbocharger. It opens when the throttle closes quickly at high boost, so the compressor does not surge and the compressor wheel keeps its speed for the next acceleration. P0035 means the voltage at the control output is too high, typically a short to battery voltage; on some engines an intermittent break in the harness has also set this code.

causes.label: Control wire shorted to battery voltage
Loose contact or broken wire, e.g. harness vibrating from heat
Solenoid coil faulty
Output driver in the engine control module faulty

symptoms: Fluttering or hissing when lifting off the throttle if the valve stays closed
Too little boost if the valve stays open

P0036.title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P0036.description: The heated oxygen sensor on bank 1 is the downstream sensor 2 behind the (first) catalytic converter, used mainly to monitor the converter. Its heating element brings it quickly to operating temperature. Typically the heater receives battery voltage via a fuse, and the engine control module switches the ground side with a pulsed signal while checking that the circuit state matches the command. P0036 is the general circuit fault: the measured state of the heater circuit does not fit the command, most often because the circuit is interrupted. Which physical fault sets the general, low or high code is defined by each manufacturer. Without heating, the sensor becomes ready late and catalyst monitoring may not complete.

causes.label: Heating element inside the sensor burnt out
Wire or connector damaged by heat or road spray
Heater fuse blown; a shared fuse can set several heater codes
Output driver or software of the engine control module

symptoms: Emissions test or readiness check failed

P0037.title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit Low (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P0037.description: The heated oxygen sensor on bank 1 is the downstream sensor 2 behind the (first) catalytic converter, used mainly to monitor the converter. Its heating element brings it quickly to operating temperature. P0037 means the control module measures too low a voltage or current in the heater control circuit, for example because of a short to ground or, depending on the system, a burnt-out element. Which physical fault sets the general, low or high code is defined by each manufacturer. Without heating, the sensor becomes ready late and catalyst monitoring may not complete.

causes.label: Control wire shorted to ground, or heating element burnt out (system-dependent)
Supply interrupted or fuse blown
Corroded connector with high contact resistance
Output driver or software of the engine control module

symptoms: Emissions test or readiness check failed

P0038.title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit High (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P0038.description: The heated oxygen sensor on bank 1 is the downstream sensor 2 behind the (first) catalytic converter, used mainly to monitor the converter. Its heating element brings it quickly to operating temperature. Typically the heater receives battery voltage via a fuse, and the engine control module switches the ground side with a pulsed signal while checking that the circuit state matches the command. P0038 means the control module sees too high a voltage in the heater control circuit, typically because the switched ground wire is shorted to battery voltage. Which physical fault sets the general, low or high code is defined by each manufacturer. Without heating, the sensor becomes ready late and catalyst monitoring may not complete.

causes.label: Heater control wire shorted to battery voltage, e.g. chafed harness
Heating element shorted internally
Water in the connector causing leakage between pins

P0039.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Bypass Valve A Control Circuit Range/Performance
P0039.description: The turbocharger bypass valve A is the compressor recirculation (diverter) valve: it connects the pressure side of the compressor with the intake side upstream of the turbocharger. It opens when the throttle closes quickly at high boost, so the compressor does not surge and the compressor wheel keeps its speed for the next acceleration. It is not the wastegate, which bypasses exhaust gas around the turbine and has its own codes. The valve is either electric or a vacuum unit controlled by a solenoid. With P0039 the circuit is electrically intact, but the valve does not behave as commanded. On valves with a position sensor, for example, the valve must reach its rest position within a set time after being switched off; the code is set if the measured position deviates too far.

causes.label: Valve sticking from carbon or oil mist, or diaphragm torn
Vacuum line or switching valve leaking (pneumatic design)
Position sensor in the valve faulty
Increased resistance in the wiring

symptoms: Fluttering noise when lifting off the throttle

P003A.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Control A Position Exceeded Learning Limit
P003A.description: The electric boost actuator A positions the variable turbine vanes or the wastegate and reports its position through a sensor. In a learning run, for example with the engine warm at idle or after switching off, the control module drives the actuator to its mechanical end stops and stores the sensor values as reference. P003A is set when a learned end position or the total travel lies outside the permitted limits. Typical reasons are worn or sticking vanes or linkage, a faulty actuator, a broken actuator lever, or a replacement actuator that has not been learned in. A usually denotes the first turbocharger in the exhaust flow.

causes.label: Electronic actuator or its control module faulty
Vane mechanism, sector gear or linkage worn or sticking
Replacement not learned in, or learning run aborted (e.g. low voltage)
Actuator lever broken
Position sensor or its wiring faulty

P003B.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Control B Position Exceeded Learning Limit
P003B.description: The electric boost actuator B positions the variable turbine vanes or the wastegate and reports its position through a sensor. In a learning run, for example with the engine warm at idle or after switching off, the control module drives the actuator to its mechanical end stops and stores the sensor values as reference. P003B is set when a learned end position or the total travel lies outside the permitted limits. Typical reasons are worn or sticking vanes or linkage, a faulty actuator, a broken actuator lever, or a replacement actuator that has not been learned in. B denotes the second actuator, for example on the second stage of a two-stage system.

causes.label: Electronic actuator or its control module faulty
Vane mechanism, sector gear or linkage worn or sticking
Replacement not learned in, or learning run aborted (e.g. low voltage)
Actuator lever broken
Position sensor or its wiring faulty

P003C.title: A Camshaft Profile Actuator A Control Performance/Stuck Off Bank 1
P003C.description: The camshaft profile actuator A switches the intake camshaft (camshaft A) on bank 1 between fixed cam profiles, usually a low-lift base profile and a high-lift profile. In most designs the unactuated state ("off") is the base profile; which profile counts as "on" is defined by the manufacturer. The control module does not need a position sensor to check the switchover: it detects the actual profile indirectly, for example from oil pressure in the switching gallery, intake pressure per cylinder or crankshaft speed fluctuations. This code is set when the switchover is commanded but the camshaft stays on the base profile, or switches too slowly or incompletely. The engine then lacks power at higher engine speed.

causes.label: Oil level too low, wrong viscosity or sludged oil, so switching pressure is missing
Profile switching solenoid sticking or its screen clogged
Oil supply to the switching elements leaking or restricted, e.g. worn seals
Locking pin in tappet or rocker arm, or sliding cam piece, sticking
Consequence of a circuit fault of the same actuator

symptoms: Lack of power at higher engine speed
Reduced power mode on some vehicles

P003D.title: A Camshaft Profile Actuator A Control Stuck On Bank 1
P003D.description: The camshaft profile actuator A switches the intake camshaft (camshaft A) on bank 1 between fixed cam profiles, usually a low-lift base profile and a high-lift profile. In most designs the unactuated state ("off") is the base profile; which profile counts as "on" is defined by the manufacturer. The control module does not need a position sensor to check the switchover: it detects the actual profile indirectly, for example from oil pressure in the switching gallery, intake pressure per cylinder or crankshaft speed fluctuations. This code is set when the base profile is commanded but the camshaft stays on the switched profile. Large lift and long opening at low engine speed cause rough idle and poor low-speed running.

causes.label: Profile switching solenoid stuck open, oil pressure is not released
Locking pin does not return (weak spring, burr or dirt)
Oil pressure too high or drain from the switching gallery blocked
Sliding cam piece stuck in the high-lift position

symptoms: Rough idle and jerking at low engine speed

P003F.description: The camshaft profile actuator A switches the intake camshaft (camshaft A) on bank 2 between fixed cam profiles, usually a low-lift base profile and a high-lift profile. In most designs the unactuated state ("off") is the base profile; which profile counts as "on" is defined by the manufacturer. P0040.title: O2 Sensor Signals Swapped Bank 1 Sensor 1/Bank 2 Sensor 1
P0040.description: On engines with two exhaust banks, the control module checks whether the upstream oxygen sensors are assigned to the right bank. It changes the mixture on one bank only, actively or as part of normal bank-wise control, and watches which sensor responds. If the sensor that should sit on the other bank reacts, the signals are swapped. This logic is documented for the manufacturer-specific predecessor codes; the usual cause is connectors plugged in crosswise after a repair. If the swap remains, each bank is controlled by the other bank's signal, so fuel trims drift towards their limits.

causes.label: Sensor connectors plugged in crosswise after a repair
Harness routed wrongly or pins swapped in a connector
Wrong harness, control module or calibration after a replacement

symptoms: Fuel trim and mixture codes possible
Unstable idle or higher consumption possible

P0041.title: O2 Sensor Signals Swapped Bank 1 Sensor 2/Bank 2 Sensor 2
P0041.description: On engines with two exhaust banks, the control module checks whether the downstream oxygen sensors are assigned to the right bank. It changes the mixture on one bank only, actively or as part of normal bank-wise control, and watches which sensor responds. If the sensor that should sit on the other bank reacts, the signals are swapped. This logic is documented for the manufacturer-specific predecessor codes; the usual cause is connectors plugged in crosswise after a repair. Behind the catalytic converters the response is slower, so detection takes longer.

P0045.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Control A Circuit/Open
P0045.description: "Boost control A" is the electrically driven actuator the engine control module uses to set boost pressure: depending on the engine a pulse-width modulated solenoid or vacuum converter at the wastegate, the control valve of variable turbine vanes, or an electric actuator with position feedback. P005A.title: B Camshaft Profile Actuator A Control Performance/Stuck Off Bank 1

In most designs the unactuated state ("off") is the base profile; which profile counts as "on" is defined by the manufacturer. The control module does not need a position sensor to check the switchover: it detects the actual profile indirectly, for example from oil pressure in the switching gallery, intake pressure per cylinder or crankshaft speed fluctuations. Oil supply to the switching elements leaking or restricted, e.g. worn seals
Locking pin in tappet or rocker arm, or sliding cam piece, sticking
Consequence of a circuit fault of the same actuator

symptoms: Lack of power at higher engine speed
Reduced power mode on some vehicles

P0062.title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit (Bank 2 Sensor 3)
P0062.description: The heated oxygen sensor on bank 2 is the third sensor further downstream, which exists only on systems with two catalyst stages. Its heating element brings it quickly to operating temperature. Typically the heater receives battery voltage via a fuse, and the engine control module switches the ground side with a pulsed signal while checking that the circuit state matches the command. P0062 is the general circuit fault: the measured state of the heater circuit does not fit the command, most often because the circuit is interrupted. Which physical fault sets the general, low or high code is defined by each manufacturer. Without heating, the sensor becomes ready late and catalyst monitoring may not complete. Bank 2 codes occur only on engines with two exhaust banks (V or boxer engines).

causes.label: Heating element inside the sensor burnt out
Wire or connector damaged by heat or road spray
Heater fuse blown; a shared fuse can set several heater codes
Output driver or software of the engine control module

symptoms: Emissions test or readiness check failed

P0063.title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit Low (Bank 2 Sensor 3)
P0063.description: The heated oxygen sensor on bank 2 is the third sensor further downstream, which exists only on systems with two catalyst stages. causes.label: Control wire shorted to ground, or heating element burnt out (system-dependent)
Supply interrupted or fuse blown
Corroded connector with high contact resistance
Output driver or software of the engine control module

symptoms: Emissions test or readiness check failed

P0065.title: Air Assisted Injector Control Range/Performance
P0065.description: Air-assisted injectors have an air sleeve around the nozzle tip: air flowing past at high speed breaks the fuel spray into finer droplets, which improves combustion and cold starts and lowers hydrocarbon emissions. On port-injected engines this air is taken upstream of the throttle and dosed by a pulse-width modulated bypass solenoid; because it bypasses the throttle, it is part of the idle air. The system is rare and mainly found on older engines. P0065 means the control is electrically in order, but the effect is implausible. One documented method compares the idle speed controller correction with the air assistance switched on and off during stable idle; if the difference is too large, the code is set.

causes.label: Air-assist solenoid sticking or dirty
Air hoses to the injectors leaking, disconnected or blocked
Air passages at the injectors coked
Air leak distorting idle control

P0066.title: Air Assisted Injector Control Circuit Low

On port-injected engines this air is taken upstream of the throttle and dosed by a pulse-width modulated bypass solenoid; because it bypasses the throttle, it is part of the idle air. The system is rare and mainly found on older engines. causes.label: Short to ground or open circuit in the control or supply wire

Connector corroded
Output driver in the engine control module faulty

P0067.title: Air Assisted Injector Control Circuit High
P0067.description: Air-assisted injectors have an air sleeve around the nozzle tip: air flowing past at high speed breaks the fuel spray into finer droplets, which improves combustion and cold starts and lowers hydrocarbon emissions. P0068.title: MAP/MAF - Throttle Position Correlation
P0068.description: The engine control module compares the air quantity measured by the manifold pressure and/or mass air flow sensor with the quantity the throttle position leads it to expect. P0068 is set when they do not match, typically because more air arrives than the nearly closed throttle allows, i.e. an air leak behind the throttle, or because the throttle body is dirty or a sensor reads wrong. On engines with electronic throttle this check protects throttle control, so the engine often goes into reduced power. Each sensor can be electrically fine on its own; regulations require such plausibility checks for input sensors with a code of their own.

causes.label: Air leak behind the throttle: intake manifold, vacuum or MAP hoses
Throttle body dirty
Mass air flow or manifold pressure sensor faulty
Engine control software (manufacturer updates exist)
Camshaft timing out of position

P0069.title: Manifold Absolute Pressure - Barometric Pressure Correlation
P0069.description: With the ignition on and the engine stopped, the intake manifold is at ambient pressure, so the manifold pressure sensor and the barometric pressure sensor (often inside the control module) must read almost the same. P0069 is set when they differ by more than a threshold. Some systems also compare the barometric reading with a value estimated from manifold pressure at wide-open throttle while driving. Altitude and weather shift both values equally and do not cause the code. Each sensor can be electrically fine on its own; regulations require such plausibility checks for input sensors with a code of their own.

causes.label: Manifold pressure sensor drifting
MAP sensor hose blocked, kinked or leaking
Barometric pressure sensor (often inside the control module) faulty
5 V reference or connector faulty

P006A.title: MAP - Mass or Volume Air Flow Correlation Bank 1
P006A.description: The engine control module compares the air quantity measured by the mass air flow sensor with the quantity it calculates from manifold pressure, engine speed and temperature. P006A is set when the two deviate too far. A typical cause is an exhaust gas recirculation valve that does not close: recirculated exhaust raises manifold pressure without passing the air flow sensor. Air leaks, a leaking crankcase ventilation hose or a dirty sensor have the same effect. Each sensor can be electrically fine on its own; regulations require such plausibility checks for input sensors with a code of their own.

causes.label: EGR valve dirty or sticking open
Air leak or crankcase ventilation hose leaking
Mass air flow sensor dirty or manifold pressure sensor faulty
Air filter or intake restricted

P006B.title: MAP - Exhaust Pressure Correlation
P006B.description: On engines with an exhaust pressure sensor, mostly turbocharged diesels, the control module checks whether manifold pressure and exhaust back pressure fit each other, for example with the engine stopped, when both should be at ambient pressure. P006B is set when they do not. No manufacturer description of this code was found; the explanation follows the general rule for plausibility checks of input sensors. Suspects are the exhaust pressure sensor or its sooted hose, and the manifold pressure sensor. Each sensor can be electrically fine on its own; regulations require such plausibility checks for input sensors with a code of their own.

causes.label: Exhaust pressure sensor faulty or its hose sooted or blocked
Manifold pressure sensor faulty
EGR or turbocharger fault distorting pressures

P006C.title: MAP - Turbocharger/Supercharger Inlet Pressure Correlation
P006C.description: On turbocharged or supercharged engines the control module compares manifold pressure with the pressure measured upstream of the throttle, for example at idle or with the throttle wide open, where the two must lie close together. P006C is set when the difference exceeds a threshold. Manufacturers interpret "inlet pressure" differently: some mean boost pressure upstream of the throttle, others the pressure at the compressor inlet. Typical causes are a leak in the charge-air path or a faulty pressure sensor. Each sensor can be electrically fine on its own; regulations require such plausibility checks for input sensors with a code of their own.

causes.label: Leak or disconnected hose in the charge-air path
Boost or inlet pressure sensor faulty
Manifold pressure sensor faulty
Throttle body fault

P006D.title: Barometric Pressure - Turbocharger/Supercharger Inlet Pressure Correlation Bank 1
P006D.description: Without boost, for example with the engine stopped or at low load, the pressure sensor ahead of the turbocharger or supercharger must read about the same as the barometric pressure sensor. P006D is set when the difference is too large; some manufacturers compare against an estimated barometric value instead and run the check once per ignition cycle. Typical causes are a faulty inlet pressure sensor, a faulty barometric sensor (often inside the control module) or a wiring or reference-voltage fault. Each sensor can be electrically fine on its own; regulations require such plausibility checks for input sensors with a code of their own.

causes.label: Inlet pressure sensor faulty
Barometric pressure sensor or control module faulty
Wiring, connector or 5 V reference faulty
Clogged air filter lowering pressure ahead of the compressor

P006E.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Control A Supply Voltage Circuit Low
P006E.description: "Boost control A" is the electrically driven actuator the engine control module uses to set boost pressure, for example a wastegate solenoid, the control valve of variable turbine vanes or an electric actuator. Some engines supply it through two driver stages in the control module: a high side that switches the supply voltage and a low side that switches ground. The low side is covered by P0045 to P0048; this code concerns the high side. P006E is set when the switched supply voltage is too low, typically because the supply wire is shorted to ground or interrupted. Without supply the actuator stays in its rest position, which on most engines means low boost and reduced power.

causes.label: Supply wire shorted to ground or interrupted
Connector at the actuator corroded or loose
Internal short in the actuator
High-side driver in the engine control module faulty

symptoms: Loss of power or reduced power mode

P006F.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Control A Supply Voltage Circuit High
P006F.description: "Boost control A" is the electrically driven actuator the engine control module uses to set boost pressure, for example a wastegate solenoid, the control valve of variable turbine vanes or an electric actuator. Some engines supply it through two driver stages in the control module: a high side that switches the supply voltage and a low side that switches ground. The low side is covered by P0045 to P0048; this code concerns the high side. causes.label: Supply wire shorted to battery voltage

Internal fault in the actuator
High-side driver in the engine control module faulty

symptoms: Loss of power or reduced power mode

P0070.title: Ambient Air Temperature Sensor Circuit A
P0070.description: The ambient air temperature sensor A is an NTC thermistor whose resistance falls as temperature rises. Its value is used by the climate control, the outside temperature display and the engine control module, which needs it to enable other diagnostics and to correct its maps. Depending on the vehicle the engine control module reads the sensor directly, or the instrument cluster or another module sends the value over the data bus; some vehicles have no sensor and estimate ambient temperature from intake air temperature. P0070 is the general circuit fault or an invalid signal, for example when the instrument cluster reports the value as invalid or the reading is implausibly low.

causes.label: Sensor faulty (exposed to spray and stone chips at the front)
Connector corroded or wire damaged, e.g. after front-end damage
Instrument cluster or data transmission faulty (vehicles with bus-supplied value)
Engine control module faulty

symptoms: Wrong or missing outside temperature display

P0071.title: Ambient Air Temperature Sensor Circuit A Range/Performance

P0075.title: Intake Valve Control Solenoid Circuit Bank 1
P0075.description: A solenoid valve on the cylinder head controls oil flow for the variable valve control on the intake side of bank 1. Depending on the manufacturer it drives a camshaft phaser (for example on Nissan engines) or a valve lift changeover (for example on Subaru engines). This code family reports electrical faults in its control circuit; P0075 is the general circuit fault: open circuit or short, without distinguishing between them. Some manufacturers use only this code for all electrical faults of the valve. Other manufacturers report the same valve under the "camshaft position actuator" codes instead. Valve control is then switched off or stays in its base position.

causes.label: Solenoid coil open or shorted
Wiring or connector interrupted, chafed or corroded
Oil at the connector, e.g. from a leaking valve O-ring
Output driver or supply in the engine control module faulty

symptoms: Less power, especially at high engine speed with lift changeover
Follow-up codes for camshaft timing or misfire possible

P007A.title: Charge Air Cooler Temperature Sensor Circuit Bank 1
P007A.description: The charge air cooler temperature sensor (an NTC thermistor) measures the temperature of the compressed charge air at the charge air cooler, depending on the manufacturer upstream or downstream of it, and is often combined with the boost pressure sensor. The engine control module uses it for the air mass calculation, boost control, component protection and to monitor cooler efficiency. causes.label: Control wire shorted to ground, or solenoid winding open (driver-dependent)
Shorted turns in the solenoid coil
Corroded or oil-soaked connector
Output driver or supply in the engine control module faulty

symptoms: Less power, especially at high engine speed with lift changeover
Follow-up codes for camshaft timing or misfire possible

P0086.title: Exhaust Valve Control Solenoid Circuit High Bank 2
P0086.description: A solenoid valve on the cylinder head controls oil flow for the variable valve control on the exhaust side of bank 2. Depending on the manufacturer it drives a camshaft phaser (for example on Nissan engines) or a valve lift changeover (for example on Subaru engines). This code family reports electrical faults in its control circuit; P0086 means the voltage in the control circuit is too high, typically a short to battery voltage. Other manufacturers report the same valve under the "camshaft position actuator" codes instead. Valve control is then switched off or stays in its base position. Bank 2 exists only on V and boxer engines.

causes.label: Control wire shorted to battery voltage
Solenoid coil faulty
Water or corrosion in the connector
Output driver in the engine control module faulty

symptoms: Less power, especially at high engine speed with lift changeover
Follow-up codes for camshaft timing or misfire possible

P0087.title: Fuel Rail/System Pressure - Too Low
P0087.description: On common-rail diesel and gasoline direct-injection engines, a high-pressure pump feeds the fuel rail, a sensor measures rail pressure, and the engine control module regulates it towards a target from its maps. P0087 is set when the actual pressure stays below the target by more than a threshold for some time. It is a system code: it does not say which component is at fault. Typical causes are a weak low-pressure supply, a worn high-pressure pump, a sticking control valve, a leak or a drifting pressure sensor; the engine usually goes into reduced power.

causes.label: Low-pressure supply too weak: lift pump, clogged filter, low tank level or waxing
High-pressure pump worn
Pressure control or metering valve sticking
High-pressure leak or excessive injector return flow
Rail pressure sensor drifting

symptoms: Loss of power or reduced power mode

P0088.title: Fuel Rail/System Pressure - Too High
P0088.description: On common-rail diesel and gasoline direct-injection engines, a high-pressure pump feeds the fuel rail, a sensor measures rail pressure, and the engine control module regulates it towards a target from its maps. P0088 is set when the actual pressure stays above the target by more than a threshold for some time. On many gasoline systems the pump can only raise pressure, which is then reduced only by injecting. Typical causes are a sticking pressure control or metering valve, a drifting pressure sensor or, on diesels with a pressure control valve, a blocked return. Real overpressure can cause harsh combustion noise and smoke.

causes.label: Pressure control or metering valve sticking
Rail pressure sensor drifting
Fuel return blocked (diesel with pressure control valve)
Engine control software

symptoms: Loss of power or reduced power mode

P0089.title: Fuel Pressure Regulator A Performance
P0089.description: On common-rail diesel and gasoline direct-injection engines, a high-pressure pump feeds the fuel rail, a sensor measures rail pressure, and the engine control module regulates it towards a target from its maps. The fuel pressure regulator A is the actuator the manufacturer designates for this: depending on the system a pressure control valve that releases fuel from the rail, or the control valve on the high-pressure pump. Some manufacturers report the pump valve under the "fuel volume regulator" codes instead. P0089 is a function check: pressure may still be plausible, but the regulator works at its limit, needs too much correction, or pressure does not follow its control signal. Typical causes are a sticking or worn regulator, a weak pump or a faulty pressure sensor.

causes.label: Pressure regulator or pump control valve sticking or worn
High-pressure pump weak
Rail pressure sensor faulty
Low-pressure supply too weak
Engine control software

symptoms: Loss of power, reduced power mode possible

P008A.title: Low Pressure Fuel System Pressure - Too Low
P008A.description: Some engines, mainly gasoline direct injection with a demand-controlled in-tank pump, have their own pressure sensor in the low-pressure line between the tank pump and the high-pressure pump. The engine control module compares this supply pressure with its target. P008A is set when the supply pressure stays too low. Besides a weak tank pump or its control unit, a clogged filter or a faulty sensor, simply running the tank empty can set this code.

causes.label: Tank run empty or very low fuel level
In-tank pump or its control unit faulty
Filter or line restricted
Low-pressure sensor faulty

P008B.title: Low Pressure Fuel System Pressure - Too High
P008B.description: Some engines, mainly gasoline direct injection with a demand-controlled in-tank pump, have their own pressure sensor in the low-pressure line between the tank pump and the high-pressure pump. The engine control module compares this supply pressure with its target. P008B is set when the supply pressure stays too high. Manufacturer bulletins name a faulty low-pressure sensor as the most common cause, for example from fuel entering the sensor and falsifying its signal; a mechanical gauge test clarifies whether the pressure is really too high.

causes.label: Low-pressure sensor faulty
Pump control unit or software
Return line or regulator blocked

P008C.title: Fuel Cooler Pump Control Circuit/Open
P008C.description: On some common-rail diesels, fuel returning from the injection system is cooled in a heat exchanger connected to a low-temperature coolant circuit. An electric coolant pump, switched by the engine control module depending on fuel temperature, drives this circuit. P008C reports an open control circuit of this pump or its relay. If the pump fails for long, the fuel runs hotter; some systems then limit power to protect components.

causes.label: Connector or wiring faulty
Fuel cooler pump faulty
Relay or fuse faulty
Output driver in the engine control module faulty

symptoms: Reduced power when fuel gets hot possible

P008D.title: Fuel Cooler Pump Control Circuit Low
P008D.description: On some common-rail diesels, fuel returning from the injection system is cooled in a heat exchanger connected to a low-temperature coolant circuit. An electric coolant pump, switched by the engine control module depending on fuel temperature, drives this circuit. P008D reports too low a voltage, typically a short to ground of this pump or its relay. If the pump fails for long, the fuel runs hotter; some systems then limit power to protect components.

causes.label: Connector or wiring faulty

Relay or fuse faulty
Output driver in the engine control module faulty

symptoms: Reduced power when fuel gets hot possible

symptoms: Reduced power when fuel gets hot possible

P008F.title: Engine Coolant Temperature/Fuel Temperature Correlation
P008F.description: After the engine has been switched off long enough, coolant and fuel should have approached the same temperature. The engine control module compares the coolant temperature sensor with the fuel temperature sensor at the next cold start and sets P008F if they differ too much. From this alone it cannot tell which sensor is wrong, so both have to be checked. Regulations require such plausibility checks for input sensors; the exact conditions are manufacturer-specific.

causes.label: Coolant temperature sensor drifting
Fuel temperature sensor drifting
Contact resistance at a connector
Values distorted, e.g. by an auxiliary heater

P0090.title: Fuel Pressure Regulator A Control Circuit/Open
P0090.description: On common-rail diesel and gasoline direct-injection engines, a high-pressure pump feeds the fuel rail, a sensor measures rail pressure, and the engine control module regulates it towards a target from its maps. The fuel pressure regulator A is the actuator the manufacturer designates for this: depending on the system a pressure control valve that releases fuel from the rail, or the control valve on the high-pressure pump. Some manufacturers report the pump valve under the "fuel volume regulator" codes instead. Rail pressure can then no longer be controlled as intended, and the engine usually runs in reduced power.

causes.label: Wire broken or connector corroded or loose
Regulator coil faulty
Fuse or supply voltage faulty
Output driver in the engine control module faulty

P0093.title: Fuel System Leak Detected - Large Leak
P0093.description: A leak in the high-pressure fuel system is not measured directly but inferred from a pressure and volume balance. P0093 means the pump is already delivering at its limit and rail pressure still stays well below target. The leak can be external (line, rail) or internal (injector return, relief valve). An external leak is a fire hazard: stop the engine and inspect it.

causes.label: High-pressure line or rail fitting leaking
Injector with excessive leak-off
Pressure relief or control valve leaking
Weak pump or low-pressure supply mistaken for a leak

symptoms: Loss of power or reduced power mode

P0094.title: Fuel System Leak Detected - Small Leak
P0094.description: A leak in the high-pressure fuel system is not measured directly but inferred from a pressure and volume balance. P0094 is typically detected when rail pressure drops too fast during overrun with injection cut off, or when more pump delivery than expected is needed at idle. Possible leaks are injectors with too much leak-off, fittings or relief valves; internal leakage can dilute the engine oil with fuel, so a rising oil level is a warning sign.

causes.label: Injector with excessive leak-off
High-pressure fitting slightly leaking
Pressure relief valve leaking
Engine control software (manufacturer updates exist)

symptoms: Rising engine oil level from fuel dilution

P0095.title: Intake Air Temperature Sensor 2 Circuit Bank 1
P0095.description: Intake air temperature sensor 2 is the second air temperature sensor in the intake path. On many turbocharged engines it sits in the intake manifold behind the compressor and charge air cooler, often combined with the manifold pressure sensor, and is used to calculate cylinder filling and ignition timing. The numbering is not standardised, so its position can differ between manufacturers. P0095 is the general circuit fault; low and high signals have their own codes. No manufacturer description naming this exact code was found.

causes.label: Connector or wiring faulty
Sensor or combined sensor faulty
Supply or ground disturbed
Engine control module faulty

symptoms: Slightly changed power or retarded ignition possible

P0096.title: Intake Air Temperature Sensor 2 Circuit Range/Performance Bank 1
P0096.description: Intake air temperature sensor 2 is the second air temperature sensor in the intake path. On many turbocharged engines it sits in the intake manifold behind the compressor and charge air cooler, often combined with the manifold pressure sensor, and is used to calculate cylinder filling and ignition timing. The numbering is not standardised, so its position can differ between manufacturers. P0096 is a plausibility check: at a start after a long standstill the sensor is compared with intake air temperature sensor 1 and others, which should then agree; some systems also flag implausibly high readings while driving. A sensor stuck at one value is detected this way.

causes.label: Sensor drifting or coated with oil or soot from crankcase and exhaust gas recirculation
Contact resistance at the connector
Comparison sensor faulty
Heat soak or leak in the intake manifold

symptoms: Slightly changed power or retarded ignition possible

P0097.title: Intake Air Temperature Sensor 2 Circuit Low Bank 1
P0097.description: Intake air temperature sensor 2 is the second air temperature sensor in the intake path; on many turbocharged engines it sits in the intake manifold, often combined with the manifold pressure sensor, and is used to calculate cylinder filling and ignition timing. For P0097, the sensor signal is below its valid range. With the usual voltage-type NTC sensor this means a short to ground, and the control module reads an extremely high temperature; some manufacturers use sensors with a frequency output, where a low signal instead corresponds to an extremely low temperature (open circuit or short to ground).

causes.label: Sensor shorted internally or signal wire shorted to ground
Connector damp or corroded

Engine control module faulty

symptoms: Slightly changed power or knock control with an implausible reading

symptoms: Emissions test or readiness check may fail

P009A.title: Intake Air Temperature/Ambient Air Temperature Correlation
P009A.description: After a long standstill with the engine cold, intake air temperature and ambient air temperature should be about the same. P009A is set when the two sensors disagree by more than a threshold at the next start. A detected engine block heater usually suspends the test. Several manufacturers perform this comparison under other codes; no manufacturer description naming P009A itself was found. Suspects are both sensors, an ambient sensor in a heat-affected position and contact resistance at a connector.

causes.label: Intake air temperature sensor drifting or contaminated
Ambient temperature sensor faulty or in a heat-affected position
Contact resistance at a connector
Engine block heater or auxiliary heater distorting the comparison

P009B.title: Fuel Pressure Relief Control Circuit/Open
P009B.description: The fuel pressure relief control is an electrically controlled valve on the fuel rail that the engine control module opens to reduce rail pressure deliberately, for example on overrun, on load drops or when the engine is switched off. It differs from the purely mechanical pressure relief valve, which opens passively at overpressure, and from the pressure regulator, which controls pressure continuously. Manufacturer documents show this code mainly on heavy-duty diesel engines. P009B reports an open control circuit of this valve. Rail pressure can then not be reduced as intended, and the engine may be derated.

causes.label: Wire broken or connector corroded
Valve coil faulty
Output driver in the engine control module faulty

P009C.title: Fuel Pressure Relief Control Circuit Low
P009C.description: The fuel pressure relief control is an electrically controlled valve on the fuel rail that the engine control module opens to reduce rail pressure deliberately, for example on overrun, on load drops or when the engine is switched off. P009F.title: Fuel Pressure Relief Control Stuck On

P00A0.title: Charge Air Cooler Temperature Sensor Circuit Bank 2
P00A0.description: The charge air cooler temperature sensor for bank 2 (an NTC thermistor) measures the charge air temperature in the second charge-air path, for example on V engines with two charge air coolers. The engine control module uses it for the air mass calculation, boost control and component protection. For P00A0, this is the general circuit fault; low and high signals have their own codes. No manufacturer description naming this exact code was found. Bank 2 codes occur only on engines with two separate intake or charge-air paths, one per cylinder bank.

Engine control module faulty
