P01C8.title: Fuel Rail/System Pressure - Too Low Bank 2
P01C8.description: Some V engines have a separate high-pressure fuel circuit per bank, each with its own pump or rail – for example Audi's 4.0 TFSI V8 with a second high-pressure pump for bank 2. These codes are the bank 2 counterparts of the system pressure codes for bank 1. P01C8 is the bank 2 counterpart of P0087: the actual pressure stays below target over time. Typical causes are a weak high-pressure pump on bank 2, a faulty volume control valve, low supply pressure or a leak. No manufacturer using exactly this code was found; the logic follows P0087 and CARB's requirement for pressure control. Not every two-rail engine uses them: GM's LT6 reports bank 2 pressure problems under other codes.

causes.label: High-pressure pump of bank 2 weak or worn
Volume control valve faulty or its control disturbed
Supply pressure too low (lift pump, filter)
Leak in the bank 2 high-pressure circuit

symptoms: Loss of power or limp mode

P01C9.title: Fuel Rail/System Pressure - Too High Bank 2
P01C9.description: Some V engines have a separate high-pressure fuel circuit per bank, each with its own pump or rail – for example Audi's 4.0 TFSI V8 with a second high-pressure pump for bank 2. These codes are the bank 2 counterparts of the system pressure codes for bank 1. P01C9 is the bank 2 counterpart of P0088: the actual pressure is above target. Audi documents it on 2013–2014 A8/S8 and S6/S7 4.0 TFSI models together with P0088: at low supply voltage the duty cycle of the volume control valve was no longer sufficient, the valve stayed shut and the pump delivered full flow – audible as noise from pump 2, sometimes with slightly reduced power. The fix was a software update. Not every two-rail engine uses them: GM's LT6 reports bank 2 pressure problems under other codes.

causes.label: Volume control valve not controlled properly (e.g. at low supply voltage), software
Volume control valve sticking
Bank 2 rail pressure sensor reading too high
Pressure relief path blocked

symptoms: Noise from the bank 2 high-pressure pump

P01CA.title: Fuel Rail Pressure Too Low - Engine Cranking Bank 2
P01CA.description: Some V engines have a separate high-pressure fuel circuit per bank, each with its own pump or rail – for example Audi's 4.0 TFSI V8 with a second high-pressure pump for bank 2. These codes are the bank 2 counterparts of the system pressure codes for bank 1. P01CA is the bank 2 counterpart of P00C6: during cranking the rail pressure on bank 2 does not rise quickly enough to the minimum needed to release injection. For bank 1 GM checks once per start that pressure exceeds about 3 MPa and does not fall below 2 MPa, with two trips. No manufacturer using exactly this code was found; GM's two-rail LT6 reports the same situation with the bank-neutral P00C6.

causes.label: High-pressure pump of bank 2 or its drive weak
Low supply pressure at start (lift pump, check valve)
Leak or leaking injector on bank 2
Bank 2 rail pressure sensor or connector

P01CB.title: Cylinder 1 Injection Timing Performance - Over Retarded
P01CB.description: Diesel engines must detect when fuel can no longer be injected at the correct crank angle – CARB requires this for every injector individually, hence one code per cylinder. The start of injection is not measured directly: during overrun with fuel cut-off the control module fires a tiny test injection into one cylinder (GM: about 1.5 mm³) and evaluates the resulting speed change at the crankshaft sensor. From this it learns how much extra energizing time the injector needs (Bosch calls this zero fuel calibration). This code means injector 1 needs clearly more energizing time than intended, i.e. it opens too late – GM sets it above 80 µs of extra time, after two trips. Documented users are GM's 6.6 litre Duramax (LML, L5P) and FCA's 3.0 litre EcoDiesel; Ford reports the same function under P2B11ff. Bulletins often point away from the injector: GM fixed false settings on 2020–2021 L5P trucks with new software and warns that vibration, for example from off-road tyres, disturbs the evaluation; FCA lists wrong injector correction codes, boost leaks and loose injector clamps.

causes.label: Injector worn, coked or sticking (opens late, delivers too little)
False setting from software or vehicle vibration (e.g. off-road tyres)
Wrong injector correction code stored after an injector replacement
Boost leak or loose injector clamp
Contaminated fuel

symptoms: Check engine light on (after two drive cycles)

P01E3.title: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor 3 Circuit
P01E3.description: Coolant temperature sensor 3 is a third NTC coolant sensor on engines with thermal management or split cooling circuits; its position is defined by the manufacturer – on Jaguar Land Rover's 2018–2019 Ingenium petrol engines it sits in the engine block water jacket, on Audi's 3.0 TFSI V6 it is part of the thermal management. As with every NTC sensor, a low signal voltage means hot and a high one cold. CARB requires such additional sensors to be monitored from model year 2019 onwards. P01E3 is the general circuit fault of this sensor without telling low from high. No manufacturer document using exactly this code was found; it is described by analogy with its documented sibling codes and the NTC principle.

causes.label: Open circuit or loose contact at connector or wiring of sensor 3
Sensor open or shorted
Short to ground or voltage in the harness
Control module

symptoms: Coolant temperature or cooling fan behaviour possibly affected

P01E4.title: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor 3 Circuit Range/Performance

As with every NTC sensor, a low signal voltage means hot and a high one cold. CARB requires such additional sensors to be monitored from model year 2019 onwards. P01E4 means the signal is electrically valid but implausible. Audi documents it on 2017–2021 3.0 TFSI V6 models together with cooling system, cylinder head temperature and 'engine temperature too low' codes: the cause was a thermostat that did not close fully, and Audi states that replacing the sensor does not fix it.

causes.label: Thermostat not closing fully
Sensor 3 drifting
Low coolant or air at the sensor
Contact resistance at the connector

symptoms: Engine warms up slowly, heater output weak
Often together with cooling system codes

P01E5.title: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor 3 Circuit Low
P01E5.description: Coolant temperature sensor 3 is a third NTC coolant sensor on engines with thermal management or split cooling circuits; its position is defined by the manufacturer – on Jaguar Land Rover's 2018–2019 Ingenium petrol engines it sits in the engine block water jacket, on Audi's 3.0 TFSI V6 it is part of the thermal management. P01E5 means the signal voltage is too low, so the module would read an implausibly hot coolant – typically a signal wire shorted to ground, coolant or moisture in the connector, or an internally shorted sensor. P01E6.title: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor 3 Circuit High

P01E7.title: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor 3 Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P01E7.description: Coolant temperature sensor 3 is a third NTC coolant sensor on engines with thermal management or split cooling circuits; its position is defined by the manufacturer – on Jaguar Land Rover's 2018–2019 Ingenium petrol engines it sits in the engine block water jacket, on Audi's 3.0 TFSI V6 it is part of the thermal management. As with every NTC sensor, a low signal voltage means hot and a high one cold. CARB requires such additional sensors to be monitored from model year 2019 onwards. P01E7 covers jumps or brief dropouts in the signal – coolant temperature cannot change that fast, so loose contacts, wires broken by vibration or a sensor that opens internally when the temperature changes are the usual causes. No manufacturer document using exactly this code was found; it is described by analogy with its documented sibling codes and the NTC principle.

causes.label: Loose contact at connector or pins
Wire break in the harness (movement, vibration)
Sensor opening internally with temperature changes
Corrosion or moisture in the connector

P01E8.title: Engine Coolant Heater A Control Circuit/Open
P01E8.description: Engine coolant heater A is an electric coolant heater switched by the engine module, directly or via a relay or power stage, to shorten warm-up – less cold-start emissions and faster cabin heat; A and B denote two separately switched heaters or stages. It is not the same as a mains-powered block heater (which the vehicle does not control) or the electrically heated thermostat (P0597–P0599). CARB requires output components to be checked for correct response or at least for circuit faults. This code reports an open control circuit – the module detects missing continuity, typically with the driver switched off. No manufacturer using these codes was found in the GM, Ford or NHTSA documents checked; the typical driver diagnosis (open circuit detected with the driver switched off, as GM does for other outputs) is an analogy, and thresholds are unknown.

causes.label: Control wire or connector to the heater or relay open
Heater element burnt out or relay coil open
Fuse in the load circuit blown
Control module output stage faulty

symptoms: Longer warm-up, cabin heat slower in winter

P01E9.title: Engine Coolant Heater A Control Circuit Low
P01E9.description: Engine coolant heater A is an electric coolant heater switched by the engine module, directly or via a relay or power stage, to shorten warm-up – less cold-start emissions and faster cabin heat; A and B denote two separately switched heaters or stages. causes.label: Control wire shorted to ground (chafed harness)
Heater element or relay coil shorted to ground
Moisture or corrosion in the connector
Control module output stage

P01EA.title: Engine Coolant Heater A Control Circuit High

P01EB.title: Engine Coolant Heater A Control Circuit Performance
P01EB.description: Engine coolant heater A is an electric coolant heater switched by the engine module, directly or via a relay or power stage, to shorten warm-up – less cold-start emissions and faster cabin heat; A and B denote two separately switched heaters or stages. P01F0.title: Coolant Temperature Relapsed Below Diagnostic Monitoring Temperature
P01F0.description: Since model years 2019–2021 CARB requires petrol engines to detect a thermostat fault not only during warm-up but also when the coolant, after reaching operating temperature, drops back below the temperature needed for other diagnostics. P01F0 is this check. GM sets it when coolant falls below 64 °C with a conventional thermostat or 70.5 °C with an electrically heated one (2019 Corvette: 65/78.5 °C) after having been above it, with at least 0.8 km driven, ambient above −7 °C, enough heat input and no long overrun downhill; two trips. GM also uses it on the 6.6 litre Duramax diesel as a 'stuck open thermostat' check. Ford does not use the code in the documents checked. Usual cause is a thermostat stuck open.

causes.label: Thermostat stuck open or not sealing
Heated map thermostat, thermal management valve or switchable water pump faulty
Radiator fan running constantly (relay stuck)
Coolant sensor drifting cold
Low coolant or air in the system

symptoms: Check engine light on (after two drive cycles)

P01F1.title: O2 Sensor Circuit Bank 1 Sensor 4
P01F1.description: Sensor 4 on bank 1 is a fourth oxygen sensor, behind a third converter or converter brick. The OBD standard provides for up to four sensors per bank, and the code standard defines sensor 4 for bank 1 only. No manufacturer or vehicle using these codes could be identified; the description rests on CARB's requirements for downstream oxygen sensors and the logic of sensors 2 and 3. A switching sensor delivers about 0.1–0.9 V. P01F1 is the general circuit code of this sensor, the counterpart of P0136/P0142 for sensors 2 and 3. Typical causes are an aged sensor, open or high-resistance wiring and a failed heater.

causes.label: Sensor 4 aged or poisoned
Wiring or connector open, high-resistance or corroded
Sensor heater failed
Control module

symptoms: Check engine light on (usually after two drive cycles)
Catalyst monitor readiness possibly not set

P01F2.title: O2 Sensor Circuit Low Voltage Bank 1 Sensor 4
P01F2.description: Sensor 4 on bank 1 is a fourth oxygen sensor, behind a third converter or converter brick. The OBD standard provides for up to four sensors per bank, and the code standard defines sensor 4 for bank 1 only. No manufacturer or vehicle using these codes could be identified; the description rests on CARB's requirements for downstream oxygen sensors and the logic of sensors 2 and 3. A switching sensor delivers about 0.1–0.9 V. P01F2 means the signal stays near 0 V – typically a signal wire shorted to ground, a faulty sensor or an exhaust leak ahead of it; GM checks its other downstream sensors for a signal below about 40–60 mV.

causes.label: Signal wire shorted to ground
Sensor faulty
Exhaust leak ahead of the sensor

symptoms: Check engine light on (usually after two drive cycles)
Catalyst monitor readiness possibly not set

P01F3.title: O2 Sensor Circuit High Voltage Bank 1 Sensor 4
P01F3.description: Sensor 4 on bank 1 is a fourth oxygen sensor, behind a third converter or converter brick. The OBD standard provides for up to four sensors per bank, and the code standard defines sensor 4 for bank 1 only. No manufacturer or vehicle using these codes could be identified; the description rests on CARB's requirements for downstream oxygen sensors and the logic of sensors 2 and 3. A switching sensor delivers about 0.1–0.9 V. P01F3 means the signal is above about 1.05–1.1 V, which a switching sensor cannot produce – typically the heater supply or another voltage on the signal wire, or a heater-to-signal short inside the sensor.

causes.label: Signal wire shorted to heater supply or battery voltage
Sensor faulty internally
Sensor ground open (bias logic)

symptoms: Check engine light on (usually after two drive cycles)
Catalyst monitor readiness possibly not set

P01F4.title: O2 Sensor Circuit Slow Response Bank 1 Sensor 4
P01F4.description: Sensor 4 on bank 1 is a fourth oxygen sensor, behind a third converter or converter brick. The OBD standard provides for up to four sensors per bank, and the code standard defines sensor 4 for bank 1 only. No manufacturer or vehicle using these codes could be identified; the description rests on CARB's requirements for downstream oxygen sensors and the logic of sensors 2 and 3. A switching sensor delivers about 0.1–0.9 V. P01F4 means the sensor reacts too slowly to mixture changes; CARB requires at least a rich-to-lean response test of downstream sensors during fuel cut-off. Behind several converters the oxygen storage buffers the change, so limits are wide.

causes.label: Sensor aged or contaminated
Exhaust leak ahead of the sensor
Sensor heater weak

symptoms: Check engine light on (usually after two drive cycles)
Catalyst monitor readiness possibly not set

P01F5.title: O2 Sensor Circuit No Activity Detected Bank 1 Sensor 4
P01F5.description: Sensor 4 on bank 1 is a fourth oxygen sensor, downstream of a further converter. No manufacturer or vehicle using sensor 4 codes could be identified (GM and Ford documents stop at sensor 3); the description follows CARB's requirements for downstream sensors and GM's checks on sensor 2. P01F5 means that with a warm engine and heated sensor the signal does not switch between rich and lean but stays in the middle or at the bias voltage the module applies. For sensor 2, GM detects this when the signal stays above 1.7 V of a 1.9 V bias, a two-trip fault. Usual causes are an open signal or ground wire or a dead sensor.

causes.label: Signal or ground wire open, connector corroded
Sensor aged or poisoned, produces no voltage
Sensor heater faulty, sensor does not reach operating temperature
Exhaust leak upstream of the sensor

symptoms: Check engine light on (usually after two drive cycles)
Catalyst monitor readiness possibly not set

P01F6.title: O2 Sensor Signal Biased/Stuck Lean Bank 1 Sensor 4
P01F6.description: Sensor 4 on bank 1 is a fourth oxygen sensor, downstream of a further converter. No manufacturer or vehicle using sensor 4 codes could be identified (GM and Ford documents stop at sensor 3); the description follows CARB's requirements for downstream sensors and GM's checks on sensor 2. P01F6 means the sensor stays lean: the module deliberately enriches the mixture, and if the sensor does not reach the expected rich voltage before a set amount of air has passed, it counts as stuck lean. GM runs this test on sensor 2 once per trip as a two-trip fault. Usual causes are an aged sensor, an exhaust leak ahead of it or a signal wire shorted to ground.

causes.label: Sensor aged, characteristic shifted lean
Exhaust leak or false air upstream of the sensor
Signal wire shorted to ground or contact resistance
Misfires or mixture fault (excess oxygen)

symptoms: Check engine light on (usually after two drive cycles)
Catalyst monitor readiness possibly not set

P01F7.title: O2 Sensor Signal Biased/Stuck Rich Bank 1 Sensor 4
P01F7.description: Sensor 4 on bank 1 is a fourth oxygen sensor, downstream of a further converter. No manufacturer or vehicle using sensor 4 codes could be identified (GM and Ford documents stop at sensor 3); the description follows CARB's requirements for downstream sensors and GM's checks on sensor 2. P01F7 means the sensor stays rich: when the module leans the mixture or cuts fuel on overrun, the signal does not drop into the lean range. CARB names exactly this rich-to-lean transition during fuel cut-off as the minimum check for downstream sensors; GM tests sensor 2 this way as a two-trip fault. Usual causes are a sooted or oil-fouled sensor or a signal wire shorted to the heater supply.

causes.label: Sensor sooted, oil-fouled or aged
Signal wire shorted to voltage (e.g. heater supply)
Mixture genuinely rich (leaking injector, coolant or oil burning)

symptoms: Check engine light on (usually after two drive cycles)
Catalyst monitor readiness possibly not set

P01F8.title: Engine Coolant Heater A Control Circuit Driver Current/Temperature Too High
P01F8.description: The engine module switches an electric coolant heater A through a power stage (driver). This code means the driver itself has reported excessive current or overheating and has shut down to protect itself – it concerns the control circuit, not the coolant temperature. Such heaters warm the coolant around a cold start, shortening warm-up and providing cabin heat sooner; a GM patent describes how the module recognises a pre-heated engine so other temperature diagnostics do not misfire. No manufacturer using this code family was found in GM, Ford or FCA documents; the description rests on CARB's requirements for output components. Siblings for heater A are P01E8–P01EB.

causes.label: Short or partial short in heater element A
Wiring or connector chafed to ground, moisture in connector
Driver stage in the module or relay faulty or overheated
Heater running without coolant (low level, air pocket)

symptoms: Check engine light or warning message (manufacturer-dependent)
Slow warm-up, little heat in cold weather

P01F9.title: Engine Coolant Heater B Control Circuit Driver Current/Temperature Too High
P01F9.description: The engine module switches an electric coolant heater B – a second heater or heating stage – through a power stage (driver). This code means the driver itself has reported excessive current or overheating and has shut down to protect itself – it concerns the control circuit, not the coolant temperature. Such heaters warm the coolant around a cold start, shortening warm-up and providing cabin heat sooner; a GM patent describes how the module recognises a pre-heated engine so other temperature diagnostics do not misfire. No manufacturer using this code family was found in GM, Ford or FCA documents; the description rests on CARB's requirements for output components. Siblings for heater B are P01EC–P01EF.

causes.label: Short or partial short in heater element B
Wiring or connector chafed to ground, moisture in connector
Driver stage in the module or relay faulty or overheated

symptoms: Check engine light or warning message (manufacturer-dependent)
Slow warm-up, little heat in cold weather

P01FA.title: Turbocharger Outlet Pressure Sensor B Circuit
P01FA.description: Turbocharger outlet pressure sensor B is a second pressure sensor at a compressor outlet – for example one per turbo on twin-turbo engines or a second measuring point; sensor A has the codes P00F8–P00FC. It is a separate family from the boost pressure sensor: GM and Ford report the pressure ahead of the throttle under the boost sensor codes P0236–P0238. No manufacturer using the sensor B codes was found; FCA documents sensor A and a second outlet sensor. P01FA is the general electrical fault that the module does not classify as low or high. Without a plausible actual pressure, boost control usually limits boost.

causes.label: Connector or pins at sensor B loose or corroded
Harness damaged (5 V reference, signal, ground)
Sensor faulty
Engine module or 5 V supply disturbed

P01FB.title: Turbocharger Outlet Pressure Sensor B Range/Performance
P01FB.description: Turbocharger outlet pressure sensor B is a second pressure sensor at a compressor outlet – for example one per turbo on twin-turbo engines or a second measuring point; sensor A has the codes P00F8–P00FC. It is a separate family from the boost pressure sensor: GM and Ford report the pressure ahead of the throttle under the boost sensor codes P0236–P0238. No manufacturer using the sensor B codes was found; FCA documents sensor A and a second outlet sensor. P01FB is the plausibility fault: the signal is electrically valid but does not fit. After a long stop all pressures should equal barometric pressure; while running the value is compared with a pressure modelled from airflow, speed and throttle – GM flags its boost sensor at deviations of roughly 25–30 kPa.

causes.label: Sensor drifting or stuck
Leaking charge air hose or blocked pressure port
Contact resistance at the connector
Fault in other model inputs (MAF, MAP)

P01FC.title: Turbocharger Outlet Pressure Sensor B Circuit Low
P01FC.description: Turbocharger outlet pressure sensor B is a second pressure sensor at a compressor outlet – for example one per turbo on twin-turbo engines or a second measuring point; sensor A has the codes P00F8–P00FC. It is a separate family from the boost pressure sensor: GM and Ford report the pressure ahead of the throttle under the boost sensor codes P0236–P0238. No manufacturer using the sensor B codes was found; FCA documents sensor A and a second outlet sensor. P01FC means the signal voltage stays below its lower limit – usually a signal wire shorted to ground or a missing 5 V reference. For comparison, GM sets its boost sensor low code below 14.4 % of 5 V, Ford below 0.19 V for 5 s.

causes.label: Signal wire shorted to ground
5 V reference open or shorted
Sensor faulty internally

P01FD.title: Turbocharger Outlet Pressure Sensor B Circuit High
P01FD.description: Turbocharger outlet pressure sensor B is a second pressure sensor at a compressor outlet – for example one per turbo on twin-turbo engines or a second measuring point; sensor A has the codes P00F8–P00FC. It is a separate family from the boost pressure sensor: GM and Ford report the pressure ahead of the throttle under the boost sensor codes P0236–P0238. No manufacturer using the sensor B codes was found; FCA documents sensor A and a second outlet sensor. P01FD means the signal voltage stays above its upper limit – typically an open signal or sensor ground (the input is pulled up) or a short to voltage. For comparison, GM sets its boost sensor high code above 86 % of 5 V, Ford above 4.88 V.

causes.label: Sensor ground or signal wire open
Signal shorted to 5 V or battery voltage
Sensor faulty

P01FE.title: Turbocharger Outlet Pressure Sensor B Intermittent/Erratic
P01FE.description: Turbocharger outlet pressure sensor B is a second pressure sensor at a compressor outlet – for example one per turbo on twin-turbo engines or a second measuring point; sensor A has the codes P00F8–P00FC. It is a separate family from the boost pressure sensor: GM and Ford report the pressure ahead of the throttle under the boost sensor codes P0236–P0238. No manufacturer using the sensor B codes was found; FCA documents sensor A and a second outlet sensor. P01FE counts brief spikes or dropouts that are too short for the low or high code. Ford's equivalent boost sensor check sets after 10 such events in one drive cycle. The usual cause is a loose or corroded contact or a wire broken by vibration and heat.

causes.label: Loose contact or corroded connector
Wire breaking from vibration or heat
Sensor erratic internally

P01FF.title: Turbocharger Outlet Pressure Sensor A/B Correlation
P01FF.description: Turbocharger outlet pressure sensor B is a second pressure sensor at a compressor outlet – for example one per turbo on twin-turbo engines or a second measuring point; sensor A has the codes P00F8–P00FC. It is a separate family from the boost pressure sensor: GM and Ford report the pressure ahead of the throttle under the boost sensor codes P0236–P0238. No manufacturer using the sensor B codes was found; FCA documents sensor A and a second outlet sensor. P01FF compares sensors A and B: with the engine off both should read barometric pressure, and in comparable operation they must agree within a tolerance. If they disagree without either being electrically faulty, this code sets; which one is wrong is found by comparing with barometric and manifold pressure. On twin-turbo engines a genuinely weaker turbo on one bank can also cause it.

causes.label: One sensor drifting
Leak or hose damage between the measuring points or on one bank
Contact resistance at one sensor's connector or ground
Uneven turbo output (twin-turbo, wastegate or vanes on one side)

P0200.title: Injector Circuit/Open
P0200.description: P0200 is the injector circuit fault without a cylinder assignment. The large US manufacturers do not use it – GM and Ford report injector faults per cylinder (P0201 ff) or as faults of the shared injector supply (P062D/P062E, P2146 ff). Saab documents it on the 3.0 V6 diesel of the 9-5, whose injectors are driven by a separate power stage behind the glovebox: there P0200 means an electrical fault in that power stage or its wiring, and the engine is shut down. Generally the cause lies in something all injectors share – supply, fuse, relay, ground or driver stage – so several cylinders are affected at once. CARB does not require separate codes for each kind of circuit fault.

causes.label: Shared injector supply open (fuse, relay, harness connector)
Separate injector power stage or its wiring faulty (diesel)
Driver stage in the engine module faulty
Ground fault of the module or power stage

symptoms: Engine does not start or shuts down

P0201.title: Cylinder 1 Injector A Circuit/Open
P0201.description: P0201 reports an electrical fault, mainly an open circuit, in the injector circuit of cylinder 1. The engine module watches each injector output: GM flags an open circuit at an impedance of 200 kΩ or more – on direct injection and diesel engines in 10 of 20 or 5 of 10 samples and with the warning light in the first trip, on some port-injected engines only after two trips. Ford's port injection reads a fault bit from the driver chip that covers open, short to ground and short to voltage alike; Ford diesels report only the open circuit here and shorts as P0261/P0262. On direct injection the affected injector is switched off; the cylinder misfires.

causes.label: Connector at the cylinder 1 injector loose, corroded or with a broken or pushed-back pin
Injector coil open
Wire between module and injector open or chafed (heat, rodents)
Injector supply missing (fuse, relay) – then usually several cylinders at once
Driver stage in the engine module faulty

symptoms: Misfire and rough running, misfire code P0301
Limp mode possible on diesel and direct injection

causes.label: Connector at the cylinder 2 injector loose, corroded or with a broken or pushed-back pin

Wire between module and injector open or chafed (heat, rodents)

P020A.title: Cylinder 1 Injection Timing
P020A.description: P020A reports a fault in the injection timing of cylinder 1 on a diesel engine. P0213.title: Cold Start Injector 1
P0213.description: A cold start injector is an additional injector in the intake manifold that sprays extra fuel for a few seconds while a cold engine is cranked. In classic Bosch systems a thermo-time switch on the block powers it directly, without the engine module – such systems cannot set a code at all. A code is only possible where the engine module drives the valve and monitors its circuit, as CARB requires for output components. From the 1990s the main injectors took over cold-start enrichment, so the code only fits early OBD II engines. P0213 concerns cold start injector 1. No manufacturer using it was found in GM, Ford or Saab documents.

causes.label: Connector or wire corroded or open
Valve coil open or valve stuck
Thermo-time switch or control relay faulty
Driver stage in the engine module faulty

symptoms: Poor cold start, long cranking in cold weather
Leaking valve: hot-start problems, flooding, black smoke

P0215.title: Engine Shutoff Solenoid
P0215.description: The engine shutoff solenoid is the electric stop valve on older diesel injection pumps, mainly distributor pumps. It is energised with the ignition on and lets fuel into the pump; with no current a spring closes it, the pump runs dry and the engine stops – also as a safety backup if the governor fails. P0215 reports a fault in this solenoid or its supply, typically a broken coil, a sticking plunger, a blown fuse or relay, or a wiring fault. The result is either an engine that will not start or dies, or one that keeps running after switch-off. Newer diesels stop through the injectors or a fuel shutoff valve with its own codes P0005–P0007. No manufacturer document describing P0215 was found; the description rests on CARB's requirements for output components and a Bosch patent on the valve.

causes.label: Shutoff solenoid faulty (open coil, sticking plunger)
Relay or fuse in the supply circuit faulty
Broken wire, corrosion or ground fault at the pump connector
Pump control module faulty
Engine module driver faulty

symptoms: Engine does not start or stalls while driving
Engine keeps running after ignition off (solenoid stuck open)

P0216.title: Injector/Injection Timing Control Circuit
P0216.description: P0216 is a diesel code for the control of injection timing. On 1990s distributor pumps with an electronic timing advance it meant that actual injection timing missed its target; today manufacturers use it for the electronic injector control, with different meanings. GM's Duramax diesels compare, inside the engine module, the summed injection pulse widths from the hardware driver with those calculated by the software; a mismatch in 30 of 124 or 60 consecutive checks sets the code with the warning light in the first trip. On GM's 3.0 litre LM2 it appeared together with P0202 from a broken pin in the injector 2 connector. Saab's 3.0 V6 diesel uses it for a fault in the separate injector power stage. The result can be loss of power, rough running, smoke and limp mode.

causes.label: Injector harness or connector (broken pin) – common rail
Engine module or injector power stage faulty internally
Distributor pump electronics or timing advance faulty
Low supply pressure on distributor pumps (lift pump, filter)
Pump installed incorrectly, drive gear misaligned

symptoms: Hard starting or stalling (distributor pump), smoke

P0217.title: Engine Coolant Over Temperature Condition
P0217.description: P0217 is a condition code: the engine module reports that coolant temperature has passed a protection threshold. The limit and the reaction depend on the manufacturer – Saab's 2.2 diesel sets it at 120 °C for over 10 s, limits fuel quantity and suspends EGR and boost diagnostics until the temperature drops; heavy-duty diesels cut power sharply and may shut down; Ford petrol engines use their own code P1299 and cut fuel to individual cylinders. Whether the warning light comes on varies, because CARB exempts overheat protection that only engages once the gauge reads red. Usual causes are low coolant, a thermostat stuck closed, a failed fan or water pump – but Ford traced some cases to a faulty coolant sensor or harness.

causes.label: Low coolant (leak, head gasket)
Thermostat stuck closed
Radiator fan, fan clutch or water pump faulty, radiator clogged
Coolant temperature sensor or harness faulty (false reading)
Extreme load (towing, gradient, heat) with an intact cooling system

symptoms: Temperature gauge in the red, overheat warning
Loss of power, limp mode, cylinders possibly shut off
Steam or coolant smell, coolant loss

P0218.title: Transmission Fluid Temperature Sensor A Over Temperature Condition
P0218.description: P0218 is a condition code: the transmission or engine module reports that transmission fluid temperature sensor A reads above an overheat limit. Saab's Aisin automatic sets it above 170 °C for more than 10 s, or above 140 °C for two minutes at high speed, shows a 'transmission overheating' warning and shifts less smoothly; afterwards a fluid change is advised because the additives are spent. Ford uses its own code on diesels and lists P0218 without the warning light on other models. Reactions include earlier torque converter lock-up, a modified shift pattern and sometimes reduced power. Causes are real overheating – towing, hills, low or old fluid, a clogged cooler – or a sensor reading wrongly.

causes.label: High load (towing, hills, sustained full throttle, stop-and-go in heat)
Transmission fluid low or aged
Fluid cooler, thermostat or lines clogged, weak cooling system
Torque converter clutch slipping or internal damage
Temperature sensor or wiring reading wrongly

symptoms: Limp mode or reduced power possible

P0219.title: Engine Overspeed Condition
P0219.description: P0219 is a condition code: engine speed has exceeded the overspeed limit even though the rev limiter already cuts fuel – so the engine was driven from outside, usually by downshifting at too high a road speed or descending in too low a gear, or the speed signal was wrong. Limits: Ford 6.7 litre diesel above 4,200 rpm, 3.0 litre above 4,800 rpm, after 0.1 s; GM/Saab 2.8 V6 petrol with manual gearbox above 7,000 rpm for 1 s; Saab 2.2 diesel above 6,200 rpm, although fuel is cut from 5,000 rpm. Many manufacturers store it without the warning light. Saab advises: together with a camshaft sensor code it was real overspeed, alone check the speed signal; after real overspeed inspect the engine for valve train damage.

causes.label: Downshift at too high a road speed (manual gearbox)
Descending in too low a gear
Fault in the speed signal (crankshaft sensor, wiring)
Diesel runaway (oil drawn into the intake) or sticking injection

symptoms: Usually no lasting symptoms, only a stored code
Briefly very high revs, limiter intervening
After real overspeed: rattling, loss of power

P0220.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch B Circuit
P0220.description: With electronic throttle control the throttle body carries two position sensors, A and B, usually with opposite or offset signals, and the engine module compares them (correlation code P2135). GM and Ford give the pedal sensors their own codes (P2120 ff), so B is in practice the second throttle sensor. P0220 is the general circuit fault of sensor B without telling low from high. GM uses it in a special sense on 2015–2016 V8 engines: the signal lies outside 0.25–4.59 V only in the monitoring processor while the main processor sees it as valid; this sets immediately with the warning light. Newer GM and Ford engines report sensor B faults as P0222/P0223. The module carries on with sensor A, limits throttle opening and power and switches off cruise control.

causes.label: Throttle body or sensor B faulty (worn track)
Wiring or connector at the throttle body (corrosion, break)
5 V reference disturbed (short in another sensor on the same reference)
Engine module input or monitoring processor faulty

symptoms: Check engine light and throttle warning light

P0221.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch B Circuit Range/Performance
P0221.description: With electronic throttle control the throttle body carries two position sensors, A and B, usually with opposite or offset signals, and the engine module compares them (correlation code P2135). GM and Ford give the pedal sensors their own codes (P2120 ff), so B is in practice the second throttle sensor. P0221 is the plausibility fault: the signal of sensor B is electrically valid but does not match sensor A or the throttle position expected from airflow. Bosch ME9 engines (Saab) set it at a deviation of more than 9 %, older Ford systems at more than 7 degrees between the sensors without the warning light; many newer engines report this only as P2135. The module carries on with sensor A, limits throttle opening and power and switches off cruise control.

causes.label: Worn track of sensor B (signal jumps)
Contact resistance at connector or wiring
Throttle dirty or sticking
Mass airflow sensor fault or false air

P0222.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch B Circuit Low
P0222.description: With electronic throttle control the throttle body carries two position sensors, A and B, usually with opposite or offset signals, and the engine module compares them (correlation code P2135). GM and Ford give the pedal sensors their own codes (P2120 ff), so B is in practice the second throttle sensor. P0222 means the signal of sensor B is below its lower limit – GM about 0.25 V, Ford below 0.25 V – typically a short to ground, an open signal wire or a missing 5 V reference. Both detect it within about a second and switch the warning light on in the first trip. If the shared reference fails, several sensors report low at once. The module carries on with sensor A, limits throttle opening and power and switches off cruise control.

causes.label: Signal or 5 V wire open or shorted to ground
Throttle body or sensor B faulty internally
5 V reference pulled down by another sensor
Connector corrosion or water ingress
Engine module faulty

symptoms: Check engine light and throttle warning light

P0223.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch B Circuit High
P0223.description: With electronic throttle control the throttle body carries two position sensors, A and B, usually with opposite or offset signals, and the engine module compares them (correlation code P2135). GM and Ford give the pedal sensors their own codes (P2120 ff), so B is in practice the second throttle sensor. P0223 means the signal of sensor B is above its upper limit – GM above 4.59 V, Ford above 4.75 V – typically an open sensor ground, a signal shorted to 5 V or battery voltage, or an open signal wire on a pulled-up input. Both detect it within about a second and switch the warning light on in the first trip. The module carries on with sensor A, limits throttle opening and power and switches off cruise control.

causes.label: Sensor ground open
Sensor B or throttle body faulty
Signal shorted to 5 V or 12 V in the harness
Engine module faulty

symptoms: Check engine light and throttle warning light

P0224.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch B Circuit Intermittent
P0224.description: With electronic throttle control the throttle body carries two position sensors, A and B, usually with opposite or offset signals, and the engine module compares them (correlation code P2135). GM and Ford give the pedal sensors their own codes (P2120 ff), so B is in practice the second throttle sensor. P0224 reports brief dropouts or jumps of sensor B that do not last long enough for the steady fault codes. No manufacturer using exactly this code was found: GM counts intermittent faults within P0222/P0223, and Ford's digital sensors report intermittent faults as P0124 for sensor A and P0229 for sensor C – after more than 0.4 s, while a steady fault needs over 4 s. Depending on frequency the result is jerking or brief limp mode.

causes.label: Loose contact or corroded connector at the throttle body
Worn spot on the sensor track
Wire breaking from engine movement or vibration
Engine module or ground connection

P0225.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch C Circuit
P0225.description: Sensor C is a third throttle or pedal position sensor whose role depends on the manufacturer. Ford uses it for the sensor of the second throttle body on engines with two throttles and digital (SENT) sensors; with other makes it can be a further pedal or throttle channel. P0225 is the general circuit fault of sensor C without telling low from high (those are P0227/P0228). Ford sets it when the digital sensor of the second throttle body has been faulty for more than 4 s and switches on the warning light and the powertrain fault lamp; communication faults of the sensor line have their own codes. The result is reduced power.

causes.label: Sensor C or second throttle body faulty
Wiring or connector (supply, signal line)
5 V reference disturbed
Engine module

symptoms: Check engine light and powertrain fault lamp

P0226.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch C Circuit Range/Performance
P0226.description: Sensor C is a third throttle or pedal position sensor whose role depends on the manufacturer. Ford uses it for the sensor of the second throttle body on engines with two throttles and digital (SENT) sensors; with other makes it can be a further pedal or throttle channel. P0226 is the plausibility fault: the signal of sensor C is electrically valid but does not match its partner sensor or the airflow model. No manufacturer using exactly this code was found – Ford does not report sensor C plausibility separately. The logic follows the sibling checks on sensors A and B (Bosch: more than 9 % deviation, Ford: more than 7 degrees). The result is limp mode with reduced power.

causes.label: Wear or dirt on sensor C or the second throttle body
Contact resistance at connector or wiring
Throttle dirty or sticking
Engine module or software

P0227.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch C Circuit Low
P0227.description: Sensor C is a third throttle or pedal position signal; its role depends on the manufacturer. Ford uses it for the sensor of the second throttle body on engines with two throttles and digital (SENT) sensors, GM does not use it. P0227 means the signal of sensor C is below its lower limit – on an analogue sensor a signal wire shorted to ground or an open signal or 5 V reference wire. The module discards sensor C and runs in limp mode with limited power. Ford reports low and high faults of its digital sensor C as U2111/U2112 instead, so no manufacturer using exactly this code was found; the description follows CARB's input monitoring requirement and the sensor A/B siblings.

causes.label: Signal wire of sensor C shorted to ground or open (chafing, connector)
5 V reference to the sensor open or loaded
Sensor C or second throttle body faulty
Corrosion or water in the throttle body connector
Engine module input faulty

symptoms: Check engine light (Ford also the wrench light)

P0228.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch C Circuit High
P0228.description: Sensor C is a third throttle or pedal position signal; its role depends on the manufacturer. Ford uses it for the sensor of the second throttle body on engines with two throttles and digital (SENT) sensors, GM does not use it. P0228 means the signal of sensor C is above its upper limit – typically an open sensor ground, which pulls the signal up to the reference, or a signal wire shorted to voltage. The module discards sensor C and runs in limp mode with limited power. Ford reports low and high faults of its digital sensor C as U2111/U2112 instead, so no manufacturer using exactly this code was found; the description follows CARB's input monitoring requirement and the sensor A/B siblings.

causes.label: Sensor ground (low reference) open
Signal wire shorted to 5 V or system voltage
Sensor C or throttle body faulty
Connector corroded or water ingress
Engine module faulty

symptoms: Check engine light (Ford also the wrench light)

P0229.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch C Circuit Intermittent
P0229.description: Sensor C is a third throttle or pedal position signal; its role depends on the manufacturer. Ford uses it for the sensor of the second throttle body on engines with two throttles and digital (SENT) sensors, GM does not use it. P0229 reports a fault of sensor C that comes and goes. Ford documents it exactly: if its digital sensor on the second throttle body reports a fault for more than 0.4 s, P0229 sets; if the fault persists beyond 4 s it becomes P0225. Both switch on the warning light and the wrench light. Typical causes are a loose contact at the second throttle body's connector or chafed wiring.

causes.label: Loose contact at the second throttle body connector (spread pins, corrosion)
Harness chafing with intermittent short or open
Sensor or second throttle body with an internal intermittent fault
Voltage dips in the supply or ground

symptoms: Check engine light and wrench light (Ford)
Brief jerking or loss of power

P022A.title: Charge Air Cooler Bypass Control A Circuit/Open
P022A.description: The charge air cooler bypass is a flap or valve that routes compressed air around the charge air cooler, so the engine and exhaust warm up faster after a cold start; when warm it closes or opens partly to control intake air temperature. It is driven by an electric motor with a built-in position sensor or by a solenoid and vacuum can. P022A is the general circuit fault of the actuator drive, mainly an open circuit: the driver sees no current or an output voltage outside its window. The module then switches bypass control off and the flap stays in its rest position. No manufacturer document using this code was found – GM and Ford do not use the bypass codes; the description rests on CARB's component monitoring requirement and a Bosch patent on the bypass valve.

causes.label: Wire or connector at the bypass actuator open
Actuator or solenoid of the bypass flap faulty (coil, motor)
Fuse or relay of the actuator supply
Driver stage in the engine module faulty

symptoms: Depending on the rest position: longer warm-up or higher charge air temperature with slight loss of power

P022B.title: Charge Air Cooler Bypass Control A Circuit Low
P022B.description: The charge air cooler bypass is a flap or valve that routes compressed air around the charge air cooler, so the engine and exhaust warm up faster after a cold start; when warm it closes or opens partly to control intake air temperature. It is driven by an electric motor with a built-in position sensor or by a solenoid and vacuum can. P022B means the drive circuit reads low – typically the control wire shorted to ground. The module then switches bypass control off and the flap stays in its rest position. No manufacturer document using this code was found – GM and Ford do not use the bypass codes; the description rests on CARB's component monitoring requirement and a Bosch patent on the bypass valve.

causes.label: Control wire shorted to ground (chafing)
Actuator winding shorted
Moisture or corrosion in the connector
Driver stage in the engine module faulty

symptoms: Depending on the rest position: longer warm-up or higher charge air temperature with slight loss of power

P022C.title: Charge Air Cooler Bypass Control A Circuit High
P022C.description: The charge air cooler bypass is a flap or valve that routes compressed air around the charge air cooler, so the engine and exhaust warm up faster after a cold start; when warm it closes or opens partly to control intake air temperature. It is driven by an electric motor with a built-in position sensor or by a solenoid and vacuum can. P022C means the drive circuit reads high – typically the control wire shorted to voltage, so the driver cannot switch it. The module then switches bypass control off and the flap stays in its rest position. No manufacturer document using this code was found – GM and Ford do not use the bypass codes; the description rests on CARB's component monitoring requirement and a Bosch patent on the bypass valve.

causes.label: Control wire shorted to voltage
Actuator shorted internally (overcurrent)
Moisture or corrosion in the connector
Driver stage in the engine module faulty

symptoms: Depending on the rest position: longer warm-up or higher charge air temperature with slight loss of power

P022D.description: The charge air cooler bypass is a flap or valve that routes compressed air around the charge air cooler, so the engine and exhaust warm up faster after a cold start; when warm it closes or opens partly to control intake air temperature. The module then switches bypass control off and the flap stays in its rest position. No manufacturer document using this code was found – GM and Ford do not use the bypass codes; the description rests on CARB's component monitoring requirement and a Bosch patent on the bypass valve.

Actuator or solenoid of the bypass flap faulty (coil, motor)
Fuse or relay of the actuator supply
Driver stage in the engine module faulty

P022E.description: The charge air cooler bypass is a flap or valve that routes compressed air around the charge air cooler, so the engine and exhaust warm up faster after a cold start; when warm it closes or opens partly to control intake air temperature. Actuator winding shorted
Moisture or corrosion in the connector
