P037A.title: Glow Plug/Heater Indicator Control Circuit Low
P037A.description: Diesel engines show the driver a wait-to-start lamp while the glow plugs preheat; the engine module switches it with a high-side driver. P037A means the lamp control circuit is too low – in practice a short to ground on the line to the instrument cluster. GM's diesels detect it in the driver itself: about 0.5 Ω to ground with the lamp commanded, only with a lamp configured, ignition on, more than 11 V and not while cranking. The 2015 engines need 3 s of fault, the 2016/2018 engines 10 of 15 samples; the check engine light follows after two trips. The glow plugs keep working; only the indication is missing, so the driver may start too early. CARB requires monitoring of the wait-to-start lamp circuit. Ford reports lamp faults under P0381 and does not use P037A.

causes.label: Lamp control wire chafed through to ground between engine module and cluster
Lamp or LED driver in the instrument cluster shorted internally
Moisture or corrosion in the module or cluster connector
Driver in the engine module faulty

symptoms: Glow plug light does not come on or stays dim
Check engine light on (GM after two trips)
Driver starts too early, possibly poor cold start

P037B.title: Glow Plug/Heater Indicator Control Circuit High
P037B.description: P037B is the counterpart of P037A: the control circuit of the wait-to-start lamp is too high, i.e. the line carries voltage although the engine module's driver is off, or the driver sees a short to battery voltage. GM's 2015 diesels check in the off state and set the fault after 1 s with more than 11 V; the 2016/2018 engines evaluate a short of about 0.5 Ω to a voltage source in the driver, 10 of 20 samples at 100 ms. In both cases the check engine light comes on after two trips. The lamp then stays on permanently or cannot be switched off, so the driver no longer gets a usable preheat signal; the driver may protect itself when commanded. There is no limp mode. Ford and Saab do not use P037B; CARB requires monitoring of the lamp circuit and of output components for shorts.

causes.label: Lamp control wire chafed against battery or ignition positive
Fault in the instrument cluster feeding voltage back
Water damage in a connector bridging to a neighbouring pin
Driver in the engine module faulty

symptoms: Glow plug light stays on or flickers
Check engine light on (after two trips)

P037C.title: Cold Start Camshaft Profile System Performance
P037C.description: To heat the catalyst quickly after a cold start, some engines select a particular camshaft profile; CARB counts altered valve timing among these cold-start measures and requires components of the cold-start strategy to have their own diagnostics. P037C checks whether the requested profile is actually engaged during this phase. It is documented by code only at GM, on the 2.7-litre turbo four-cylinder (L3B) with a three-step sliding camshaft: while catalyst heating is active, the measured lift state is compared with the cold-start target, and if it is wrong in 100 of 120 cylinder events the code is set in the first trip. Two GM bulletins (19-NA-145 for 2019 Silverado/Sierra 1500 with stalling on remote start below −6 °C, 20-NA-174 for the 2020 Cadillac CT4) trace P037C to a software fault and reprogram the engine module.

causes.label: Engine module software (GM L3B, reprogramming)
Profile actuator (sliding cam pin) sticking or not switching
Actuator circuit (connector, wiring)
Wrong oil viscosity or low oil level, mechanism stiff when cold

symptoms: Rough running or stalling when cold (for example on remote start)

P037D.title: Glow Plug Sense Circuit
P037D.description: To check the glow plugs, the engine module reads back the voltage or current of the glow plug supply through a sense circuit – CARB requires glow plug circuits to be monitored for correct current and voltage drop, and from model year 2010 the failure of a single plug to be detected. In the J2012 scheme P037D is the general code for this sense circuit, P037E and P037F its low and high counterparts. None of the manufacturer documents available to us uses P037D: GM's 2016/2018 diesels use only P037E/P037F, Ford 2023 its own glow plug codes (P0671 ff, P064C) and Saab reports the feedback of its glow plug control module as P0380/P0382. The description therefore follows CARB and the GM sister codes. Typically glow plug monitoring is inactive; glowing itself can work normally.

causes.label: Sense wire open or high resistance, connector corroded
Glow relay or glow plug control module giving an implausible feedback
Fuse or fusible link of the glow plug supply blown
Engine module internal

symptoms: Check engine light or glow plug light on
Possibly poor cold start if the cause also affects the glow plug supply

P037E.title: Glow Plug Sense Circuit Low
P037E.description: P037E means the voltage read back from the glow plug supply is too low. GM's 2016/2018 diesels, whose glow plug output stages sit in the engine module, compare the feedback with the battery voltage while glowing: if it is lower by more than a calibrated, current-dependent threshold – excessive voltage drop or a short to ground of the sense line – a sample counts as faulty, and 60 of 120 samples in a 50 ms grid set the code, roughly 3 of 6 s. The check only runs with the engine running (afterglow), not while cranking, and is suspended if a single plug or the supply already has an electrical fault. GM classes the cause as internal to the module (measuring circuit) and turns on the check engine light after two trips. There is no limp mode; glow plug monitoring is restricted.

causes.label: High contact resistance in the glow plug supply (connector, ground, fusible link)
Measuring circuit or output stage in the engine module
Sense or supply wire shorted to ground
Weak battery or vehicle voltage at the edge of the enable range

symptoms: Possibly hard starting or knocking when cold

P037F.title: Glow Plug Sense Circuit High
P037F.description: P037F means the voltage read back from the glow plug supply is too high. GM's 2016/2018 diesels set it when the feedback lies above a threshold derived from the run/crank relay voltage, with a feedback above 5.0 V – for example voltage is reported although the plugs are not energised, or the sense line is shorted to positive. The code needs 40 of 80 samples at 50 ms, about 2 of 4 s, only with the engine running, and turns on the check engine light after two trips; GM classes the cause as internal to the module. If there is a real short to positive or a stuck relay or output stage, the plugs can stay energised permanently, overheating them and draining the battery – then also check the single plug codes P0671 ff and P066x. CARB requires glow plug circuits to be monitored for correct current and voltage drop.

causes.label: Sense wire chafed against positive or bridged in the connector
Glow relay sticking or output stage shorted (supply stays on)
Measuring circuit in the engine module

symptoms: Glow plugs possibly energised permanently (flat battery, plug damage)

P0380.title: Glow Plug/Heater Circuit A
P0380.description: P0380 concerns glow plug circuit A – depending on the manufacturer the first group of plugs, glow relay 1 or feedback line A of the glow plug control module. Saab's 3.0 TiD (9-5, 2002) has two feedback lines from the control module; if line A at the engine module stays above 4.0 V for more than 3 s while glowing, the module is reporting a plug or circuit fault, checked once per drive cycle with the warning lamp on. In Saab's 1.9 TiD (EDC16) the glow plug control module drives two pairs of plugs, monitors them itself and reports faults over a diagnostic line that should switch inversely to the activation line. The 2010/11 Saab 9-5 2.0 TiD sets P0380 for implausible feedback or a missing supply of the module, there without check engine light. Newer GM and Ford diesels report single plugs under P0671 ff instead.

causes.label: Glow plug(s) in circuit A burnt out
Glow plug control module or glow relay faulty
Wiring or connector fault (feedback line, plug connector, supply)
Missing battery or ignition supply of the control module (fuse)

symptoms: Hard starting when cold, long cranking
White or blue smoke and rough running after a cold start
Glow plug light or check engine light on or flashing

P0381.title: Glow Plug/Heater Indicator Control Circuit/Open
P0381.description: P0381 monitors the circuit of the wait-to-start lamp for an open circuit or, more generally, for faults that keep the lamp dark when commanded – CARB names a burnt-out bulb as the example, with exemptions for LCD clusters and for engines that only release the starter after preheating. GM's 2015–2018 diesels detect an open circuit in the driver by a high load impedance (about 200 kΩ in 2015), in 0.2 s or 10 of 15 samples, with the check engine light after two trips; on the 2014 Duramax LML P0381 still covered all lamp circuit faults including a short to ground. Ford's 2023 diesels check via the instrument cluster: if it reports the lamp off although on is commanded, P0381 is set within about 1 s at key-on. There is no limp mode; the risk is starting too early in the cold.

causes.label: Control wire open or connector fault between engine module and cluster
Lamp or LED in the instrument cluster burnt out
Instrument cluster faulty or communication problem (Ford)
Driver in the engine module

symptoms: Glow plug light does not come on at key-on
Check engine light on (GM after two trips)
Driver starts too early in the cold

P0382.title: Glow Plug/Heater Circuit B
P0382.description: P0382 is the counterpart of P0380 for glow plug circuit B – depending on the manufacturer the second group of plugs, glow relay 2 or feedback line B of the glow plug control module. A code-specific manufacturer description exists from Saab: the 3.0 TiD V6 diesel in the 9-5 (2002) reads two feedback lines from its glow plug control module, and if line B stays above 4.0 V for more than 3 s while glowing, the module is reporting a fault in the second group of plugs; the check runs once per drive cycle, the warning lamp comes on and there is no further system reaction. Newer GM and Ford diesels report single plugs under P0671 ff and do not use P0382. CARB requires glow plug circuits to be monitored for correct current and voltage drop. The typical consequence is a poor cold start with smoke.

causes.label: Glow plug(s) in circuit B burnt out
Glow plug control module or glow relay 2 faulty
Feedback line B, plug connector or busbar faulty

symptoms: Hard starting when cold, long cranking
White or blue smoke and rough running after a cold start
Glow plug light or check engine light on or flashing

P0383.title: Glow Plug Control Module 1 Control Circuit Low
P0383.description: Many diesels have a separate glow plug control module that the engine module commands over a control line. P0383 means this line is too low. In GM's logic for the 2010/11 Saab 9-5 2.0 TiD the engine module drives the module with a PWM signal and holds about 10 V on the line at rest (9.5–10.5 V at the signal terminal); if it reads too little voltage for more than 0.5 s – short to ground, or an open circuit or high resistance – it sets P0383, with ignition on, 9–16 V, once per ignition cycle. In that European version the code does not turn on the check engine light. Without a valid command the module does not glow, so the engine starts poorly when cold. Ford uses P0384 differently and not P0383; GM's 2016/2018 diesels have their output stages in the engine module and no such line. For US vehicles there is no code-specific source.

causes.label: Control line between engine module and glow plug module shorted to ground or open
Corroded connector at the glow plug module in the engine bay
Glow plug control module faulty (input pulls the line down)
Driver in the engine module

symptoms: Warning lamp depending on the manufacturer

P0384.title: Glow Plug Control Module 1 Control Circuit High
P0384.description: P0384 is the counterpart of P0383: the control line from the engine module to the glow plug control module is too high, i.e. shorted to positive. In GM's logic for the 2010/11 Saab 9-5 2.0 TiD the signal terminal should show 9.5–10.5 V; a higher voltage for more than 0.5 s, with ignition on and 9–16 V, sets the code, there without check engine light. Ford's 2023 diesels (6.7 and 3.0 litre) use P0384 differently from the J2012 name, for the supply voltage of the glow plug module: below 6.5 V, above 16.5 V or open, detected in about 1 s – today J2012 has P052F for that. So with Ford, check battery, alternator and the module's supply first. The consequence is missing or irregular preheating or a protective shutdown of the module, with a poor cold start.

causes.label: Control line chafed against positive or bridged in the connector
Glow plug control module faulty internally (feeding back)
Ford: supply of the module outside 6.5–16.5 V or open (battery, alternator, fuse)
Engine module

symptoms: No or irregular preheating, hard starting when cold
Warning lamp depending on the manufacturer

P0385.title: Crankshaft Position Sensor B Circuit
P0385.description: Some engines have a second crankshaft sensor or a second track on the tone wheel, which the engine module checks against sensor A or the camshaft. P0385 means its signal is missing or does not match. GM's 2004 Northstar 4.6 V8 counts the crank pulses per cam pulse (target 48 ± 1, fault in 8 of 10 tests) and also flags 2 s while cranking or 0.4 s running without a match, after two trips; an active P0385 suspends the cam sensor check. GM's 3.8-litre V6 (2006) sets it when its low resolution track stays silent while the medium resolution track delivers 36 pulses, 40 of 50 samples. The Honda 3.5-litre in the 2004 Saturn Vue Redline sets it when the second crank signal is missing while the first runs, judged after 17 revolutions, in the first trip. The engine usually keeps running on sensor A.

causes.label: Crankshaft position sensor B faulty
Connector or wiring open or corroded
Tone wheel or second track damaged
Engine module

P0386.title: Crankshaft Position Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance
P0386.description: P0386 means the signal of the second crankshaft sensor or second tone wheel track is present but implausible. GM's 2004 Northstar 4.6 V8 sets it after 5 resynchronisations within 10 s, after two trips. GM's 3.8-litre V6 (2006) expects exactly 0 or 6 low resolution pulses per 36 medium resolution pulses and one cam pulse; any other count in 40 of 50 samples sets the code, also after two trips. The Honda 3.5-litre in the 2004 Saturn Vue Redline counts implausible signals of its second crank sensor (target 44 crank pulses per 3 cam pulses, checked every half revolution, the counter dropping by one every 10 s) and sets the code at 30, about 2.2 s at idle, in the first trip. Typical causes are interference pulses, a dirty sensor or a wrong air gap; the result is jerking, misfire or longer cranking.

causes.label: Interference pulses (wiring near the ignition, shielding)
Sensor dirty or air gap wrong
Tone wheel damaged
Sensor faulty

P0387.title: Crankshaft Position Sensor B Circuit Low
P0387.description: By its J2012 name P0387 means the signal of the second crankshaft sensor stays at a low level – typically a short to ground of the signal wire, a missing or shorted sensor supply, or with an inductive sensor an amplitude that is too small. No manufacturer document available to us uses P0387: the engines with a sensor B that we found (GM Northstar 4.6 and 3.8-litre V6, the Honda 3.5-litre in the Saturn Vue Redline) report its electrical faults under P0385 and implausible signals under P0386. The description therefore follows the J2012 name, the function of sensor B and CARB's monitoring requirement for crank angle sensors. As long as sensor A works, the engine usually keeps running; together with a sensor A fault it may not start.

causes.label: Signal wire shorted to ground
Sensor faulty
Sensor supply too low or shorted
Engine module

symptoms: Rough running, no start if sensor A also fails

P0388.title: Crankshaft Position Sensor B Circuit High
P0388.description: Some engines have a second crankshaft sensor or a second track on the tone wheel – GM's 3.4/3.5/3.8-litre V6 use the low resolution track of a dual Hall sensor, the Honda 3.5-litre in the Saturn Vue Redline a second sensor – which the engine module checks against sensor A or the camshaft. By its J2012 name P0388 means the signal of sensor B stays above its upper limit – with a Hall sensor typically an open signal wire held high by the module's pull-up, or a short to positive. No manufacturer document available to us uses P0388: the engines with a sensor B report its electrical faults under P0385 and implausible signals under P0386. The description therefore follows the J2012 name, these component sources and CARB's monitoring requirement for crank angle sensors. The engine usually keeps running on sensor A; longer cranking is possible.

causes.label: Signal wire of sensor B open or connector corroded or loose
Signal wire shorted to positive or reference voltage
Sensor ground open
Sensor B faulty internally
Engine module input

symptoms: Often no noticeable symptoms while sensor A takes over

P0389.title: Crankshaft Position Sensor B Circuit Intermittent
P0389.description: Some engines have a second crankshaft sensor or a second track on the tone wheel – GM's 3.4/3.5/3.8-litre V6 use the low resolution track of a dual Hall sensor, the Honda 3.5-litre in the Saturn Vue Redline a second sensor – which the engine module checks against sensor A or the camshaft. By its J2012 name P0389 means the signal of sensor B drops out for moments or becomes erratic – missing or extra edges – without staying permanently low or high. Such faults are typically found by counting pulses against sensor A or the camshaft, as GM's 3.8-litre V6 and the Honda engine do; both, however, report the result under P0385/P0386, and no manufacturer document available to us uses P0389. The description therefore follows the J2012 name, these component sources and CARB. Typical causes are a loose contact, a broken wire and interference.

causes.label: Loose contact or corrosion at the sensor B connector
Wire break or chafing that appears with engine movement
Electrical interference (add-on devices, routing near ignition or relays)
Tone wheel damaged or dirty, air gap too large
Sensor faulty, temperature-dependent

symptoms: Check engine light on, possibly only after several trips

P038A.title: Ignition I Control Signal Circuit/Open
P038A.description: Ignition I is one of the control signal lines from the engine module to an ignition module, ignition output stage or group of coils; which cylinders it serves is defined by the manufacturer, not by the code standard. The code concerns the logic-level control signal, not the coil's primary current (that has its own codes, P0351 ff and P2300 ff). P038A means the control line is open – the module sees a voltage with its driver off that indicates high resistance. No manufacturer using these codes was found – neither GM nor Ford use the Ignition A to J codes; GM reports coil control faults as P0351 ff – so the description follows CARB and that analogy. The affected coils fire wrongly or not at all, causing misfire; many modules then shut off injection to those cylinders to protect the catalyst.

causes.label: Control line or connector pin open (corrosion, pushed-back pin)
Ignition module or coil with integrated driver of this group faulty
Supply or ground of the ignition module faulty
Driver stage in the engine module

symptoms: Loss of power, possibly cylinders shut off

P038B.title: Ignition I Control Signal Circuit Low
P038B.description: Ignition I is one of the control signal lines from the engine module to an ignition module, ignition output stage or group of coils; which cylinders it serves is defined by the manufacturer, not by the code standard. The code concerns the logic-level control signal, not the coil's primary current (that has its own codes, P0351 ff and P2300 ff). P038B means the control line reads low – typically shorted to ground. No manufacturer using these codes was found – neither GM nor Ford use the Ignition A to J codes; GM reports coil control faults as P0351 ff – so the description follows CARB and that analogy. The affected coils fire wrongly or not at all, causing misfire; many modules then shut off injection to those cylinders to protect the catalyst.

causes.label: Control line shorted to ground (chafing)
Input of the ignition module or coil shorted
Moisture or corrosion in the connector
Driver stage in the engine module

symptoms: Loss of power, possibly cylinders shut off

P038C.title: Ignition I Control Signal Circuit High
P038C.description: Ignition I is one of the control signal lines from the engine module to an ignition module, ignition output stage or group of coils; which cylinders it serves is defined by the manufacturer, not by the code standard. The code concerns the logic-level control signal, not the coil's primary current (that has its own codes, P0351 ff and P2300 ff). P038C means the control line reads high – typically shorted to voltage. No manufacturer using these codes was found – neither GM nor Ford use the Ignition A to J codes; GM reports coil control faults as P0351 ff – so the description follows CARB and that analogy. The affected coils fire wrongly or not at all, causing misfire; many modules then shut off injection to those cylinders to protect the catalyst.

causes.label: Control line shorted to a supply wire
Ignition module or coil faulty
Moisture or corrosion in the connector
Driver stage in the engine module

symptoms: Loss of power, possibly cylinders shut off

P038D.title: Ignition J Control Signal Circuit/Open
P038D.description: Ignition J is one of the control signal lines from the engine module to an ignition module, ignition output stage or group of coils; which cylinders it serves is defined by the manufacturer, not by the code standard. The code concerns the logic-level control signal, not the coil's primary current (that has its own codes, P0351 ff and P2300 ff). P038D means the control line is open – the module sees a voltage with its driver off that indicates high resistance. No manufacturer using these codes was found – neither GM nor Ford use the Ignition A to J codes; GM reports coil control faults as P0351 ff – so the description follows CARB and that analogy. The affected coils fire wrongly or not at all, causing misfire; many modules then shut off injection to those cylinders to protect the catalyst.

causes.label: Control line or connector pin open (corrosion, pushed-back pin)
Ignition module or coil with integrated driver of this group faulty
Supply or ground of the ignition module faulty
Driver stage in the engine module

symptoms: Loss of power, possibly cylinders shut off

P038E.title: Ignition J Control Signal Circuit Low
P038E.description: Ignition J is one of the control signal lines from the engine module to an ignition module, ignition output stage or group of coils; which cylinders it serves is defined by the manufacturer, not by the code standard. The code concerns the logic-level control signal, not the coil's primary current (that has its own codes, P0351 ff and P2300 ff). P038E means the control line reads low – typically shorted to ground. No manufacturer using these codes was found – neither GM nor Ford use the Ignition A to J codes; GM reports coil control faults as P0351 ff – so the description follows CARB and that analogy. The affected coils fire wrongly or not at all, causing misfire; many modules then shut off injection to those cylinders to protect the catalyst.

causes.label: Control line shorted to ground (chafing)
Input of the ignition module or coil shorted
Moisture or corrosion in the connector
Driver stage in the engine module

symptoms: Loss of power, possibly cylinders shut off

P038F.title: Ignition J Control Signal Circuit High
P038F.description: Ignition J is one of the control signal lines from the engine module to an ignition module, ignition output stage or group of coils; which cylinders it serves is defined by the manufacturer, not by the code standard. The code concerns the logic-level control signal, not the coil's primary current (that has its own codes, P0351 ff and P2300 ff). P038F means the control line reads high – typically shorted to voltage. No manufacturer using these codes was found – neither GM nor Ford use the Ignition A to J codes; GM reports coil control faults as P0351 ff – so the description follows CARB and that analogy. The affected coils fire wrongly or not at all, causing misfire; many modules then shut off injection to those cylinders to protect the catalyst.

causes.label: Control line shorted to a supply wire
Ignition module or coil faulty
Moisture or corrosion in the connector
Driver stage in the engine module

symptoms: Loss of power, possibly cylinders shut off

P0390.title: Camshaft Position Sensor B Circuit Bank 2
P0390.description: Camshaft position sensor B is the exhaust camshaft sensor; bank 2 is the side without cylinder 1, so the code only occurs on V and boxer engines with one exhaust cam sensor per bank. P0390 means no or too few exhaust cam pulses arrive from bank 2 while the crankshaft turns. GM's 3.0 twin-turbo V6 (LGW) sets it after 5.5 s without a cam pulse, 4 s of cranking or fewer than 4 pulses in 3 s, after two trips; for GM it collects all circuit faults. GM's 3.6-litre V6 in the Saab 9-4X also counts 800 of 1,000 engine cycles without a pulse. Ford checks the crank-to-cam ratio from 200 rpm within 5 s, and the 2004 Northstar counts missing signal changes up to 16. The bank 2 exhaust phaser then locks in its base position; the engine keeps running on the crank and intake cam sensors. FCA advises saving the synchronisation data before replacing the sensor.

causes.label: Connector or wiring of the bank 2 exhaust sensor open or corroded (signal, 5 V, ground)
Camshaft position sensor faulty
Oil contamination or leak at the sensor, sensor loose
Tone wheel on the phaser damaged or wrongly fitted after timing chain work
Engine module, or 5 V reference shorted by another sensor

symptoms: Loss of power (bank 2 exhaust cam timing in its base position)

P0391.title: Camshaft Position Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance Bank 2
P0391.description: Camshaft position sensor B is the exhaust camshaft sensor; bank 2 is the side without cylinder 1, so the code only occurs on V and boxer engines with one exhaust cam sensor per bank. P0391 means the bank 2 exhaust cam signal is present, but the number or position of its pulses does not fit the crankshaft. GM's 3.0 twin-turbo V6 (LGW) expects 4 to 6 pulses in the first 12 reference events and 398 to 402 per 100 engine cycles on the four-tooth wheel, after two trips; the Saab 9-4X 2.8 turbo V6 (LAU) checks pulses per crank revolution below 2,520 rpm. The 2004 Northstar requires each edge within a window of crank teeth, and GM's 2004 3.6-litre V6 (LY7) counts implausible signals over two drive cycles. The phaser then goes to its base position and the engine cranks longer. Mechanical causes – damaged tone wheel, jumped chain – matter more here than with P0390.

causes.label: Tone wheel on the bank 2 exhaust phaser damaged, loose or wrongly fitted
Interference or loose contact producing extra edges
Sensor loose, wrong O-ring or gap, chips on the magnet
Timing chain stretched or jumped
Sensor faulty

symptoms: Loss of power (bank 2 exhaust cam timing in its base position)

P0392.title: Camshaft Position Sensor B Circuit Low Bank 2
P0392.description: Camshaft position sensor B is the exhaust camshaft sensor; bank 2 is the side without cylinder 1, so the code only occurs on V and boxer engines with one exhaust cam sensor per bank. P0392 means the bank 2 exhaust cam signal stays low without edges – typically a short to ground of the signal wire, a sensor output stuck low or a missing 5 V reference. Only manufacturers with separate low and high codes use it: on the Saab 9-4X 2.8 turbo V6 (GM LAU) the signal must stay low without pulses for more than 1 s, or 10 s cumulatively, after more than 10 crank revolutions and below 2,520 rpm, after two trips; GM's 2004/2005 3.6-litre V6 (LY7, LP1) counts the fault over two drive cycles. Newer GM petrol engines (2015–2020) and Ford report the same fault as P0390. The consequence is as for P0390: cam timing on bank 2 in its base position, loss of power, longer cranking.

causes.label: Signal wire shorted to ground
Sensor faulty internally (output stuck low)
5 V reference missing (shorted by another sensor on the same circuit)
Engine module

symptoms: Loss of power (bank 2 exhaust cam timing in its base position)

P0393.title: Camshaft Position Sensor B Circuit High Bank 2
P0393.description: Camshaft position sensor B is the exhaust camshaft sensor; bank 2 is the side without cylinder 1, so the code only occurs on V and boxer engines with one exhaust cam sensor per bank. P0393 means the bank 2 exhaust cam signal stays high without edges. Because the engine module pulls the Hall sensor's signal line up, an open wire leads to 'high' just like a short to positive – GM's 2004 3.6-litre V6 (LY7) therefore calls the fault 'circuit continuity or high' and counts it over two drive cycles. On the Saab 9-4X 2.8 turbo V6 (GM LAU) the signal must stay high without pulses for more than 1 s, or 10 s cumulatively, after two trips. Only manufacturers with separate low and high codes use it; newer GM petrol engines and Ford report the fault as P0390. The consequence is as for P0390: cam timing on bank 2 in its base position, loss of power, longer cranking.

causes.label: Signal wire open or connector off
Sensor ground open
Signal wire shorted to positive
Sensor faulty

symptoms: Loss of power (bank 2 exhaust cam timing in its base position)

P0394.title: Camshaft Position Sensor B Circuit Intermittent Bank 2
P0394.description: Camshaft position sensor B is the exhaust camshaft sensor; bank 2 is the side without cylinder 1, so the code only occurs on V and boxer engines with one exhaust cam sensor per bank. P0394 means the bank 2 exhaust cam signal now and then appears at a position where it is not expected relative to the crank reference – sporadic extra or missing edges. Ford checks this in its camshaft ignition system test from 200 rpm and decides within 5 s. FCA also uses the code and asks dealers to save the cam/crank synchronisation event data before replacing parts, a hint that the sensor itself is often not the culprit. GM does not use P0394 and reports such faults under P0391. Typical causes are a loose contact, interference or a damaged tone wheel.

causes.label: Loose contact or corrosion at the sensor connector or harness
Interference (ignition wiring, add-on devices, ground problems)
Tone wheel or phaser damaged, or sensor loose
Sensor faulty, temperature-dependent

P0395.title: Cylinder 1 Pressure Sensor Circuit
P0395.description: Some diesels have a combustion pressure sensor in the glow plug; the engine module uses it to control injection for each cylinder. This code concerns cylinder 1. P0395 is the general circuit code for this pressure sensor, meant for modules that do not separate open circuits and shorts into low and high. The only manufacturer we found using this code family – GM's European 2.0 CDTI diesel, documented in Saab 9-5 workshop information – splits the faults into low and high (P0397, P0398) and does not use P0395; VW's US 2.0 TDI engines with pressure-sensing glow plugs report such faults with their own codes (P13CE ff). The description therefore follows CARB's requirement to monitor input sensors for circuit faults. The sensor has three wires (5 V reference, ground, signal); without it the module drops combustion control for that cylinder.

causes.label: Connector at the pressure-sensing glow plug loose or corroded
Reference, signal or ground wire open or shorted
Sensor electronics in the glow plug faulty
Engine module (reference voltage or input)

symptoms: Check engine light on (often after two trips)
Usually barely noticeable – combustion control for the cylinder is switched off
Possibly rougher running, more noise or slightly higher consumption

P0396.title: Cylinder 1 Pressure Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P0396.description: Some diesels have a combustion pressure sensor in the glow plug; the engine module uses it to control injection for each cylinder. This code concerns cylinder 1. P0396 means the sensor signal is electrically fine but does not fit the expected value. No manufacturer document available to us describes the code; a GM patent shows how such a check works: in overrun the measured peak pressure is compared with a compression pressure calculated from manifold pressure and compression ratio, and the pressure values are also compared with limits and with crankshaft speed fluctuation. GM's European diesel in the Saab 9-5 uses the peak pressure in overrun anyway to find top dead centre. Typical causes are sensor drift from combustion deposits or a glow plug that leaks or is wrongly torqued. CARB requires a two-sided plausibility check of input sensors where feasible.

causes.label: Sensor in the glow plug drifting (deposits, ageing)
Glow plug leaking or wrongly torqued (pressure transmitted wrongly)
Contact resistance in connector or ground
Actual compression pressure differs (valve, rings)

symptoms: Combustion control for the cylinder off – slightly rough running, more noise

P0397.title: Cylinder 1 Pressure Sensor Circuit Low
P0397.description: Some diesels have a combustion pressure sensor in the glow plug; the engine module uses it to control injection for each cylinder. This code concerns cylinder 1. P0397 means the sensor signal stays below its lower limit. GM's European 2.0 CDTI diesel (Saab 9-5, 2010) sets it when the signal is below the threshold for more than 2 s with the engine running, checked once per drive cycle, with the check engine light after two trips; the displayed maximum combustion pressure then reads 0 kPa instead of the normal 0–9,000 kPa. Saab names an open or grounded 5 V reference and a signal wire shorted to ground as causes; the glow plug should measure 3–12 Ω between reference and ground. Without the signal, combustion control for this cylinder is switched off, which is usually barely noticeable.

causes.label: 5 V reference wire open or shorted to ground
Signal wire shorted to ground
Sensor electronics of the glow plug faulty
Engine module supplies no reference

symptoms: Check engine light on (often after two trips)
Usually barely noticeable – combustion control for the cylinder is switched off
Possibly rougher running, more noise or slightly higher consumption

P0398.title: Cylinder 1 Pressure Sensor Circuit High
P0398.description: Some diesels have a combustion pressure sensor in the glow plug; the engine module uses it to control injection for each cylinder. This code concerns cylinder 1. P0398 means the sensor signal stays above its upper limit. GM's European 2.0 CDTI diesel (Saab 9-5, 2010) sets it when the signal is above the threshold for more than 2 s with the engine running, checked once per drive cycle, with the check engine light after two trips; the displayed maximum combustion pressure then reads 10,000 kPa instead of the normal 0–9,000 kPa. Saab names a 5 V reference shorted to positive, an open signal wire or one shorted to positive, and an open ground wire as causes – an unplugged connector is the most common. Without the signal, combustion control for this cylinder is switched off, which is usually barely noticeable.

causes.label: Connector off or loose, signal wire open
Sensor ground wire open
Sensor in the glow plug faulty
Signal or reference wire shorted to positive

symptoms: Check engine light on (often after two trips)
Usually barely noticeable – combustion control for the cylinder is switched off
Possibly rougher running, more noise or slightly higher consumption

P0399.title: Cylinder 1 Pressure Sensor Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0399.description: Some diesels have a combustion pressure sensor in the glow plug; the engine module uses it to control injection for each cylinder. This code concerns cylinder 1. P0399 means the sensor signal is erratic or drops out for moments. GM's European 2.0 CDTI diesel (Saab 9-5, 2010) calls it 'circuit erratic' and sets it when the signal is outside its range for more than 0.2 s with the engine running; its fault table groups the erratic and pressure variation codes together as signal performance faults. The test plan checks a reference of 4.8–5.2 V and a ground below 5 Ω before the glow plug is replaced. Typical causes are a loose contact at the glow plug connector, a chafed engine harness or sensor electronics that become unstable with temperature. The code often comes and goes; combustion control for the cylinder is suspended while it is active.

causes.label: Loose contact at the glow plug connector
Chafing or broken wire in the engine harness
Sensor electronics of the glow plug unstable with temperature
Interference from ground problems

symptoms: Often no symptoms, the code comes and goes

P039A.title: Cylinder 1 Pressure Too Low
P039A.description: Some diesels have a combustion pressure sensor in the glow plug; the engine module uses it to control injection for each cylinder. This code concerns cylinder 1. P039A means the pressure measured in the cylinder is lower than expected while the sensor itself is electrically fine. No manufacturer document available to us describes the code; GM patents show how such an evaluation works: peak and minimum pressure are compared with limits and with a motoring pressure calculated from manifold pressure and compression ratio, and the ratio of measured to motoring pressure is compared between cylinders. A low value can mean weak combustion or compression – leaking valve, worn rings, leaking glow plug seat, an injector delivering too little – or a sensor drifting downwards. The usual consequence is rough running and more smoke.

causes.label: Compression loss (valve, piston rings, leaking glow plug seat)
Injector delivering too little or coked
Sensor drifting downwards (deposits)
Misfire or partial combustion

symptoms: Lack of power, rough running, possibly misfire on this cylinder

P039B.title: Cylinder 1 Pressure Too High
P039B.description: Some diesels have a combustion pressure sensor in the glow plug; the engine module uses it to control injection for each cylinder. This code concerns cylinder 1. P039B means the pressure measured or calculated for the cylinder is higher than expected. It is documented by code at Audi, surprisingly on a petrol engine: on the 2015 S3 (2.0 TFSI, engine CYFB) the four 'pressure too high' codes came on with the EPC lamp, usually together with misfire codes P0300–P0304 and the manufacturer code for hiding a cylinder; the cause was a software fault that mis-detected misfire, and a software update fixed it. How Audi determines the pressure, the bulletin does not say. On diesels with pressure-sensing glow plugs GM patents describe a peak pressure above its limit – too much or too early injection, or a sensor drifting upwards. If the cylinder is shut off, power drops noticeably.

causes.label: Engine module software (Audi S3 2015, engine CYFB)
Injector delivering too much or dripping
Sensor drifting upwards (diesel pressure-sensing glow plug)
Knock or pre-ignition on a petrol engine

symptoms: EPC or check engine light on
Misfire codes, possibly a cylinder shut off with noticeable loss of power

P039C.title: Cylinder 1 Pressure Variation Low
P039C.description: Some diesels have a combustion pressure sensor in the glow plug; the engine module uses it to control injection for each cylinder. This code concerns cylinder 1. GM's European 2.0 CDTI diesel (Saab 9-5, 2010) uses P039C as 'pressure variation too low', with three sub-checks, and sets it when the signal is outside its range for more than 0.2 s with the engine running; its fault table counts it among the signal performance faults together with the erratic code. What exactly is measured, Saab does not explain; presumably it is the swing of the pressure signal within an engine cycle – too small a swing means the signal barely responds, for example because the glow rod is stuck by carbon and no longer transmits the pressure, or because pressure build-up is missing. Usually there are no noticeable symptoms.

causes.label: Pressure-sensing glow plug faulty or coked (glow rod stuck)
Contact resistance in connector or ground
Actual compression loss or misfire in the cylinder

symptoms: Possibly rough running or combustion noise because control is off

P039D.title: Cylinder 1 Pressure Variation High
P039D.description: Some diesels have a combustion pressure sensor in the glow plug; the engine module uses it to control injection for each cylinder. This code concerns cylinder 1. GM's European 2.0 CDTI diesel (Saab 9-5, 2010) uses P039D as 'pressure variation too high' and sets it when the signal is outside its range for more than 0.2 s with the engine running; its fault table counts it among the signal performance faults together with the erratic code. What exactly is measured, Saab does not explain; presumably it is the swing of the pressure signal within an engine cycle – too large a swing points to a noisy or overshooting signal or implausible pressure peaks, for example from faulty sensor electronics, interference on the signal wire or, less often, a combustion anomaly such as a dripping injector. Usually there are no noticeable symptoms.

causes.label: Sensor in the glow plug faulty (signal noise)
Loose contact or interference on the signal wire
Combustion anomaly (dripping injector, harsh combustion)

symptoms: Possibly rough running or combustion noise because control is off

P039E.title: Cylinder 1 Combustion Performance
P039E.description: Some diesels have a combustion pressure sensor in the glow plug; the engine module uses it to control injection for each cylinder. This code concerns cylinder 1. P039E means the combustion quality in the cylinder, evaluated from the combustion pressure, is abnormal. No manufacturer document available to us describes the code; a GM patent shows the method: the ratio of measured to motoring pressure is turned into a measure of combustion energy, an inequality index against the neighbouring cylinders in firing order is formed, and a two-sided threshold detects partial combustion, misfire, injector and compression faults. CARB requires engines with a combustion or combustion quality sensor to detect misfire more sharply (5 % in 1,000 revolutions). Typical causes are a coked or leaking injector, compression loss or poor fuel; the engine runs roughly and smokes more.

causes.label: Injector coked, leaking or delivering the wrong quantity
Compression loss (valve, rings)
Partial combustion or misfire (fuel quality, EGR distribution)
Pressure sensor drifting

symptoms: Loss of power, more smoke and consumption

P039F.title: Cylinder 2 Pressure Sensor Circuit
P039F.description: Some diesels have a combustion pressure sensor in the glow plug; the engine module uses it to control injection for each cylinder. This code concerns cylinder 2. P039F is the general circuit code for this pressure sensor, meant for modules that do not separate open circuits and shorts into low and high. The only manufacturer we found using this code family – GM's European 2.0 CDTI diesel, documented in Saab 9-5 workshop information – splits the faults into low and high (P03A1, P03A2) and does not use P039F; VW's US 2.0 TDI engines with pressure-sensing glow plugs report such faults with their own codes (P13CE ff). The description therefore follows CARB's requirement to monitor input sensors for circuit faults. The sensor has three wires (5 V reference, ground, signal); without it the module drops combustion control for that cylinder.

causes.label: Connector at the pressure-sensing glow plug loose or corroded
Reference, signal or ground wire open or shorted
Sensor electronics in the glow plug faulty
Engine module (reference voltage or input)

symptoms: Check engine light on (often after two trips)
Usually barely noticeable – combustion control for the cylinder is switched off
Possibly rougher running, more noise or slightly higher consumption

P03A0.title: Cylinder 2 Pressure Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P03A0.description: Some diesels have a combustion pressure sensor in the glow plug; the engine module uses it to control injection for each cylinder. This code concerns cylinder 2. P03A0 means the sensor signal is electrically fine but does not fit the expected value. Contact resistance in connector or ground
Actual compression pressure differs (valve, rings)

symptoms: Combustion control for the cylinder off – slightly rough running, more noise

P03A1.title: Cylinder 2 Pressure Sensor Circuit Low

Signal wire shorted to ground
Sensor electronics of the glow plug faulty
Engine module supplies no reference

Usually barely noticeable – combustion control for the cylinder is switched off
Possibly rougher running, more noise or slightly higher consumption

P03A4.title: Cylinder 2 Pressure Too Low

P03A5.title: Cylinder 2 Pressure Too High

Misfire codes, possibly a cylinder shut off with noticeable loss of power

P03A6.title: Cylinder 2 Pressure Variation Low

P03A8.title: Cylinder 2 Combustion Performance

Partial combustion or misfire (fuel quality, EGR distribution)
Pressure sensor drifting

symptoms: Loss of power, more smoke and consumption

P03D9.description: Some diesels have a combustion pressure sensor in the glow plug; the engine module uses it to control injection for each cylinder. This code concerns cylinder 7. P03D9 means the swing of the pressure signal is too large. The only manufacturer we found using this code family, GM's European 2.0 CDTI four-cylinder diesel (Saab 9-5, 2010), uses 'pressure variation too high' for cylinders 1 to 4: signal outside its range for more than 0.2 s with the engine running; what exactly is measured, Saab does not explain – presumably a noisy or overshooting signal, from faulty sensor electronics, interference or a combustion anomaly. For cylinder 7, which only engines with at least 7 cylinders have, no manufacturer document available to us uses the code; the description follows that logic and CARB. Usually there are no noticeable symptoms.

causes.label: Sensor in the glow plug faulty (signal noise)
Loose contact or interference on the signal wire
Combustion anomaly (dripping injector, harsh combustion)

symptoms: Possibly rough running or combustion noise because control is off

P03DA.title: Cylinder 7 Combustion Performance
P03DA.description: Some diesels have a combustion pressure sensor in the glow plug; the engine module uses it to control injection for each cylinder. This code concerns cylinder 7. P03DA means the combustion quality in the cylinder, evaluated from the combustion pressure, is abnormal. No manufacturer document available to us describes the code; a GM patent shows the method: the ratio of measured to motoring pressure is turned into a measure of combustion energy, an inequality index against the neighbouring cylinders in firing order is formed, and a two-sided threshold detects partial combustion, misfire, injector and compression faults. CARB requires engines with a combustion or combustion quality sensor to detect misfire more sharply (5 % in 1,000 revolutions). Typical causes are a coked or leaking injector, compression loss or poor fuel; the engine runs roughly and smokes more.

causes.label: Injector coked, leaking or delivering the wrong quantity
Compression loss (valve, rings)
Partial combustion or misfire (fuel quality, EGR distribution)
Pressure sensor drifting

symptoms: Loss of power, more smoke and consumption

P03DB.title: Cylinder 8 Pressure Sensor Circuit
P03DB.description: Some diesels have a combustion pressure sensor in the glow plug; the engine module uses it to control injection for each cylinder. This code concerns cylinder 8. P03DB is the general circuit code for this pressure sensor, meant for modules that do not separate open circuits and shorts into low and high. The only manufacturer we found using this code family, GM's European 2.0 CDTI four-cylinder diesel (Saab 9-5), splits such faults into low and high codes for cylinders 1 to 4, and VW's US 2.0 TDI engines with pressure-sensing glow plugs use their own codes (P13CE ff). For cylinder 8, which only engines with at least 8 cylinders have, no manufacturer document available to us uses the code; the description follows that logic and CARB. The sensor has three wires (5 V reference, ground, signal); without it the module drops combustion control for that cylinder.

causes.label: Connector at the pressure-sensing glow plug loose or corroded
Reference, signal or ground wire open or shorted
Sensor electronics in the glow plug faulty
Engine module (reference voltage or input)

symptoms: Check engine light on (often after two trips)
Usually barely noticeable – combustion control for the cylinder is switched off
Possibly rougher running, more noise or slightly higher consumption

P03DC.title: Cylinder 8 Pressure Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P03DC.description: Some diesels have a combustion pressure sensor in the glow plug; the engine module uses it to control injection for each cylinder. This code concerns cylinder 8. P03DC means the sensor signal is electrically fine but does not fit the expected value. No manufacturer document available to us describes the code; a GM patent shows how such a check works: in overrun the measured peak pressure is compared with a compression pressure calculated from manifold pressure and compression ratio, and the pressure values are also compared with limits and with crankshaft speed fluctuation. GM's European diesel in the Saab 9-5 uses the peak pressure in overrun anyway to find top dead centre. Typical causes are sensor drift from combustion deposits or a glow plug that leaks or is wrongly torqued. CARB requires a two-sided plausibility check of input sensors where feasible.

causes.label: Sensor in the glow plug drifting (deposits, ageing)
Glow plug leaking or wrongly torqued (pressure transmitted wrongly)
Contact resistance in connector or ground
Actual compression pressure differs (valve, rings)

symptoms: Combustion control for the cylinder off – slightly rough running, more noise

P03DD.title: Cylinder 8 Pressure Sensor Circuit Low
P03DD.description: Some diesels have a combustion pressure sensor in the glow plug; the engine module uses it to control injection for each cylinder. This code concerns cylinder 8. P03DD means the sensor signal stays below its lower limit – typically an open or grounded 5 V reference or a signal wire shorted to ground. The only manufacturer we found using this code family, GM's European 2.0 CDTI four-cylinder diesel (Saab 9-5, 2010), uses it for cylinders 1 to 4: signal below the threshold for more than 2 s with the engine running, check engine light after two trips, displayed pressure 0 kPa. For cylinder 8, which only engines with at least 8 cylinders have, no manufacturer document available to us uses the code; the description follows that logic and CARB. Without the signal, combustion control for this cylinder is switched off.

causes.label: 5 V reference wire open or shorted to ground
Signal wire shorted to ground
Sensor electronics of the glow plug faulty
Engine module supplies no reference

symptoms: Check engine light on (often after two trips)
Usually barely noticeable – combustion control for the cylinder is switched off
Possibly rougher running, more noise or slightly higher consumption

P03DE.title: Cylinder 8 Pressure Sensor Circuit High
P03DE.description: Some diesels have a combustion pressure sensor in the glow plug; the engine module uses it to control injection for each cylinder. This code concerns cylinder 8. Sensor ground wire open
Sensor in the glow plug faulty
Signal or reference wire shorted to positive

P03DF.title: Cylinder 8 Pressure Sensor Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P03DF.description: Some diesels have a combustion pressure sensor in the glow plug; the engine module uses it to control injection for each cylinder. This code concerns cylinder 8. P03DF means the sensor signal is erratic or drops out for moments – typically a loose contact at the glow plug connector, a chafed harness or sensor electronics unstable with temperature. The only manufacturer we found using this code family, GM's European 2.0 CDTI four-cylinder diesel (Saab 9-5, 2010), uses it for cylinders 1 to 4 as 'circuit erratic': signal outside its range for more than 0.2 s with the engine running. For cylinder 8, which only engines with at least 8 cylinders have, no manufacturer document available to us uses the code; the description follows that logic and CARB. The code often comes and goes.

causes.label: Loose contact at the glow plug connector
Chafing or broken wire in the engine harness
Sensor electronics of the glow plug unstable with temperature
Interference from ground problems

symptoms: Often no symptoms, the code comes and goes

P03E0.title: Cylinder 8 Pressure Too Low
P03E0.description: Some diesels have a combustion pressure sensor in the glow plug; the engine module uses it to control injection for each cylinder. This code concerns cylinder 8. P03E0 means the pressure measured in the cylinder is lower than expected while the sensor itself is electrically fine. No manufacturer document available to us describes the code; GM patents show how such an evaluation works: peak and minimum pressure are compared with limits and with a motoring pressure calculated from manifold pressure and compression ratio, and the ratio of measured to motoring pressure is compared between cylinders. A low value can mean weak combustion or compression – leaking valve, worn rings, leaking glow plug seat, an injector delivering too little – or a sensor drifting downwards. The usual consequence is rough running and more smoke.

causes.label: Compression loss (valve, piston rings, leaking glow plug seat)
Injector delivering too little or coked
Sensor drifting downwards (deposits)
Misfire or partial combustion

symptoms: Lack of power, rough running, possibly misfire on this cylinder

P03E1.title: Cylinder 8 Pressure Too High
P03E1.description: Some diesels have a combustion pressure sensor in the glow plug; the engine module uses it to control injection for each cylinder. This code concerns cylinder 8. P03E1 means the pressure measured or calculated for the cylinder is higher than expected. The 'pressure too high' codes are documented only at Audi, for cylinders 1 to 4 of the 2015 S3 petrol engine, where a software fault mis-detected misfire. On diesels with pressure-sensing glow plugs GM patents describe a peak pressure above its limit – too much or too early injection, or a sensor drifting upwards. For cylinder 8, which only engines with at least 8 cylinders have, no manufacturer document available to us uses the code; the description follows that logic and CARB. If the cylinder is shut off, power drops noticeably.

causes.label: Injector delivering too much or dripping
Sensor drifting upwards (diesel pressure-sensing glow plug)
Knock or pre-ignition on a petrol engine

symptoms: EPC or check engine light on
Misfire codes, possibly a cylinder shut off with noticeable loss of power

P03E2.title: Cylinder 8 Pressure Variation Low
P03E2.description: Some diesels have a combustion pressure sensor in the glow plug; the engine module uses it to control injection for each cylinder. This code concerns cylinder 8. P03E2 means the swing of the pressure signal is too small. The only manufacturer we found using this code family, GM's European 2.0 CDTI four-cylinder diesel (Saab 9-5, 2010), uses 'pressure variation too low' for cylinders 1 to 4: signal outside its range for more than 0.2 s with the engine running; what exactly is measured, Saab does not explain – presumably the signal barely responds, for example because a coked glow rod no longer transmits the pressure. For cylinder 8, which only engines with at least 8 cylinders have, no manufacturer document available to us uses the code; the description follows that logic and CARB. Usually there are no noticeable symptoms.

causes.label: Pressure-sensing glow plug faulty or coked (glow rod stuck)
Contact resistance in connector or ground
Actual compression loss or misfire in the cylinder

symptoms: Possibly rough running or combustion noise because control is off

P03E5.title: A Camshaft Position Actuator Position Sensor C Circuit Bank 1
P03E5.description: On some engines the intake cam phaser (camshaft position actuator A) has its own position sensors, which tell the engine module where the phaser actually is; sensor C is the third of them, bank 1 the side with cylinder 1. P03E5 is the general circuit code for this sensor: the module sees an open circuit or a signal outside its valid window on the supply, signal or ground line. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code. GM's 2.7-litre engine monitors comparable position sensors on its sliding camshaft under other codes (P2C05 ff), with an open circuit above 200 kΩ and a short below 0.5 Ω in 4 of 5 samples – only as a comparison. The phaser is then usually held in its base position. CARB requires electronic parts of variable valve timing systems to be monitored as comprehensive components.

causes.label: Connector or harness to position sensor C open or corroded
Position sensor C faulty
5 V reference or ground disturbed (also by another sensor on the same circuit)
Engine module

symptoms: Cam phasing held in its base position, loss of power
Possibly rough idle or higher consumption

P03E6.title: A Camshaft Position Actuator Position Sensor C Range/Performance Bank 1
P03E6.description: On some engines the intake cam phaser (camshaft position actuator A) has its own position sensors, which tell the engine module where the phaser actually is; sensor C is the third of them, bank 1 the side with cylinder 1. P03E6 means the sensor signal is electrically valid but implausible – for example the number or position of its edges per engine cycle does not match the crankshaft sensor, it jumps, or it lies outside the phaser's adjustment range. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code. GM's 2.7-litre engine monitors comparable position sensors on its sliding camshaft under other codes (P2C05 ff), with an open circuit above 200 kΩ and a short below 0.5 Ω in 4 of 5 samples – only as a comparison. Typical causes are a dirty sensor or wrong air gap, a damaged or wrongly fitted phaser, or interference.

causes.label: Sensor dirty (metal debris on the magnet) or air gap wrong
Phaser or sensor target damaged or wrongly fitted (timing)
Loose contact or interference
Sensor faulty

symptoms: Cam phasing held in its base position, loss of power
Possibly rough idle or higher consumption

P03E7.title: A Camshaft Position Actuator Position Sensor C Circuit Low Bank 1
P03E7.description: On some engines the intake cam phaser (camshaft position actuator A) has its own position sensors, which tell the engine module where the phaser actually is; sensor C is the third of them, bank 1 the side with cylinder 1. P03E7 means the sensor signal stays below its lower limit – signal or reference wire shorted to ground, supply open, or the sensor shorted internally; if the 5 V reference is the cause, other sensors on the same circuit often set codes too. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code. GM's 2.7-litre engine monitors comparable position sensors on its sliding camshaft under other codes (P2C05 ff), with an open circuit above 200 kΩ and a short below 0.5 Ω in 4 of 5 samples – only as a comparison. causes.label: Signal wire shorted to ground (chafed harness)
5 V supply open or shorted
Sensor faulty internally
Engine module

symptoms: Cam phasing held in its base position, loss of power
Possibly rough idle or higher consumption

P03E8.title: A Camshaft Position Actuator Position Sensor C Circuit High Bank 1
P03E8.description: On some engines the intake cam phaser (camshaft position actuator A) has its own position sensors, which tell the engine module where the phaser actually is; sensor C is the third of them, bank 1 the side with cylinder 1. P03E8 means the sensor signal stays above its upper limit – typically an open sensor ground, a signal wire shorted to 5 V or battery voltage, or a faulty sensor. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code. The phaser is then usually held in its base position, with a loss of power.

causes.label: Sensor ground open or connector corroded
Signal wire shorted to 5 V or vehicle voltage
Sensor faulty
Engine module

symptoms: Cam phasing held in its base position, loss of power
Possibly rough idle or higher consumption

P03E9.title: A Camshaft Profile Actuator Position Sensor A Exceeded Learning Limit
P03E9.description: Engines with cam profile switching move the intake camshaft between lift profiles with actuators – for example pins that shift a sliding cam – and position sensors report which profile is engaged. The engine module learns reference values of position sensor A, such as its end-position levels or the expected pulse position relative to the crankshaft and camshaft sensors; a Ford patent describes correcting this position for the cam phase. P03E9 means the learned value lies outside the permitted adaptation limit, so profile detection is no longer reliable and the module usually stays in a safe profile. No manufacturer document available to us describes the code or its limits; GM's 2.7-litre sliding cam has no learning-limit code. CARB lists a pin that does not reach its position among the faults to be detected.

causes.label: Position sensor A or actuator with integrated sensor worn or faulty (signal drift)
Actuator pin or sliding piece stiff, guide worn, dirty oil
Actuator not relearned or wrongly fitted after replacement
Connector or wiring with contact resistance
Engine module software (learning algorithm)

symptoms: Profile switching disabled: less power at high revs or higher consumption
Possibly further profile actuator or sensor codes

P03EA.title: A Camshaft Profile Actuator Position Sensor B Exceeded Learning Limit
P03EA.description: Engines with cam profile switching move the intake camshaft between lift profiles with actuators – for example pins that shift a sliding cam – and position sensors report which profile is engaged. The engine module learns reference values of position sensor B, such as its end-position levels or the expected pulse position relative to the crankshaft and camshaft sensors; a Ford patent describes correcting this position for the cam phase. P03EA means the learned value lies outside the permitted adaptation limit, so profile detection is no longer reliable and the module usually stays in a safe profile. No manufacturer document available to us describes the code or its limits; GM's 2.7-litre sliding cam has no learning-limit code. CARB lists a pin that does not reach its position among the faults to be detected.

causes.label: Position sensor B or actuator with integrated sensor worn or faulty (signal drift)
Actuator pin or sliding piece stiff, guide worn, dirty oil

Engine module software (learning algorithm)

symptoms: Profile switching disabled: less power at high revs or higher consumption
Possibly further profile actuator or sensor codes

causes.label: Position sensor C or actuator with integrated sensor worn or faulty (signal drift)
Actuator pin or sliding piece stiff, guide worn, dirty oil

symptoms: Profile switching disabled: less power at high revs or higher consumption
Possibly further profile actuator or sensor codes

P03EC.title: A Camshaft Profile Actuator C Control Circuit/Open Bank 1
P03EC.description: With a sliding camshaft, the intake camshaft (camshaft A) carries movable cam pieces with several lift profiles; solenoid actuators shoot a pin into a groove in the piece and shift it axially. Actuator C is the third of these actuators – not a profile position. The only known user is GM's 2.7-litre turbo four (L3B, three-step sliding cam, from model year 2019). P03EC means the actuator's control circuit is open: GM checks the circuit with the driver on and sets the code at an impedance of 200 kΩ or more (4 of 5 samples, above 11 V, MIL on the first trip). The actuator can then not shift its cam piece, and lift switching and cylinder deactivation are blocked.

causes.label: Actuator connector loose, corroded or pin pushed back (often after valve cover work)
Actuator solenoid open
Wire broken in the engine harness
Driver in the engine module

symptoms: Lift switching and cylinder deactivation blocked, higher consumption
Possibly rough running if a cam piece stays in the wrong position

P03ED.title: A Camshaft Profile Actuator C Control Circuit Low Bank 1
P03ED.description: With a sliding camshaft, the intake camshaft (camshaft A) carries movable cam pieces with several lift profiles; solenoid actuators shoot a pin into a groove in the piece and shift it axially. Actuator C is the third of these actuators – not a profile position. The only known user is GM's 2.7-litre turbo four (L3B, three-step sliding cam, from model year 2019). P03ED means the control circuit is shorted to ground: GM checks with the driver on and sets the code at 0.5 Ω or less between signal and ground (4 of 5 samples, above 11 V, MIL on the first trip). The actuator can then not shift its cam piece, and lift switching and cylinder deactivation are blocked.

Shorted turns in the actuator solenoid
Oil or moisture in the connector
Driver in the engine module

symptoms: Lift switching and cylinder deactivation blocked, higher consumption

P03EF.title: A Camshaft Profile Actuator C Control Performance/Stuck Off Bank 1
P03EF.description: With a sliding camshaft, the intake camshaft (camshaft A) carries movable cam pieces with several lift profiles; solenoid actuators shoot a pin into a groove in the piece and shift it axially. Actuator C is the third of these actuators – not a profile position. The only known user is GM's 2.7-litre turbo four (L3B, three-step sliding cam, from model year 2019). P03EF is the function check: in the standard's wording the actuator does not do what is commanded. A Hall sensor in the actuator reports the pin position. GM uses this code for a pin that extends without being commanded (4 of 5 cylinder events, MIL on the first trip); a pin that does not extend on command shows up there through the cam piece position sensors (GM-specific codes P30BE ff). GM bulletins name swapped actuator connectors and actuators fitted to the wrong camshaft after repairs.

causes.label: Actuator faulty inside: pin extends uncommanded (weak return spring)
Actuator connectors swapped, or intake and exhaust actuators fitted to the wrong camshaft
Interference in the Hall feedback signal (ground, connector)
Cam piece sticking or shift groove worn

symptoms: Ticking or rattling at the camshaft carrier
Misfire, rough idle or less power in the wrong lift profile
Lift switching and cylinder deactivation out of service

P03F0.title: A Camshaft Profile Actuator C Control Stuck On Bank 1
P03F0.description: With a sliding camshaft, the intake camshaft (camshaft A) carries movable cam pieces with several lift profiles; solenoid actuators shoot a pin into a groove in the piece and shift it axially. Return ramp of the shift groove damaged or cam piece sticking
Solenoid stays energized (control wire shorted to ground)
Hall feedback faulty

symptoms: Ticking or rattling at the camshaft carrier
Misfire, rough idle or less power in the wrong lift profile
Lift switching and cylinder deactivation out of service

P03F5.title: B Camshaft Profile Actuator C Control Stuck On Bank 1
P03F5.description: With a sliding camshaft, the exhaust camshaft (camshaft B) carries movable cam pieces with several lift profiles; solenoid actuators shoot a pin into a groove in the piece and shift it axially. Actuator C is the third of these actuators – not a profile position. The only known user is GM's 2.7-litre turbo four (L3B, three-step sliding cam, from model year 2019). P03F5 means the actuator stays on: its pin remains extended although it was commanded off. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code – GM monitors its exhaust actuators only for circuit faults and uncommanded extension; the description follows the intake counterpart P03F0, where GM sets the code if the pin does not retract by the end of the engine cycle.

causes.label: Pin sticking in the actuator (sludge, wear)
Return ramp of the shift groove damaged or cam piece sticking
Solenoid stays energized (control wire shorted to ground)
Hall feedback faulty

symptoms: Ticking or rattling at the camshaft carrier
Misfire, rough idle or less power in the wrong lift profile
Lift switching and cylinder deactivation out of service

P03F6.title: B Camshaft Position Actuator Position Sensor C Circuit Bank 1
P03F6.description: On some engines the exhaust cam phaser (camshaft position actuator B) has its own position sensors, which tell the engine module where the phaser actually is; sensor C is the third of them, bank 1 the side with cylinder 1. This is a different family from the sliding-cam position sensors (P2C05 ff). P03F6 is the general circuit code for this sensor: the module sees an open circuit or a signal outside its valid window on the supply, signal or ground line. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code (GM, Ford and FCA tables checked); the intake counterpart P03E5 ff is equally unused. The phaser is then usually held in its base position.

causes.label: Connector or harness to position sensor C open or corroded
Position sensor C faulty
5 V reference or ground disturbed
Engine module

symptoms: Exhaust cam phasing held in its base position, loss of power
Possibly rough idle or poorer emissions

P03F7.title: B Camshaft Position Actuator Position Sensor C Range/Performance Bank 1
P03F7.description: On some engines the exhaust cam phaser (camshaft position actuator B) has its own position sensors, which tell the engine module where the phaser actually is; sensor C is the third of them, bank 1 the side with cylinder 1. This is a different family from the sliding-cam position sensors (P2C05 ff). P03F7 means the signal is electrically valid but implausible – it does not match the commanded phaser position or the camshaft and crankshaft sensors, jumps, or lies outside the adjustment range. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code (GM, Ford and FCA tables checked); the intake counterpart P03E5 ff is equally unused. The phaser is then usually held in its base position.

causes.label: Sensor signal implausible (drift, loose target or magnet)
Phaser stiff, actual position deviates
Loose contact or interference
Valve timing wrong after a repair

symptoms: Exhaust cam phasing held in its base position, loss of power
Possibly rough idle or poorer emissions

P03F8.title: B Camshaft Position Actuator Position Sensor C Circuit Low Bank 1
P03F8.description: On some engines the exhaust cam phaser (camshaft position actuator B) has its own position sensors, which tell the engine module where the phaser actually is; sensor C is the third of them, bank 1 the side with cylinder 1. This is a different family from the sliding-cam position sensors (P2C05 ff). P03F8 means the signal stays below its lower limit – signal wire shorted to ground, 5 V supply open, or the sensor shorted internally. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code (GM, Ford and FCA tables checked); the intake counterpart P03E5 ff is equally unused. The phaser is then usually held in its base position.

causes.label: Signal wire shorted to ground or 5 V supply open
Sensor faulty internally
Connector corroded
Engine module

symptoms: Exhaust cam phasing held in its base position, loss of power
Possibly rough idle or poorer emissions

P03F9.title: B Camshaft Position Actuator Position Sensor C Circuit High Bank 1
P03F9.description: On some engines the exhaust cam phaser (camshaft position actuator B) has its own position sensors, which tell the engine module where the phaser actually is; sensor C is the third of them, bank 1 the side with cylinder 1. P03F9 means the signal stays above its upper limit – typically an open sensor ground, a signal wire shorted to 5 V or battery voltage, or a faulty sensor. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code (GM, Ford and FCA tables checked); the intake counterpart P03E5 ff is equally unused. The phaser is then usually held in its base position.

causes.label: Sensor ground open or signal wire shorted to 5 V or battery voltage
Sensor faulty
Connector wet or corroded
Engine module

symptoms: Exhaust cam phasing held in its base position, loss of power
Possibly rough idle or poorer emissions

P03FA.title: Ignition K Control Signal Circuit/Open
P03FA.description: Ignition K is one of up to twelve control signal lines (A to L) from the engine module to an ignition coil with integrated output stage or to an ignition module – plausibly the 11th channel, but the code standard leaves the assignment to the manufacturer. The code concerns this logic-level signal, not the coil's primary circuit (coil K has its own codes, P0361 and P2330 ff). P03FA means the control line is open or high-resistance: with its driver switched off the module sees a voltage that indicates a missing load (GM uses more than 30 kΩ for comparable coil drivers). The coil fires wrongly or not at all; the misfire usually also sets P0300 ff, and many modules shut off injection to that cylinder to protect the catalyst. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code – it would only concern twelve-cylinder engines, whose makers publish no OBD summaries; GM and Ford tables stop at eight and ten cylinders.

causes.label: Control line or connector pin open (corrosion, pushed-back pin)
Coil with integrated output stage or ignition module faulty
Supply or ground of the coil or module missing
Driver in the engine module

symptoms: Check engine light on, may flash with severe misfire
Misfire on the cylinder of this channel, rough running
Loss of power, cylinder possibly shut off

P03FB.title: Ignition K Control Signal Circuit Low
P03FB.description: Ignition K is one of up to twelve control signal lines (A to L) from the engine module to an ignition coil with integrated output stage or to an ignition module – plausibly the 11th channel, but the code standard leaves the assignment to the manufacturer. The code concerns this logic-level signal, not the coil's primary circuit (coil K has its own codes, P0361 and P2330 ff). P03FB means the signal stays too low – typically the control line is shorted to ground or the input of the output stage is shorted, so the driver never sees a high level. The coil fires wrongly or not at all; the misfire usually also sets P0300 ff, and many modules shut off injection to that cylinder to protect the catalyst. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code – it would only concern twelve-cylinder engines, whose makers publish no OBD summaries; GM and Ford tables stop at eight and ten cylinders.

causes.label: Control line shorted to ground (chafed harness)
Input of the coil output stage shorted
Moisture or corrosion in the connector
Driver in the engine module

symptoms: Check engine light on, may flash with severe misfire
Misfire on the cylinder of this channel, rough running
Loss of power, cylinder possibly shut off

P03FC.title: Ignition K Control Signal Circuit High
P03FC.description: Ignition K is one of up to twelve control signal lines (A to L) from the engine module to an ignition coil with integrated output stage or to an ignition module – plausibly the 11th channel, but the code standard leaves the assignment to the manufacturer. The code concerns this logic-level signal, not the coil's primary circuit (coil L has its own codes, P0362 and P2333 ff). Coil output stage faulty
Moisture or corrosion in the connector
