It draws very high current through a relay (on recent Ram a solid-state relay) and is switched by the engine module before and after starting; CARB requires cold-start aids to be monitored. Cummins checks it by the manifold temperature rise, Iveco by the battery voltage dip when the relay switches. P0540 is the general circuit fault of heater A without low/high assignment. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; GM's Duramax LML has an intake heater but reports it under its own codes P154A–P154D.

causes.label: Heater relay faulty (contacts welded or burnt, solid-state relay shorted)
Heating grid burnt out
Power cable or ring terminal corroded or overheated, control connector
Engine module driver

symptoms: Hard cold start, white smoke, rough cold idle
With welded relay: battery drained, heater stays on

P0541.title: Intake Air Heater A Circuit Low
P0541.description: Some diesels – typically Cummins engines in Ram pick-ups and commercial vehicles, and Iveco – heat the intake air with a grid heater in the intake manifold instead of or alongside glow plugs. It draws very high current through a relay (on recent Ram a solid-state relay) and is switched by the engine module before and after starting; CARB requires cold-start aids to be monitored. Cummins checks it by the manifold temperature rise, Iveco by the battery voltage dip when the relay switches. P0541 means the voltage in the monitored circuit stays too low – typically a control line or relay coil shorted to ground or open, so the relay does not switch and there is no preheating. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; GM's Duramax LML has an intake heater but reports it under its own codes P154A–P154D.

causes.label: Relay control line shorted to ground (chafing)
Relay coil open or solid-state relay faulty
Connector at relay or module corroded
Engine module driver

P0542.title: Intake Air Heater A Circuit High
P0542.description: Some diesels – typically Cummins engines in Ram pick-ups and commercial vehicles, and Iveco – heat the intake air with a grid heater in the intake manifold instead of or alongside glow plugs. It draws very high current through a relay (on recent Ram a solid-state relay) and is switched by the engine module before and after starting; CARB requires cold-start aids to be monitored. P0542 means the voltage stays high although the heater is commanded on – a control line shorted to positive or a relay that does not switch. A shorted or welded relay can also power the heater permanently; Ram recalled 6.7 L Cummins trucks because a shorted heater relay could start a fire. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; GM's Duramax LML has an intake heater but reports it under its own codes P154A–P154D.

causes.label: Heater relay faulty (solid-state relay shorted, contacts stuck)
Control line shorted to positive, harness chafed on a power cable
Power circuit overheated, cable scorched
Engine module driver

symptoms: Battery drained when heater stays on
Burning smell or scorched wiring at the relay

P0543.title: Intake Air Heater A Circuit Open
P0543.description: Some diesels – typically Cummins engines in Ram pick-ups and commercial vehicles, and Iveco – heat the intake air with a grid heater in the intake manifold instead of or alongside glow plugs. It draws very high current through a relay (on recent Ram a solid-state relay) and is switched by the engine module before and after starting; CARB requires cold-start aids to be monitored. P0543 means an open circuit at heater A – in the control line or relay coil, or depending on the maker in the power circuit or heating element itself. It is detected by driver diagnosis with the output off, by a missing voltage dip on switching on or by a missing temperature rise. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; GM's Duramax LML has an intake heater but reports it under its own codes P154A–P154D.

causes.label: Heating grid burnt out
Relay coil or contact open
Broken cable, loose nut or ring terminal at the grid
Fusible link in the heater circuit

symptoms: White smoke or knocking while warming up

P0544.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Bank 1 Sensor 1
P0544.description: The exhaust gas temperature sensor is a thermistor in a voltage divider with the module's pull-up resistor; the first one (sensor 1) sits before the turbocharger, the oxidation catalyst or after it depending on the maker. Diesels use it for particulate filter regeneration and component protection; CARB names it explicitly as a monitored input. P0544 is the general fault of bank 1 sensor 1. Ford's 6.7 L diesel uses it not as a circuit fault but for plausibility against an exhaust temperature model: after at least 6 h off it compares sensor and model over 200–400 s, a fault exceeding ±80 °C for 20 s, once per trip. GM's Duramax does not use P0544. The module then runs on a model value and may restrict filter regeneration.

causes.label: Sensor aged or drifting, soot on the tip
Cable or connector damaged by heat or vibration
Exhaust leak before the sensor
Exhaust temperature really deviating (injection fault)

symptoms: Particulate filter regeneration missing, filter warning

P0545.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Low Bank 1 Sensor 1
P0545.description: The exhaust gas temperature sensor is a thermistor in a voltage divider with the module's pull-up resistor; the first one (sensor 1) sits before the turbocharger, the oxidation catalyst or after it depending on the maker. Diesels use it for particulate filter regeneration and component protection; CARB names it explicitly as a monitored input. P0545 means the signal is below range: GM L5P below 142 Ω in 10 of 20 samples, GM LML below 0.65 V, Ford 6.7 L below 0.10 V for about 2 s, Saab 9-5 2.0 TiD below 0.1 V for 1 s. Usually a signal shorted to ground. GM USA uses two trips, GM Europe in the Saab one. The module uses a substitute value and blocks filter regeneration.

causes.label: Signal line shorted to ground (chafed on the exhaust or bracket)
Sensor shorted internally
Connector damp or corroded
Engine module

symptoms: Particulate filter regeneration missing, filter warning

P0546.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit High Bank 1 Sensor 1
P0546.description: The exhaust gas temperature sensor is a thermistor in a voltage divider with the module's pull-up resistor; the first one (sensor 1) sits before the turbocharger, the oxidation catalyst or after it depending on the maker. Diesels use it for particulate filter regeneration and component protection; CARB names it explicitly as a monitored input. P0546 means the signal is above range: GM L5P above 922 Ω, GM LML above 2.21 V, Ford 6.7 L above 2.66 V for about 2 s, Saab 9-5 2.0 TiD above 4.9 V for 1 s. Most often an open circuit pulled up to the reference, otherwise a short to positive; live data then show −40 °C or the maximum. The module uses a substitute value and blocks filter regeneration.

causes.label: Sensor element or internal lead open (vibration, heat)
Connector loose or corroded, broken wire
Signal line shorted to positive
Engine module

symptoms: Particulate filter regeneration missing, filter warning

P0547.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Bank 2 Sensor 1
P0547.description: The exhaust gas temperature sensor is a thermistor in a voltage divider with the module's pull-up resistor; the first one (sensor 1) sits before the turbocharger, the oxidation catalyst or after it depending on the maker. Diesels use it for particulate filter regeneration and component protection; CARB names it explicitly as a monitored input. Bank 2 sensor 1 exists only on V engines with a separate exhaust path per cylinder bank. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; the thresholds known for bank 1 apply by analogy. P0547 is the general circuit fault, the counterpart of P0544.

causes.label: Sensor faulty or aged
Cable or connector damaged by heat or vibration
Exhaust leak before the sensor
Engine module

symptoms: Particulate filter regeneration missing, filter warning

P0548.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Low Bank 2 Sensor 1
P0548.description: The exhaust gas temperature sensor is a thermistor in a voltage divider with the module's pull-up resistor; the first one (sensor 1) sits before the turbocharger, the oxidation catalyst or after it depending on the maker. Diesels use it for particulate filter regeneration and component protection; CARB names it explicitly as a monitored input. Bank 2 sensor 1 exists only on V engines with a separate exhaust path per cylinder bank. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; the thresholds known for bank 1 apply by analogy. P0548 means the signal is below range, usually a short to ground – for bank 1 GM uses below 142 Ω, Ford below 0.10 V.

causes.label: Signal line shorted to ground
Sensor shorted internally
Connector damp or corroded
Engine module

symptoms: Particulate filter regeneration missing, filter warning

P0549.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit High Bank 2 Sensor 1
P0549.description: The exhaust gas temperature sensor is a thermistor in a voltage divider with the module's pull-up resistor; the first one (sensor 1) sits before the turbocharger, the oxidation catalyst or after it depending on the maker. Diesels use it for particulate filter regeneration and component protection; CARB names it explicitly as a monitored input. Bank 2 sensor 1 exists only on V engines with a separate exhaust path per cylinder bank. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; the thresholds known for bank 1 apply by analogy. P0549 means the signal is above range, usually an open circuit or a short to positive – for bank 1 GM uses above 922 Ω, Ford above 2.66 V.

causes.label: Sensor or internal lead open
Connector loose, broken wire
Short to positive
Engine module

symptoms: Particulate filter regeneration missing, filter warning

P054A.title: Cold Start B Camshaft Position Timing Over-Advanced Bank 1
P054A.description: Camshaft B is the exhaust camshaft. During catalyst heating after a cold start some engines set it to a specific position; CARB requires such commanded elements to be monitored with their own codes, separate from the normal cam codes. Ford watches the deviation with an averaged variance index for each direction; GM (Saab 9-4X V6) uses only the retard codes, above 6° for 1 s or 4 s cumulative, type B. The commonest cause is oil pressure building too slowly when cold. P054A means bank 1 was too far advanced. Mercedes (M276) traces it to slow oil pressure – 1 bar should be reached after about 3 s; Audi (Q5 3.2) and VW (Atlas 3.6 and 2.0 T) fixed it by software.

causes.label: Oil pressure building too slowly when cold (oil level, viscosity, pick-up, pump)
Exhaust oil control valve sticking or screens clogged
Module software (threshold too tight)
Cam phaser defective, locking pin
Timing chain stretched or misassembled

symptoms: Check engine light on, usually without noticeable symptom

P054B.title: Cold Start B Camshaft Position Timing Over-Retarded Bank 1
P054B.description: Camshaft B is the exhaust camshaft. During catalyst heating after a cold start some engines set it to a specific position; CARB requires such commanded elements to be monitored with their own codes, separate from the normal cam codes. Ford watches the deviation with an averaged variance index for each direction; GM (Saab 9-4X V6) uses only the retard codes, above 6° for 1 s or 4 s cumulative, type B. The commonest cause is oil pressure building too slowly when cold. P054B means bank 1 stayed too far retarded. GM's test procedure checks oil level and pressure, a phaser sweep from 0 to 40° and the control valve at 7–12 Ω.

causes.label: Oil pressure building too slowly when cold (oil level, viscosity, pick-up, pump)
Exhaust oil control valve sticking or screens clogged
Module software (threshold too tight)
Cam phaser defective, locking pin
Timing chain stretched or misassembled

symptoms: Check engine light on, usually without noticeable symptom

P054C.title: Cold Start B Camshaft Position Timing Over-Advanced Bank 2
P054C.description: Camshaft B is the exhaust camshaft. During catalyst heating after a cold start some engines set it to a specific position; CARB requires such commanded elements to be monitored with their own codes, separate from the normal cam codes. Ford watches the deviation with an averaged variance index for each direction; GM (Saab 9-4X V6) uses only the retard codes, above 6° for 1 s or 4 s cumulative, type B. The commonest cause is oil pressure building too slowly when cold. P054C means bank 2 of a V engine was too far advanced. Together with P054A it points to a common cause such as oil pressure or software (Mercedes M276, Audi 3.2).

causes.label: Oil pressure building too slowly when cold (oil level, viscosity, pick-up, pump)
Exhaust oil control valve bank 2 sticking or screens clogged
Module software (threshold too tight)
Cam phaser bank 2 defective, locking pin
Timing chain stretched or misassembled

symptoms: Check engine light on, usually without noticeable symptom

P054D.title: Cold Start B Camshaft Position Timing Over-Retarded Bank 2
P054D.description: Camshaft B is the exhaust camshaft. During catalyst heating after a cold start some engines set it to a specific position; CARB requires such commanded elements to be monitored with their own codes, separate from the normal cam codes. Ford watches the deviation with an averaged variance index for each direction; GM (Saab 9-4X V6) uses only the retard codes, above 6° for 1 s or 4 s cumulative, type B. The commonest cause is oil pressure building too slowly when cold. P054D means bank 2 of a V engine stayed too far retarded. Only bank 2 points to that bank's valve or phaser; together with P054B to the oil supply.

causes.label: Oil pressure building too slowly when cold (oil level, viscosity, pick-up, pump)
Exhaust oil control valve bank 2 sticking or screens clogged
Module software (threshold too tight)
Cam phaser bank 2 defective, locking pin
Timing chain stretched or misassembled

symptoms: Check engine light on, usually without noticeable symptom

P054E.title: Idle Control System Fuel Quantity Lower Than Expected
P054E.description: Diesel only. At controlled idle the module compares the fuel quantity the idle governor needs for target speed with a model value; CARB sets the limit from 2013 at ±50 % of what a sound engine needs. Ford's diesel sets the codes beyond ±50 % for 5 s at standstill with warm engine and no filter regeneration; GM compares with 0.5 times a minimum map or 1.5 times a maximum map, 200 of 255 samples, type B. P054E means the engine holds idle with much less fuel than expected – more energy arrives than commanded, for example from injectors delivering too much, oil entering combustion or wrong injector correction codes.

causes.label: Injectors delivering more than commanded (drift, coking, leaking needle)
Oil entering combustion (turbo seal, crankcase ventilation)
Rail pressure actually higher than measured
Wrong injector correction codes after replacement

symptoms: Blue or white smoke, knocking at idle

P054F.title: Idle Control System Fuel Quantity Higher Than Expected
P054F.description: Diesel only. At controlled idle the module compares the fuel quantity the idle governor needs for target speed with a model value; CARB sets the limit from 2013 at ±50 % of what a sound engine needs. Ford's diesel sets the codes beyond ±50 % for 5 s at standstill with warm engine and no filter regeneration; GM compares with 0.5 times a minimum map or 1.5 times a maximum map, 200 of 255 samples, type B. P054F means the governor needs much more fuel than expected – the commanded quantity does not arrive or the engine has extra losses: clogged injectors, low compression, an EGR valve stuck open or additional load from accessories.

causes.label: Injectors delivering too little (coked, high return flow)
Rail pressure actually lower, fuel supply (filter, air)
Mechanical losses: compression, seizing accessories
EGR valve stuck open or intake blocked

P0550.title: Power Steering Pressure Sensor/Switch Circuit
P0550.description: Hydraulic power steering has a pressure switch or sensor on the high-pressure line; when the wheel is turned at standstill, pump pressure and engine load rise sharply, so the engine module raises idle air in advance to stop the engine stalling. That makes it an input to idle control under CARB. Switches (Saab, Mitsubishi) ground a pull-up; analogue 5 V sensors (Toyota) give about 0.45 V at zero pressure. GM's and Ford's tables do not use P0550–P0554. P0550 is the general circuit fault. No manufacturer document available to us uses it. Without the signal the engine can drop or stall at full lock, or the module raises idle permanently as a substitute.

causes.label: Connector or wire open or corroded (splash zone at the pump)
Sensor or switch faulty, often also leaking
5 V reference or ground disturbed
Engine module

symptoms: Check engine light (depending on the maker)
Idle drops when steering at standstill, engine may stall

P0551.title: Power Steering Pressure Sensor/Switch Circuit Range/Performance
P0551.description: Hydraulic power steering has a pressure switch or sensor on the high-pressure line; when the wheel is turned at standstill, pump pressure and engine load rise sharply, so the engine module raises idle air in advance to stop the engine stalling. That makes it an input to idle control under CARB. Switches (Saab, Mitsubishi) ground a pull-up; analogue 5 V sensors (Toyota) give about 0.45 V at zero pressure. GM's and Ford's tables do not use P0550–P0554. P0551 means the switch reports high pressure where that is implausible – at speed there is hardly any steering. Mitsubishi sets it when the switch stays on through 10 drive-and-stop cycles; Saab's Trionic T8 after 600 s above 50 km/h, keeping raised idle as substitute and without warning lamp.

causes.label: Pressure switch stuck closed or faulty internally
Signal line shorted to ground (ground means active)
Permanently high pressure (steering valve sticking, kinked line)
Vehicle speed signal faulty (Saab depends on P0501)

symptoms: Check engine light depending on the maker (Saab: none)

P0552.title: Power Steering Pressure Sensor/Switch Circuit Low
P0552.description: Hydraulic power steering has a pressure switch or sensor on the high-pressure line; when the wheel is turned at standstill, pump pressure and engine load rise sharply, so the engine module raises idle air in advance to stop the engine stalling. That makes it an input to idle control under CARB. Switches (Saab, Mitsubishi) ground a pull-up; analogue 5 V sensors (Toyota) give about 0.45 V at zero pressure. GM's and Ford's tables do not use P0550–P0554. P0552 means the signal of an analogue sensor is below range – an open 5 V supply, a signal shorted to ground or a faulty sensor, not low pressure. Toyota's 2007–08 Tundra set P0552/P0553 from a series sensor fault and replaced it with a revised part, with the warning lamp on.

causes.label: Sensor faulty (Tundra 2007–08 series part)
5 V supply open or signal shorted to ground
Connector corroded or oily (leaking sensor)
Engine module 5 V reference

symptoms: Idle drops when steering at standstill
Possible fluid leak at the sensor

P0553.title: Power Steering Pressure Sensor/Switch Circuit High
P0553.description: Hydraulic power steering has a pressure switch or sensor on the high-pressure line; when the wheel is turned at standstill, pump pressure and engine load rise sharply, so the engine module raises idle air in advance to stop the engine stalling. That makes it an input to idle control under CARB. Switches (Saab, Mitsubishi) ground a pull-up; analogue 5 V sensors (Toyota) give about 0.45 V at zero pressure. GM's and Ford's tables do not use P0550–P0554. P0553 means the signal is above range – usually an open sensor ground or signal pulled up, a short to 5 V or battery, or a faulty sensor; high pressure alone does not reach the limit (Toyota's sensor gives 4.05 V at 7000 kPa). Toyota's 2007–08 Tundra set it from a series sensor fault.

causes.label: Sensor faulty (Tundra 2007–08 series part)
Sensor ground or signal line open
Signal shorted to voltage
Engine module

symptoms: Permanently raised idle or no load pre-control
Possible fluid leak at the sensor

P0554.title: Power Steering Pressure Sensor/Switch Circuit Intermittent
P0554.description: Hydraulic power steering has a pressure switch or sensor on the high-pressure line; when the wheel is turned at standstill, pump pressure and engine load rise sharply, so the engine module raises idle air in advance to stop the engine stalling. That makes it an input to idle control under CARB. Switches (Saab, Mitsubishi) ground a pull-up; analogue 5 V sensors (Toyota) give about 0.45 V at zero pressure. GM's and Ford's tables do not use P0550–P0554. P0554 means the signal flutters. Mitsubishi sets it when the switch changes state at 10 Hz or more for 20 s above 50 km/h – no sound switch switches that fast. Causes are electrical (loose contact) as well as hydraulic: pressure pulsation from air or low fluid, or an unsteady pump.

causes.label: Loose contact or corrosion at connector or wire
Low fluid or air in the system (pressure pulsation)
Pressure switch worn (contact bounce)
Steering pump delivering unsteady pressure

symptoms: Check engine light depending on the maker

P0555.title: Brake Booster Pressure Sensor Circuit
P0555.description: The brake booster pressure sensor (5 V reference, signal, ground) measures the vacuum in the brake booster. On direct-injection, turbo, stop-start and hybrid engines intake vacuum is scarce, so the engine module watches it and creates vacuum when needed – closing the throttle, suppressing engine stop or running an electric vacuum pump. That makes it an input to idle and throttle control. P0555 is the general circuit fault without low/high distinction. No manufacturer document available to us uses it; GM splits circuit faults into P0557 and P0558. The module then assumes a substitute value and keeps vacuum available as a precaution.

causes.label: Connector or wire to the sensor open or corroded
Sensor faulty
5 V reference disturbed (short at another sensor on the same reference)
Engine module

symptoms: Check engine light or brake booster warning

P0556.title: Brake Booster Pressure Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P0556.description: The brake booster pressure sensor (5 V reference, signal, ground) measures the vacuum in the brake booster. On direct-injection, turbo, stop-start and hybrid engines intake vacuum is scarce, so the engine module watches it and creates vacuum when needed – closing the throttle, suppressing engine stop or running an electric vacuum pump. That makes it an input to idle and throttle control. P0556 means the signal is valid but implausible. GM compares it with intake vacuum (MAP) with the throttle nearly closed for over 3 s, filtered, type B with two trips. VW and Porsche also check the electric vacuum pump with it – Porsche compares the pressure at wake-up and 1.5 s later – so P0556 can also mean a weak pump or a leak. VW fixed false setting on the 2016–17 Jetta 1.4 T by software.

causes.label: Leaking or kinked vacuum line or faulty check valve
Sensor stuck or drifting
Electric vacuum pump or its relay weak (hybrid, Porsche, turbo DI)
Module software (false setting)
Booster diaphragm leaking

symptoms: Check engine light and/or brake booster warning
Hard brake pedal with real vacuum loss

P0557.title: Brake Booster Pressure Sensor Circuit Low
P0557.description: The brake booster pressure sensor (5 V reference, signal, ground) measures the vacuum in the brake booster. On direct-injection, turbo, stop-start and hybrid engines intake vacuum is scarce, so the engine module watches it and creates vacuum when needed – closing the throttle, suppressing engine stop or running an electric vacuum pump. That makes it an input to idle and throttle control. P0557 means the signal voltage is too low: GM 2018 below 5 % of the 5 V reference in 320 of 400 samples (about 5 s), GM 2006 below 0.04 V; type B, two trips. Typical are a signal shorted to ground or an open signal or 5 V line. As low voltage means plenty of vacuum, the module would wrongly assume enough – so it uses a substitute value.

causes.label: Signal line open or shorted to ground, connector loose or corroded
5 V reference open or shorted to ground
Sensor faulty internally
Engine module

symptoms: Check engine light or brake booster warning

P0558.title: Brake Booster Pressure Sensor Circuit High
P0558.description: The brake booster pressure sensor (5 V reference, signal, ground) measures the vacuum in the brake booster. On direct-injection, turbo, stop-start and hybrid engines intake vacuum is scarce, so the engine module watches it and creates vacuum when needed – closing the throttle, suppressing engine stop or running an electric vacuum pump. That makes it an input to idle and throttle control. P0558 means the signal voltage is too high: GM 2018 above 95 % of the reference in 2000 of 2400 samples (about 30 s), GM 2006 above 4.89 V; type B, two trips. Typical are a signal shorted to 5 V or battery voltage or an open sensor ground. A real loss of vacuum does not set P0558 but P0556 or, depending on the maker, P050F.

causes.label: Sensor ground open (connector, wire)
Signal shorted to 5 V reference or battery voltage
Sensor faulty
Engine module

symptoms: Check engine light or brake booster warning

P0559.title: Brake Booster Pressure Sensor Circuit Intermittent
P0559.description: The brake booster pressure sensor (5 V reference, signal, ground) measures the vacuum in the brake booster. On direct-injection, turbo, stop-start and hybrid engines intake vacuum is scarce, so the engine module watches it and creates vacuum when needed – closing the throttle, suppressing engine stop or running an electric vacuum pump. That makes it an input to idle and throttle control. P0559 means the signal jumps briefly – a loose contact or broken wire under movement – without staying out of range long enough for P0557 or P0558. No manufacturer document available to us uses it; GM catches dropouts through the sample counters of P0557/P0558. CARB requires input components to be checked for circuit faults.

causes.label: Loose contact at the sensor connector (pin tension, corrosion)
Broken or chafed wire moving with the engine
Sensor with internal dropouts

symptoms: Check engine light (depending on the maker)

P055A.title: Engine Oil Pressure Sensor/Switch B Circuit
P055A.description: Oil pressure sensor B is a second sensor, usually in the oil feed to the cam phasers or valve lift switching – on GM's 2.5 L (2014 Impala and Malibu) in the camshaft cover – while sensor A measures the main gallery. Documented only by GM (type B, two trips); Ford uses no sensor B. P055A is the general circuit fault without low/high assignment. No manufacturer document available to us uses it – GM reports sensor B only as P055B–P055D. The module then uses a substitute value and may set cam phasers or valve lift to their base position.

causes.label: Connector or harness to sensor B open, corroded or oily
Sensor B open internally
Shared 5 V reference or ground disturbed
Engine module

symptoms: Cam phasing or valve lift switching possibly restricted

P055B.title: Engine Oil Pressure Sensor/Switch B Range/Performance
P055B.description: Oil pressure sensor B is a second sensor, usually in the oil feed to the cam phasers or valve lift switching – on GM's 2.5 L (2014 Impala and Malibu) in the camshaft cover – while sensor A measures the main gallery. Documented only by GM (type B, two trips); Ford uses no sensor B. P055B compares sensors A and B with the phasers almost idle: GM sets it when they differ by more than 220 kPa below 1850 rpm, 80 of 100 samples. With the engine off, sensor B must read about atmospheric pressure (around 90 kPa); a GM bulletin for the 2014 2.5 L uses exactly that as a test. A real difference can also come from a clogged screen in the cylinder head feed.

causes.label: Sensor B drifting or stuck
Sensor A wrong (comparison fails because of A)
Real pressure difference: clogged screen, oil level or quality
Contact resistance in the connector

symptoms: Cam phasing or valve lift switching possibly restricted

P055C.title: Engine Oil Pressure Sensor/Switch B Low
P055C.description: Oil pressure sensor B is a second sensor, usually in the oil feed to the cam phasers or valve lift switching – on GM's 2.5 L (2014 Impala and Malibu) in the camshaft cover – while sensor A measures the main gallery. Documented only by GM (type B, two trips); Ford uses no sensor B. P055C means the signal is too low – an open 5 V supply or signal line or a short to ground, not low oil pressure. GM sets it at a reading of 10 or less in 120 of 150 samples; real low pressure is P0524. The module uses a substitute value.

causes.label: 5 V supply or signal open, connector loose or corroded
Signal shorted to ground (chafing)
Sensor B faulty internally
Module's 5 V reference disturbed

symptoms: Cam phasing or valve lift switching possibly restricted

P055D.title: Engine Oil Pressure Sensor/Switch B High
P055D.description: Oil pressure sensor B is a second sensor, usually in the oil feed to the cam phasers or valve lift switching – on GM's 2.5 L (2014 Impala and Malibu) in the camshaft cover – while sensor A measures the main gallery. Documented only by GM (type B, two trips); Ford uses no sensor B. P055D means the signal is too high – a signal shorted to 5 V or battery voltage or an open sensor ground. GM sets it at a reading of 1000 kPa or more in 120 of 150 samples. Real excess oil pressure is reported separately, by Ford under P055F. The module uses a substitute value.

causes.label: Sensor ground open
Signal shorted to 5 V or 12 V
Sensor B faulty internally
Engine module

symptoms: Cam phasing or valve lift switching possibly restricted

P055E.title: Oxygen Sensor Control Module System Voltage
P055E.description: Some engines use wide-band or NOx sensors with their own evaluation module that reports over CAN. That module measures its supply; outside its working range it sets P055E, and lambda control and the sensor diagnoses are suspended because no valid values exist. No manufacturer document available to us uses P055E – Ford's diesel monitors the comparable supply of its smart NOx/O2 sensor as P220A/P220B, below 8.5 V or above 16.5 V. CARB requires modules delivering emission-relevant signals to be monitored.

causes.label: Fuse, relay or supply line to the sensor module
Poor module ground
Battery or alternator (under- or overvoltage)
Sensor module faulty

symptoms: Lambda control in open loop, possibly higher consumption

P055F.title: Engine Oil Pressure Out of Range
P055F.description: P055F is a condition code: the measured oil pressure is above the maximum expected for speed and oil temperature – Ford, which documents it, calls it 'too high' and pairs it with P0524 (too low). Ford checks continuously for 5 s, only with plausible oil pressure, oil temperature and coolant sensors, as engine protection. Background are regulated oil pumps, whose control valve (P06DA ff) defaults to full pressure on failure. An electrically high signal is P0523 or P055D instead.

causes.label: Oil pump control valve or variable pump stuck at high pressure
Pump relief valve stuck
Wrong viscosity, very cold oil
Sensor A reading high within range

symptoms: Check engine light or oil pressure warning
Possible engine protection or power limit
Possible oil filter or seal leaks

P0560.title: System Voltage
P0560.description: The module measures its own supply voltage. CARB allows other monitors to be suspended below 11 V, and above a maker's threshold only if the voltage itself is diagnosed – that is what these codes record. GM's engine modules and Ford's PCM set them without warning lamp. P0560 is the general code without low/high split, used differently: Saab's 2002 9-5 transmission module sets it below 9 V or above 18 V for 1 s and goes into limp mode; Saab's EDC16 diesel only above 17 V (24 V charger or jump start); the GM-built 9-4X as a low-voltage code. GM's and Ford's engine modules use P0562/P0563 instead.

causes.label: Battery weak or faulty
Alternator or regulator (under- or overcharging)
Jump start or charger at 24 V
Corroded or loose battery terminals or ground strap

symptoms: Several modules report codes, starting problems

P0561.title: System Voltage Unstable
P0561.description: The module measures its own supply voltage. CARB allows other monitors to be suspended below 11 V, and above a maker's threshold only if the voltage itself is diagnosed – that is what these codes record. GM's engine modules and Ford's PCM set them without warning lamp. GM interprets P0561 as a difference between the module's two supply inputs: permanent battery and switched ignition supply may differ by at most 3 V, otherwise it sets after 50 of 63 samples. In the engine module that is type C without warning lamp, in GM's 9-speed transmission module type A with the lamp after one trip. Other makers use it for a fluctuating voltage.

causes.label: Fuse, relay or line of the ignition supply (voltage drop)
Loose or corroded connector or ground at the module
Voltage regulator fluctuating
Battery terminal loose

symptoms: Transmission warning or check engine light (GM transmission module)

P0562.title: System Voltage Low
P0562.description: The module measures its own supply voltage. CARB allows other monitors to be suspended below 11 V, and above a maker's threshold only if the voltage itself is diagnosed – that is what these codes record. GM's engine modules and Ford's PCM set them without warning lamp. P0562 means the voltage is below its threshold with the engine running, when the charging system should deliver: GM 9 V or less at 400 rpm or more in 400 of 500 samples (about 5 s), type C. Saab's 9-4X modules may switch off temporarily below about 9 V. Many other modules, such as GM's brake module, set P0562 themselves.

causes.label: Alternator or regulator delivering too little
Battery faulty (shorted cell)
Corroded terminals, ground straps or alternator cable
High quiescent current or many consumers at idle

P0563.title: System Voltage High
P0563.description: The module measures its own supply voltage. CARB allows other monitors to be suspended below 11 V, and above a maker's threshold only if the voltage itself is diagnosed – that is what these codes record. GM's engine modules and Ford's PCM set them without warning lamp. P0563 means the voltage is above its threshold: GM's engine module 18 V or more in 400 of 500 samples, type C; Saab's 9-4X above 18 V for 5 s. Typical are an overcharging regulator or a jump start or charger at 24 V. Saab's EDC16 diesel reports the same condition as P0560 instead.

causes.label: Regulator or alternator overcharging
24 V jump start or fast charger
Missing battery or poor battery terminal (voltage spikes)
Alternator control line from the module (smart charging)

symptoms: Several modules switch off or report faults

P0564.title: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input A Circuit
P0564.description: Cruise control buttons are almost always a resistor ladder on one or two signal lines, each button giving its own voltage; the module reading it (GM and Saab from about 2010: the body module; FCA: steering column module or PCM) sends the button state to the engine module over CAN. CARB names cruise control as the example of an emission-neutral diagnosis – it is simply switched off – so GM lists all these codes as type C and Ford as non-MIL: no warning lamp, the engine runs normally. P0564 watches signal line A of the ladder: only voltage windows matching a button or no button are valid. GM sets it when the ratio sits in a gap between windows for over 0.5 s (2014: 2.5 s), the body module in the Saab 9-4X and 9-5 after an invalid voltage for 2 s. Cruise control is locked out for the ignition cycle.

causes.label: Cruise or steering wheel switch faulty or dirty (moisture, worn contacts)
Clockspring or steering wheel connector with contact resistance
Supply or signal line to the body module open or shorted
Body module

symptoms: Cruise control cannot be switched on or switches off
No check engine light, engine runs normally

P0565.title: Cruise Control On Signal
P0565.description: Cruise control buttons are almost always a resistor ladder on one or two signal lines, each button giving its own voltage; the module reading it (GM and Saab from about 2010: the body module; FCA: steering column module or PCM) sends the button state to the engine module over CAN. CARB names cruise control as the example of an emission-neutral diagnosis – it is simply switched off – so GM lists all these codes as type C and Ford as non-MIL: no warning lamp, the engine runs normally. P0565 concerns the on signal. GM sets it when the on/off button is reported pressed for over 20 s. Subaru (also in the Saab 9-2X) uses another principle and the warning lamp after two trips: cruise is reported active below 20 km/h for 10 s, where it cannot be active; the signal goes to the automatic transmission.

causes.label: On/off button stuck or faulty
Moisture or wear in the steering wheel switch
Contact resistance in clockspring or steering wheel connector
Body module or cruise module

symptoms: Cruise control inoperative, indicator permanently on or off
No check engine light, engine runs normally

P0566.title: Cruise Control Off Signal
P0566.description: Cruise control buttons are almost always a resistor ladder on one or two signal lines, each button giving its own voltage; the module reading it (GM and Saab from about 2010: the body module; FCA: steering column module or PCM) sends the button state to the engine module over CAN. CARB names cruise control as the example of an emission-neutral diagnosis – it is simply switched off – so GM lists all these codes as type C and Ford as non-MIL: no warning lamp, the engine runs normally. P0566 concerns the off signal of the main switch – implausible, stuck or invalid. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code. GM reports the on/off button under P0565 and the cancel button under P056C.

causes.label: On/off button stuck or faulty
Moisture or wear in the steering wheel switch
Contact resistance in clockspring or steering wheel connector
Body module or cruise module

symptoms: Cruise control cannot be switched on or off
No check engine light, engine runs normally

P0567.title: Cruise Control Resume Signal
P0567.description: Cruise control buttons are almost always a resistor ladder on one or two signal lines, each button giving its own voltage; the module reading it (GM and Saab from about 2010: the body module; FCA: steering column module or PCM) sends the button state to the engine module over CAN. CARB names cruise control as the example of an emission-neutral diagnosis – it is simply switched off – so GM lists all these codes as type C and Ford as non-MIL: no warning lamp, the engine runs normally. P0567 concerns the resume button. GM sets it when the button is reported pressed for over 89 s – much longer than the 20 s for on or cancel, because holding resume to accelerate is normal. The body module in the Saab 9-4X also sets it for an invalid voltage for 2 s.

causes.label: Resume button stuck or faulty
Moisture or wear in the steering wheel switch
Contact resistance in clockspring or steering wheel connector
Body module or cruise module

symptoms: No check engine light, engine runs normally

P0568.title: Cruise Control Set Signal
P0568.description: Cruise control buttons are almost always a resistor ladder on one or two signal lines, each button giving its own voltage; the module reading it (GM and Saab from about 2010: the body module; FCA: steering column module or PCM) sends the button state to the engine module over CAN. CARB names cruise control as the example of an emission-neutral diagnosis – it is simply switched off – so GM lists all these codes as type C and Ford as non-MIL: no warning lamp, the engine runs normally. P0568 concerns the set button, at GM usually combined with coast. GM sets it when the button is reported pressed for over 89 s; the body module in the Saab 9-5 after an invalid voltage for 2 s.

causes.label: Set button stuck or faulty
Moisture or wear in the steering wheel switch
Contact resistance in clockspring or steering wheel connector
Body module or cruise module

symptoms: No check engine light, engine runs normally

P0569.title: Cruise Control Coast Signal
P0569.description: Cruise control buttons are almost always a resistor ladder on one or two signal lines, each button giving its own voltage; the module reading it (GM and Saab from about 2010: the body module; FCA: steering column module or PCM) sends the button state to the engine module over CAN. CARB names cruise control as the example of an emission-neutral diagnosis – it is simply switched off – so GM lists all these codes as type C and Ford as non-MIL: no warning lamp, the engine runs normally. P0569 concerns a separate coast button (minus, lower the speed) – stuck or implausible. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code. GM combines set and coast and has no coast code of its own.

causes.label: Coast (minus) button stuck or faulty
Moisture or wear in the steering wheel switch
Contact resistance in clockspring or steering wheel connector
Body module or cruise module

symptoms: Speed cannot be lowered with cruise control
No check engine light, engine runs normally

P056A.title: Cruise Control Increase Distance Signal
P056A.description: Cruise control buttons are almost always a resistor ladder on one or two signal lines, each button giving its own voltage; the module reading it (GM and Saab from about 2010: the body module; FCA: steering column module or PCM) sends the button state to the engine module over CAN. CARB names cruise control as the example of an emission-neutral diagnosis – it is simply switched off – so GM lists all these codes as type C and Ford as non-MIL: no warning lamp, the engine runs normally. P056A exists only with adaptive cruise control: the button to increase following distance is stuck or invalid. FCA's switch reads the distance button over the same ladder as the others. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code. GM and Ford mostly report adaptive cruise faults in the radar module.

causes.label: Distance button stuck or faulty
Moisture or wear in the steering wheel switch
Contact resistance in clockspring or steering wheel connector
Body module or cruise module

symptoms: No check engine light, engine runs normally

P056B.title: Cruise Control Decrease Distance Signal
P056B.description: Cruise control buttons are almost always a resistor ladder on one or two signal lines, each button giving its own voltage; the module reading it (GM and Saab from about 2010: the body module; FCA: steering column module or PCM) sends the button state to the engine module over CAN. CARB names cruise control as the example of an emission-neutral diagnosis – it is simply switched off – so GM lists all these codes as type C and Ford as non-MIL: no warning lamp, the engine runs normally. P056B exists only with adaptive cruise control: the button to decrease following distance is stuck or invalid; counterpart of P056A. FCA's switch reads the distance button over the same ladder as the others. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code.

causes.label: Distance button stuck or faulty
Moisture or wear in the steering wheel switch
Contact resistance in clockspring or steering wheel connector
Body module or cruise module

symptoms: No check engine light, engine runs normally

P056C.title: Cruise Control Cancel Signal
P056C.description: Cruise control buttons are almost always a resistor ladder on one or two signal lines, each button giving its own voltage; the module reading it (GM and Saab from about 2010: the body module; FCA: steering column module or PCM) sends the button state to the engine module over CAN. CARB names cruise control as the example of an emission-neutral diagnosis – it is simply switched off – so GM lists all these codes as type C and Ford as non-MIL: no warning lamp, the engine runs normally. P056C concerns the cancel button, which interrupts control but keeps the set speed – unlike the off signal P0566. GM (from about 2015) sets it when the button is reported pressed for over 20 s. Older code lists still show it as reserved.

causes.label: Cancel button stuck or faulty
Moisture or wear in the steering wheel switch
Contact resistance in clockspring or steering wheel connector
Body module or cruise module

symptoms: Cruise control cannot be engaged or cancels immediately
No check engine light, engine runs normally

P056D.title: Reductant Control Module System Voltage
P056D.description: Diesels with SCR may have a separate module for AdBlue/DEF dosing (pump, heaters, dosing valve) talking to the engine module over CAN. It measures its supply; outside its window no safe dosing is possible, so dosing and SCR diagnoses are suspended and NOx rises, and if it persists the SCR warnings and power limits apply. No manufacturer document available to us uses P056D – Ford's diesel reports the dosing module supply as P21CB below 8.5 V and P21CC above 19 V. CARB requires SCR modules to be monitored.

causes.label: Fuse, relay or supply line of the DEF module
Corrosion at module connector or ground (underbody, road salt)
System under- or overvoltage
Module faulty

symptoms: Check engine light and DEF warning
Possible countdown to start inhibit or power limit

P056E.title: Cold Start Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Control A Performance
P056E.description: CARB requires every element commanded by the cold-start strategy to respond measurably in the commanded direction, with its own codes separate from the general monitoring of the same part. During catalyst heating the boost control is positioned deliberately – diesels close the variable turbine for load and heat, petrol engines open the wastegate so heat reaches the catalyst. P056E means boost control A (the first or only charger) did not follow its cold-start target. Its only documented user is Stellantis: the 2025 Ram 3500 cab chassis with 6.7 L Cummins lists it among codes that can light the warning lamp, fixed by a PCM software update; customers noticed hard cold starts and raised cold idle. Ford and GM do not use it.

causes.label: Variable turbine or wastegate actuator stiff (coking, cold)
Module software or calibration
Vacuum or boost hose leaking
Position or boost sensor faulty

symptoms: Hard cold start or rough warm-up

P056F.title: Cold Start Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Control B Performance
P056F.description: CARB requires every element commanded by the cold-start strategy to respond measurably in the commanded direction, with its own codes separate from the general monitoring of the same part. During catalyst heating the boost control is positioned deliberately – diesels close the variable turbine for load and heat, petrol engines open the wastegate so heat reaches the catalyst. P056F is the same check for boost control B – a second charger on twin-turbo or sequential systems, or a second stage. No manufacturer document available to us uses P056F; the Ram 6.7 L with a single charger only lists P056E. The description follows CARB's cold-start rules.

causes.label: Charger B actuator stiff or faulty
Vacuum or charge air line of charger B leaking
Software or calibration
Boost or position sensor B

P0570.title: Cruise Control Accelerate Signal
P0570.description: Cruise control buttons are almost always a resistor ladder on one or two signal lines, each button giving its own voltage; the module reading it (GM and Saab from about 2010: the body module; FCA: steering column module or PCM) sends the button state to the engine module over CAN. CARB names cruise control as the example of an emission-neutral diagnosis – it is simply switched off – so GM lists all these codes as type C and Ford as non-MIL: no warning lamp, the engine runs normally. P0570 classically concerns the accelerate (plus) button. Ford's 2023 diesel uses it differently, only with adaptive cruise: the CAN message with the maximum acceleration request from the radar module to the engine module is faulty, checked every 10 ms, fault after 0.1 s. GM does not use P0570 (resume and accelerate share P0567).

causes.label: Accelerate button faulty (conventional systems)
Ford adaptive cruise: CAN fault or software of radar module or PCM
Contact problem in steering wheel switch or clockspring
Module faulty

symptoms: Cruise control does not accelerate, adaptive cruise unavailable
No check engine light, engine runs normally

P0571.title: Brake Switch A Circuit
P0571.description: Brake switch A is the brake light switch or its signal to the engine module. The module needs it to cancel cruise control and for brake-throttle override, stop-start, idle control and the shift interlock. As cruise control is simply switched off, CARB treats such faults as emission-neutral – usually without warning lamp. P0571 is the general fault, usually detected by plausibility: Saab's 3.0 TiD (Bosch) sets it when the car brakes three times from over 49 km/h to standstill at 1.6 m/s² or more without a switch signal; Bosch EDC16 then switches cruise control off. NHTSA found Hyundai and Kia setting P0571 with P0504 from misadjusted brake light switches. Ford and GM petrol engines use P0572/P0573 instead.

causes.label: Brake light switch misadjusted
Brake light switch faulty (worn contact)
Connector, wire or brake light fuse
Engine or body module

symptoms: Cruise control cannot be set or switches off
Brake lights not working or permanently on

P0572.title: Brake Switch A Circuit Low
P0572.description: Brake switch A is the brake light switch or its signal to the engine module. The module needs it to cancel cruise control and for brake-throttle override, stop-start, idle control and the shift interlock. As cruise control is simply switched off, CARB treats such faults as emission-neutral – usually without warning lamp. P0572 means the switch signal stays low – never pressed – although the car brakes. Ford petrol checks over 25 brake applications, Ford diesel over 40 decelerations; GM in the Saab 9-4X and 9-5 compares the input with the body module's message, 8 of 10 samples over 2 s. Cruise control is locked out; Ford shows only the wrench lamp.

causes.label: Brake light switch faulty or misadjusted (not switching)
Brake light or switch supply fuse blown
Signal line open or shorted to ground, connector
Body or engine module

symptoms: Brake lights not lit (depending on cause)
Wrench lamp (Ford), no check engine light

P0573.title: Brake Switch A Circuit High
P0573.description: Brake switch A is the brake light switch or its signal to the engine module. The module needs it to cancel cruise control and for brake-throttle override, stop-start, idle control and the shift interlock. P0573 means the switch signal stays high – always pressed – although the car is not braking. causes.label: Brake light switch stuck closed or misadjusted (pedal stop buffer missing)
Brake pedal not returning fully (floor mat, return spring)
Signal line shorted to positive
Body or engine module

causes.label: Driving situation (long descent, towing) where speed cannot be held
Implausible speed signal (speed sensor, ABS wheel speed)
Software or cruise logic

symptoms: Cruise control switches off at high speed
No check engine light, engine runs normally

P0576.title: Cruise Control Input Circuit Low

symptoms: No check engine light, engine runs normally

P0577.title: Cruise Control Input Circuit High
P0577.description: Cruise control buttons are almost always a resistor ladder on one or two signal lines, each button giving its own voltage; the module reading it (GM and Saab from about 2010: the body module; FCA: steering column module or PCM) sends the button state to the engine module over CAN. Module faulty

P0578.title: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input A Circuit Stuck
P0578.description: Cruise control buttons are almost always a resistor ladder on one or two signal lines, each button giving its own voltage; the module reading it (GM and Saab from about 2010: the body module; FCA: steering column module or PCM) sends the button state to the engine module over CAN. P0579.title: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input A Circuit Range/Performance
P0579.description: Cruise control buttons are almost always a resistor ladder on one or two signal lines, each button giving its own voltage; the module reading it (GM and Saab from about 2010: the body module; FCA: steering column module or PCM) sends the button state to the engine module over CAN. causes.label: Oxidised or dirty contacts at the steering wheel connector
Switch contact for signal 1 not closing
Clockspring faulty
Wiring or module

symptoms: Cruise control cannot be switched on at times
No check engine light, engine runs normally

P057A.title: Brake Pedal Position Sensor A Circuit/Open
P057A.description: The brake pedal position sensor is an analogue 5 V sensor, usually Hall-type, giving the pedal position continuously instead of a switch – for brake lights, cruise control, stop-start, brake-throttle override and regenerative braking. GM (from about 2012) and Stellantis read it in the engine module, Saab's 9-4X and 9-5 in the body module; its learned rest position (about 1 V) must be relearned after replacement. P057A is the general circuit or open-circuit fault. No manufacturer document available to us uses it; GM reports an open circuit as P057C or P057D depending on the line, type A with one trip, and sets the pedal position to 0 %. Brake detection then relies on the brake light switch.

causes.label: Connector at the sensor loose or corroded, pins pushed back
5 V reference, signal or ground line open
Sensor faulty internally
Engine or body module

P057B.title: Brake Pedal Position Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P057B.description: The brake pedal position sensor is an analogue 5 V sensor, usually Hall-type, giving the pedal position continuously instead of a switch – for brake lights, cruise control, stop-start, brake-throttle override and regenerative braking. GM (from about 2012) and Stellantis read it in the engine module, Saab's 9-4X and 9-5 in the body module; its learned rest position (about 1 V) must be relearned after replacement. P057B means the signal is valid but the pedal does not move as expected or the rest position is wrong. GM rates pedal movement once per ignition cycle while driving at 8 km/h or more without throttle (fail below 0.40, pass above 0.80), type A, one trip. If the module sees the pedal slightly pressed, it cuts power – GM and Stellantis bulletins name misinstalled or wrongly learned sensors.

causes.label: Sensor misinstalled or not learned after replacement
Contact fault on 5 V reference or signal causes wrong rest position learning
Sensor faulty internally (sticking)
Pedal mechanism stiff, floor mat

P057C.title: Brake Pedal Position Sensor A Circuit Low
P057C.description: The brake pedal position sensor A is an analogue 5 V sensor giving pedal travel continuously; its rest position (about 1 V) is learned. GM reads it in the engine module from about 2012 and uses it as an enabling condition of transmission monitors – hence type A, warning lamp after one trip, unlike cruise control codes. On any circuit fault GM sets the pedal to 0 %, so brake detection relies on the brake light switch. P057C means the signal is too low – a short to ground: GM below 5 in 20 of 32 samples. GM bulletins for 2012–14 pick-ups and SUVs name connector X205 under the left defroster duct, with cruise, brake light and stability messages and reduced power.

causes.label: Connector or terminals at sensor or inline connector (GM X205) loose, pushed back or corroded
Signal or 5 V reference shorted to ground
Sensor faulty internally
5 V reference pulled down by another sensor

symptoms: Check engine light on (GM, one trip)
Cruise control, brake light or stability functions restricted

P057D.title: Brake Pedal Position Sensor A Circuit High
P057D.description: The brake pedal position sensor A is an analogue 5 V sensor giving pedal travel continuously; its rest position (about 1 V) is learned. GM reads it in the engine module from about 2012 and uses it as an enabling condition of transmission monitors – hence type A, warning lamp after one trip, unlike cruise control codes. On any circuit fault GM sets the pedal to 0 %, so brake detection relies on the brake light switch. P057D means the signal is too high: GM above 95 in 20 of 32 samples and calls this explicitly an open circuit – an open signal or ground line is pulled up. A short to 5 V or battery acts the same. 'High' means signal, not a fully pressed pedal. GM bulletins name connector X205 on 2012–14 pick-ups.

causes.label: Ground or signal line open, connector X205 with poor contact
Sensor faulty
Signal shorted to voltage
Sensor misinstalled or misadjusted

symptoms: Check engine light on (GM, one trip)
Cruise unavailable, brake light or stability messages

P057E.title: Brake Pedal Position Sensor A Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P057E.description: The brake pedal position sensor A is an analogue 5 V sensor giving pedal travel continuously; its rest position (about 1 V) is learned. GM reads it in the engine module from about 2012 and uses it as an enabling condition of transmission monitors – hence type A, warning lamp after one trip, unlike cruise control codes. On any circuit fault GM sets the pedal to 0 %, so brake detection relies on the brake light switch. P057E means implausibly fast signal jumps within the valid range: GM sets it at jumps above 11 in 5 of 20 samples. Brief interruptions can also make GM's engine module learn a wrong rest position – it then sees the brake pressed and cuts power; GM names fretting at the 5 V reference or signal.

causes.label: Loose contact or fretting corrosion at sensor or inline connector
Broken or chafed wire near the pedal
Sensor worn internally (signal jumping)
Interference on the 5 V reference

P057F.title: Battery A State of Charge Performance
P057F.description: P057F means the state of charge of battery A behaves implausibly or leaves its expected range – a performance code, not a circuit fault. Its documented use is on plug-in hybrids of the VW group: the 2025 Porsche Panamera E-Hybrid and Bentley Continental and Flying Spur set it in the high-voltage battery controller, which requests the warning lamp; both causes were software. CARB requires hybrids to monitor battery and charging performance. A use for a 12 V battery sensor was not found; GM and Ford do not list P057F.

causes.label: Software of the battery controller (state of charge miscalculated)
State of charge not relearned after deep discharge, long standstill or disconnection
Battery ageing or cell imbalance
Faulty current or voltage measurement in the battery system

symptoms: Hybrid function restricted (less electric range or power)

P0580.title: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input A Circuit Low
P0580.description: Cruise control buttons form a resistor ladder on one or two signal lines, each button giving its own voltage window. FCA uses two lines with offset windows – signal 1 is input A, signal 2 input B – and both must report the same button; GM evaluates the ratio to the reference. Any fault locks out cruise control; CARB treats this as emission-neutral, and GM and Ford set these codes without warning lamp. P0580 means signal line A is too low: GM at a ratio of 0–0.185 for over 2 s (short to ground or, depending on wiring, open circuit); FCA treats signal 1 below 0.216 V as circuit low. Work at the steering wheel involves the driver airbag.

causes.label: Signal line shorted to ground (steering wheel wiring, clockspring)
Button block faulty (water, dirt)
Steering wheel or clockspring connector corroded or off
Evaluating module

symptoms: Cruise control cannot be switched on, indicator missing

P0581.title: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input A Circuit High
P0581.description: Cruise control buttons form a resistor ladder on one or two signal lines, each button giving its own voltage window. FCA uses two lines with offset windows – signal 1 is input A, signal 2 input B – and both must report the same button; GM evaluates the ratio to the reference. Any fault locks out cruise control; CARB treats this as emission-neutral, and GM and Ford set these codes without warning lamp. P0581 means signal line A is too high: GM at a ratio of 1.005–1.035 for over 2 s (short to power); FCA treats 4.706–5.0 V as circuit high. In FCA's recalls of the Jeep Wrangler JK (2007–2016), P0581 indicates a dusty clockspring, which is replaced. Ford lists it without warning lamp.

causes.label: Clockspring dirty or faulty
Signal line shorted to positive or ground open
Button block faulty
Corroded steering wheel connector

symptoms: Cruise control inoperative, on the Jeep JK possibly airbag warning

P0582.title: Cruise Control Vacuum Control Circuit/Open
P0582.description: Older engines without electronic throttle use a vacuum cruise servo on the throttle cable: a vacuum valve (closed when unpowered) opens the throttle with intake vacuum, a vent valve (open when unpowered) holds or releases it, and a dump valve fed through the brake switch vents it when braking. Where the engine module drives these valves, it checks each circuit and switches cruise off; CARB treats this as emission-neutral, usually without warning lamp. P0582 concerns the vacuum valve circuit: an open circuit, checked with ignition on and cruise control active. Without current the vacuum valve stays closed – the safe state.

causes.label: Connector at the servo loose or corroded
Vacuum valve coil in the servo open
Wire between servo and engine module open
Engine module driver

symptoms: Cruise control cannot be engaged or switches off
Cruise indicator goes out or flashes (depending on vehicle)
Usually no check engine light, code stored only

P0583.title: Cruise Control Vacuum Control Circuit Low
P0583.description: Older engines without electronic throttle use a vacuum cruise servo on the throttle cable: a vacuum valve (closed when unpowered) opens the throttle with intake vacuum, a vent valve (open when unpowered) holds or releases it, and a dump valve fed through the brake switch vents it when braking. Where the engine module drives these valves, it checks each circuit and switches cruise off; CARB treats this as emission-neutral, usually without warning lamp. P0583 means the voltage at the vacuum valve driver is too low – a control line shorted to ground or a shorted coil, so the valve could stay powered. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code.

causes.label: Vacuum control line shorted to ground (chafing)
Vacuum valve coil shorted

Engine module

symptoms: Cruise control cannot be engaged or switches off
Cruise indicator goes out or flashes (depending on vehicle)

causes.label: Vacuum control line shorted to positive

Clockspring faulty

P0589.title: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input B Circuit

P058A.title: Battery Monitor Module Performance
P058A.description: The battery monitor module (intelligent battery sensor) sits on the negative terminal of the 12 V battery: a shunt measures current, electronics also measure voltage and temperature and calculate state of charge, health and cranking ability, reporting over LIN. Energy management uses the data for alternator control, idle boost and stop-start release, which is why the engine module diagnoses it. GM sets P058A–P058F in its engine modules from 2016 as type B, warning lamp after two trips. P058A means the module reports an internal fault of its own over LIN. GM checks it every 250 ms above 9 V, without LIN faults and at outside temperatures of −20 to 50 °C. Battery data are then unreliable – stop-start is blocked and the alternator usually runs a fixed substitute voltage. Loss of communication is a separate U code.

causes.label: Battery sensor faulty internally
Poor supply or ground at the sensor (loose terminal, corroded connector)
Sensor not relearned after battery replacement or disconnection
Module or engine module software

P058B.title: Battery Monitor Module Current Monitoring Performance
P058B.description: The battery monitor module (intelligent battery sensor) sits on the negative terminal of the 12 V battery: a shunt measures current, electronics also measure voltage and temperature and calculate state of charge, health and cranking ability, reporting over LIN. Energy management uses the data for alternator control, idle boost and stop-start release, which is why the engine module diagnoses it. GM sets P058A–P058F in its engine modules from 2016 as type B, warning lamp after two trips. P058B concerns current measurement. In the sensor variant the module itself reports implausible current; GM's eAssist and stop-start engines compare it with their own reference and set it at 22 A difference in 160 of 200 samples. GM bulletins for the 2014–16 Malibu and Impala name a ground ring lying on the sensor's shunt or a loose terminal – current then bypasses the shunt.

causes.label: Ground ring touching the shunt or loose
Fretting corrosion in the sensor connector, loose ground splice
Battery sensor faulty
Retrofitted loads grounded directly at the negative post

symptoms: Wrong state of charge display or battery warning

P058C.title: Battery Monitor Module Temperature Monitoring Performance
P058C.description: The battery monitor module (intelligent battery sensor) sits on the negative terminal of the 12 V battery: a shunt measures current, electronics also measure voltage and temperature and calculate state of charge, health and cranking ability, reporting over LIN. GM compares two raw temperature values and sets it above 10 °C difference in 8 of 10 samples, also on values stored during sleep. P058D.title: Battery Monitor Module Voltage Monitoring Performance

Battery sensor faulty

P058E.title: Battery Monitor Module Temperature Too High
P058E.description: The battery monitor module (intelligent battery sensor) sits on the negative terminal of the 12 V battery: a shunt measures current, electronics also measure voltage and temperature and calculate state of charge, health and cranking ability, reporting over LIN. Energy management uses the data for alternator control, idle boost and stop-start release, which is why the engine module diagnoses it. GM sets P058A–P058F in its engine modules from 2016 as type B, warning lamp after two trips. P058E means the module reports a temperature above its plausible range: GM sets it above 120 °C in 4 of 5 samples. As the outside temperature must lie between −20 and 50 °C, such a value points to a sensor fault or strong local heating from contact resistance at the terminal or shunt. It suspends P058C.

causes.label: Battery sensor faulty internally
High contact resistance at terminal or ground ring heating the sensor
Missing battery heat shield after repair

P058F.title: Battery Monitor Module Temperature Too Low
P058F.description: The battery monitor module (intelligent battery sensor) sits on the negative terminal of the 12 V battery: a shunt measures current, electronics also measure voltage and temperature and calculate state of charge, health and cranking ability, reporting over LIN. Energy management uses the data for alternator control, idle boost and stop-start release, which is why the engine module diagnoses it. GM sets P058A–P058F in its engine modules from 2016 as type B, warning lamp after two trips. P058F means the module reports a temperature below its plausible range: GM sets it below −43 °C in 4 of 5 samples, but only with an outside temperature above −20 °C – so the value is physically implausible, usually an open sensing circuit or faulty sensor. It suspends P058C; the charge voltage then lacks correct temperature compensation.

causes.label: Battery sensor faulty internally (temperature element open)
Sensor software or initialisation after power loss
Supply or connector problem at the sensor

P0590.title: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input B Circuit Stuck
P0590.description: Cruise control buttons form a resistor ladder on one or two signal lines, each button giving its own voltage window. FCA uses two lines with offset windows – signal 1 is input A, signal 2 input B – and both must report the same button; GM evaluates the ratio to the reference. Any fault locks out cruise control; CARB treats this as emission-neutral, and GM and Ford set these codes without warning lamp. P0590 means input B reports a pressed button permanently – a button stuck or a voltage hanging in one window. No manufacturer document available to us uses P0590; FCA reports a stuck button with its own code P1593 or with P0585, and GM has no stuck code for input B. Counterpart of P0578 for input A.

causes.label: Button stuck mechanically (trim, dirt, spilled drink)
Short in the button block's resistor ladder
Moisture or corrosion in the switch
Module

symptoms: Cruise control cannot be engaged, button noticeably sticking

P0591.title: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input B Circuit Range/Performance
P0591.description: Cruise control buttons form a resistor ladder on one or two signal lines, each button giving its own voltage window. FCA uses two lines with offset windows – signal 1 is input A, signal 2 input B – and both must report the same button; GM evaluates the ratio to the reference. Any fault locks out cruise control; CARB treats this as emission-neutral, and GM and Ford set these codes without warning lamp. P0591 means signal 2 is outside its window while a button is pressed – for on/off FCA expects 0.900 V and sets the code above 0.980 V, active only while the button is held. Usual cause is oxidation at the six-pin steering wheel connector; in the Jeep Wrangler JK recalls it indicates a faulty clockspring. GM does not use P0591.

causes.label: Oxidised steering wheel connector at clockspring or column module
Clockspring dirty or faulty
Button block aged
Column module or PCM

symptoms: Cruise control working sporadically or not at all

P0592.title: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input B Circuit Low
P0592.description: Cruise control buttons form a resistor ladder on one or two signal lines, each button giving its own voltage window. Any fault locks out cruise control; CARB treats this as emission-neutral, and GM and Ford set these codes without warning lamp. causes.label: Line B shorted to ground (steering wheel, clockspring)
Button block faulty or damp
Corroded connector
Module

symptoms: Cruise control and distance or mode buttons inoperative

P0593.title: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input B Circuit High
P0593.description: Cruise control buttons form a resistor ladder on one or two signal lines, each button giving its own voltage window. FCA uses two lines with offset windows – signal 1 is input A, signal 2 input B – and both must report the same button; GM evaluates the ratio to the reference. causes.label: Clockspring dirty or faulty
Line B shorted to positive or ground open
Button block or connector
Module

symptoms: Cruise control inoperative, possibly airbag warning (Jeep JK)

P0594.title: Cruise Control Servo Control Circuit/Open
P0594.description: Older engines without electronic throttle use a vacuum cruise servo on the throttle cable: a vacuum valve (closed when unpowered) opens the throttle with intake vacuum, a vent valve (open when unpowered) holds or releases it, and a dump valve fed through the brake switch vents it when braking. Where the engine module drives these valves, it checks each circuit and switches cruise off; CARB treats this as emission-neutral, usually without warning lamp. P0594 concerns the servo control or supply circuit: an open circuit. Where the servo is fed through the cruise contact of the brake light switch, braking interrupts this supply on purpose, so the brake switch and its wiring are typical causes and brake lights may be affected too. No manufacturer document available to us describes P0594 in detail.

causes.label: Brake light switch (cruise contact) faulty or misadjusted
Supply line open or shorted to ground
Servo connector or servo
Engine module output

symptoms: Cruise control cannot be engaged or switches off
Usually no check engine light, code stored only
Possibly brake light problem as well (shared switch)

P0595.title: Cruise Control Servo Control Circuit Low
P0595.description: Older engines without electronic throttle use a vacuum cruise servo on the throttle cable: a vacuum valve (closed when unpowered) opens the throttle with intake vacuum, a vent valve (open when unpowered) holds or releases it, and a dump valve fed through the brake switch vents it when braking. Where the engine module drives these valves, it checks each circuit and switches cruise off; CARB treats this as emission-neutral, usually without warning lamp. P0595 means the voltage in the servo supply or control circuit is too low – a short to ground or a missing 12 V source. As this supply feeds both valves, it is checked before P0583 or P0587. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code.

causes.label: Supply line from brake switch to servo shorted to ground
Brake light switch (cruise contact)
Servo shorted internally
Engine module

symptoms: Cruise control cannot be engaged or switches off
Cruise indicator goes out or flashes (depending on vehicle)
Usually no check engine light, code stored only

causes.label: Servo supply line shorted to positive
Brake light switch sticking
Servo faulty
Engine module

symptoms: Cruise control cannot be engaged or switches off
Cruise indicator goes out or flashes (depending on vehicle)
Usually no check engine light, code stored only

P0597.title: Thermostat Heater Control Circuit/Open
P0597.description: A map-controlled thermostat is a wax thermostat with a built-in heating resistor (Valeo: about 10 Ω). Unheated it opens late, for hot running at part load; the engine module heats it by map under full load or towing so it opens earlier. CARB requires the thermostat to be monitored and the heater circuit counts as an output component. GM switches it to ground with a low-side driver and checks it every second, fault after 15 of 30 samples, type B; Hyundai/Kia/Genesis and VW/Audi use the codes as well. P0597 means the heater circuit is open – GM above 200 kΩ with the driver off. The thermostat then only works through its wax and opens late, so coolant runs hotter under load; Audi's 4.2 FSI also limits engine speed. Genesis (G80/G90 3.3 T, 3.8) replaced thermostats from an early production lot.

causes.label: Heating resistor in the thermostat open
Connector at the thermostat loose or corroded, coolant in the connector
Broken wire or missing supply (fuse, relay)
Engine module driver

symptoms: Check engine light on (after two trips)
Coolant temperature higher than usual under load
Audi/VW: coolant warning and engine speed limit possible

P0598.title: Thermostat Heater Control Circuit Low
P0598.description: A map-controlled thermostat is a wax thermostat with a built-in heating resistor (Valeo: about 10 Ω). With a low-side driver the heater then stays on permanently and the thermostat opens early, so the engine runs cool; Kia's Cadenza bulletins list it with P0128 and replace the thermostat.

causes.label: Internal short in thermostat or heater, coolant in the connector
Control line shorted to ground (chafing)
Engine module driver

symptoms: Engine slow to reach operating temperature (possibly P0128)
Weak cabin heating in winter, higher consumption

P0599.title: Thermostat Heater Control Circuit High
P0599.description: A map-controlled thermostat is a wax thermostat with a built-in heating resistor (Valeo: about 10 Ω). Coolant or corrosion in the connector
Engine module driver

symptoms: Coolant warning and engine speed limit (Audi)

P059A.title: Active Grille Air Shutter A Position Sensor Circuit
P059A.description: The active grille shutter (A = upper or only shutter, B = second) closes louvres to cut drag and speed warm-up and opens them for cooling; CARB names it as an off-cycle CO2 technology and requires its components to be monitored. A separately evaluated position sensor, as these titles assume, is described in Ford patents (Hall sensor on the motor or sensor on the linkage). No manufacturer document available to us uses this code: today the sensor sits inside the LIN actuator, whose faults appear as P059F/P05AE, P05A1/P05B0 or U0284/U0285. Without position feedback the shutter is usually driven open. P059A (shutter A) is the general circuit fault of the position sensor – signal missing or wire open, without low/high split.

causes.label: Position sensor in the actuator faulty (replaced as a unit)
Actuator connector corroded or with water ingress
Wire open in the front bumper harness (accident, rodents)
Engine module or reference voltage

symptoms: Shutter stays in one position (usually open) or does not react
Slightly higher consumption, longer warm-up in winter

P059B.title: Active Grille Air Shutter A Position Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P059B.description: The active grille shutter (A = upper or only shutter, B = second) closes louvres to cut drag and speed warm-up and opens them for cooling; CARB names it as an off-cycle CO2 technology and requires its components to be monitored.
