P059F.title: Active Grille Air Shutter A Performance/Stuck Off
P059F.description: The active grille shutter (A = upper or only shutter, B = second) closes louvres to cut drag and speed warm-up and opens them for cooling; CARB names it as an off-cycle CO2 technology and requires its components to be monitored. P059F compares commanded and reached position. GM checks it in two stages – detection, then five clearing attempts – type B, two trips; Ford's 3.0 L diesel at over 6° deviation in operation or 20° when learning fully open. 'Stuck off' means stuck closed at Toyota (failure type 73) and Nissan; GM and Ford use P059F for any deviation. Typical are ice, snow, debris or a bent bracket – a closed shutter can make the engine run hot in traffic.

causes.label: Louvres blocked by ice, snow or debris
Bent bracket or bumper part blocking the louvres
Actuator, gear or shaft faulty (shutter stays closed)
Louvres unhooked or rubbing on horn or intake duct
Calibration or software

symptoms: Shutter not opening: engine temperature rises in traffic, fan running often
Often after frost, gone after thawing

P05A0.title: Active Grille Air Shutter A Stuck On
P05A0.description: The active grille shutter (A = upper or only shutter, B = second) closes louvres to cut drag and speed warm-up and opens them for cooling; CARB names it as an off-cycle CO2 technology and requires its components to be monitored. P05A0 is the counterpart of P059F: at Toyota failure type 72 means the actuator stuck open, 74 slipping; VW, Audi and Mazda use it for sticking in general (Mazda after up to three clearing cycles). GM and Ford do not use it. An open shutter does not harm the engine but costs drag and warm-up time. Several fixes were software updates (Mazda, Audi Q7, VW Jetta); Audi's 2022–24 A3 limits top speed to 100 mph with a shutter fault.

causes.label: Debris or ice holding the louvres open or blocking them
Engine module or actuator software setting the code too early
Actuator slipping or gear worn
Louvres or linkage broken

symptoms: Grille shutter warning (Toyota, Audi), speed limit (Audi)

P05A1.title: Active Grille Air Shutter A Position Sensor Minimum/Maximum Stop Performance
P05A1.description: The active grille shutter (A = upper or only shutter, B = second) closes louvres to cut drag and speed warm-up and opens them for cooling; CARB names it as an off-cycle CO2 technology and requires its components to be monitored. P05A1 checks whether the shutter reaches its end stops (fully closed and open), which serve as reference for the position sensor in the self-learning run. Ford's 3.0 L diesel sets it at deviations above 40° when learning closed, 20° when learning open or 20° in operation, after 10 s; a Ford patent detects the stop by stall current and requests recalibration. GM, Toyota and VW do not use it.

causes.label: Louvres not reaching the stop (ice, debris, bent louvres or bracket)
Actuator or gear weak, linkage worn
Misassembled or not learned after replacement
Position sensor in the actuator faulty

symptoms: Check engine light (depending on the maker)
Shutter not opening or closing fully
Possibly higher engine temperature or consumption

P05A2.title: Active Grille Air Shutter A Control Circuit/Open
P05A2.description: An active grille shutter closes louvres in the grille to cut drag and speed warm-up and opens them for cooling; CARB names it as an off-cycle CO2 technology and treats the actuator as an output component. Smart actuators (Ford 3.0 L diesel, Toyota) check their own coil and supply and report over LIN; simpler ones (VW 1.8 T) have their own supply and a control line from the engine module. GM uses none of P05A2–P05A8. A fault usually only costs fuel and warm-up time. P05A2 concerns the control or motor coil circuit. Ford's 3.0 L diesel reports an open and a shorted coil under it, checked by the actuator at the start and 500 ms after each movement, fault after 10 s. Toyota uses P05A2 as a collective code with a failure-type byte for short to ground, short to positive, open or stuck.

causes.label: Actuator motor coil open or shorted
Connector corroded or damaged (front bumper, splash water, stone chips)
Front harness damaged (accident, rodents)
Engine module

P05A3.title: Active Grille Air Shutter A Control Circuit Range/Performance
P05A3.description: An active grille shutter closes louvres in the grille to cut drag and speed warm-up and opens them for cooling; CARB names it as an off-cycle CO2 technology and treats the actuator as an output component. Actuator with faulty software or defective
Control line or connector with contact resistance
Insufficient supply or ground at the actuator

P05A4.title: Active Grille Air Shutter A Control Circuit High

Without position feedback the shutter is usually driven open. P05AB (shutter B) means the signal is above its valid range – usually an open ground or signal line pulled up, or a short to 5 V or battery; high refers to the signal, not the louvre position.

causes.label: Signal shorted to supply or ground line open
Connector corroded or with water ingress
Position sensor in the actuator faulty internally
Engine module

symptoms: Shutter stays in one position (usually open) or does not react
Slightly higher consumption, longer warm-up in winter

Without position feedback the shutter is usually driven open. P05AC (shutter B) means the signal is below its valid range – a signal shorted to ground or an open 5 V reference or signal line.

causes.label: Signal shorted to ground or 5 V reference open
Bumper harness chafed or damaged (accident, parking knock)
Position sensor in the actuator faulty
Engine module or reference regulator

symptoms: Shutter stays in one position (usually open) or does not react
Slightly higher consumption, longer warm-up in winter

P05AD.title: Active Grille Air Shutter B Position Sensor Circuit Intermittent

Broken wire in the front bumper harness
Position sensor in the actuator (wear, electronics)
Moisture after washing or rain

Slightly higher consumption, longer warm-up in winter

P05AE.title: Active Grille Air Shutter B Performance/Stuck Off
P05AE.description: Shutter B is the second active grille shutter – at GM, Ford and Stellantis the lower one in the bumper. Shutters cut drag and speed warm-up when closed and open for cooling; CARB names them as an off-cycle CO2 technology and treats the actuator as an output component. Smart actuators report over LIN (loss of communication: U0285); a fault usually costs fuel and warm-up time, a closed shutter can make the engine run hot under load. P05AE compares commanded and reached position. GM checks in two stages with five clearing attempts, type B, two trips; Ford's 3.0 L diesel at over 6° deviation in operation or 20° when learning open; Stellantis uses it too. GM, Ford and Stellantis do not distinguish the direction. GM bulletins for 2019–21 Silverado and Sierra name stones or ice at the bottom of the lower shutter, often with U0285.

causes.label: Debris, stones, ice or snow in the lower shutter
Louvres unhooked or broken, rubbing on bracket or horn, impact damage
Water or corrosion in connector or harness
Actuator B faulty

symptoms: Check engine light on (GM after two trips)
Lower shutter not moving or incompletely, possibly U0285 or P059F
Higher coolant temperature under load or slightly higher consumption

P05AF.title: Active Grille Air Shutter B Stuck On

Shutters cut drag and speed warm-up when closed and open for cooling; CARB names them as an off-cycle CO2 technology and treats the actuator as an output component. Smart actuators report over LIN (loss of communication: U0285); a fault usually costs fuel and warm-up time, a closed shutter can make the engine run hot under load. P05AF is the counterpart of P05AE: shutter B stuck open. Documented only in the VW group – Audi's 2022–24 A3, S3 and RS3 describe it internally as 'grille shutter 2 sticks open' and limit top speed to 100 mph on a shutter fault; the warning was sometimes set by engine module software. GM, Ford and Stellantis report everything under P05AE.

causes.label: Engine module software (sporadic false message)
Louvres blocked open (ice, dirt, debris, accident damage)
Actuator or shutter unit B faulty
Poor supply or ground at the actuator

symptoms: Grille shutter warning, top speed limited (Audi)

P05B0.title: Active Grille Air Shutter B Position Sensor Minimum/Maximum Stop Performance
P05B0.description: Shutter B is the second active grille shutter – at GM, Ford and Stellantis the lower one in the bumper. Shutters cut drag and speed warm-up when closed and open for cooling; CARB names them as an off-cycle CO2 technology and treats the actuator as an output component. Smart actuators report over LIN (loss of communication: U0285); a fault usually costs fuel and warm-up time, a closed shutter can make the engine run hot under load. P05B0 checks whether shutter B reaches its end stops, the reference for position feedback in the self-learning run. Ford's 3.0 L diesel sets it at over 40° when learning closed, 20° when learning open or 20° in operation, after 10 s. Ford's petrol F-150 of 2024–25 uses it too: a Ford service message says to fit a new lower shutter before further diagnosis.

causes.label: Lower shutter or actuator faulty
Louvres blocked or bent (ice, stone chips, impact)
Shutter misassembled or connector off after repair
Connector or harness corroded

P05B1.title: Active Grille Air Shutter B Control Circuit/Open

Shutters cut drag and speed warm-up when closed and open for cooling; CARB names them as an off-cycle CO2 technology and treats the actuator as an output component. Smart actuators report over LIN (loss of communication: U0285); a fault usually costs fuel and warm-up time, a closed shutter can make the engine run hot under load. P05B1 concerns the control or motor coil circuit of actuator B. Ford's 3.0 L diesel reports an open and a shorted coil under it, checked at the start and 500 ms after each movement, fault after 10 s. Toyota's RAV4 Hybrid uses P05B1 as a collective code with failure types for short to positive, short to ground or open, and no signal. GM does not use it.

causes.label: Actuator B coil open or shorted
Connector corroded or damaged (lower bumper, splash water)
Front harness damaged (impact, chafing, rodents)
Module

P05B2.title: Active Grille Air Shutter B Control Circuit Range/Performance
P05B2.description: Shutter B is the second active grille shutter – at GM, Ford and Stellantis the lower one in the bumper. Shutters cut drag and speed warm-up when closed and open for cooling; CARB names them as an off-cycle CO2 technology and treats the actuator as an output component. Smart actuators report over LIN (loss of communication: U0285); a fault usually costs fuel and warm-up time, a closed shutter can make the engine run hot under load. P05B2 means the control signal or actuator feedback is outside its expected range. Documented only in the VW group: Audi's 2022–24 A3 describes it internally as 'grille shutter 2 communication lost', with top speed limited to 100 mph; causes included engine module software. VW's check order: remove blockage, measure supply and ground at the four-pin connector, actuator test, replace the shutter.

causes.label: Engine module software (sporadic)
Actuator or shutter B faulty
Control line or connector with contact resistance or corrosion
Mechanical blockage (ice, dirt, accident damage)

symptoms: Grille shutter warning, top speed limited (Audi)

P05B3.title: Active Grille Air Shutter B Control Circuit High
P05B3.description: Shutter B is the second active grille shutter – at GM, Ford and Stellantis the lower one in the bumper. Shutters cut drag and speed warm-up when closed and open for cooling; CARB names them as an off-cycle CO2 technology and treats the actuator as an output component. Smart actuators report over LIN (loss of communication: U0285); a fault usually costs fuel and warm-up time, a closed shutter can make the engine run hot under load. P05B3 means the control circuit voltage of actuator B is too high – a control line shorted to positive or a driver unable to pull it to ground. In this family high comes before low. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code, like its shutter A counterpart. Ford reports coil shorts under P05B1, Toyota as P05B1 with failure type 12.

causes.label: Actuator B faulty internally
Control line shorted to positive (front harness)
Water or corrosion in the connector
Module driver

P05B4.title: Active Grille Air Shutter B Control Circuit Low
P05B4.description: Shutter B is the second active grille shutter – at GM, Ford and Stellantis the lower one in the bumper. Shutters cut drag and speed warm-up when closed and open for cooling; CARB names them as an off-cycle CO2 technology and treats the actuator as an output component. Smart actuators report over LIN (loss of communication: U0285); a fault usually costs fuel and warm-up time, a closed shutter can make the engine run hot under load. P05B4 means the control circuit voltage of actuator B is too low – typically the control line shorted to ground; the actuator cannot be driven. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code, like its shutter A counterpart. Toyota reports a short to ground or open circuit as P05B1 with failure type 14.

causes.label: Actuator B faulty internally
Control line shorted to ground (chafing, impact)
Corroded connector
Module

P05B5.title: Active Grille Air Shutter B Supply Voltage Circuit/Open
P05B5.description: Shutter B is the second active grille shutter – at GM, Ford and Stellantis the lower one in the bumper. Shutters cut drag and speed warm-up when closed and open for cooling; CARB names them as an off-cycle CO2 technology and treats the actuator as an output component. Smart actuators report over LIN (loss of communication: U0285); a fault usually costs fuel and warm-up time, a closed shutter can make the engine run hot under load. P05B5 means the battery supply of actuator B via fuse or relay is missing or open; without it there is no movement, and smart actuators drop off the LIN bus. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code, like its shutter A counterpart. VW's check measures supply and ground at the actuator connector; GM feeds its actuators via a relay but uses other codes.

causes.label: Fuse blown or relay faulty
Broken wire or connector off in the lower front end
Ground connection open
Actuator faulty internally

P05B6.title: Active Grille Air Shutter B Supply Voltage Circuit Low
P05B6.description: Shutter B is the second active grille shutter – at GM, Ford and Stellantis the lower one in the bumper. Shutters cut drag and speed warm-up when closed and open for cooling; CARB names them as an off-cycle CO2 technology and treats the actuator as an output component. Smart actuators report over LIN (loss of communication: U0285); a fault usually costs fuel and warm-up time, a closed shutter can make the engine run hot under load. P05B6 means the supply of actuator B is present but too low. Ford's 3.0 L diesel sets it at once when the actuator measures its internal supply below 6.9 V while system voltage is 9–16.26 V, from 5 s after start – pointing to a voltage drop in feed or ground or an internal fault.

causes.label: Contact resistance in connector, wire or ground (corrosion)
Actuator faulty internally (measuring wrong)
Weak battery or charging system

symptoms: Possibly further voltage codes or U0285

P05B7.title: Active Grille Air Shutter B Supply Voltage Circuit High
P05B7.description: Shutter B is the second active grille shutter – at GM, Ford and Stellantis the lower one in the bumper. Shutters cut drag and speed warm-up when closed and open for cooling; CARB names them as an off-cycle CO2 technology and treats the actuator as an output component. Smart actuators report over LIN (loss of communication: U0285); a fault usually costs fuel and warm-up time, a closed shutter can make the engine run hot under load. P05B7 means the supply of actuator B is too high – system overvoltage or a short to another circuit; the actuator switches off for protection. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code, like its shutter A counterpart. Ford monitors only undervoltage (P05B6). With P0563 check alternator and regulator first.

causes.label: System overvoltage (regulator, jump start)
Actuator faulty internally (measuring wrong)
Supply shorted to another circuit

symptoms: Possibly P0563 or further voltage codes

P05B8.title: Restraint Deployment Signal Circuit/Open
P05B8.description: After a crash the restraint control module tells the engine module that airbags or belt tensioners have fired; the engine module then cuts the fuel pump (Ford: until the ignition is cycled) and possibly the engine. Depending on the maker the message travels over CAN and/or a dedicated wire with a defined level or voltage drop. P05B8 means the wired signal line is open – no valid rest level arrives. After a real crash the fuel cut-off may then not be triggered via this line. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; it is a safety function, not an emission-relevant monitor, so usually without warning lamp.

causes.label: Signal wire or connector between restraint and engine module open (e.g. after accident repair or seat removal)
Corroded or spread pin at either module
Replacement module not configured
Restraint module output stage

symptoms: Possibly message that fuel cut-off is unavailable

P05B9.title: Restraint Deployment Signal Circuit Low
P05B9.description: After a crash the restraint control module tells the engine module that airbags or belt tensioners have fired; the engine module then cuts the fuel pump (Ford: until the ignition is cycled) and possibly the engine. Depending on the maker the message travels over CAN and/or a dedicated wire with a defined level or voltage drop. P05B9 means the signal line stays below its valid rest level – usually a short to ground. Where deployment is coded as a voltage drop, a short to ground could resemble a deployment, so makers cross-check with the CAN message. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; it is a safety function, not an emission-relevant monitor, so usually without warning lamp.

causes.label: Signal wire chafed to ground (harness under seat or console)
Water in the connector (footwell)
Restraint module output stuck low
Engine module input

P05BA.title: Restraint Deployment Signal Circuit High
P05BA.description: After a crash the restraint control module tells the engine module that airbags or belt tensioners have fired; the engine module then cuts the fuel pump (Ford: until the ignition is cycled) and possibly the engine. Depending on the maker the message travels over CAN and/or a dedicated wire with a defined level or voltage drop. P05BA means the signal line stays above its valid range – a short to battery or ignition voltage, or with a pull-up in the engine module an open circuit. The fuel cut-off may then not work via this line. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; it is a safety function, not an emission-relevant monitor, so usually without warning lamp.

causes.label: Signal wire shorted to battery or ignition voltage
Open circuit with pull-up in the engine module
Retrofitted loads or harness damage after accident repair
Restraint or engine module

P05BB.title: Restraints Deployed
P05BB.description: After a crash the restraint control module tells the engine module that airbags or belt tensioners have fired; the engine module then cuts the fuel pump (Ford: until the ignition is cycled) and possibly the engine. Depending on the maker the message travels over CAN and/or a dedicated wire with a defined level or voltage drop. P05BB is an event code: the engine module received a valid deployment message. The fuel pump is cut, the engine may stop, doors are unlocked by other modules, and Ford's engine module freezes recorded data. After a crash the restraint module must be replaced; a used module with a stored crash can also cause it. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; it is a safety function, not an emission-relevant monitor, so usually without warning lamp.

causes.label: Real accident with airbag or belt tensioner deployment
Deployment after a hard underbody hit (e.g. off-road)
False message from wiring or module fault
Used restraint module with stored crash fitted

symptoms: Engine stops or will not start (fuel cut-off)

P05BC.title: Stop-Start Mode Switch Circuit/Open
P05BC.description: The stop-start off switch lets the driver disable automatic engine stop for the current drive. It is read directly or via another module over CAN – on Stellantis' 2025 Ram 1500 it sits in the electronic shifter module. CARB names a stop-start diagnosis as its example of an emission-neutral diagnosis, so no warning lamp is required; stop-start is usually just disabled. P05BC means the switch circuit is open. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; Stellantis documents only its sibling P05BD. Typical are a connector left off after console or dashboard work or an open switch contact.

causes.label: Open circuit in switch, connector or wire
Switch faulty (contact or resistor ladder)
Connector not refitted after console or dashboard work
Reading module or software

symptoms: Stop-start cannot be switched off or stays disabled

P05BD.title: Stop-Start Mode Switch Circuit Range/Performance
P05BD.description: The stop-start off switch lets the driver disable automatic engine stop for the current drive. It is read directly or via another module over CAN – on Stellantis' 2025 Ram 1500 it sits in the electronic shifter module. The first fix is an engine module software update, not parts; Stellantis warns not to replace the ignition switch for it.

causes.label: Engine module software (Stellantis: fixed by update)
Sticking or bouncing stop-start button in the shifter module
Very frequent pressing by occupants
Shifter module faulty

symptoms: Stop-start button not reacting or status jumping
Code stored in the engine module

P05BE.title: Stop-Start Mode Switch Circuit Low
P05BE.description: The stop-start off switch lets the driver disable automatic engine stop for the current drive. It is read directly or via another module over CAN – on Stellantis' 2025 Ram 1500 it sits in the electronic shifter module. CARB names a stop-start diagnosis as its example of an emission-neutral diagnosis, so no warning lamp is required; stop-start is usually just disabled. P05BE means the switch circuit voltage is too low – a signal or reference shorted to ground, or with a resistor ladder a voltage below the lowest valid step. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code.

causes.label: Signal line shorted to ground

5 V reference of the reading module pulled down
Module input

P05BF.title: Stop-Start Mode Switch Circuit High

Switch faulty
Module input

symptoms: Stop-start cannot be switched off or stays disabled

P05C0.title: Active Grille Air Shutter Module A Over Temperature
P05C0.description: Shutters cut drag and speed warm-up when closed and open for cooling; CARB names them as an off-cycle CO2 technology and treats the actuator as an output component. Smart actuators report over LIN (loss of communication: U0285); a fault usually costs fuel and warm-up time, a closed shutter can make the engine run hot under load. P05C0 means the smart actuator of shutter A (the upper one) measures its control chip above 140 °C for 10 s and switches its driver off for protection. Documented only for Ford's 3.0 L diesel. causes.label: Actuator faulty internally (driver overheating)
Shutter stiff or blocked (ice, dirt, bent louvres) causing continuous current
High heat load at the mounting point (radiator, traffic, towing)

causes.label: Actuator faulty internally (driver overheating)
Shutter stiff or blocked (ice, dirt, bent louvres) causing continuous current
High heat load at the mounting point (radiator, traffic, towing)

P05C2.title: Engine Coolant Pressure Sensor Circuit
P05C2.description: An engine coolant pressure sensor (5 V reference, ratiometric signal) measures pressure in the cooling circuit; in a sealed circuit pressure rises with temperature, so deviations reveal leaks or a loose cap – described in Navistar and GE patents for commercial and rail engines. No manufacturer document available to us uses P05C2–P05C6 for passenger cars; CARB requires input components to be checked for circuit faults, range and plausibility. P05C2 is the general circuit fault – signal, reference or ground open, or no communication from a digital sensor. Leak detection is then unavailable.

causes.label: Connector corroded or loose, wire open (coolant and heat zone)
Sensor faulty internally
5 V reference disturbed
Module or software

symptoms: Check engine light or warning (depending on the maker)
Coolant pressure or leak warning unavailable

P05C3.title: Engine Coolant Pressure Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P05C3.description: An engine coolant pressure sensor (5 V reference, ratiometric signal) measures pressure in the cooling circuit; in a sealed circuit pressure rises with temperature, so deviations reveal leaks or a loose cap – described in Navistar and GE patents for commercial and rail engines. Combustion gas in the coolant (head gasket)

Coolant loss or smell with a real leak

Sensor faulty
Connector corroded

P05C7.title: Economy Mode Switch Circuit/Open
P05C7.description: The economy mode switch selects a fuel-saving mode (flatter pedal map, earlier upshifts, sometimes reduced A/C). It is usually a resistor ladder with 5 V reference read by the engine module; CARB names a driver-selectable eco mode as an off-cycle technology whose use must be counted. GM reports the same switch with its own codes P159F/P15A0, type B with warning lamp after two trips; P05C7–P05CA appear in no manufacturer document available to us. P05C7 means the switch circuit is open; eco mode cannot be selected and the vehicle runs in normal mode.

causes.label: Wire or connector to the switch open
Switch faulty (resistor ladder or contact)
Connector loose after console work
Module input

P05C8.title: Economy Mode Switch Circuit Range/Performance
P05C8.description: The economy mode switch selects a fuel-saving mode (flatter pedal map, earlier upshifts, sometimes reduced A/C). It is usually a resistor ladder with 5 V reference read by the engine module; CARB names a driver-selectable eco mode as an off-cycle technology whose use must be counted. GM reports the same switch with its own codes P159F/P15A0, type B with warning lamp after two trips; P05C7–P05CA appear in no manufacturer document available to us. P05C8 means the signal is in range but implausible – between valid ladder steps or permanently pressed; GM accepts a press only for 0.094–1.5 s.

causes.label: Switch stuck (permanently pressed)
Contact resistance or corrosion shifting the voltage step
Software
Module input

symptoms: Eco mode switching unintentionally or not at all

P05C9.title: Economy Mode Switch Circuit Low
P05C9.description: The economy mode switch selects a fuel-saving mode (flatter pedal map, earlier upshifts, sometimes reduced A/C). It is usually a resistor ladder with 5 V reference read by the engine module; CARB names a driver-selectable eco mode as an off-cycle technology whose use must be counted. GM reports the same switch with its own codes P159F/P15A0, type B with warning lamp after two trips; P05C7–P05CA appear in no manufacturer document available to us. P05C9 means the switch circuit voltage is too low – signal or reference shorted to ground; GM's equivalent P159F detects the same fault on the same part.

causes.label: Signal or reference line shorted to ground
Switch shorted internally
Shared 5 V reference loaded by another sensor
Module

P05CA.title: Economy Mode Switch Circuit High
P05CA.description: The economy mode switch selects a fuel-saving mode (flatter pedal map, earlier upshifts, sometimes reduced A/C). It is usually a resistor ladder with 5 V reference read by the engine module; CARB names a driver-selectable eco mode as an off-cycle technology whose use must be counted. Switch faulty
Module

P05CB.title: Vehicle Hardware Incompatibility
P05CB.description: P05CB means a control module has found that installed hardware does not match the vehicle configuration – a wrong variant or part number, an unprogrammed replacement module, or messages from another vehicle type. No admissible manufacturer document available to us uses P05CB. CARB requires a calibration verification number showing that emission software is valid for the vehicle, but no hardware code. Ford reports configuration and compatibility faults under P0610 (vehicle options) and P0630 (VIN not programmed or incompatible) instead. Typical cause is a replaced module or battery that was not matched or programmed.

causes.label: Replacement module or battery with wrong part number or for another variant
Module not programmed or configured after replacement
Faulty module software level

P05CC.title: Cold Start A Camshaft Position Timing Performance Bank 1
P05CC.description: During catalyst heating after a cold start the engine module commands a specific cam phaser position for more residual gas and exhaust heat; CARB requires this to be monitored under codes separate from the normal cam codes. Engine module software

P05D0.title: Driver Mode Select Switch A Circuit
P05D0.description: The driver mode select switch (tour, sport, eco, snow, off-road, towing) changes engine and transmission maps such as shift points, pedal map and cylinder deactivation, so CARB requires it to be monitored as an input. GM reads switch A as an eight-position resistor ladder in the body module and sets P05D1–P05D3 in its 2025 tables when a condition is present for 4 s within 5 s, type B with warning lamp after two trips. A fault blocks mode selection; the vehicle stays in its basic mode. P05D0 is the general circuit fault of switch A without low/high assignment. No manufacturer document available to us uses it; GM covers the same switch with the more specific P05D1–P05D3.

P05D8.title: PCV Regulator Valve Control Circuit/Open
P05D8.description: Some turbo engines have an electrically controlled crankcase ventilation valve that decides when and how much blow-by gas is drawn into the intake (part-load versus full-load path). The engine module monitors its driver output; CARB requires output components to be checked for circuit faults and the PCV system to be monitored. Nissan's 1.5 L KR15DDT (Rogue 2024–25) sets P05D8/P05D9 with the warning lamp from a severed harness at the valve; Mercedes M270/M274 have such a valve but report it under P052E. P05D8 means the valve control circuit is open – wire, coil or connector; the driver sees no load.

P05DB.title: Brake Pedal Position Sensor B Circuit/Open
P05DB.description: Brake-by-wire and hybrid systems use a dual-channel pedal travel sensor; channel B runs opposite to A at Toyota (3.6–4.4 V at rest, falling when pressed), so a common fault of both channels shows up. It feeds brake assist and regenerative blending; CARB requires inputs used by other diagnoses to be monitored. A channel fault blocks the A/B correlation P05E0 and usually limits brake assist or regeneration. P05DB is the general circuit or open-circuit fault of channel B. Toyota's electronically controlled brake (RAV4 Hybrid 2024–25) reports channel B faults under it; while it is stored, the A/B correlation does not run.

causes.label: Harness or connector at the pedal sensor (open, contact fault)
Pedal sensor assembly faulty
Retrofitted wiring near the pedal (e.g. trailer brake controller)
Brake or hybrid module

symptoms: Regeneration or brake assist reduced, pedal feel changed

P05E0.title: Brake Pedal Position Sensor A/B Correlation

P05E1.title: A/C Refrigerant Pressure Sensor A Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P05E1.description: The refrigerant pressure sensor (three wires, 5 V reference, signal rising with pressure) tells the engine module the A/C pressure; it uses it to switch the radiator fan, to block the compressor at too high or too low pressure and to pre-control idle load. CARB requires such inputs to be checked for circuit faults and plausibility, but they need not light the lamp if they do not affect emissions. 'Intermittent/Erratic' means the signal jumps implausibly fast or briefly leaves its valid range without staying low or high long enough for those codes. Sensor A is usually the high-pressure sensor; GM and Saab report it only as P0532/P0533 (circuit low/high, at GM below 3 % or above 98 % of 5 V) and P0531, so no manufacturer document available to us uses P05E1 itself. Typically the compressor is blocked and the fan runs. GM rates sensor A faults without the lamp, the Saab 9-4X with it.

causes.label: Loose contact or corrosion at the sensor connector (front end, splash water)
Chafed or broken wire (5 V, signal, ground)
Sensor faulty internally (signal jumps)
Shared 5 V reference disturbed by another sensor

symptoms: A/C intermittently not cooling (compressor switched off)
Radiator fan runs unnecessarily or irregularly
Idle speed fluctuates when A/C engages
Warning lamp depending on the maker

P05E3.title: Park Brake Sensor/Switch Circuit
P05E3.description: The engine module reads the park brake status, directly or via another module, because strategies depend on it: a parked diesel filter regeneration only runs with the park brake applied (Navistar), idle shutdown and PTO logic use it, and Ford delays an automatic restart while the electric park brake moves. CARB requires such inputs to be monitored. The only documented user of this code family is Volvo Trucks: since OBD 2021 a second park brake sensor (about 0.5 V applied, 3.5 V released) must agree with the old switch; the engine module reports the fault. No passenger car maker uses it verifiably. P05E3 is the general circuit fault – usually an open circuit or undefined state. Low and high signals are P05E4 and P05E5.

P05E8.title: Engine Oil Bypass Valve Control Circuit/Open
P05E8.description: The engine oil bypass valve is an electrically switched solenoid that, according to patents (Hyundai/Kia), routes oil around the oil cooler when cold so the engine warms up faster with less friction, and through the cooler once the oil is hot. It is not the purely mechanical oil filter bypass. CARB requires output components to be checked for circuit faults. No manufacturer document available to us uses P05E8–P05EA, and no vehicle with these codes was found. If the circuit fails, the valve stays in its unpowered position – depending on design oil may run too hot under load or warm up slowly. P05E8 means the control circuit is open: the driver sees missing voltage or high resistance.

causes.label: Connector at the valve loose, corroded or spread
Valve solenoid coil open
Broken wire in the harness
Output driver in the module faulty

symptoms: Check engine light (if rated as emission related)
Oil too hot under load or slow warm-up, depending on rest position

P05E9.title: Engine Oil Bypass Valve Control Circuit Low
P05E9.description: The engine oil bypass valve is an electrically switched solenoid that, according to patents (Hyundai/Kia), routes oil around the oil cooler when cold so the engine warms up faster with less friction, and through the cooler once the oil is hot. It is not the purely mechanical oil filter bypass. CARB requires output components to be checked for circuit faults. No manufacturer document available to us uses P05E8–P05EA, and no vehicle with these codes was found. If the circuit fails, the valve stays in its unpowered position – depending on design oil may run too hot under load or warm up slowly. P05E9 means the control circuit voltage is too low – control wire shorted to ground or shorted coil turns.

causes.label: Control wire chafing against ground (block, bracket)
Shorted turns in the valve
Moisture or oil in the connector
Output driver in the module

symptoms: Check engine light (if rated as emission related)
Oil too hot under load or slow warm-up, depending on rest position

P05EA.title: Engine Oil Bypass Valve Control Circuit High
P05EA.description: The engine oil bypass valve is an electrically switched solenoid that, according to patents (Hyundai/Kia), routes oil around the oil cooler when cold so the engine warms up faster with less friction, and through the cooler once the oil is hot. It is not the purely mechanical oil filter bypass. CARB requires output components to be checked for circuit faults. No manufacturer document available to us uses P05E8–P05EA, and no vehicle with these codes was found. If the circuit fails, the valve stays in its unpowered position – depending on design oil may run too hot under load or warm up slowly. P05EA means the control circuit voltage is too high – a short to battery or overcurrent at the driver, so the valve cannot be operated.

causes.label: Control wire touching battery or ignition voltage
Valve coil shorted (overcurrent at the driver)
Connector or wiring damage
Control module

symptoms: Check engine light (if rated as emission related)
Oil too hot under load or slow warm-up, depending on rest position

P05EB.title: Cold Start SCR NOx Catalyst Inlet Temperature Too Low
P05EB.description: After a cold start a diesel heats its exhaust actively – retarded and post injection, intake or exhaust throttling, higher idle, EGR cooler bypass – so the SCR catalyst quickly reaches the temperature at which urea dosing can start (around 180–200 °C). P05EB sets when the measured temperature at the SCR inlet stays below the expected or modelled value within a set time after the start: the heating strategy is not working. CARB requires this 'catalyst warm-up' monitor for light-duty diesels from model year 2026 (20 %) to 2028 (100 %); GM 2025 and Ford 2023 tables do not contain the code yet. Volvo Trucks used it on 2016–17 heavy-duty engines and advised a software check instead of replacing parts. The lamp comes on; no power limitation from this code alone is known.

causes.label: Engine module software or calibration (false trigger)
Exhaust temperature sensor before the SCR reads low or slow
Heating measure not effective: throttle, EGR cooler bypass or turbo vanes sticking
Post or retarded injection not effective (injectors)
Exhaust leak before the sensor or extremely cold conditions

symptoms: Higher NOx emissions after cold start (not noticeable)

P05EC.title: Cold Start Injection Timing Performance
P05EC.description: To heat the exhaust after a cold start, a diesel shifts its start of injection, usually later, plus post injections. CARB requires faults of such elements during the cold start strategy to be reported under codes separate from normal operation – hence P05EC. GM's 2025 diesels compare the start of injection requested by the application software with the timing actually scheduled for the injector drivers, during cold start only; a deviation beyond ±4 or ±5 in 88 of 176 or 8 of 16 samples sets the code and the lamp in the first trip. Ford's 2023 diesel instead checks whether the cold start operating mode is really activated when requested (10 s). Mechanical injector timing faults in normal operation are P01CB ff and P020A ff; the petrol counterpart for ignition timing is P050B.

causes.label: Engine module software or internal fault (request and execution differ)
Cold start mode blocked by other faults (coolant or fuel temperature, rail pressure)
Injector driver or injector circuit
Weak battery during cold start

symptoms: Possibly more white smoke or rougher running after cold start

P05ED.title: Reductant Heater Control Module Supply Voltage
P05ED.description: Some diesels use a separate control module or power stage for the DEF heaters in tank, pump and lines; without heating, frozen fluid cannot thaw in winter and dosing stays blocked. P05ED reports that this module's supply voltage is outside its allowed window – a blown main fuse, an open feed or ground, or system voltage too low or too high. Chrysler (FCA) lists this code among those that trigger the DEF inducement: a 'Service DEF System' warning, a countdown after 50 miles and no restart after 150 miles (P241D). Thresholds are not published; GM's L5P monitors the comparable heater supply under its own codes and flags a drop of more than 3 V below battery voltage while heating is requested. Start with fuse, feed, ground and battery or charging system.

causes.label: Main fuse or feed wire to the heater module faulty, connector corroded (splash zone)
Poor module ground
Weak battery or charging fault (system voltage too low or too high)
Heater control module faulty internally

symptoms: DEF/AdBlue warning, possibly countdown to no-restart
In cold weather: DEF frozen, dosing blocked, further heater codes

P05EE.title: Reductant Pump Supply Voltage Circuit/Open
P05EE.description: The electric supply pump in the diesel exhaust fluid (DEF, AdBlue) tank module builds the dosing pressure for the SCR catalyst. Its supply voltage is monitored separately from the pump control circuit (P208A ff); CARB requires SCR components and their outputs to be checked for circuit faults and function. P05EE means the supply circuit is open: when the supply is switched on, no voltage or current reaches the pump branch. Ford's comparable check flags a pump controller voltage below 6 V. Chrysler (FCA) lists this code among those that trigger the DEF inducement: a 'Service DEF System' warning, a countdown after 50 miles and no restart after 150 miles (P241D). Without supply the pump cannot build pressure, dosing stops and NOx rises; pressure or SCR efficiency codes may follow.

causes.label: Connector at the pump or tank module corroded or loose
Open wire in the harness to the tank
Fuse or relay of the pump supply faulty
Pump or tank module open internally

symptoms: DEF/AdBlue warning, possibly countdown to no-restart
Follow-up codes for low DEF pressure or SCR efficiency

P05EF.title: Reductant Pump Supply Voltage Circuit Low
P05EF.description: The electric supply pump in the diesel exhaust fluid (DEF, AdBlue) tank module builds the dosing pressure for the SCR catalyst. Its supply voltage is monitored separately from the pump control circuit (P208A ff); CARB requires SCR components and their outputs to be checked for circuit faults and function. P05EF means the supply voltage is too low or the supply line is shorted to ground. GM's 6.6 L diesel monitors the same high-side driver under P1043 (short to ground with driver on, about 0.5 Ω, 3 s, first trip); Ford flags its pump controller voltage below 8.5 V. No manufacturer document available to us uses this exact code; GM and Ford monitor the same function under their own codes. Without supply the pump cannot build pressure, dosing stops and NOx rises; pressure or SCR efficiency codes may follow.

causes.label: Supply line shorted to ground (chafed against the frame)
High contact resistance or corrosion in the connector
Pump shorted internally or stiff (high current)
Weak battery or charging system

symptoms: DEF/AdBlue warning, possibly countdown to no-restart
Follow-up codes for low DEF pressure or SCR efficiency

P05F0.title: Reductant Pump Supply Voltage Circuit High
P05F0.description: The electric supply pump in the diesel exhaust fluid (DEF, AdBlue) tank module builds the dosing pressure for the SCR catalyst. Its supply voltage is monitored separately from the pump control circuit (P208A ff); CARB requires SCR components and their outputs to be checked for circuit faults and function. P05F0 means the supply voltage is too high, or voltage is present although the supply is switched off (short to battery). GM's 6.6 L diesel monitors this as P1044 (two trips); Ford flags pump voltage above 16 V or controller voltage above 19 V. No manufacturer document available to us uses this exact code; GM and Ford monitor the same function under their own codes. Without supply the pump cannot build pressure, dosing stops and NOx rises; pressure or SCR efficiency codes may follow.

causes.label: Pump supply shorted to battery positive in the harness
Overvoltage from the charging system or a jump start
Moisture or corrosion causing leakage current in the connector
Relay or driver does not switch off

symptoms: DEF/AdBlue warning, possibly countdown to no-restart
Follow-up codes for low DEF pressure or SCR efficiency

P05F1.title: Reductant Pump Supply Voltage Circuit Stuck On
P05F1.description: The electric supply pump in the diesel exhaust fluid (DEF, AdBlue) tank module builds the dosing pressure for the SCR catalyst. Its supply voltage is monitored separately from the pump control circuit (P208A ff); CARB requires SCR components and their outputs to be checked for circuit faults and function. P05F1 means the pump supply stays on although the module switches it off – typically detected after the switch-off command, e.g. during after-run, when the feedback still shows voltage. A welded relay or a shorted semiconductor switch is the usual reason. Chrysler (FCA) lists this code among those that trigger the DEF inducement: a 'Service DEF System' warning, a countdown after 50 miles and no restart after 150 miles (P241D). Without supply the pump cannot build pressure, dosing stops and NOx rises; pressure or SCR efficiency codes may follow.

causes.label: Pump supply relay stuck (welded contacts)
Semiconductor driver shorted
External voltage or short to positive in the harness
Software or calibration fault

symptoms: DEF/AdBlue warning, possibly countdown to no-restart
Follow-up codes for low DEF pressure or SCR efficiency
Pump keeps running after switch-off, battery drains

P05F2.title: Reductant Pump Supply Voltage Circuit Stuck Off
P05F2.description: The electric supply pump in the diesel exhaust fluid (DEF, AdBlue) tank module builds the dosing pressure for the SCR catalyst. Its supply voltage is monitored separately from the pump control circuit (P208A ff); CARB requires SCR components and their outputs to be checked for circuit faults and function. P05F2 means the pump supply cannot be switched on: after the switch-on command no voltage or feedback appears at the pump branch, so no pressure builds up. Chrysler (FCA) lists this code among those that trigger the DEF inducement: a 'Service DEF System' warning, a countdown after 50 miles and no restart after 150 miles (P241D). Without supply the pump cannot build pressure, dosing stops and NOx rises; pressure or SCR efficiency codes may follow.

causes.label: Relay does not pull in or fuse blown
Open in the relay control or load circuit
Output driver in the engine module faulty
Electronics of the tank module faulty (no feedback)

symptoms: DEF/AdBlue warning, possibly countdown to no-restart
Follow-up codes for low DEF pressure or SCR efficiency

P05F3.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Power Relay Control Circuit/Open
P05F3.description: A power relay, switched by the engine module through an output driver, feeds aftertreatment consumers such as the DEF pump, tank and line heaters and possibly NOx sensors or the SCR module. CARB requires such outputs to be checked for circuit faults and function. P05F3 means the driver detects an open relay control (coil) circuit. Ford's comparable relay check flags 'driver on but 0 V' or a heater relay current below 0.2 A, within 5 s. Chrysler (FCA) lists this code among those that trigger the DEF inducement: a 'Service DEF System' warning, a countdown after 50 miles and no restart after 150 miles (P241D). If the relay fails, heaters, pump and SCR control drop out and dosing stops.

causes.label: Relay missing, coil open or not seated properly
Corroded connector or relay socket
Harness damaged
Output driver in the engine module faulty

symptoms: DEF/AdBlue warning, possibly countdown to no-restart
Follow-up codes for heaters, pump or NOx sensor supply

P05F4.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Power Relay Control Circuit Low
P05F4.description: A power relay, switched by the engine module through an output driver, feeds aftertreatment consumers such as the DEF pump, tank and line heaters and possibly NOx sensors or the SCR module. CARB requires such outputs to be checked for circuit faults and function. P05F4 means the relay control circuit is shorted to ground or its voltage is too low. Ford's comparable heater relay check flags a current above 6 A with the driver on, within 5 s. No manufacturer document available to us uses this exact code; GM and Ford monitor the same function under their own codes. If the relay fails, heaters, pump and SCR control drop out and dosing stops.

causes.label: Control line shorted to ground
Corroded connector or relay socket
Harness damaged
Output driver in the engine module faulty

symptoms: DEF/AdBlue warning, possibly countdown to no-restart
Follow-up codes for heaters, pump or NOx sensor supply

P05F5.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Power Relay Control Circuit High
P05F5.description: A power relay, switched by the engine module through an output driver, feeds aftertreatment consumers such as the DEF pump, tank and line heaters and possibly NOx sensors or the SCR module. CARB requires such outputs to be checked for circuit faults and function. P05F5 means the relay control circuit is shorted to battery positive: the voltage stays high although the driver is off. Ford's comparable check flags more than 5 V with the driver off, within 5 s. No manufacturer document available to us uses this exact code; GM and Ford monitor the same function under their own codes. If the relay fails, heaters, pump and SCR control drop out and dosing stops.

causes.label: Control line shorted to battery positive
Corroded connector or relay socket
Harness damaged
Output driver in the engine module faulty

symptoms: DEF/AdBlue warning, possibly countdown to no-restart
Follow-up codes for heaters, pump or NOx sensor supply

P05F6.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Power Relay Control Circuit Stuck On
P05F6.description: A power relay, switched by the engine module through an output driver, feeds aftertreatment consumers such as the DEF pump, tank and line heaters and possibly NOx sensors or the SCR module. CARB requires such outputs to be checked for circuit faults and function. P05F6 is a function check on the load side: the relay stays closed although it is switched off, so the consumers keep their supply, e.g. during after-run. A patent by Delphi describes this kind of check via the voltage at the heater node. No manufacturer document available to us uses this exact code; GM and Ford monitor the same function under their own codes. If the relay fails, heaters, pump and SCR control drop out and dosing stops.

causes.label: Relay contacts welded or sticking
External voltage on the load side (short to positive)
Corroded connector or relay socket
Output driver in the engine module faulty

symptoms: DEF/AdBlue warning, possibly countdown to no-restart
Follow-up codes for heaters, pump or NOx sensor supply
Consumers stay powered after switch-off, battery drains

P05F7.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Power Relay Control Circuit Stuck Off
P05F7.description: A power relay, switched by the engine module through an output driver, feeds aftertreatment consumers such as the DEF pump, tank and line heaters and possibly NOx sensors or the SCR module. CARB requires such outputs to be checked for circuit faults and function. P05F7 is the opposite function check: the relay does not close although it is commanded on, so the load side stays without voltage. No manufacturer document available to us uses this exact code; GM and Ford monitor the same function under their own codes. If the relay fails, heaters, pump and SCR control drop out and dosing stops.

causes.label: Relay contacts burnt or coil faulty, relay does not close
Fuse on the load side blown
Corroded connector or relay socket
Output driver in the engine module faulty

symptoms: DEF/AdBlue warning, possibly countdown to no-restart
Follow-up codes for heaters, pump or NOx sensor supply

P05F8.title: Reductant Heater Control Module Performance
P05F8.description: P05F8 is the function check of the DEF heater control module: its feedback does not match the command – heating current or power, temperature rise, or an internal module fault. The code is documented for Chrysler's 3.0 L EcoDiesel in the 2014 Ram 1500 and Jeep Grand Cherokee: several bulletins list it together with the heater codes P20BA, P20BE and P20C2, and the fix in each case was only reprogramming the engine module – a diagnostic that was too sensitive rather than a hardware defect. It is not on Chrysler's inducement list. Ford checks the same function under heater plausibility codes. Thresholds for P05F8 are not published. If it returns after a software update, check the heater elements in tank and lines and the module supply (P05ED).

causes.label: Engine module software (Chrysler 3.0 L 2014: diagnostic revised by reflash)
Heater control module faulty internally
Heater element or line in tank or hose with abnormal current
Unstable module supply or ground

symptoms: DEF warning in cold weather, possible heater codes P20BA/P20BE/P20C2

P05F9.title: Stop-Start Status Signal Circuit
P05F9.description: A discrete stop-start status line tells the engine module (or another module) whether stop-start is active, inhibited or has just stopped the engine. On most current cars this status travels over CAN instead, so a hard-wired line and these codes are rare; no manufacturer document available to us uses P05F9–P05FB. CARB names stop-start as its example of an 'emissions neutral' reaction: a module that simply disables stop-start when a fault appears may report it without the check engine light, which is what Ford does for its stop-start codes. P05F9 is the general circuit fault or open line. The typical reaction is that stop-start is disabled; the driver-operated stop-start switch has its own codes.

causes.label: Open status line or connector problem
Sending module without supply or faulty
Wrong software or variant coding (stop-start set without hardware)

symptoms: Stop-start indicator or message in the cluster
Check engine light only with some makers

P05FA.title: Stop-Start Status Signal Circuit Low
P05FA.description: A discrete stop-start status line tells the engine module (or another module) whether stop-start is active, inhibited or has just stopped the engine. On most current cars this status travels over CAN instead, so a hard-wired line and these codes are rare; no manufacturer document available to us uses P05F9–P05FB. CARB names stop-start as its example of an 'emissions neutral' reaction: a module that simply disables stop-start when a fault appears may report it without the check engine light, which is what Ford does for its stop-start codes. P05FA means the status line stays below its lower limit – a short to ground or a missing pull-up supply. Stop-start is then disabled.

causes.label: Status line shorted to ground
Sending module pulls the line to ground permanently (faulty output)
Moisture or corrosion in the connector

symptoms: Stop-start indicator or message in the cluster

P05FB.title: Stop-Start Status Signal Circuit High
P05FB.description: A discrete stop-start status line tells the engine module (or another module) whether stop-start is active, inhibited or has just stopped the engine. On most current cars this status travels over CAN instead, so a hard-wired line and these codes are rare; no manufacturer document available to us uses P05F9–P05FB. CARB names stop-start as its example of an 'emissions neutral' reaction: a module that simply disables stop-start when a fault appears may report it without the check engine light, which is what Ford does for its stop-start codes. P05FB means the status line stays above its upper limit – an open line pulled up or a short to voltage. Stop-start is then disabled.

causes.label: Open status line or connector off
Sending module faulty or without ground
Short to voltage

symptoms: Stop-start indicator or message in the cluster

P05FC.title: Cold Start Fuel Pressure Performance Bank 2
P05FC.description: During a cold start, direct injection petrol engines usually raise rail pressure for finer atomisation with multiple injections while the catalyst heats up. P05FC monitors whether the actual rail pressure of bank 2 stays within the target window during this phase – only engines with separate rails and pressure sensors per bank (V or boxer engines with two high-pressure circuits) can set it. CARB lists fuel pressure as a cold start component that must respond measurably beyond what would happen without the strategy. No manufacturer document available to us uses P05FC; Ford checks the single-rail counterpart P053F and flags a fault when the share of cold start time inside the pressure window is 0.70 or less, and Kia replaced the engine module of the 2018 Stinger 2.0T for P053F with stumbling during warm-up. GM uses P2C1E–P2C20 instead.

causes.label: High-pressure pump or volume control valve of bank 2 weak or sticking
Low supply pressure (low-pressure pump, filter)
Rail pressure sensor of bank 2 inaccurate
Engine module software
Leaking injector or pressure relief on bank 2

symptoms: Stumbling, hesitation or rough idle during warm-up

P05FD.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Control A Temperature Too High
P05FD.description: Electric variable-geometry turbo actuators use a DC motor with gearing, driven by an H-bridge in the engine module or in the actuator itself. Constant high load – sooted or stiff vanes, running against a stop, an internal motor short – drives up current and temperature. GM's 2025 diesels set P05FD when the H-bridge driver exceeds 170 °C in 240 of 300 samples (about 3 s) and light the lamp in the first trip. The driver then shuts off for protection, the actuator stops or returns to its rest position, and boost control is limited – underboost or overboost and reduced power can follow. GM Europe's earlier 2.0 diesels reported the same protection under P0046. Circuit faults of the actuator are P0045–P0048, the position sensor P2563 ff.

causes.label: Vane mechanism sooted or stiff, actuator works constantly against resistance
Electric actuator faulty internally (shorted turns, bearing)
High ambient heat at the actuator (missing heat shield, exhaust leak)
Engine module or driver

symptoms: Loss of power or limp mode

P05FE.title: Active Grille Air Shutter C Performance/Stuck Off
P05FE.description: Active grille shutters close the air inlet when little cooling is needed, to reduce drag and speed up warm-up. P05FE is the performance check of a third shutter C – target and actual position do not match, as P059F does for shutter A and P05AE for shutter B. Only vehicles with three separately driven shutters could set it, and no manufacturer was found that uses a shutter C: GM and Ford use only A (upper) and B (lower). This description therefore follows A and B: control is suspended and the shutter stays where it is or opens; if it sticks closed, cooling air is missing under load. GM and Ford light the lamp for A and B after two trips. Ice and debris are frequent causes, and GM fixed false A/B codes in snow by software on the 2025 Equinox. Stuck on is P2C73.

causes.label: Debris or ice blocking the louvres
Louvres unhooked or broken (impact)
Shutter C actuator faulty
Connector, wiring or supply corroded
Software false trigger in frost

symptoms: Check engine light (depending on the maker)
Higher coolant temperature under load or slower warm-up

P05FF.title: Brake Pressure Sensor/Brake Pedal Position Sensor Correlation
P05FF.description: Stop-start decides when to stop and restart the engine from the brake: Ford stops it when the pedal switch is on and master cylinder pressure is high enough, and restarts when pressure falls below a filtered reference. P05FF means brake pressure (from the sensor in the ABS unit, sent over the network) and brake pedal position do not agree – for example pedal pressed without pressure build-up, or pressure without pedal. Ford's 2020–23 petrol vehicles check this continuously in the section 'Brake Diagnostics for Stop-Start Dependability' and set the code within 1 s, without the check engine light; stop-start is blocked so the engine is not stopped or started unexpectedly. Ford gives no threshold for the deviation. GM monitors the pedal travel sensor under P057x instead. Brake switch disagreement is P0504.

causes.label: Brake pedal position sensor or switch misadjusted or faulty
Master cylinder pressure sensor in the ABS unit faulty
Network communication or software between ABS module and engine module
Air in the brake system or hydraulic fault (long pedal travel without pressure)

symptoms: No check engine light at Ford, possibly wrench or service warning
Possible related codes P0504 or brake pressure codes

P0600.title: Serial Communication Link
P0600.description: P0600 means a serial data link that the module relies on has failed. At Ford it is the internal link between the main processor and the monitoring processor ('quizzer') of the electronic throttle safety concept: if data cannot be exchanged or check bytes are invalid, the code sets within about a second (diesel: 5 s), usually with the check engine and wrench lamps and a throttle failure mode such as an RPM limit. Subaru (also sold as Saab 9-2X) uses it for the dedicated serial line between engine and transmission module. GM does not use P0600. Lost CAN messages from a named module are reported separately as U0100 and following. Before replacing anything: check battery, grounds and supply, look for a software bulletin, reprogram with a stable power supply, and replace the module only if the code returns.

causes.label: Internal module fault in the processor-to-processor link
Faulty module software (update available)
Open or short in a dedicated serial line between engine and transmission module (e.g. Subaru)
Low voltage, voltage dips or a poor ground or supply at the module
Fault in the transmission module at the other end of the line

symptoms: Check engine light, at Ford also the wrench lamp
Reduced power or RPM limit (throttle failure mode)
Harsh shifts or transmission limp mode where the line links engine and gearbox
Other monitors such as the catalyst monitor do not run

P0601.title: Internal Control Module Memory Checksum Error
P0601.description: The module continuously calculates a checksum over its program and calibration memory (flash) and compares it with the stored value; on newer units the flash error correction also reports bit errors it cannot repair. A mismatch means the stored software is corrupted. GM sets P0601 in the engine module after one failed pass (or five once the first pass is complete) and turns on the lamp in the first trip; in body modules after two trips. Ford reports the same check as P0605, while GM, VW and Mazda use P0601. Typical causes are an interrupted reflash and manufacturer software errors – VW (2.0 TFSI) and Mazda (MX-5 2013) fixed it by reprogramming. The code alone does not say which module set it – the scan tool shows whether it is the engine, transmission, brake or body module.

causes.label: Interrupted or faulty reprogramming
Faulty module software (update available)
Defective flash memory in the module
Low voltage, voltage dips or a poor ground or supply at the module

symptoms: Possibly no start or limp mode if the software is badly damaged
Transmission limp mode if the transmission module is affected

P0602.title: Control Module Programming Error
P0602.description: P0602 reports that the module is not, or not completely, programmed for this vehicle. GM checks at power-up and then every second whether a service replacement module still carries no calibration, and sets the code in the first trip; in brake modules a missing calibration set or a sensor ID that does not match also counts. Ford uses P0602 when the checksum of the vehicle identification block (tyre size, axle ratio, VIN) is wrong. Typical triggers are a new module that was never programmed, a reflash interrupted by a voltage dip or lost connection, or wrong software. Depending on the maker the engine may not start, run with reduced power or only show the lamp; GM Europe engines show a service lamp instead of the check engine light. The fix is almost always reprogramming with a stable power supply; replace the module only if the code returns.

causes.label: Module replaced and not (completely) programmed
Programming interrupted by a voltage dip or lost connection
Wrong or incompatible software, calibration or configuration block
Internal memory defect in the module

symptoms: Check engine light or service lamp
Engine may not start or runs in limp mode
Appears right after a module replacement or software update

P0603.title: Internal Control Module Keep Alive Memory (KAM) Error
P0603.description: Keep alive memory holds learned values – fuel trim, idle and shift adaptation, readiness status – while the engine is off, as long as the module has constant battery power; CARB defines it as memory that is lost when the battery or fuse is disconnected. The module stores a checksum of this memory at shutdown and compares it at the next start (Ford, GM Europe); GM calls the check 'long term memory reset', and the Ford diesel watches the supply of its engine-off timer chip (below 0.25 V). By far the most common trigger is outside the module: a disconnected, flat or replaced battery or an interrupted constant feed – Nissan bulletins name exactly this and ask for at least 11 V before clearing. Learned values then start from default and the readiness monitors are reset. Whether the lamp comes on depends on the maker.

causes.label: Battery disconnected, deeply discharged or replaced
Interrupted constant power feed to the module (fuse, wire, corrosion)
Main relay drops out too early, memory not saved completely at shutdown
Internal memory defect (EEPROM/NVM)

symptoms: Check engine light on (depending on the maker)
Rough idle or changed shifting until values are relearned

P0604.title: Internal Control Module Random Access Memory (RAM) Error
P0604.description: P0604 means the module's working memory (RAM) failed its self-test: a value written to a cell does not read back correctly, a built-in hardware test fails, error correction reports faults, or protected memory is written without permission. GM's engine module scans the whole RAM within 30 s of start-up and then keeps checking in the background, setting the code after repeated failures with the lamp in the first trip; Ford tests RAM during initialisation, the GM gateway with error correction at start (two trips). Unlike most memory codes, P0604 is used the same way by GM, Ford, Chrysler and Saab. Consequences depend on the module: a transmission module goes into limp mode with maximum line pressure and a fixed gear, an engine module may reduce power. The code alone does not say which module set it – the scan tool shows whether it is the engine, transmission, brake or body module.

causes.label: Internal hardware defect of the module (RAM)
Low voltage, voltage dips or a poor ground or supply at the module
Faulty module software (update available)
Moisture or corrosion in the module or at its connector

symptoms: Limp mode or transmission limp mode
Several module codes at the same time

P0605.title: Internal Control Module Read Only Memory (ROM) Error
P0605.description: P0605 reports an error in the module's program memory (ROM, today flash), found by a checksum or error-correction check at start-up or in the background. Ford is the main user: its engine and transmission modules compare a ROM checksum and set P0605 with the check engine light; the diesel transmission module tests once per trip at start. GM's engine module does not use P0605 and reports the same fault as P0601; the GM gateway (2025) uses it for uncorrectable ROM bit errors with two-trip logic, and GM Europe's 1.6 L engine even assigns it to processor faults of the throttle control. Which of P0601 and P0605 appears is therefore the manufacturer's choice. The usual repair is reprogramming, which restores the memory contents; replace the module only if the code returns.

causes.label: Program memory corrupted by an interrupted reflash
Internal flash or ROM defect
Faulty module software (update available)
Low voltage, voltage dips or a poor ground or supply at the module

symptoms: Transmission limp mode if the transmission module is affected

P0606.title: Control Module Processor
P0606.description: P0606 means the module doubts the integrity of its own processor. Checks include a question-and-answer game between main and monitoring processor (GM: new seed via SPI within 450 ms; Ford: 'quizzer' level 3), arithmetic unit and register tests, stack overflow, the order in which safety-critical software runs, and the internal voltage supply (Ford diesel: 5 V rail outside 4.7–5.3 V). Because it belongs to the electronic throttle safety concept, the module usually reacts with a failure mode – reduced power, RPM limit or throttle default position – and the lamp in the first trip. Many cases are software issues fixed by reprogramming (Chrysler 3.6 L 2014, VW Routan, GM brake module 2024), so check bulletins before replacing hardware. The code alone does not say which module set it – the scan tool shows whether it is the engine, transmission, brake or body module.

causes.label: Faulty module software (update available)
Low voltage, voltage dips or a poor ground or supply at the module
Internal hardware defect (processor, voltage regulator, output stage chip)
Short on a 5 V sensor reference loading the internal supply

symptoms: Check engine light, at Ford also the wrench lamp
Limp mode with reduced power or RPM limit
Often together with voltage codes P0562/P0563

P0607.title: Control Module Performance
P0607.description: P0607 is the general 'module not working correctly' code, used when no specific memory or processor part is named. Ford sets it for wrong instruction execution or too many processor resets in engine and transmission modules; the Ford diesel after five communication errors with its monitoring chip within 20 s (a complete loss of that link is P0600). GM introduced it in the engine module only recently: the 2025 tables evaluate the results of built-in self-tests and error-correction counters, with the lamp in the first trip. Resets can cause brief stumbling or stalling, and some systems switch to limp mode. Software updates fixed it on the Alfa Romeo Giulia 2.9 V6 and Ram 6.7 Cummins, so check bulletins first. The code alone does not say which module set it – the scan tool shows whether it is the engine, transmission, brake or body module.

causes.label: Faulty module software (update available)
Internal module defect (processor, clock, monitoring chip)
Low voltage, voltage dips or a poor ground or supply at the module
Electrical interference, e.g. from a faulty alternator or ignition

P0608.title: Control Module VSS Output A
P0608.description: Many engine or powertrain modules turn the raw wheel or output-shaft speed into a cleaned-up vehicle speed signal and pass it on through their own driver – a square-wave signal whose frequency rises with speed – to the instrument cluster, cruise control, radio or steering. P0608 concerns output A: the module compares the commanded driver state with the actual line state and reports a short to ground or voltage, an open circuit or an internal driver fault, as CARB requires for output components. Output A is the first such output, usually the speedometer feed. If the speed sensor itself fails, P0500–P0503 set instead. No manufacturer table available to us gives thresholds; GM lists the code in older vehicles. On modern cars speed is shared over CAN, so the code mainly affects older vehicles with a hard-wired speedometer signal.

causes.label: Short or open in the output line A to the receiving module
Corroded or spread connector pins at the module or receiver
Faulty receiving module pulling the line to ground
Internal driver fault in the module

P0609.title: Control Module VSS Output B
P0609.description: Many engine or powertrain modules turn the raw wheel or output-shaft speed into a cleaned-up vehicle speed signal and pass it on through their own driver – a square-wave signal whose frequency rises with speed – to the instrument cluster, cruise control, radio or steering. P0609 concerns output B: the module compares the commanded driver state with the actual line state and reports a short to ground or voltage, an open circuit or an internal driver fault, as CARB requires for output components. Output B is a second output; which device hangs on it (cruise module, radio, body builder interface) depends on the wiring diagram. If the speed sensor itself fails, P0500–P0503 set instead. No manufacturer table available to us gives thresholds; GM lists the code in older vehicles. On modern cars speed is shared over CAN, so the code mainly affects older vehicles with a hard-wired speedometer signal.

causes.label: Short or open in the output line B to the receiving module
Corroded or spread connector pins at the module or receiver
Faulty receiving module pulling the line to ground
Internal driver fault in the module

symptoms: Speed-dependent function of the receiver on output B disturbed
Cruise control or add-on device without speed signal

P060A.title: Internal Control Module Monitoring Processor Performance
P060A.description: Electronic throttle systems use three levels: level 1 runs the engine, level 2 recalculates key values independently on the same processor, and level 3 is a separate monitoring processor that quizzes the main one and can shut down the throttle outputs. P060A means this monitoring processor (level 3) or its cooperation with the main processor is faulty: the question-and-answer game fails, an operating system call ends with an unrecoverable error, or the self-test of the monitoring module fails (Ford diesel: 5 s). Ford sets it with the check engine and wrench lamps since generation 3 throttle systems (older generation 2 without the check engine light); GM Europe's 1.6 L turbo rates it type C with a service lamp and reduced power. GM North America does not use P060A. Nissan (Rogue 2021) and Ford (Explorer 2.3 2025) fixed it by reprogramming – often there are no driving symptoms at all.

causes.label: Faulty module software (update available)
Unstable supply voltage or poor ground at the module (weak battery, voltage spikes)
Internal hardware defect (monitoring processor, memory)
Moisture or corrosion in the module or connector

symptoms: Check engine light, at Ford also the wrench lamp

P060B.title: Internal Control Module A/D Processing Performance
P060B.description: The analog-to-digital converter turns every analog sensor voltage into a number, so a faulty converter can falsify many values at once. The module checks it by timing its start-up calibration (GM 6.6 L diesel: 0.30 s or longer is a fault), by converting fixed internal reference voltages (about 4.73–4.83 V must be read), by grounding a test channel that must then read near 0 V (Ford diesel: over 249 mV is a fault) and by comparing with a second converter. GM sets it in the first trip, Ford with the check engine and wrench lamps as a level 3 check; the module usually enters limp mode. Ford fixed an F-150 2.7 L case (with misfire codes) by reprogramming. GM also uses P060B in the brake module – then ABS warnings appear and the engine module is not the culprit. The old wording 'A and D' simply spelled out 'A/D'.

causes.label: Faulty module software (update available)
Unstable supply voltage or poor ground at the module (weak battery, voltage spikes)
Internal defect of the converter or its chip
Shorted sensor input pulling the converter reference

symptoms: Check engine light, at Ford also the wrench lamp
Several sensor or misfire codes at the same time
ABS/ESC warning if the brake module set the code

P060C.title: Internal Control Module Main Processor Performance
P060C.description: P060C reports a fault in the main processor that actually runs the engine, found either by the monitoring processor (Ford 'quizzer', level 3) or by duplicate storage and recalculation (GM). Typical findings are corrupted RAM or ROM data, arithmetic unit errors, memory address violations, a wrong program sequence or internal supply or temperature out of range (Ford diesel: internal voltage outside 1.3–3.3 V, 5 s). GM's 2025 petrol table flags a torque compensation outside ±52.9 Nm for 475 ms and sets the code in the first trip. Reactions range from reduced power to engine shutdown. Software is the most common cause: GM (2022 full-size trucks and SUVs), VW (Tiguan 2021, with cruise control faults), Nissan and Mercedes (transmission module, E-Class hybrid) fixed it by reprogramming.

causes.label: Faulty module software (update available)
Unstable supply voltage or poor ground at the module (weak battery, voltage spikes)
Internal hardware defect (memory, processor)
Overheating or moisture in the module

symptoms: Driver assistance such as adaptive cruise unavailable
Transmission limp mode if the transmission module is affected

P060D.title: Internal Control Module Accelerator Pedal Position Performance
P060D.description: The accelerator pedal has two sensor tracks. With P060D the module's own cross-check of the pedal value fails: two processors (GM: main and 'motor' processor) calculate pedal position independently and must agree, and an active test briefly pulls one track to ground – the other must not follow, otherwise the tracks are shorted together. Thresholds: GM 2005 difference over 0.142 V or track 2 over 2.05 V during the test; GM 2006 over 5 %; Ford diesel compares track 1 against twice track 2 (half slope), fault above 547 or 1055 mV for 5 s. GM sets it in the first trip, Ford since 2020 with the check engine and wrench lamps (2012 only the wrench lamp). Unlike P2138, where the two pedal tracks disagree outside the module, P060D is the internal plausibility check.

causes.label: Short between the two pedal sensor signal lines or moisture in the pedal connector
Faulty pedal sensor (tracks drifting)
Faulty module software (update available)
Internal module fault (converter, processor)

symptoms: Reduced power, engine barely responds to the pedal
Check engine light or wrench lamp

P060E.title: Internal Control Module Throttle Position Performance
P060E.description: P060E is the throttle counterpart of P060D. The throttle body also has two position sensor tracks, and the module checks whether it can still detect a short between them: during an active test one track is influenced briefly, and the second processor (GM 'motor processor') confirms that the test actually ran. GM 2005 sets the code when track 2 exceeds 1.75 V during the test or no test activity is seen for 500 ms, GM 2006 at 2.05 V or 498 ms, each after two counts of about 155 ms, with the lamp in the first trip; GM Europe rates it type C with reduced power. Ford does not use P060E. The throttle opening is limited or set to its default position. External disagreement between the two tracks is P2135; circuit faults of single tracks are P0120–P0123 and P0220–P0223.

causes.label: Short between the throttle sensor signal lines or moisture in the throttle connector
Faulty throttle body (sensor)
Internal module fault (test circuit, second processor)
Faulty module software (update available)

symptoms: Check engine light (GM) or service lamp (GM Europe)

P060F.title: Internal Control Module Coolant Temperature Performance
