GM's 6.6 L Duramax LB7/LLY (2004–05) sets it below 4.7 V for 2 s; GM Europe's 2.0 L turbo after 1 s or 10 s cumulative, each with the lamp in the first trip. Newer GM engines report it under the collective code P0651, and Ford does not use P0652. All sensors on the circuit then read low, with matching codes, limp mode and possibly starting problems.

causes.label: 5 V reference wire shorted to ground (chafing)
Sensor on the reference circuit shorted internally
Moisture or corrosion in a connector
Module

P0653.title: Sensor Reference Voltage B Circuit High
P0653.description: The engine module feeds several sensors (camshaft, pedal, pressure sensors) from separate regulated 5 V reference circuits; 'B' is circuit 2. A short at one sensor pulls the whole reference down, so every sensor on it reports at once – unplug them one by one until the reference returns to 4.8–5.2 V. P0653 means reference B is too high – often a signal wire of a connected sensor has chafed onto a 12 V line, less often the reference wire itself. GM's Duramax LB7/LLY (2004–05) sets it above 5.2 V for 2 s; GM Europe's 2.0 L turbo after 1 s or 10 s cumulative, each with the lamp in the first trip. Newer GM engines report it as P0651, Ford does not use it. Sensor readings then become implausibly high and limp mode follows.

causes.label: Reference or sensor signal wire shorted to a 12 V line
Faulty sensor feeding in external voltage
Module voltage regulator

symptoms: Implausible sensor values in live data

P0654.title: Engine RPM Output Circuit/Open
P0654.description: The engine module switches this hard-wired output with its own driver and checks the circuit electrically (open, short to ground or voltage) – it cannot see whether the lamp lights; on CAN-based cars such faults appear as U codes. P0654 concerns the engine speed output: the module turns the crankshaft signal into a cleaned-up square wave for the tachometer and other modules – Saab's 1999 9-3, for example, sends two pulses per revolution, about 30 Hz at idle. P0654 reports an open circuit or other fault on this output. Saab's EDC16 diesels use P0654 differently (a sensor supply group). No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; the description follows CARB and the component. The tachometer then reads zero or jumps; devices using the signal may fail, while the engine itself runs normally because the crankshaft input is intact.

causes.label: Wire between module and tachometer or receiver open, connector corroded
Output wire shorted
Instrument cluster or receiving module faulty (input stage)
Output driver in the module faulty

symptoms: Functions using the speed signal disturbed (accessories, cruise control, shift indicator)
Check engine light depending on the maker

P0655.title: Engine Hot Lamp Output Control Circuit
P0655.description: The engine module switches this hard-wired output with its own driver and checks the circuit electrically (open, short to ground or voltage) – it cannot see whether the lamp lights; on CAN-based cars such faults appear as U codes. P0655 concerns the engine hot or coolant warning lamp that the engine module switches by wire from the coolant temperature signal. CARB links overtemperature protection strategies to this lamp: a protective reaction that only starts after the hot lamp lights needs no MIL. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; the description follows CARB and the component. If the circuit fails, the driver may not be warned of overheating – check it promptly even though the check engine light usually stays off. Actual overheating is P0217; the coolant sensor circuit is P0117/P0118.

causes.label: Wire or connector between module and receiver open, corroded or shorted
Bulb/LED or instrument cluster faulty
Lamp supply missing (fuse)
Output driver in the module faulty

symptoms: Temperature warning lamp does not light at bulb check or when overheating
Warning lamp stays on without overheating
Code stored, check engine light depending on the maker

P0656.title: Fuel Level Output Circuit
P0656.description: The engine module switches this hard-wired output with its own driver and checks the circuit electrically (open, short to ground or voltage) – it cannot see whether the lamp lights; on CAN-based cars such faults appear as U codes. Where the engine module reads the fuel level sender itself – it needs the level for the evaporative leak test – it passes the level on to the fuel gauge. GM Europe's 2010 Saab 9-5 reads two senders (0.5–3.5 V), calculates the level in percent and sends it over CAN via the body module to the instrument cluster; there a failure would be a U code. P0656 reports a fault on a hard-wired level output. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; the description follows CARB and the component. The gauge then reads empty, full or jumps and the low fuel warning is wrong; engine and evaporative test are not affected. Sender input faults are P0460–P0464.

causes.label: Wire or connector between module and instrument cluster open or shorted
Instrument cluster (fuel gauge input) faulty
Output driver in the module faulty
Fuel level sender fault as root cause

symptoms: Fuel gauge reads empty, full or jumps

P0657.title: Actuator Supply Voltage A Circuit/Open
P0657.description: Actuator supply A is a high-side switch feeding several actuators together; its use differs by maker (Ford transmission solenoids, GM shared high-side driver, GM Europe 2.0 CDTI internal 5 V supply). P0657 is the open-circuit code; it is documented at Ford: the high-side switch of the 5R110W and 6R80 automatics feeds all shift solenoids, and the 2023 diesels split them into two supplies (P0657 and P2669), checked continuously. On a fault the solenoids are de-energised and the transmission falls back to a mechanical limp gear with maximum line pressure – harsh shifts and a single forward gear. Ford's 6.8 L V10 reports it with or without the lamp depending on the variant. GM does not use P0657 and reports opens together with ground faults under P0658.

causes.label: Open or connector fault at the transmission pass-through connector or wire to the valve body
Damaged harness
Internal high-side switch in the engine or transmission module
Internal transmission harness

symptoms: Check engine light (depending on the variant)

P0658.title: Actuator Supply Voltage A Circuit Low
P0658.description: Actuator supply A is a high-side switch feeding several actuators together; its use differs by maker (Ford transmission solenoids, GM shared high-side driver, GM Europe 2.0 CDTI internal 5 V supply). P0658 means the supply output is too low with the driver on – a short to ground (0.5 Ω or less). GM's engine module checks its shared high-side driver in 20 of 25 samples; the lamp rating changed from none (2016) via two trips (2017–18) to the first trip (2025). GM's transmission modules include an open circuit here, set it in the first trip and block the solenoid diagnostics, so the gearbox goes into limp mode. On GM Europe's 2.0 CDTI it means the internal 5 V supply is too low – no MIL, and if it recurs, the engine module is replaced.

causes.label: Actuator supply wire shorted to ground
Actuator (solenoid) shorted internally
Transmission harness or connector (also open, in transmission modules)
Module internal (main cause on the Saab diesel)

symptoms: Transmission limp mode or fixed gear

P0659.title: Actuator Supply Voltage A Circuit High
P0659.description: Actuator supply A is a high-side switch feeding several actuators together; its use differs by maker (Ford transmission solenoids, GM shared high-side driver, GM Europe 2.0 CDTI internal 5 V supply). P0659 means a short to voltage on the supply output, checked with the driver off – the output should then be dead (GM: 0.5 Ω or less to the supply, 20 of 25 samples; lamp after two trips in 2017–18, none in 2016). The driver can then no longer switch the actuators off; GM's transmission modules block their solenoid diagnostics while P0658/P0659 are active, and limp mode follows. On GM Europe's 2.0 CDTI it means the internal 5 V supply is too high, without MIL – the engine module is replaced.

causes.label: Actuator supply wire shorted to battery or ignition voltage
Harness chafed against a 12 V line
Module (driver shorted; internal on the Saab diesel)
External voltage fed back through a faulty actuator

P065A.title: Generator System Performance
P065A.description: Demand-controlled (smart) charging lets the module vary alternator voltage; the charging system is not an emission component, so these codes usually come without the check engine light. P065A is the function check of the whole charging strategy. Chrysler (Stellantis) explains it as a non-MIL code: the engine module switches off demand-controlled charging and falls back to normal charging because of electrical faults in other modules – returned alternators replaced for P065A were found to be fine. Other Stellantis cases trace it, together with P2503/P2504, to loose B+ or high-current connections, and the Ram 1500 3.0 EcoDiesel Gen 3 received a software update. The result is a constant charging voltage instead of smart charging, possibly with a battery lamp; there is no power limitation. Check codes in other modules and the main battery connections before replacing the alternator.

causes.label: Electrical fault in another module (lighting, wipers, blower) disabling smart charging
Loose or corroded B+ or high-current connection
Engine module software
Alternator or regulator faulty

P065B.title: Generator A Control Circuit Range/Performance
P065B.description: Demand-controlled (smart) charging lets the module vary alternator voltage; the charging system is not an emission component, so these codes usually come without the check engine light. P065B is the plausibility check of the control channel to the alternator regulator (LIN or a dedicated smart-charge line): command and feedback do not match, or the signal is out of range (too low or too high). A manufacturer table published via NHTSA for a gateway with LIN alternator shows the battery lamp and disabled stop-start, notes that jump starting or charging can set it briefly, and says to check P065C (belt) first; Ford's 6.8 L V10 reports it with or without the lamp depending on the variant. The regulator then falls back to a default target voltage. Circuit faults are P0620; L and F lines are P0621/P0622.

causes.label: LIN or control wire between alternator and module (connector, corrosion, open)
Weak battery, jump start or external charging
Alternator regulator faulty
Ground or B+ connections

P065C.title: Generator A Mechanical Performance
P065C.description: Demand-controlled (smart) charging lets the module vary alternator voltage; the charging system is not an emission component, so these codes usually come without the check engine light. P065C points to the alternator's mechanical drive: the alternator does not deliver as commanded or its feedback does not match engine speed, typically because the belt slips. The only manufacturer document found – a table for a gateway with LIN alternator published via NHTSA – shows the battery lamp and disabled stop-start and names checking and adjusting the drive belt tension as the fix, to be checked before P065B. Thresholds are not published. Belt wear or oil contamination, a weak tensioner, a faulty overrunning pulley or a stiff alternator bearing are the obvious mechanical causes. Hybrid starter-generators use other codes.

causes.label: Drive belt slipping (tension, wear, oil)
Weak belt tensioner
Alternator overrunning pulley faulty
Alternator bearing or rotor stiff

P065D.title: Reductant System Malfunction Lamp Control Circuit
P065D.description: The engine module switches this hard-wired output with its own driver and checks the circuit electrically (open, short to ground or voltage) – it cannot see whether the lamp lights; on CAN-based cars such faults appear as U codes. On SCR diesels a separate lamp or symbol warns of low DEF/AdBlue level, poor quality or system faults and announces speed or start restrictions (inducement). P065D reports a fault in the control circuit of this lamp. CARB requires inputs and outputs of the inducement strategy to be monitored on diesels from model years 2019–2021, and US federal rules define the inducement stages; Detroit Diesel, for example, shows the symbol below 1/8 tank and flashes it with a speed limit when empty. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; the description follows CARB and the component. Without the lamp the driver may run into an inducement stage without warning; the code itself is not known to trigger one.

causes.label: Wire or connector between module and receiver open, corroded or shorted
Bulb/LED or instrument cluster faulty
Lamp supply missing (fuse)
Driver in the engine or SCR module faulty

symptoms: AdBlue warning lamp does not light at ignition on, or stays on
No early warning of low AdBlue (risk of speed limit or no-restart without notice)
Check engine light possible (depending on the maker)

P065E.title: Intake Manifold Tuning Valve Performance Bank 1
P065E.description: The intake manifold tuning valve switches the manifold length or plenum connection with engine speed (more torque low, more power high); it is not the runner or swirl flap (IMRC, P2004 ff). P065E is the function check for bank 1 (or the only valve): the valve does not follow its command. It can be detected with a position sensor or, as a GM patent describes, without one from the intake pressure pulsation in steady running – a closed, tuned manifold pulses more. No manufacturer table available to us uses P065E itself: GM reports the same fault on this valve as P2070/P2071 (end position not reached within 5 s, 320 of 400 samples, two trips), and Ford's valve has no feedback at all. A valve stuck in one position leaves a torque gap in part of the rev range; sooted shafts and broken linkages are typical causes.

causes.label: Valve shaft or linkage stiff or sooted (oil mist from crankcase ventilation or EGR)
Plastic lever or ball joint between actuator and shaft broken or detached
Actuator motor or solenoid faulty (weak, gears)
Manifold leak or, on vacuum-operated actuators, a leak in the vacuum line

symptoms: Check engine light (depending on the maker)
Torque gap in one rev band
Rattling or clicking from the intake manifold

P065F.title: Intake Manifold Tuning Valve Performance Bank 2
P065F.description: The intake manifold tuning valve switches the manifold length or plenum connection with engine speed (more torque low, more power high); it is not the runner or swirl flap (IMRC, P2004 ff). P065F is the function check of the bank 2 valve: it does not follow its command, detected via a position sensor or the intake pressure pulsation (GM patent). Bank 2 codes require a V-engine manifold with two separately switched valves; many V engines use a single central valve between the plenums, and no manufacturer document available to us uses this code, so the description follows bank 1. A stuck valve causes a torque gap in one rev band and can make the banks fill unevenly. Bank 2 circuit faults are P0663–P0665.

causes.label: Bank 2 valve or shaft sooted or stiff
Linkage between actuator and valve broken or unhooked
Bank 2 actuator faulty internally
Manifold or vacuum leak

symptoms: Check engine light (depending on the maker)
Torque gap in one rev band

P0660.title: Intake Manifold Tuning Valve Control Circuit/Open Bank 1
P0660.description: The intake manifold tuning valve switches the manifold length or plenum connection with engine speed (more torque low, more power high); it is not the runner or swirl flap (IMRC, P2004 ff). P0660 means the control circuit of the bank 1 (or only) valve is open. GM evaluates the line voltage with the driver off: too low means the supply through the coil is missing (200 kΩ or more). GM's engines with this valve (low-side driver) check with ignition voltage of at least 11 V and the engine above 400 rpm and set the code after 40 of 50 samples (about 0.6 s), with the check engine light after two trips. Ford uses P0660 (older: P1549) as the electrical check of its actuator, which has no position feedback and stays closed and unpowered below about 2600 rpm – without the check engine light (5 s). The valve then stays in its rest position and power at high revs suffers.

causes.label: Actuator connector loose, corroded or spread
Actuator coil or motor open internally
Broken or chafed wire (control or supply)
Supply (fuse, main relay) to the actuator missing
Output driver in the engine module faulty

symptoms: Check engine light (GM after two trips; Ford without)
Less power in the upper or middle rev range
Actuator does not click at ignition on or when switching

P0661.title: Intake Manifold Tuning Valve Control Circuit Low Bank 1
P0661.description: The intake manifold tuning valve switches the manifold length or plenum connection with engine speed (more torque low, more power high); it is not the runner or swirl flap (IMRC, P2004 ff). P0661 means the bank 1 control circuit voltage is too low with the driver off – a short to ground (0.5 Ω or less), which bypasses the driver and keeps the valve energised; GM also includes an open circuit (200 kΩ or more) here, so P0660 may set alongside. GM's engines with this valve (low-side driver) check with ignition voltage of at least 11 V and the engine above 400 rpm and set the code after 40 of 50 samples (about 0.6 s), with the check engine light after two trips. Ford does not use P0661.

causes.label: Low-side control wire shorted to ground by chafing on engine or manifold
Actuator shorted internally to housing or ground
Open circuit (connector, coil) – included under P0661 at GM
Output driver in the engine module faulty

symptoms: Check engine light after two trips (GM)
Torque or power gap in one rev band
Possibly blown fuse, further codes of the same supply circuit

P0662.title: Intake Manifold Tuning Valve Control Circuit High Bank 1
P0662.description: The intake manifold tuning valve switches the manifold length or plenum connection with engine speed (more torque low, more power high); it is not the runner or swirl flap (IMRC, P2004 ff). P0662 means a short to voltage in the bank 1 control circuit: with the driver on, the low-side line should be pulled to ground, but the voltage stays high (0.5 Ω or less to positive); the driver protects itself and the valve is not actuated. GM's engines with this valve (low-side driver) check with ignition voltage of at least 11 V and the engine above 400 rpm and set the code after 40 of 50 samples (about 0.6 s), with the check engine light after two trips. Ford does not use P0662. The valve stays in its rest position, with a power loss around the switch-over speed.

causes.label: Control wire shorted to battery or supply voltage (harness)
Actuator winding shorted (very low resistance, overcurrent)
Moisture or corrosion in the connector between supply and control pin
Output driver in the engine module faulty

symptoms: Check engine light (depending on the maker)
Loss of power in part of the rev range
Actuator does not click when switching

P0663.title: Intake Manifold Tuning Valve Control Circuit/Open Bank 2
P0663.description: The intake manifold tuning valve switches the manifold length or plenum connection with engine speed (more torque low, more power high); it is not the runner or swirl flap (IMRC, P2004 ff). P0663 means the control circuit of the bank 2 valve is open. Bank 2 codes require a V-engine manifold with two separately switched valves; many V engines use a single central valve between the plenums, and no manufacturer document available to us uses this code, so the description follows bank 1. At GM the bank 1 equivalent (P0660) flags 200 kΩ or more with the driver off and lights the lamp after two trips; Ford runs bank-specific checks only for its runner control flaps (IMRC, P2005/P2011) and treats the tuning valve without the lamp. The valve stays in its rest position, with a power loss around the switch-over speed.

causes.label: Actuator connector loose, corroded or spread
Bank 2 actuator coil open
Broken wire in the harness
Output driver in the engine module faulty

symptoms: Check engine light (depending on the maker)
Loss of power in part of the rev range
Actuator does not click when switching

P0664.title: Intake Manifold Tuning Valve Control Circuit Low Bank 2
P0664.description: The intake manifold tuning valve switches the manifold length or plenum connection with engine speed (more torque low, more power high); it is not the runner or swirl flap (IMRC, P2004 ff). P0664 means the bank 2 control circuit voltage is too low with the driver off – typically a short to ground; with GM-style logic an open circuit is included. Bank 2 codes require a V-engine manifold with two separately switched valves; many V engines use a single central valve between the plenums, and no manufacturer document available to us uses this code, so the description follows bank 1. At GM the bank 1 equivalent (P0661) flags 0.5 Ω or less to ground in 40 of 50 samples, with the lamp after two trips.

causes.label: Bank 2 control wire shorted to ground
Bank 2 actuator shorted internally to ground
Open circuit (included with GM-style logic)
Output driver in the engine module faulty

symptoms: Check engine light (depending on the maker)
Loss of power in part of the rev range
Actuator does not click when switching

P0665.title: Intake Manifold Tuning Valve Control Circuit High Bank 2
P0665.description: The intake manifold tuning valve switches the manifold length or plenum connection with engine speed (more torque low, more power high); it is not the runner or swirl flap (IMRC, P2004 ff). P0665 means the bank 2 control line stays high with the driver on – a short to voltage or overcurrent, after which the driver shuts off. Bank 2 codes require a V-engine manifold with two separately switched valves; many V engines use a single central valve between the plenums, and no manufacturer document available to us uses this code, so the description follows bank 1. At GM the bank 1 equivalent (P0662) flags 0.5 Ω or less to positive in 40 of 50 samples, with the lamp after two trips.

causes.label: Bank 2 control wire shorted to voltage
Actuator winding shorted (overcurrent)
Corrosion or moisture in the connector
Output driver in the engine module faulty

symptoms: Check engine light (depending on the maker)
Loss of power in part of the rev range
Actuator does not click when switching

P0666.title: Control Module Internal Temperature Sensor A Circuit
P0666.description: Control modules measure their own circuit board temperature with an internal sensor to protect output stages (overtemperature is P0634) and, in GM transmission modules, as a substitute for fluid temperature. In GM's 6T70/6T75 and related automatics the sensor sits in the transmission module inside the valve body, with no external wiring – so the repair is practically always the module or valve body assembly. P0666 is the general circuit fault of this sensor A. No manufacturer table available to us uses P0666 itself – GM splits the circuit faults into low (P0668) and high (P0669), plausibility is P0667. Expect a warning lamp and, in a transmission module, changed shift quality because a substitute temperature is used.

causes.label: Module faulty internally (temperature sensor or measuring circuit)
Moisture or corrosion in the module or valve body
Supply or ground problems of the module

P0667.title: Control Module Internal Temperature Sensor A Range/Performance
P0667.description: Control modules measure their own circuit board temperature with an internal sensor to protect output stages (overtemperature is P0634) and, in GM transmission modules, as a substitute for fluid temperature. In GM's 6T70/6T75 and related automatics the sensor sits in the transmission module inside the valve body, with no external wiring – so the repair is practically always the module or valve body assembly. P0667 is the plausibility check: GM compares the module (substrate) temperature with the transmission fluid temperature and the temperature measured at power-up. The Saab 9-4X sets it when, within 5 of 6 minutes, fluid and substrate differ by more than 20–50 °C and power-up and substrate by more than 8–10 °C (two trips); GM's 2019 table uses 3000 of 3750 samples. The module then uses the power-up temperature instead. Check the fluid temperature sensor (P0711) first – it is the comparison partner.

causes.label: Transmission module or valve body (internal sensor) faulty
Transmission fluid temperature sensor reads wrong (comparison partner)
Unusual conditions (long standing in extreme cold or heat, fluid level or condition)

P0668.title: Control Module Internal Temperature Sensor A Circuit Low
P0668.description: Control modules measure their own circuit board temperature with an internal sensor to protect output stages (overtemperature is P0634) and, in GM transmission modules, as a substitute for fluid temperature. In GM's 6T70/6T75 and related automatics the sensor sits in the transmission module inside the valve body, with no external wiring – so the repair is practically always the module or valve body assembly. P0668 means the sensor signal is at the low voltage end: GM converts it into a temperature and treats −249 °C or less – a physically impossible value – for 60 s as a fault, with the lamp after two trips and the power-up temperature as substitute. 'Low' refers to the voltage; depending on the sensor type that need not mean a low temperature.

causes.label: Module faulty internally (sensor or measuring circuit shorted)
Moisture or fluid in the electronics of the valve body
Module supply problem

symptoms: Scan tool shows an implausibly low module temperature

P0669.title: Control Module Internal Temperature Sensor A Circuit High
P0669.description: Control modules measure their own circuit board temperature with an internal sensor to protect output stages (overtemperature is P0634) and, in GM transmission modules, as a substitute for fluid temperature. In GM's 6T70/6T75 and related automatics the sensor sits in the transmission module inside the valve body, with no external wiring – so the repair is practically always the module or valve body assembly. P0669 means the sensor signal is at the high voltage end (internal open or short to voltage): GM treats a converted value of 249 °C or more for 60 s as a fault, with the lamp after two trips and the power-up temperature as substitute. Unlike P0634, which reports a plausibly high real temperature (GM: 142 °C), P0669 reports a physically impossible value.

causes.label: Module faulty internally (sensor open)
Moisture or corrosion in the electronics
Module supply or software

symptoms: Scan tool shows an implausibly high module temperature

P066A.title: Cylinder 1 Glow Plug Control Circuit Low
P066A.description: Modern diesel glow systems switch each glow plug through its own power semiconductor (in a glow plug module or the engine module), so current and faults can be measured per plug; a faulty channel is switched off. CARB requires glow plugs to be checked for correct current and voltage drop and, since model year 2010, a single plug outside specification to be detected and named. P066A means the circuit to the cylinder 1 glow plug is shorted to ground or draws overcurrent. GM's engine-module drivers flag a circuit impedance to ground below 0.11 Ω (10 of 20 samples at 100 ms) with the check engine and glow plug lamps after two trips; Ford's 2023 Power Stroke checks during heating for more than 22 A for 0.3 s or 20–22 A for 2 s. The channel is switched off, so plug 1 no longer heats – harder cold starts and white smoke follow. A plug shorted internally is the usual cause; a wrong plug type is another.

causes.label: Glow plug cylinder 1 shorted internally (element against body)
Plug wire insulation damaged and shorted to ground (block, bracket)
Wrong plug type (resistance or voltage rating)
Driver in the glow or engine module faulty, or software (GM 3.0 L 2020)

symptoms: Check engine and glow plug lamp
Harder cold start, especially in frost
Rough running and white smoke right after a cold start

P066B.title: Cylinder 1 Glow Plug Control Circuit High
P066B.description: Modern diesel glow systems switch each glow plug through its own power semiconductor (in a glow plug module or the engine module), so current and faults can be measured per plug; a faulty channel is switched off. CARB requires glow plugs to be checked for correct current and voltage drop and, since model year 2010, a single plug outside specification to be detected and named. P066B means the circuit to the cylinder 1 glow plug is shorted to battery voltage, so the driver cannot switch it off. GM's engine-module drivers detect an impedance to the supply below 0.5 Ω (0.14 Ω for low-resistance plugs) in 10 of 20 samples, with the lamps after two trips; Ford's 2023 Power Stroke sees 0 A through its measuring path while the plug is commanded on (about 1 s). A permanently powered low-voltage plug can overheat and burn through, after which an open-circuit code follows, and the battery may drain.

causes.label: Cylinder 1 plug wire touching battery positive (chafing in the harness)
Moisture or corrosion in the module or plug connector (leakage between pins)
Driver in the glow or engine module shorted (permanently on)
Glow module software (GM 3.0 L 2020)

symptoms: Check engine and glow plug lamp
Plug permanently powered, possible battery drain
Plug burns through, then an open-circuit code

P0670.title: Glow Plug Control Module 1 Control Circuit/Open
P0670.description: In today's J2012 meaning P0670 is the electrical check of the activation line from the engine module to glow plug control module 1 for an open circuit; a short to ground is P0383, a short to voltage P0384, and serial communication between the modules P0683/P0684. On Bosch systems (Saab 2.2 TiD and EDC16) the engine module switches this line, detects an open load with the output off and a short to voltage with it on, and also compares the glow module's diagnostic feedback, which must switch inversely – Saab reports all line faults under P0670. GM's LB7/LLY Duramax (2004–05) used P0670 in an older meaning for glow module performance (50 of 100 samples, two trips). No current GM or Ford table uses it. If the line fails, no plug heats: hard or no cold start in frost, smoke and rough running.

causes.label: Wire or connector between engine and glow module open or corroded (bent pin, contact tension)
Glow module faulty (input open) or without supply or ground (fuse, terminal 30)
Control line shorted (makers reporting all line faults under P0670, e.g. Saab)

symptoms: Glow plug lamp behaves implausibly (stays off or on)

P0671.title: Cylinder 1 Glow Plug Circuit/Open

P0671 means the load circuit of the cylinder 1 glow plug is open while glowing. Thresholds: GM engine-module drivers 200 kΩ or more (two trips), GM's L5P glow module less than 4.0 A at over 6 V, Ford's 2023 Power Stroke less than 1 A for about 1 s. Older GM systems (LB7/LLY, LML) report open and short under this one code. Chrysler advises checking the main B+ feed and ground of the glow module first when several cylinder codes appear together.

Glow module supply or ground (several cylinder codes at once)
Glow module or driver faulty, or software (GM 3.0 L 2020)

symptoms: Check engine light (GM also glow plug lamp)

Rough idle, knocking and white or blue smoke after a cold start

P0683.title: Glow Plug Control Module 1 to PCM Communication Circuit
P0683.description: Glow plug module 1 reports to the engine module over a feedback wire (Bosch-type systems expect it inverse to the activation line) or the bus; GM and Ford report a lost bus link as U0106, Saab as P0380/P1380, and no manufacturer document available to us uses P0683/P0684 themselves. The engine module then no longer receives plug status reports, so the individual plug monitoring fails; depending on design the glow module keeps glowing on its own timing or not at all. The activation line in the other direction is P0670/P0383/P0384.

causes.label: Communication or feedback wire between glow and engine module open, chafed or connector corroded
Glow module without supply or ground (fuse, main cable) – does not answer
Glow module faulty internally
Glow or engine module software or programming

symptoms: Check engine light (glow plug lamp may flash or stay on)
Harder cold start, long cranking in frost
Rough running and white smoke after a cold start
No individual plug reports any more

P0684.title: Glow Plug Control Module 1 to PCM Communication Circuit Range/Performance
P0684.description: Glow plug module 1 reports to the engine module over a feedback wire (Bosch-type systems expect it inverse to the activation line) or the bus; GM and Ford report a lost bus link as U0106, Saab as P0380/P1380, and no manufacturer document available to us uses P0683/P0684 themselves. P0684 means communication exists but is implausible: wrong level or duty cycle, implausible content or a feedback that does not match the activation state – as in the Saab logic, where the feedback must be the inverse of the command. The engine module can then no longer rely on the glow system status; individual plug faults may go unreported. Contact resistance at the pins and voltage dips at the glow module during high glow currents are typical causes.

causes.label: Contact resistance or corrosion at connectors or pins of the communication line (signal distorted)
Supply or ground problem at the glow module (voltage dip at high glow currents)
Glow module faulty, or software/configuration not matching the engine module
Engine module input stage faulty

symptoms: Check engine light (glow plug lamp may flash or stay on)
Harder cold start, long cranking in frost
Rough running and white smoke after a cold start
No individual plug reports any more

P0685.title: ECM/PCM Power Relay Control Circuit/Open
P0685.description: The engine module switches its main relay coil to ground (control circuit), reads the switched voltage back on a sense line and keeps the relay on briefly after ignition off to save learned values. P0685 means the relay control circuit is open: GM measures with the driver off and flags 200 kΩ or more to ground. GM checks with run/crank voltage above 11 V and sets the code after 8 of 10 samples at 250 ms, with the lamp after two trips. GM Europe's 2.0 L turbo compares commanded and actual state for 2 s, Ford's 2023 diesel checks continuously within 0.5 s. A real open keeps the relay from pulling in – no start; on Saab's V6 there is then no communication with the engine module and the MIL flashes. GM notes P0686 may set alongside.

causes.label: Open or corroded control wire between relay coil and module or connector
Relay coil open or relay badly seated
Relay coil supply missing (fuse, battery positive)
Weak battery or voltage dip
Module driver faulty

symptoms: Engine does not start or stalls
No communication with the engine module (Saab)
MIL flashes rapidly, other relays click (Saab)

P0686.title: ECM/PCM Power Relay Control Circuit Low
P0686.description: The engine module switches its main relay coil to ground (control circuit), reads the switched voltage back on a sense line and keeps the relay on briefly after ignition off to save learned values. P0686 means the control line is shorted to ground: with the driver off it should carry battery voltage through the coil, but it sits at ground (0.5 Ω or less). The relay then stays energised and the module can no longer switch it off – after-run and shutdown are disturbed and the battery can drain. GM checks with run/crank voltage above 11 V and sets the code after 8 of 10 samples at 250 ms, with the lamp after two trips. The former obdex title (the wording of P0685) was a shifted entry; P0686 is the 'low' code.

causes.label: Control wire between relay and module chafed to ground
Relay shorted internally or water in the relay carrier
Module driver shorted internally

symptoms: Relay stays on after ignition off, battery drains

P0687.title: ECM/PCM Power Relay Control Circuit High
P0687.description: The engine module switches its main relay coil to ground (control circuit), reads the switched voltage back on a sense line and keeps the relay on briefly after ignition off to save learned values. P0687 means the control line is shorted to voltage: when the driver switches on and should pull it to ground, it stays high (0.5 Ω or less to positive) or the driver goes into overcurrent protection, so the relay does not pull in – no supply to the loads, no start or stalling. GM checks with run/crank voltage above 11 V and sets the code after 8 of 10 samples at 250 ms, with the lamp after two trips. The former obdex title (a sense-circuit wording) was a shifted entry; P0687 is the 'high' code of the control circuit. A high voltage on the sense line is P0690.

causes.label: Control wire shorted to positive (harness, external voltage)
Relay coil shorted (very low resistance)
Module driver faulty

symptoms: Engine does not start or stalls

P0688.title: ECM/PCM Power Relay Sense Circuit/Open
P0688.description: The engine module switches its main relay coil to ground (control circuit), reads the switched voltage back on a sense line and keeps the relay on briefly after ignition off to save learned values. P0688 means the expected switched voltage does not arrive on the sense line – the line is open, a fuse in the monitored path has blown or the contact does not close. Chrysler (Stellantis) calls the relay 'auto shutdown (ASD) relay'; a service case for intermittent no-starts with P0688 points first to spread or pushed-back terminals in the ASD circuit connector. GM does not use P0688 and reports an open sense line as P0689. The former obdex title (a duplicate of P0690) was a shifted entry.

causes.label: Terminal in the sense or ASD circuit connector bent, pushed back or spread
Blown fuse in the monitored load circuit (e.g. shorted ignition coil)
Relay contact does not close
Module input faulty

symptoms: Engine cranks but intermittently does not start (Stellantis)

P0689.title: ECM/PCM Power Relay Sense Circuit Low
P0689.description: The engine module switches its main relay coil to ground (control circuit), reads the switched voltage back on a sense line and keeps the relay on briefly after ignition off to save learned values. P0689 means the sense voltage is too low although the relay is commanded on – the contact does not close or has high resistance, the sense line is open or grounded, or a fuse in the load circuit has blown. GM sets it at 5 V or less with more than 9 V supply in 5 of 6 samples at 1 s, lamp after two trips; GM Europe's V6 below 6 V for 1 s and the 2.0 L turbo below 5 V, both without the lamp. GM includes an open sense line here. Starting problems or stalling follow, and on Saab the throttle control, which uses this voltage, may go into limp mode.

causes.label: Relay contact burnt or not closing, relay faulty
Fuse in the relay load or sense path blown
High resistance or corrosion in relay carrier, connector or wire
Weak battery

symptoms: Check engine light (depending on the maker)

P068A.title: ECM/PCM Power Relay De-Energized Performance Too Early

P068A means the relay dropped out before the module released it. Ford explains it as the non-volatile memory write after ignition off not being completed before the module lost power; the 2023 diesel checks continuously within 0.5 s. GM Europe's 2.0 diesel checks with the engine running for an unexpected loss of relay voltage (no MIL). VW (2017–18 Jetta 1.4 T) and Stellantis (2026 Dodge Charger 3.0 twin turbo) fixed false reports by software updates. Real triggers include disconnecting the battery right after switch-off and loose contacts in the relay supply; learned values may be lost.

causes.label: Engine module software (false report)
Battery disconnected during or right after switch-off, or severe voltage dip
Open, high resistance or short to ground in the relay coil or contact supply
Relay faulty (drops out with vibration or heat)

symptoms: Lost learned values, rough idle after restart
With a contact fault: stalling or no start

P068B.title: ECM/PCM Power Relay De-Energized Performance Too Late
P068B.description: The engine module switches its main relay coil to ground (control circuit), reads the switched voltage back on a sense line and keeps the relay on briefly after ignition off to save learned values. P068B is the counterpart of P068A: after ignition off and the module's switch-off command the relay voltage remains – the relay drops out late or not at all. GM Europe's 2.0 diesel runs this check from ignition off until the module shuts down and names a control line shorted to ground (coil stays energised), an output line shorted to voltage or a sticking contact as causes, without lighting the MIL. Modules and loads then stay powered and the battery drains. GM reports the same electrical faults as P0686/P0690 instead. A Ford diesel table lists 'P068B' for a memory error, which is evidently a typo for P06B8.

causes.label: Relay contact sticking or welded
Relay control wire shorted to ground (coil stays energised)
Relay output or load line shorted to voltage
Module driver or software

symptoms: Relay or module stays active after ignition off (fan or pump keeps running)
Possibly check engine light (depending on the maker)

P069E.title: Fuel Pump Control Module Requested MIL Illumination
P069E.description: P069E is not a component fault but a notice in the engine module: the separate fuel pump control module has detected and stored an emission-related fault of its own and requests the check engine light – over serial data or, on older systems, a request line. P06A0.title: Variable A/C Compressor Control Circuit
P06A0.description: Variable-displacement A/C compressors change their swash-plate stroke via an electric control valve: a PWM current sets the crankcase pressure and thus the output. Where the engine module drives this valve (Ford's 'EVDC' compressors 2013–2019), it monitors the circuit; where the climate control module drives it (Hyundai, VW/Audi, GM), faults appear in that module instead. CARB requires monitoring only where the A/C affects engine control. P06A0 is the general circuit fault of the compressor control valve. Ford's service messages for its EVDC compressors (2013–2019) describe it with weak or no cooling, typically from a valve with an open coil or a corroded connector at the compressor; low refrigerant can also mislead the diagnosis. The compressor then runs at minimum stroke or does not cool. Not emission relevant in most cases.

Engine module driver faulty

symptoms: A/C cools weakly or not at all

Module supply or software

P06AD.title: Control Module Internal Temperature Sensor B Circuit Low
P06AD.description: Control modules can carry a second internal temperature sensor (B). In GM's 6T70/6T75 and related automatics, sensor A measures the circuit board (substrate) temperature, sensor B the 'power-up temperature' used as a reference and substitute; both sit inside the transmission module in the valve body, so repairs mean module or valve body. Unlike most temperature sensors, low here corresponds to an implausibly cold reading. The module then uses a substitute value.

causes.label: Transmission module or valve body (internal sensor) faulty
Moisture or fluid in the module electronics
Module supply or software

symptoms: Implausible module temperature in the scan tool

P06AF.title: Torque Management System Forced Engine Shutdown
P06AF.description: GM uses P06AF for a cross-check between two control modules: the monitored module (engine or transmission module, each with main and secondary processor) sends a fixed answer sequence over CAN only if both its processors work together correctly; the monitoring module (engine, transmission or hybrid control module) sets P06AF if the pattern is wrong or missing. In all GM tables from 2016 to 2025 it is type A – lamp in the first trip – and the torque management may shut the engine down for safety. Typical causes are processor or software faults in one of the modules, communication problems or supply interruptions. Look for further processor codes (P0606, P060A, P060B) and software bulletins. No other manufacturer document available to us uses P06AF.

causes.label: Software fault in engine, transmission or hybrid module
Processor fault in one of the modules
CAN communication disturbance between the modules
Supply interruption or poor ground of a module

symptoms: Engine shuts off or does not start

P06B0.title: Sensor Power Supply A Circuit/Open
P06B0.description: Despite the similar name, 'sensor power supply' is not the 5 V sensor reference (P0641 ff). It is documented in GM hybrid drive motor control modules: a 15 V supply that excites the motor position sensor (resolver) and powers the gate drivers of the inverter transistors, kept separate from the 5 V reference and the 12 V supply. In GM's 2008 Two-Mode hybrid, A and B are the two motor control modules. P06B0 is the general or open-circuit code of supply A. Only Mitsubishi's 2022 Outlander bulletin lists this code (as a main code with low/high sub-codes), without thresholds or sensor assignment. Low and high are P06B1/P06B2; GM documents those with thresholds. Check fuses and feeds of the motor control module first.

causes.label: Blown fuse or open feed to the module
Internal supply circuit of the motor control module faulty
Connector or wiring fault
Short in a supplied component (resolver, gate driver)

symptoms: Check engine or hybrid warning light
Electric drive or hybrid mode limited or disabled
Further motor position or inverter codes

P06B6.title: Internal Control Module Knock/Combustion Vibration Sensor Processor 1 Performance
P06B6.description: To detect an open knock sensor circuit, GM's engine modules feed a 20 kHz test signal into the sensor circuit and check whether it returns. P06B6 checks the internal test circuit or knock signal processor for sensor 1: it sets when the returned 20 kHz component lies between the open-circuit thresholds, so the module cannot decide 'connected' or 'open'. GM rates it type B (two trips), type A in some 2025 modules; Saab retards ignition timing as a reaction. GM bulletin 22-NA-229 calls for reprogramming only, not part replacement. Ford uses P06B6 for lost communication with its knock chip (more than 200 cylinder events). Knock sensor circuit codes are P0325–P0328.

causes.label: Engine module software (GM bulletin)
Internal knock processor or test circuit faulty
Knock sensor wiring with high resistance or intermittent contact
Knock sensor faulty

symptoms: Retarded ignition, less power and higher consumption

P06B7.title: Internal Control Module Knock/Combustion Vibration Sensor Processor 2 Performance

P06B8.title: Internal Control Module Non-Volatile Random Access Memory (NVRAM) Error
P06B8.description: Non-volatile RAM keeps its content without power; among other things it stores the permanent fault codes CARB requires, which cannot be cleared with a scan tool. Ford sets P06B8 when the checksum of this permanent-code memory is wrong; a common companion is P068A (main relay dropped out too early, memory write incomplete). Ford's commercial and propane variants list it with or without the check engine light depending on the vehicle; Ford's 2023 diesel table misprints it as 'P068B'. GM and Saab do not use P06B8. Typical causes are interrupted shutdowns (battery disconnected, voltage dips), software faults and, rarely, a memory defect. After a software check, clearing and an ignition cycle with normal shutdown often resolve it.

Engine module software
Weak battery or poor ground
Memory defect in the module

symptoms: Check engine light (depending on the vehicle)

P06B9.title: Cylinder 1 Glow Plug Circuit Range/Performance
P06B9.description: The glow module calculates each plug's resistance from voltage and current while glowing. 'Range/performance' means the circuit is electrically intact but the resistance or current lies outside the specified window – typically an aged, high-resistance or wrong plug or contact resistance at the connector. CARB requires a single plug outside specification to be detected from model year 2010. Ford's 2023 6.7 L/3.0 L Power Stroke runs this check during heating after the open and short checks and flags a circuit above 2 Ω after about 3 s. GM does not use this code family. Ram's 6.7 L Cummins (from model year 2025, with glow plugs instead of the grid heater) set these codes falsely; the fix was reprogramming the engine module. On the 2014–15 Ram ProMaster 3.0 L diesel, plugs without an inner O-ring caused it; all plugs were replaced.

causes.label: Glow plug cylinder 1 aged or high-resistance
Contact resistance at plug connector or terminal nut
Wrong plug type or a plug with a manufacturing fault
Engine or glow module software (Ram 6.7 L from 2025)

symptoms: Check engine and glow plug lamp
Rough running and white smoke after a cold start

P06C5.title: Cylinder 1 Glow Plug Incorrect
P06C5.description: A glow plug has no identification; the control unit recognises its type only from its electrical behaviour – cold resistance at switch-on and how resistance rises during heating (R = U/I). A Beru patent describes how steel and ceramic plugs are told apart this way so the right heating profile is used and a wrong or mixed type is reported. A low-voltage plug on an 11 V control burns out, an 11 V plug on a low-voltage control glows too weakly. GM uses 'incorrect' for any resistance outside the window: the 2025 diesels check 0.22–2.00 Ω (15 of 25 samples, two trips), the L5P glow module a ramp-dependent window. P06C5 reports this for cylinder 1. VW's 2.0 TDI (Jetta, Golf, Passat 2011–13) checks the type 2 s after ignition on – starting during that time caused false codes from the voltage dip, fixed with new glow module software.

causes.label: Wrong glow plug type fitted in cylinder 1 (steel/ceramic, voltage rating)
Plug resistance drifted (ageing, damage)
Glow module software or check during cranking (false report)
Contact resistance at the plug connector

symptoms: Check engine and glow plug lamp
Harder cold start or white smoke
Possibly plug burnt out (low-voltage plug on 11 V control)

P06D1.title: Internal Control Module Ignition Coil Control Performance
P06D1.description: On ignition systems where the coils are driven through a separate driver chip inside the engine module, P06D1 reports that this internal coil control does not work correctly. Ford checks the communication with the coil driver chip continuously and sets the code within 1 s at 200–3200 rpm, positive torque and 11–16 V. GM Europe's V6 (Saab 9-5 2.8 T) reports it as an internal engine module fault with the lamp after two trips. Misfires or rough running can follow if coils are no longer fired correctly. Primary circuit faults of individual coils are P0351–P0360, driver shorts P2300 ff. Check supply and ground, look for software updates; otherwise the module is the likely cause.

causes.label: Coil driver chip or internal communication in the engine module faulty
Engine module software
Supply or ground problem at the module
Shorted coil overloading the driver

P06D2.title: Sensor Reference Voltage E Circuit/Open
P06D2.description: The engine module feeds sensors from several regulated 5 V reference circuits; a short at one sensor pulls the whole circuit down and all its sensors report at once – unplug them one by one to find the culprit. P06D2 is the general code for circuit E. GM uses it as the collective code for its fifth 5 V reference: petrol engines 2015–2019 flag a reference outside 4.875–5.125 V in 19 of 39 samples with the lamp in the first trip, the 6.6 L Duramax LML/LGH 4.6 V or less for 0.1 s with two trips; GM includes it in its 'engine power limited' group. Which sensors are on circuit E is not listed. GM's hybrid control module uses P06D2 for a separate 12 V reference.

causes.label: Short in the wire or sensor of a connected sensor
Chafing or water in harness or connector
A connected sensor faulty internally
Module internal voltage regulator or components

P06D3.title: Sensor Reference Voltage E Circuit Low
P06D3.description: The engine module feeds sensors from several regulated 5 V reference circuits; a short at one sensor pulls the whole circuit down and all its sensors report at once – unplug them one by one to find the culprit. P06D3 means reference E is too low – typically a short to ground. Ram's 2023 6.7 L Cummins set P06D3 together with P0642/P0652 because of a leaking capacitor in the engine module; the fix was replacing the module. GM reports circuit E under the collective code P06D2.

causes.label: Short in the wire or sensor of a connected sensor
Chafing or water in harness or connector
A connected sensor faulty internally
Engine module internal fault (e.g. leaking capacitor, Ram 2023)

P06D4.title: Sensor Reference Voltage E Circuit High
P06D4.description: The engine module feeds sensors from several regulated 5 V reference circuits; a short at one sensor pulls the whole circuit down and all its sensors report at once – unplug them one by one to find the culprit. P06D4 means reference E is too high – often a sensor signal wire shorted to 12 V. No manufacturer document available to us names P06D4 itself; Ram's 6.7 L Cummins uses the neighbouring P06D3, and GM reports circuit E under P06D2. Sensors on the circuit then read too high.

causes.label: Reference or sensor signal wire shorted to 12 V
Chafing or water in harness or connector
A connected sensor faulty internally
Module internal voltage regulator or components

P06D5.title: Sensor Reference Voltage E Circuit Range/Performance

causes.label: Short in the wire or sensor of a connected sensor

A connected sensor faulty internally
Module internal voltage regulator or components

P06DA.title: Engine Oil Pressure Control Circuit/Open
P06DA.description: A switchable or variable oil pump saves fuel by lowering its output at part load; a solenoid valve sets the stage. GM and Ford design it so the pump runs at full output, i.e. high pressure, when the valve is unpowered – the safe default – and at the low stage when powered. P06DA means the control circuit of this valve is open: it can no longer be powered, so the pump stays at high pressure. GM measures the voltage with the driver off and flags more than 200 kΩ after two trips; some GM modules set P06DB instead. GM checks the low-side driver at 11 V or more relay voltage over 40 of 50 samples (100 ms); Ford's smart driver reports output faults after 5 s with the battery at 11 V or more. Mitsubishi's 2022 Outlander uses the same code. The engine is not at risk, the pump just can no longer be regulated.

causes.label: Connector at the control valve loose or corroded (often at the pump in the oil pan)
Valve coil open or valve broken
Supply (main relay) or control wire broken
Engine module software

symptoms: Check engine light after two trips
Usually no noticeable symptom, oil pressure permanently high

P06DB.title: Engine Oil Pressure Control Circuit Low
P06DB.description: A switchable or variable oil pump saves fuel by lowering its output at part load; a solenoid valve sets the stage. GM and Ford design it so the pump runs at full output, i.e. high pressure, when the valve is unpowered – the safe default – and at the low stage when powered. P06DB means the control wire behind the valve is shorted to ground. With a low-side driver the valve is then powered all the time, so the pump stays at the low stage even at high load and speed. That endangers the engine, so GM flags a short below 0.5 Ω after just one trip, unlike open circuit and short to positive. GM checks the low-side driver at 11 V or more relay voltage over 40 of 50 samples (100 ms); Ford's smart driver reports output faults after 5 s with the battery at 11 V or more. A short to positive is P06DC, a pump stuck at low pressure without a circuit fault P06DE.

causes.label: Control wire chafing against ground (engine block, oil pan)
Control valve shorted internally
Oil or moisture in the connector
Engine module driver stage

symptoms: Check engine light at once (GM after one trip)
Low oil pressure at high engine speed, possibly oil pressure warning

P06DC.title: Engine Oil Pressure Control Circuit High
P06DC.description: A switchable or variable oil pump saves fuel by lowering its output at part load; a solenoid valve sets the stage. GM and Ford design it so the pump runs at full output, i.e. high pressure, when the valve is unpowered – the safe default – and at the low stage when powered. P06DC means the control wire is shorted to positive: the low-side driver can no longer pull it to ground, so the valve stays unpowered and the pump at high pressure – the safe state. GM checks this with the driver on and flags a short below 0.5 Ω after two trips. GM checks the low-side driver at 11 V or more relay voltage over 40 of 50 samples (100 ms); Ford's smart driver reports output faults after 5 s with the battery at 11 V or more. Apart from slightly higher consumption there are usually no symptoms. An open circuit is P06DA, a short to ground P06DB.

causes.label: Control wire shorted to positive
Valve coil shorted (looks like a short to positive at the driver)

symptoms: Check engine light after two trips
Usually no noticeable symptom, oil pressure permanently high

P06DD.title: Engine Oil Pressure Control Circuit Performance/Stuck Off
P06DD.description: A switchable oil pump changes its output via a solenoid valve; unpowered it delivers high pressure. To test it, the module switches the pump between stages (GM up to 15 times, with oil at 50–110 °C and 1350–2500 rpm, expecting more than 100 kPa difference) and watches the oil pressure sensor; Ford checks each switch-over of a two-stage pump within 1 s, or a variable pump over 10 s, from 30 s after start. P06DD means the pressure does not react and stays above the threshold – the pump acts as if the valve were stuck off, at high pressure; GM sets it after two trips. Yet GM bulletins for V8 and 2.5 L engines list P06DD with low oil pressure, too: broken valve tips, unseated valves, a loose pump drive gear or worn tensioners also stop the pressure from changing. Check oil level and pressure before replacing parts.

causes.label: Control valve stuck or broken, screen clogged
Oil level too low, wrong viscosity or sludge
Mechanical pump or drive damage (tensioner, drive gear, pump face)
Valve not seated correctly (retaining clip)
Oil pressure sensor inaccurate

symptoms: Check engine light after two trips
Oil pressure stays high – or, with pump damage, low or fluctuating

P06DE.title: Engine Oil Pressure Control Circuit Stuck On
P06DE.description: A switchable oil pump changes its output via a solenoid valve; powered it runs at the low stage. To test it, the module switches the pump between stages (GM up to 15 times, with oil at 50–110 °C and 1350–2500 rpm, expecting more than 100 kPa difference) and watches the oil pressure sensor; Ford checks each switch-over of a two-stage pump within 1 s, or a variable pump over 10 s, from 30 s after start. P06DE is the counterpart of P06DD: the commanded high stage is not reached and the pressure stays below the threshold, as if the valve were stuck on. Too little oil pressure at high load endangers the engine, so GM sets it after just one trip; a Ford patent raises idle speed in this case. A short to ground on the control wire (P06DB) has the same effect electrically. An FCA bulletin for the 3.6 L V6 fixes false codes by software.

causes.label: Control valve stuck in the powered position
Low oil level, diluted or sludged oil, aeration
Pump wear or internal leakage
Engine module software (FCA 3.6 L)
Oil pressure sensor

symptoms: Oil pressure warning at higher engine speed possible
Possibly reduced power or raised idle
Valvetrain or chain tensioner noise from lack of oil

P06DF.title: Glow Plug Control Module 1 Memory Checksum Error
P06DF.description: A diesel glow plug control module has its own microcontroller. On power-up it forms a checksum over its memory and compares it with the stored value; P06DF means they differ, so the module's program or data cannot be trusted. Ford's 2023 6.7 L and 3.0 L Power Stroke list P06DF among the glow module checks, run at power-up and flagged on a RAM checksum mismatch after about 1 s. GM's L5P performs the same check on ROM (4.5 s, two trips) but reports it as P064C. CARB treats the module as a 'smart device' whose internal faults need not be pinpointed, so this is extra diagnosis by the manufacturer. The usual remedy is reprogramming or replacing the module; until then preheating may be missing.

causes.label: Glow plug control module faulty internally (memory, controller)
Failed or interrupted programming of the module
Voltage dip or spike at power-up (weak battery, poor ground)
Moisture or corrosion in module or connector

symptoms: Check engine light, possibly glow plug/wait-to-start lamp
White smoke and knocking after cold start

P06E0.title: Cylinder 11 Glow Plug Control Circuit Low
P06E0.description: Diesel glow systems switch each plug through its own power semiconductor and switch off a faulty channel; CARB requires single-plug detection from model year 2010. P06E0 means the circuit to the cylinder 11 glow plug is shorted to ground or draws overcurrent. For cylinders 1–8, GM's engine-module drivers flag below 0.11 Ω to ground after two trips, and Ford's 2023 Power Stroke more than 22 A for 0.3 s or 20–22 A for 2 s while heating. The channel is switched off and the plug stays cold; the other plugs keep working. An internally shorted plug or a chafed wire is the usual cause. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code – it needs at least 11 cylinders, and the only US OBD II diesel above eight, VW's Touareg V10 TDI, has ten; the description follows cylinders 1–8.

causes.label: Cylinder 11 glow plug shorted internally
Plug wire chafed through to ground
Burnt connector or terminal nut, tracking through oil or moisture
Driver stage in the glow module defective

symptoms: Check engine light (GM: also glow plug lamp)
Rough cold idle, white smoke after cold start

P06E1.title: Cylinder 11 Glow Plug Control Circuit High
P06E1.description: Diesel glow systems switch each plug through its own power semiconductor and switch off a faulty channel; CARB requires single-plug detection from model year 2010. P06E1 means the circuit to the cylinder 11 glow plug is shorted to positive: voltage is present although the driver is off, or no current flows when it is on. For cylinders 1–8, GM's engine-module drivers flag a short to positive below 0.5 Ω after two trips, and Ford's 2023 Power Stroke 0 A while commanded for about 1 s. The plug may glow permanently and fail early; the other plugs keep working. Wiring shorted to supply or a failed driver are the usual causes. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code – it needs at least 11 cylinders, and the only US OBD II diesel above eight, VW's Touareg V10 TDI, has ten; the description follows cylinders 1–8.

causes.label: Plug wire shorted to supply in the harness
Driver stage in the glow module shorted (permanently on)
Moisture or corrosion bridging to a supply pin
Glow module software

symptoms: Check engine light (GM: also glow plug lamp)
Rough cold idle, white smoke after cold start
Plug may glow permanently and fail early

P06E4.title: Control Module Wake-up Circuit Performance
P06E4.description: Control modules are woken by a dedicated wake-up line or a network wake-up – at ignition on, when a charging cable is plugged in, or on a timer for engine-off diagnostics and battery management. P06E4 means this wake-up signal is implausible: the module wakes too late or not at all, stays awake, or the line state does not match the network status. In practice the code appears mainly on hybrids: FCA fixes it on the Pacifica plug-in hybrid and the Wrangler 4xe with module software, where it remained as a permanent code that blocked emission inspections; GM's hybrid integration module lists it as a fault bundle. No manufacturer publishes thresholds or timing.

causes.label: Module software (false setting, permanent code does not clear)
Wake-up line or connector open or shorted
Weak 12 V battery, voltage dips at wake-up
Engine or hybrid control module faulty

P06E5.title: Glow Plug Control Module 1 Performance
P06E5.description: P06E5 means glow plug control module 1 does not respond correctly to the glow command: its outputs do not switch or its internal drivers report faults or overheating. Ford's 2023 6.7 L and 3.0 L Power Stroke list P06E5 among the glow module checks, run continuously, with a fault after about 1 s when internal drivers for glow plugs, DEF heaters or relays fail to switch or overheat for more than 1 s – Ford does not assign each threshold to a single code. GM files the same check under P064C: on the L5P a plug commanded on but drawing under 3.2 A with 0 V at the plug for 3.5 s, on the LML a total current under 6.6 A; both after two trips. The plugs then heat partly or not at all, with hard cold starts and white smoke. There is no limp mode.

causes.label: Glow plug control module faulty internally (drivers do not switch)
Poor supply or ground of the module (main feed, fuse, ground)
Module overheating (mounting location, short at a plug)
Module software

symptoms: Check engine light, possibly glow plug/wait-to-start lamp
White smoke and rough running after cold start
Often stored together with plug codes or P064C/P263C

P06E6.title: Sensor Power Supply C Circuit/Open
P06E6.description: 'Sensor power supply' is a separate J2012 family next to the 5 V sensor reference (P0697 ff): an additional supply from the module for sensors or drivers – in GM hybrids a 15 V supply for resolvers and inverter gate drivers, there as supplies A and B. Supply C is a third such circuit. P06E6 is the general or open-circuit code of supply C: the module measures the output of its supply regulator and finds the voltage missing. Low and high are P06E7/P06E8. Only Mitsubishi's 2022 Outlander lists P06E6 as a main code with sub-codes for low and high, called internal control module, without thresholds or the sensors fed. All sensors on the circuit then deliver invalid values, so several follow-up codes and limp mode are possible.

causes.label: Open circuit or connector problem in the supply circuit
Short in the supply wire or a supplied sensor
Supply regulator inside the module faulty
Vehicle under- or overvoltage

symptoms: Several sensor codes at the same time
Limp mode or reduced power possible
Possibly starting problems or rough running

P06E7.title: Sensor Power Supply C Circuit Low
P06E7.description: 'Sensor power supply' is a separate J2012 family next to the 5 V sensor reference (P0697 ff): an additional supply from the module for sensors or drivers – in GM hybrids a 15 V supply for resolvers and inverter gate drivers, there as supplies A and B. Supply C is a third such circuit. P06E7 means the voltage of supply C is too low – a short to ground, an overload from a supplied sensor or a failed regulator; Mitsubishi marks it as a short-to-ground sub-code. Open circuit and high are P06E6/P06E8. Only Mitsubishi's 2022 Outlander lists P06E6 as a main code with sub-codes for low and high, called internal control module, without thresholds or the sensors fed. All sensors on the circuit then deliver invalid values, so several follow-up codes and limp mode are possible.

causes.label: Short to ground in the supply wire or a supplied sensor
Supply regulator inside the module faulty
Connector problem in the supply circuit
Vehicle undervoltage

symptoms: Several sensor codes at the same time
Limp mode or reduced power possible
Possibly starting problems or rough running

P06E8.title: Sensor Power Supply C Circuit High
P06E8.description: 'Sensor power supply' is a separate J2012 family next to the 5 V sensor reference (P0697 ff): an additional supply from the module for sensors or drivers – in GM hybrids a 15 V supply for resolvers and inverter gate drivers, there as supplies A and B. Supply C is a third such circuit. P06E8 means the voltage of supply C is too high – external voltage, a short to positive or a regulator fault; Mitsubishi marks it as a short-to-battery sub-code. Open circuit and low are P06E6/P06E7. Only Mitsubishi's 2022 Outlander lists P06E6 as a main code with sub-codes for low and high, called internal control module, without thresholds or the sensors fed. All sensors on the circuit then deliver invalid values, so several follow-up codes and limp mode are possible.

causes.label: Short to positive in the supply wire or a supplied sensor
Supply regulator inside the module faulty
Vehicle overvoltage (alternator)

symptoms: Several sensor codes at the same time
Limp mode or reduced power possible
Possibly starting problems or rough running

P06E9.title: Engine Starter Performance
P06E9.description: On cars with stop-start or keyless start the engine module operates the starter relay itself and watches the start: if cranking is commanded but the engine does not turn, turns too slowly or the start is aborted, it sets P06E9. CARB counts an engine start from 150 rpm below warm idle. Thresholds for speed and time are not published. Bulletins show both sides: VW traces P06E9 on the Tiguan to dirt inside the starter that opens its contacts intermittently, and on the Atlas has relays, battery and voltage drop checked; Audi's SQ5 and FCA's Jeep Compass need module software instead. Ford lists P06E9 among the starter faults that disable stop-start.

causes.label: Starter worn or solenoid contacts intermittently open
Weak battery, voltage drop on main cables or ground
Starter relay or its control
Engine module software

symptoms: Check engine light depending on manufacturer (FCA: yes)

P06EA.title: NOx Sensor Processor Performance Bank 1 Sensor 1
P06EA.description: A modern NOx sensor is a smart sensor: a ceramic sensing element with pump cells and heater plus its own control unit with a microcontroller, which regulates the pump currents, calculates NOx and oxygen and sends them to the engine module over CAN. P06EA means this control unit of sensor 1 (before the SCR catalyst) reports an internal fault – its self-tests of RAM and ROM or EEPROM checksums fail – so the electronics, not the sensing element, are at fault. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code: Ford's 2023 diesels run exactly these checks continuously, with a fault after 5 s, but report them as P2200; GM uses the P2200 family and U029D/U029E. The NOx value is then invalid, so SCR dosing runs on a model or stops, a warning appears and, depending on market, a countdown to a start lock.

causes.label: Faulty electronics in the NOx sensor control unit
Moisture or corrosion in control unit or connector (underbody location)
Under- or overvoltage or dips in the sensor supply
Unsuitable replacement sensor or software

symptoms: Check engine light or emissions warning
Message to check AdBlue/emission system, possibly countdown to start lock
Follow-up codes for SCR efficiency or NOx plausibility

P06EB.title: NOx Sensor Processor Performance Bank 1 Sensor 2
P06EB.description: A modern NOx sensor is a smart sensor: a ceramic sensing element with pump cells and heater plus its own control unit with a microcontroller, which regulates the pump currents, calculates NOx and oxygen and sends them to the engine module over CAN. P06EB means this control unit of sensor 2 (after the SCR catalyst) reports an internal fault – its self-tests of RAM and ROM or EEPROM checksums fail – so the electronics, not the sensing element, are at fault. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code: Ford's 2023 diesels run exactly these checks continuously, with a fault after 5 s, but report them as P229E; GM uses the P2200 family and U029D/U029E. The NOx value is then invalid, so SCR dosing runs on a model or stops, a warning appears and, depending on market, a countdown to a start lock.

causes.label: Faulty electronics in the NOx sensor control unit
Moisture or corrosion in control unit or connector (underbody location)
Under- or overvoltage or dips in the sensor supply
Unsuitable replacement sensor or software

symptoms: Check engine light or emissions warning
Message to check AdBlue/emission system, possibly countdown to start lock
Follow-up codes for SCR efficiency or NOx plausibility

P06EC.title: Fuel Injector Control Module Requested MIL Illumination
P06EC.description: P06EC is a notice code like P0700: a separate fuel injector control module has stored an emission-related fault of its own and asks the engine module over CAN to switch on the check engine light. The actual fault is stored in that module and must be read there; simple OBD readers show only P06EC. GM uses it on the 2019 Corvette ZR1, whose LT5 engine adds port injection driven by its own module with its own crank and cam inputs; the code runs continuously from key on and is listed as type A without its own MIL – the lamp comes from the module's fault. Older separate injector modules (Ford 6.0 L Power Stroke, GM bi-fuel CNG trucks) report through P0611 or U codes instead. Any limp mode follows the module's fault.

causes.label: Emission-related fault in the injector control module or its injectors/sensors (code stored there)
Supply, ground or relay problem of the module
Internal module fault (memory, processor)
Software level of engine or injector module

symptoms: Generic scanner shows only P06EC – details in the injector module
Depending on the fault, power loss, misfire or limp mode

P06ED.title: Engine RPM Output Circuit Low
P06ED.description: The engine module turns the crankshaft signal into a cleaned-up square wave for the tachometer, transmission or body-builder modules – Saab's 1999 9-3, for example, sends two pulses per revolution, about 30 Hz at idle. P06ED means this output is too low, typically shorted to ground, so it can no longer switch high. It is the counterpart of P0654 (open circuit) and P06EE (high). CARB requires output circuits to be checked; the signal is emission-relevant only if a receiving module uses it for emission functions. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; the description follows CARB, the component and P0654. The tachometer then reads zero or jumps, and modules using the signal lose it, while the engine runs normally.

causes.label: Speed output wire chafing against ground
Receiver (instrument, add-on device) shorted internally
Aftermarket tachometer or accessory wired wrongly
Engine module driver stage

P06EE.title: Engine RPM Output Circuit High
P06EE.description: The engine module turns the crankshaft signal into a cleaned-up square wave for the tachometer, transmission or body-builder modules – Saab's 1999 9-3, for example, sends two pulses per revolution, about 30 Hz at idle. P06EE means this output is too high, typically shorted to supply voltage, so it can no longer switch to ground; the driver may shut down for protection. It is the counterpart of P0654 (open circuit) and P06ED (low). CARB requires output circuits to be checked. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; the description follows CARB, the component and P0654. The tachometer then reads nothing or full scale, and modules using the signal lose it, while the engine runs normally.

causes.label: Output wire shorted to 12 V
Wrongly connected accessory (speed pick-up)
Receiving device faulty
Engine module

symptoms: Tachometer shows nothing or full scale

P06EF.title: Engine Restart Performance
P06EF.description: P06EF concerns the automatic restart after the system itself has stopped the engine – stop-start or hybrid. The restart, by starter, reinforced stop-start starter or belt starter-generator, takes too long or fails. CARB does not count such a commanded shutdown as a stall. No manufacturer publishes the time limit. VW's Tiguan bulletins list P06EF together with P06E9 and trace both to dirt inside the starter; FCA fixes it on the 2019 Jeep Wrangler with engine-module software and lights the check engine light. Stop-start is then disabled. Besides the starter, a weak stop-start battery or fuel and ignition problems at restart can be the cause.

causes.label: Starter or starter-generator worn, contacts intermittently open
Engine module software
Weak stop-start battery (AGM/EFB) or battery sensor
Fuel pressure or ignition at restart

symptoms: Engine does not restart or restarts late after stop-start

P06F0.title: Reductant Control Module Internal Temperature Sensor Circuit
P06F0.description: Some SCR diesels have a separate reductant control module that drives the DEF pump, heaters and dosing valve – Ford calls it the pump motor controller (fault above 130 °C under P20FF), GM's L5P an SCR power module. It measures its own board temperature with an internal sensor to protect itself from heat. P06F0 is the general circuit fault of this internal sensor: the signal is missing, open or cannot be evaluated. Range, low and high are P06F1–P06F3; the DEF tank temperature sensor is a different part. No manufacturer document available to us uses P06F0–P06F3; Ford and GM report related faults under P20FF or own codes. Without a valid temperature the module limits or stops heaters and pump, so dosing is restricted and an SCR warning, up to a start lock countdown, may follow.

causes.label: Reductant control module or pump unit faulty (sensor is on the board)
Water ingress or corrosion in the module (DEF crystals, underbody location)
Supply or ground problems at the module
Module software or calibration

symptoms: Check engine light or SCR warning
Message to check AdBlue system, possibly countdown to start lock
DEF heating or pump inactive (no thawing in frost)

P06F1.title: Reductant Control Module Internal Temperature Sensor Range/Performance
P06F1.description: Some SCR diesels have a separate reductant control module that drives the DEF pump, heaters and dosing valve – Ford calls it the pump motor controller (fault above 130 °C under P20FF), GM's L5P an SCR power module. It measures its own board temperature with an internal sensor to protect itself from heat. P06F1 means the signal is electrically valid but implausible – it jumps, freezes or differs from comparison temperatures such as ambient or tank temperature after a long stop. Circuit faults are P06F0, P06F2 and P06F3. No manufacturer document available to us uses P06F0–P06F3; Ford and GM report related faults under P20FF or own codes. Without a valid temperature the module limits or stops heaters and pump, so dosing is restricted and an SCR warning, up to a start lock countdown, may follow.

causes.label: Reductant control module or pump unit faulty (sensor is on the board)
Water ingress or corrosion in the module (DEF crystals, underbody location)
Supply or ground problems at the module
Module software or calibration

symptoms: Check engine light or SCR warning
Message to check AdBlue system, possibly countdown to start lock
DEF heating or pump inactive (no thawing in frost)

P06F2.title: Reductant Control Module Internal Temperature Sensor Circuit Low
P06F2.description: Some SCR diesels have a separate reductant control module that drives the DEF pump, heaters and dosing valve – Ford calls it the pump motor controller (fault above 130 °C under P20FF), GM's L5P an SCR power module. It measures its own board temperature with an internal sensor to protect itself from heat.
