symptoms: Transmission stays in one gear, no further shifts

P072F.title: Stuck in Gear 4
P072F.description: Ford's DPS6 dry dual-clutch transmission moves its gears with two electrically driven shift drums whose position is read by Hall sensors: drum A shifts 1st, 3rd and 5th, drum B reverse, 2nd, 4th and 6th. Ford's 2012 summary lists 'stuck in gear' codes for each drum: the module commands the drum out of a gear, but the gear stays engaged. It gives no thresholds or MIL rating. P072F is the code for drum B: fourth gear cannot be disengaged. The car stays in fourth or sub-gearbox B is locked out. Slip in fourth gear is P0734.

causes.label: Shift fork or synchronizer for this gear sticking
Shift drum B motor, Hall position sensing or driver faulty
Transmission module
On planetary automatics: clutch or brake not releasing (sticking valve)

symptoms: Transmission stays in one gear, no further shifts

P0730.title: Incorrect Gear Ratio
P0730.description: P0730 reports a wrong transmission ratio without assigning it to a gear. Two uses are documented. Older Aisin-type automatics (a 2006 GM table, Saab's 9-5 of 2002) set it when fourth or fifth gear shows the ratio of third – a shift solenoid (Saab: S3) is not switching; GM lights the MIL at once, Saab enters limp mode. GM's continuously variable transmissions of 2023 and 2025 use it when the pulleys do not reach the commanded variator ratio – the belt or chain slips or clamping pressure is too low – after one trip. Ford and newer GM step automatics use gear-specific or clutch valve codes instead. Check fluid level and condition first.

causes.label: Fluid level or quality (CVT fluid or ATF)
Shift solenoid or pressure control valve sticking or faulty
Clutch or brake wear, or worn variator belt, chain or pulleys
Faulty speed sensor signal

symptoms: Slipping, engine speed rises without drive
Wrong gear or missing upper gears, limp mode
Check engine light (GM) or transmission warning

P0731.title: Gear 1 Incorrect Ratio
P0731.description: The transmission module divides input (turbine) speed by output speed and compares the result with the ratio of the commanded gear; a deviation means slip – a clutch or brake not holding, too little pressure – or a wrong gear. Thresholds: Ford more than 30 rpm off for 1.8 s three times (diesel 2023: over 20 % for 12 s), GM's 2006 tables and the Allison 1000 converter slip of 200–230 rpm for 2.25 s after one trip, Saab's Aisin boxes over 20 % twelve times without MIL. P0731 concerns first gear. A 2006 GM table uses a tighter 4 % limit here and caps output speed at 1260 rpm; Saab's 2002 9-5 flags 3 % with the brake released. With a one-way clutch in first, slip shows as slipping when pulling away. On GM manual transmissions it checks the gear position sensor instead.

causes.label: Fluid level too low or fluid worn or contaminated
Clutch or brake for first gear worn (linings, piston seal)
Sticking shift or pressure valve, leaking valve body gasket, blocked passages
GM manual transmissions only: gear position sensor faulty or not learned

symptoms: Slipping or flare in first gear, engine speed higher than expected
Limp mode (Aisin: second gear and reverse only), transmission warning
Check engine light depending on manufacturer

P0732.title: Gear 2 Incorrect Ratio
P0732.description: The transmission module divides input (turbine) speed by output speed and compares the result with the ratio of the commanded gear; a deviation means slip – a clutch or brake not holding, too little pressure – or a wrong gear. Thresholds: Ford more than 30 rpm off for 1.8 s three times (diesel 2023: over 20 % for 12 s), GM's 2006 tables and the Allison 1000 converter slip of 200–230 rpm for 2.25 s after one trip, Saab's Aisin boxes over 20 % twelve times without MIL. P0732 concerns second gear. In the Aisin limp mode, with all solenoids unpowered, second gear is the one left – so slip there also affects limp-home driving. Ford stores it only if the fault fits no particular solenoid. On GM manual transmissions it checks the gear position sensor instead.

causes.label: Fluid level too low or fluid worn or contaminated
Clutch or brake for second gear worn (linings, piston seal)
Sticking shift or pressure valve, leaking valve body gasket, blocked passages
GM manual transmissions only: gear position sensor faulty or not learned

symptoms: Slipping or flare in second gear, engine speed higher than expected
Limp mode (Aisin: second gear and reverse only), transmission warning
Check engine light depending on manufacturer

P0733.title: Gear 3 Incorrect Ratio
P0733.description: The transmission module divides input (turbine) speed by output speed and compares the result with the ratio of the commanded gear; a deviation means slip – a clutch or brake not holding, too little pressure – or a wrong gear. Thresholds: Ford more than 30 rpm off for 1.8 s three times (diesel 2023: over 20 % for 12 s), GM's 2006 tables and the Allison 1000 converter slip of 200–230 rpm for 2.25 s after one trip, Saab's Aisin boxes over 20 % twelve times without MIL. P0733 concerns third gear. Slip typically shows as flare on the 2–3 shift. If fourth or fifth gear shows the ratio of third, Aisin-type logic sets P0730 instead. Ford stores it only if the fault fits no particular solenoid. On GM manual transmissions it checks the gear position sensor.

causes.label: Fluid level too low or fluid worn or contaminated
Clutch or brake for third gear worn (linings, piston seal)
Sticking shift or pressure valve, leaking valve body gasket, blocked passages
GM manual transmissions only: gear position sensor faulty or not learned

symptoms: Slipping or flare in third gear, engine speed higher than expected
Limp mode (Aisin: second gear and reverse only), transmission warning
Check engine light depending on manufacturer

P0734.title: Gear 4 Incorrect Ratio
P0734.description: The transmission module divides input (turbine) speed by output speed and compares the result with the ratio of the commanded gear; a deviation means slip – a clutch or brake not holding, too little pressure – or a wrong gear. Thresholds: Ford more than 30 rpm off for 1.8 s three times (diesel 2023: over 20 % for 12 s), GM's 2006 tables and the Allison 1000 converter slip of 200–230 rpm for 2.25 s after one trip, Saab's Aisin boxes over 20 % twelve times without MIL. P0734 concerns fourth gear. A 2006 GM table separates it explicitly from P0730: fourth gear showing the ratio of third is P0730, any other deviation P0734. Slip shows as raised engine speed or no upshift into fourth. On GM manual transmissions it checks the gear position sensor.

causes.label: Fluid level too low or fluid worn or contaminated
Clutch or brake for fourth gear worn (linings, piston seal)
Sticking shift or pressure valve, leaking valve body gasket, blocked passages
GM manual transmissions only: gear position sensor faulty or not learned

symptoms: Slipping or flare in fourth gear, engine speed higher than expected
Limp mode (Aisin: second gear and reverse only), transmission warning
Check engine light depending on manufacturer

P0735.title: Gear 5 Incorrect Ratio
P0735.description: The transmission module divides input (turbine) speed by output speed and compares the result with the ratio of the commanded gear; a deviation means slip – a clutch or brake not holding, too little pressure – or a wrong gear. Thresholds: Ford more than 30 rpm off for 1.8 s three times (diesel 2023: over 20 % for 12 s), GM's 2006 tables and the Allison 1000 converter slip of 200–230 rpm for 2.25 s after one trip, Saab's Aisin boxes over 20 % twelve times without MIL. P0735 concerns fifth gear. Slip shows as raised engine speed in fifth or no fifth gear at all; the Allison 1000 checks it with the same slip logic as the other gears. On GM manual transmissions it checks the gear position sensor instead.

causes.label: Fluid level too low or fluid worn or contaminated
Clutch or brake for fifth gear worn (linings, piston seal)
Sticking shift or pressure valve, leaking valve body gasket, blocked passages
GM manual transmissions only: gear position sensor faulty or not learned

symptoms: Slipping or flare in fifth gear, engine speed higher than expected
Limp mode (Aisin: second gear and reverse only), transmission warning
Check engine light depending on manufacturer

P0736.title: Reverse Incorrect Ratio
P0736.description: The transmission module divides input (turbine) speed by output speed and compares the result with the ratio of the commanded gear; a deviation means slip – a clutch or brake not holding, too little pressure – or a wrong gear. Thresholds: Ford more than 30 rpm off for 1.8 s three times (diesel 2023: over 20 % for 12 s), GM's 2006 tables and the Allison 1000 converter slip of 200–230 rpm for 2.25 s after one trip, Saab's Aisin boxes over 20 % twelve times without MIL. P0736 concerns reverse. The check needs reversing under load, so short manoeuvres are often not enough; a 2006 GM table sets it after 2 s of slip above 100 rpm without the diagnostic gear step used for forward gears. Slipping or delayed engagement of reverse, especially uphill, is typical; a worn reverse clutch or low/reverse brake is the usual cause.

causes.label: Fluid level or condition
Reverse clutch or low/reverse brake worn
Valve body, shift valve or gasket
Oil pump or pump cover

symptoms: Delayed or slipping engagement of reverse
No reverse uphill or under load
Transmission warning, limp mode, check engine light depending on manufacturer

P0737.title: TCM Engine Speed Output Circuit
P0737.description: Some transmission modules pass an engine speed signal on to other devices such as a tachometer over a wire of their own. CARB requires output circuits to be checked. No manufacturer document available to us uses P0737–P0739 – engine speed is shared over CAN today; the description follows CARB and the engine module's own speed output (P0654), which sends, for example, two pulses per revolution. P0737 is the general circuit fault of this output; low and high are P0738/P0739. Not to be confused with the engine speed input at the transmission module (P0725 ff). A tachometer or dependent display then reads wrong or nothing, while driving is usually unaffected.

causes.label: Wire to the receiver open or shorted
Receiver (e.g. instrument cluster) shorted internally
Connector corroded
Driver stage in the transmission module faulty

symptoms: Tachometer or dependent display not working or wrong

P0738.title: TCM Engine Speed Output Circuit Low
P0738.description: Some transmission modules pass an engine speed signal on to other devices such as a tachometer over a wire of their own. CARB requires output circuits to be checked. No manufacturer document available to us uses P0737–P0739 – engine speed is shared over CAN today; the description follows CARB and the engine module's own speed output (P0654), which sends, for example, two pulses per revolution. P0738 means this output is too low, typically shorted to ground, so it can no longer switch high. The opposite is P0739, the general fault P0737. A tachometer or dependent display then reads zero or jumps, while driving is usually unaffected.

causes.label: Output wire shorted to ground
Receiver shorted internally
Connector corroded
Driver stage in the transmission module faulty

P0739.title: TCM Engine Speed Output Circuit High
P0739.description: Some transmission modules pass an engine speed signal on to other devices such as a tachometer over a wire of their own. CARB requires output circuits to be checked. No manufacturer document available to us uses P0737–P0739 – engine speed is shared over CAN today; the description follows CARB and the engine module's own speed output (P0654), which sends, for example, two pulses per revolution. P0739 means this output is too high, typically shorted to positive or, depending on the driver, open, so it can no longer switch to ground. The opposite is P0738, the general fault P0737. A tachometer or dependent display then reads nothing or full scale, while driving is usually unaffected.

causes.label: Output wire shorted to positive or open
Receiver faulty
Connector corroded
Driver stage in the transmission module faulty

symptoms: Tachometer shows nothing or full scale

P073A.title: Stuck in Gear 5
P073A.description: Ford's DPS6 dry dual-clutch transmission moves its gears with two electrically driven shift drums whose position is read by Hall sensors: drum A shifts 1st, 3rd and 5th, drum B reverse, 2nd, 4th and 6th. Ford's 2012 summary lists 'stuck in gear' codes for each drum: the module commands the drum out of a gear, but the gear stays engaged. It gives no thresholds or MIL rating. P073A is the code for drum A: fifth gear cannot be disengaged. The car stays in fifth – very weak pulling away – or sub-gearbox A is locked out. Slip in fifth gear is P0735.

causes.label: Shift fork or synchronizer for this gear sticking
Shift drum A motor, Hall position sensing or driver faulty
Transmission module
On planetary automatics: clutch or brake not releasing (sticking valve)

symptoms: Transmission stays in one gear, no further shifts

P073B.title: Stuck in Gear 6
P073B.description: Ford's DPS6 dry dual-clutch transmission moves its gears with two electrically driven shift drums whose position is read by Hall sensors: drum A shifts 1st, 3rd and 5th, drum B reverse, 2nd, 4th and 6th. Ford's 2012 summary lists 'stuck in gear' codes for each drum: the module commands the drum out of a gear, but the gear stays engaged. It gives no thresholds or MIL rating. P073B is the code for drum B: sixth gear cannot be disengaged. The car stays in sixth – it can hardly pull away – or sub-gearbox B is locked out. Slip in sixth gear is P0729.

causes.label: Shift fork or synchronizer for this gear sticking
Shift drum B motor, Hall position sensing or driver faulty
Transmission module
On planetary automatics: clutch or brake not releasing (sticking valve)

symptoms: Transmission stays in one gear, no further shifts

P073C.title: Stuck in Gear 7
P073C.description: Ford's DPS6 dry dual-clutch transmission moves its gears with two electrically driven shift drums whose position is read by Hall sensors: drum A shifts 1st, 3rd and 5th, drum B reverse, 2nd, 4th and 6th. Ford's 2012 summary lists 'stuck in gear' codes for each drum: the module commands the drum out of a gear, but the gear stays engaged. It gives no thresholds or MIL rating. P073C would be the code for a seventh gear that cannot be disengaged, which only exists on transmissions with seven or more gears. No manufacturer document available to us uses it – the six-speed DPS6 has no seventh gear, GM's 9- and 10-speeds report clutch valve codes and Ford's 10R80 solenoid codes instead. Slip in seventh gear is P076F.

causes.label: Shift fork or synchronizer for this gear sticking
Shift drum B motor, Hall position sensing or driver faulty
Transmission module
On planetary automatics: clutch or brake not releasing (sticking valve)

symptoms: Transmission stays in one gear, no further shifts

P073D.title: Unable to Engage Neutral
P073D.description: P073D means neutral is commanded but not reached or not held. GM uses it on vehicles with electronic gear selection (shift-by-wire, e.g. Cadillac XT4): the selector or engine module compares commanded and actual range from the range sensor and flags it after 1.8–2 s in the selector module or 10 s in the engine module, after two trips. For Ford's 6F35 the supplier Sonnax describes a mechanical cause: a forward or direct clutch dragging in neutral, visible as turbine speed staying only 200–400 rpm below engine speed. The car may creep in N; range changes may be locked. The opposite, stuck in neutral, is P072A.

causes.label: Ford 6F35: forward or direct clutch dragging (balance piston, plates, seal)
Shift-by-wire: range actuator or park module, range sensor or its calibration
Valve body (manual valve, missing check ball, sticking solenoid)
CAN communication or control module

symptoms: Vehicle creeps in N or engine is loaded when shifting to N
N selection not accepted, warning message
Check engine light after two trips (GM)

P073E.title: Unable to Engage Reverse
P073E.description: P073E means reverse is commanded but not reached. Two uses are documented. With electronic gear selection (shift-by-wire) GM compares the commanded range with the actual range reported by the transmission and flags it if reverse is not reached within 1.8–3 s in the selector or diesel engine module, or 10 s in petrol engine modules, after two trips; GM bulletins name a range actuator centred wrongly (LaCrosse, XT5) and software after an over-the-air update (2025 Equinox/Terrain). On dual-clutch transmissions (2020–23 Corvette, Maserati MC20) it means the reverse gear cannot be engaged. Stuck in reverse is P072B, slip in reverse P0736.

causes.label: Range actuator or park module centred wrongly or faulty (shift-by-wire)
Module software (e.g. after an over-the-air update)
Range sensor reports the wrong actual range
Reverse clutch or brake, valve or shift fork (DCT)
Fluid level or system pressure

symptoms: No reverse, or R not accepted
Transmission warning, check engine light after two trips (GM)
Display shows R but the vehicle does not reverse

P073F.title: Unable to Engage Gear 1
P073F.description: 'Unable to engage' means the transmission does not reach the commanded gear – the opposite of 'stuck in gear', where a gear cannot be disengaged. Documented users are dual-clutch transmissions, whose shift forks are moved hydraulically and watched by travel sensors: GM's 8-speed in the 2020–23 Corvette, Maserati's MC20 and – for the odd gears only – Acura's RLX Sport Hybrid, whose 'odd gear monitor' is part of an emission recall with permanent codes. No manufacturer publishes thresholds. P073F means the first gear, on the odd sub-gearbox, cannot be engaged; a gear that will not disengage is P072C, slip in an engaged gear P0731. GM's bulletin first runs a learn procedure and cleans valves only if system pressure codes are present; Maserati checks system pressure (20–30 bar). If neither helps, the mechanics are at fault.

causes.label: Shift fork valve or solenoid in the mechatronic unit sticking (dirt, wear)
System pressure unstable or too low (pressure valve, pump, fluid level)
Shift fork, sleeve, synchronizer or dogs damaged
Learned shift fork or clutch values lost or wrong
Module software or calibration

symptoms: Transmission warning or check engine light, possibly limp mode with one sub-gearbox locked out
Jerking, delayed pulling away or shifting

P0740.title: Torque Converter Clutch Circuit/Open
P0740.description: The torque converter clutch (lock-up) connects pump and turbine mechanically; a solenoid – on/off, pulse-width modulated or proportional – moves a control valve in the valve body. Slip is engine speed minus turbine speed. Manufacturers do not use P0740–P0744 uniformly: Ford uses P0740 for open, P0742 for short to ground and P0744 for short to power, and reports stuck on as P2758. P0740 concerns the control circuit of the converter clutch solenoid. Ford flags an open circuit when the driver feedback line disagrees with the command for 0.5–5 s, with MIL; a 2006 GM table checks 0/12 V with more than 43 of 50 failed counts after two trips – newer GM units use P2761/P2763/P2764. FCA's Ram 6.7 reads P0740 as converter slip out of range and moved it to two trips by software in 2013. The clutch is then switched off: higher engine speed when cruising, more fuel, hotter fluid.

causes.label: Open or corroded harness or transmission pass-through connector
Converter clutch solenoid coil open
Internal transmission harness or mechatronic unit
Driver stage in the module faulty
FCA: actual converter slip (clutch wear, fluid) or software

symptoms: Check engine light or transmission warning
No lock-up: engine speed about 100–300 rpm higher when cruising
Higher fuel consumption, hotter transmission fluid

P0741.title: Torque Converter Clutch Circuit Performance/Stuck Off
P0741.description: P0741 means the converter clutch does not lock although commanded – slip stays too high while the circuit is electrically fine. Thresholds: GM's T43 at least 130 rpm for 5 s twice, the 6T70 50 rpm for 5 s three times, Saab's Aisin AF40 over 100 rpm for 2 s, all after two trips; Ford over 100–200 rpm or a speed ratio below 0.93 over five lock-up events; Subaru engine speed more than 9/8 of target for 10.2 s. The module then locks out the clutch, sometimes the top gear, and uses a hot-mode shift pattern. Low or burnt fluid, a worn control valve in the valve body and a glazed converter clutch are the usual causes; Hyundai's 8-speed bulletin calls for a new converter.

causes.label: Fluid level too low, old or burnt fluid
Converter clutch control valve worn or sticking, bore worn
Lock-up clutch in the converter worn or glazed
Solenoid mechanically sluggish (electrically fine)
Leaking turbine shaft seals or pump

symptoms: Check engine light or transmission warning
Higher engine speed when cruising, 'rubber band' feel
Possibly shudder when the clutch applies

P0742.title: Torque Converter Clutch Circuit Stuck On
P0742.description: P0742 means the converter clutch stays applied although commanded off – there is almost no slip. GM's T43 flags −50 to +13 rpm for 1.5 s six times and the 6T70 −20 to +30 rpm for 2.5 s, both after one trip; Allison and Saab's Aisin AF40 after two trips, the AF40 also when the engine stalls without slip. Typical is the engine stalling when stopping or when selecting D or R, plus jerking at low speed. Note the different uses: Ford's P0742 is a short to ground in the clutch solenoid circuit (stuck on is P2758 there), and Saab's 9-3 of 2003 uses it for a mechanical lock-up fault.

causes.label: Converter clutch control valve sticking in the applied position
Solenoid stuck open (or short to ground with low-side control)
Lock-up clutch seized in the converter
Wrong fluid level or contaminated fluid
Engine or turbine speed signal implausible

symptoms: Engine stalls when stopping or selecting D/R
Jerking or bucking at low speed
Check engine light or transmission warning

P0743.title: Torque Converter Clutch Circuit Electrical
P0743.description: The torque converter clutch (lock-up) connects pump and turbine mechanically; a solenoid – on/off, pulse-width modulated or proportional – moves a control valve in the valve body. Slip is engine speed minus turbine speed. Manufacturers do not use P0740–P0744 uniformly: Ford uses P0740 for open, P0742 for short to ground and P0744 for short to power, and reports stuck on as P2758. P0743 is the collective electrical code for the converter clutch solenoid circuit – open, short to ground or to positive – detected by terminal voltage, driver feedback or current. Subaru flags it after 0.14 s and lights the MIL after two trips, Saab's 9-3 of 2003 above 1356 mA for 500 ms, Allison after 1.5 s; older Ford transmissions also use it. The clutch is switched off; Saab's Aisin boxes go into limp mode, Subaru does not.

causes.label: Transmission harness or pass-through connector (corrosion, chafing, oil in connector)
Solenoid coil open or shorted
Internal harness or mechatronic unit
Driver stage in the transmission or engine module

symptoms: Check engine light or transmission warning
No lock-up: engine speed about 100–300 rpm higher when cruising

P0744.title: Torque Converter Clutch Circuit Intermittent
P0744.description: The torque converter clutch (lock-up) connects pump and turbine mechanically; a solenoid – on/off, pulse-width modulated or proportional – moves a control valve in the valve body. Slip is engine speed minus turbine speed. Manufacturers do not use P0740–P0744 uniformly: Ford uses P0740 for open, P0742 for short to ground and P0744 for short to power, and reports stuck on as P2758. In J2012 P0744 is an intermittent fault in the converter clutch circuit, but no manufacturer document available to us uses it that way: Ford flags a short to power via the driver feedback line after 0.5–5 s with MIL, and Nissan's CVT bulletins treat it as a functional converter fault checked at the valve body and belt. GM does not use it. Short interruptions make the clutch drop out and reapply, and lock-up may be disabled for the trip.

causes.label: Loose contact or corrosion at the transmission connector or harness
Ford: control wire shorted to positive
Solenoid with temperature-dependent winding fault
Nissan CVT: converter or valve body mechanical

symptoms: Lock-up missing or jerky at times

P0745.title: Pressure Control Solenoid A
P0745.description: Pressure control solenoid A sets line or clutch pressure by current; most are 'normally high', so with no current – as in limp mode – maximum pressure applies. 'A' is usually the line pressure valve, on GM clutch-to-clutch transmissions (6T, 8L, 9T) the pressure valve of clutch 1. Ford does not use P0745–P0749 but P0960–P0963. P0745 is the general code for this valve; the sub-codes P0746–P0749 follow. It is documented on Mitsubishi CVTs as a current plausibility check: at most 400 mA while 750 mA or more is commanded for 5 s, or 1.34 A or more for 1 s. A failure usually leaves the valve unpowered, so pressure goes to maximum: harsh shifts and, depending on the transmission, limp mode in a fixed gear.

causes.label: Pressure control solenoid (coil) faulty
Transmission harness or connector
Contaminated fluid, valve sluggish
Transmission module

symptoms: Limp mode in a fixed gear
Transmission warning or check engine light

P0746.title: Pressure Control Solenoid A Performance/Stuck Off
P0746.description: Pressure control solenoid A sets line or clutch pressure by current; most are 'normally high', so with no current – as in limp mode – maximum pressure applies. 'A' is usually the line pressure valve, on GM clutch-to-clutch transmissions (6T, 8L, 9T) the pressure valve of clutch 1. Ford does not use P0745–P0749 but P0960–P0963. P0746 means the valve is electrically fine but the commanded pressure does not build. GM's clutch-to-clutch units detect it as slip: 400 rpm or more for 1.5 s (T87), or clutch 1 slip over 200 rpm for 3 s three times (9-speed), after one trip; Allison when the oncoming clutch does not apply. Mitsubishi's dual-clutch flags 500 mA current deviation. Slipping or flaring on shifts, a missed gear and limp mode follow; GM's 9-speed bulletin checks clutch plates and replaces the valve body.

causes.label: Pressure valve or spool worn or dirty
Fluid level too low, burnt fluid, clogged filter
Clutch plates or piston seals of the affected clutch worn
Line pressure too low (pump, main regulator)
Learned values missing after repair

symptoms: Slipping or engine flare on shifts
Gear not reached, limp mode in a fixed gear
Check engine light or transmission warning

P0747.title: Pressure Control Solenoid A Stuck On
P0747.description: Pressure control solenoid A sets line or clutch pressure by current; most are 'normally high', so with no current – as in limp mode – maximum pressure applies. 'A' is usually the line pressure valve, on GM clutch-to-clutch transmissions (6T, 8L, 9T) the pressure valve of clutch 1. Ford does not use P0745–P0749 but P0960–P0963. P0747 means the valve is electrically fine but pressure stays applied. On GM's clutch-to-clutch units the off-going clutch 1 does not release – slip stays below 50 rpm (9-speed, 0.8 s on loaded downshifts), and Allison flags 25 rpm or less for 0.3–1 s, both after one trip. On line pressure valves it means permanently high pressure. Harsh, abrupt shifts, a tied-up transmission and a default gear follow. GM noted false settings on 2017 8-speeds: clear and retest first.

causes.label: Pressure or clutch valve or spool sticking (dirt, debris)
Valve body worn
Software or false setting
Wrong or contaminated fluid
Clutch plates stuck or burnt

symptoms: Transmission ties up, engine speed drops on shifts

P0748.title: Pressure Control Solenoid A Electrical
P0748.description: Pressure control solenoid A sets line or clutch pressure by current; most are 'normally high', so with no current – as in limp mode – maximum pressure applies. 'A' is usually the line pressure valve, on GM clutch-to-clutch transmissions (6T, 8L, 9T) the pressure valve of clutch 1. Ford does not use P0745–P0749 but P0960–P0963. P0748 is the electrical code of this valve, checked by current, duty cycle or terminal voltage: Subaru after 0.14 s with MIL after two trips and limp mode in third, Allison against an 8 Ω current model after 125 ms, GM's diesel 4L80-E for a duty cycle outside 0.5–95 % for 2 s without MIL. Saab's 2010 9-5 uses P0748 for a current deviation instead.

causes.label: Harness or transmission connector (corrosion, oil, chafing)
Pressure control solenoid faulty (resistance out of spec)
Internal harness, electronic module or mechatronic unit
System voltage too low
Transmission module driver

symptoms: Limp mode in a fixed gear
Transmission warning or check engine light

P0749.title: Pressure Control Solenoid A Intermittent
P0749.description: Pressure control solenoid A sets line or clutch pressure by current; most are 'normally high', so with no current – as in limp mode – maximum pressure applies. Brief current or voltage dropouts make the module switch the valve off – maximum pressure – and retest it, so harsh shifts or limp mode appear at times and vanish after a restart.

causes.label: Loose contact or corrosion at the transmission connector
Chafed harness (intermittent short)
Valve with temperature-dependent winding fault
Voltage dips or poor ground

symptoms: Occasional limp mode, normal again after restart

P0750.title: Shift Solenoid A
P0750.description: A shift solenoid is an electrically switched valve in the valve body. Manufacturers use these codes differently: Ford reports an open circuit with the base code and shorts separately, newer GM units have separate low/high codes, and the letter is not tied to a valve number (Saab's 9-5: A = valve S2). P0750 is the general code for solenoid A and is used in practice for an open circuit: Ford's step automatics (2012–2023) set it when the smart driver feedback disagrees with the command for 0.5–5 s, with shorts to ground and power as P0973/P0974; Ram's 6.7 L with Aisin transmission calls it 'control circuit open', and a 2023 bulletin traces it to a leaking capacitor in the engine module. GM does not use P0750. With the solenoid unpowered the transmission falls back to a hydraulic default gear with maximum pressure.

causes.label: Open or corroded wire or transmission pass-through connector
Solenoid coil open or shorted
Internal harness or electronic module in the transmission
Module driver faulty or valve supply missing

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning lamp
Limp mode in a fixed gear, no upshifts
Harsh shifts from maximum line pressure

P0751.title: Shift Solenoid A Performance/Stuck Off
P0751.description: A shift solenoid is an electrically switched valve in the valve body; together the solenoid states select the gear, and the module checks the result by gear ratio, slip or a pressure switch – the pattern of wrong gears shows which solenoid hangs off or on. P0751 means solenoid A is commanded on but valve, clutch or gear do not follow. GM's 6T70 flags a ratio of 1.34–1.48 with slip of 400 rpm for 0.3 s eight times and locks out first gear; GM 4-speeds recognise the pattern 2-2-3-3; both after two trips. Allison checks its pressure switch for 5 s after one trip. Ford's 'functionally failed off' covers the whole clutch circuit, and its 10R80 and 8F35 bulletins show purely mechanical causes such as a leaking clutch cylinder.

causes.label: Shift spool in the valve body sticking (dirt, debris)
Internal leak or clutch fault in the circuit
Solenoid mechanically sluggish or screen clogged
Fluid level or quality wrong

symptoms: Pulling away in the wrong gear, weak acceleration

P0752.title: Shift Solenoid A Stuck On
P0752.description: A shift solenoid is an electrically switched valve in the valve body; together the solenoid states select the gear, and the module checks the result by gear ratio, slip or a pressure switch – the pattern of wrong gears shows which solenoid hangs off or on. P0752 means solenoid A is commanded off but its clutch stays applied. GM's 6T70 flags slip of 400 rpm for 2 s five times after one trip and then runs only reverse, first and third with maximum pressure; GM's T43 a ratio of 3.83–4.23 (first instead of fourth); GM 4-speeds the pattern 1-1-4-4 after two trips; Allison its pressure switch after 2 s. Ford calls it 'functionally failed on'. A clutch that does not release can tie up the transmission.

causes.label: Shift spool sticking in the applied position
Solenoid stuck open or leaking
Clutch not releasing (burnt or stuck)
Contaminated or wrong fluid

symptoms: Wrong, often too low gear, engine revs high

P075A.title: Shift Solenoid G
P075A.description: Shift solenoid G only exists on transmissions with seven or more solenoids. Electronic module or internal harness
Connector or wiring

P075E.title: Shift Solenoid G Intermittent

P075F.title: Transmission Fluid Level Too High
P075F.description: P075F is not a circuit fault but a condition: a working fluid level sensor reports a level above the target band – the counterpart of P070F. In the Allison patent the transmission module reports 'too high, drain a quart or more', measuring only with the vehicle at rest, warm fluid and low input speed. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code. Overfilling makes rotating parts churn the fluid, which foams, pressure control becomes unsteady, fluid escapes at the vent and temperature rises; an FCA bulletin traces poor shifting after repairs to overfilling. Automatic transmission fluid level depends strongly on temperature – topping up cold often overfills.

causes.label: Overfilled at fluid change or repair (wrong check temperature or procedure)
Level sensor drifting (reads too high)
Measured under poor conditions (slope, cold fluid)

symptoms: Fluid escaping at the transmission vent
Foaming fluid, unsteady or harsh shifts

P0760.title: Shift Solenoid C
P0760.description: A shift solenoid is an electrically switched valve in the valve body. Manufacturers use these codes differently: Ford reports an open circuit with the base code and shorts separately, and the letter is not tied to a valve number (Saab's Aisin 9-5: C = valve S4, D = valve S5). P0760 is the general code for solenoid C and, at Ford, means an open circuit: the smart driver feedback disagrees with the command for 0.5–5 s, continuously; shorts to ground and power are P0979/P0980. On Ford's 6R80, 6F35/6F55 and 6R140, solenoid C is the proportional valve of the CB26 brake for second and sixth gear. If the solenoid supply is switched off, Ford transmissions keep park, reverse, neutral and fifth gear with maximum pressure.

causes.label: Open or corroded wire, connector or internal harness
Solenoid coil open or shorted
Solenoid supply (high-side switch) missing
Module driver faulty

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning lamp
Limp mode in a fixed gear (Ford: fifth with maximum pressure)
Second and sixth gear missing (Ford CB26)

P0761.title: Shift Solenoid C Performance/Stuck Off
P0761.description: A shift solenoid is an electrically switched valve in the valve body; the module checks whether its clutch follows the command by gear ratio, shift time or a pressure switch. P0761 means solenoid C is commanded on but its clutch does not follow. GM's Honda-built five-speed (Saturn Vue) combines a ratio check – first gear running in the window of second for 1.2 s – with a 3–4 shift faster than 0.8 s, after two trips. The 2007 Allison 1000 checks pressure switch 3 for 5 s, after one trip. Ford's 'functionally failed off' covers the CB26 brake circuit; Dodge's Aisin AS6 uses the code for solenoid 3, while Mitsubishi uses it for pressure switches.

causes.label: Clutch or brake of this circuit leaking or worn (piston seal, linings)
Shift spool or proportional valve sticking (dirt, debris)
Fluid level or quality
Pressure switch faulty (Allison, Aisin)

symptoms: Slip or engine flare on shifts

P0762.title: Shift Solenoid C Stuck On
P0762.description: A shift solenoid is an electrically switched valve in the valve body; the module checks whether its clutch follows the command by gear ratio, shift time or a pressure switch. P0762 means solenoid C is commanded off but its clutch stays applied. GM's Honda-built five-speed flags a 2–3 shift slower than 0.8 s together with a 4–5 shift faster than 0.8 s, after two trips; the Allison 1000 a pressure switch 3 still applied after 2 s (up to 4 s when cold), after one trip. Ford calls it 'functionally failed on' – the CB26 brake does not release, which ties up the transmission when leaving second or sixth gear. Ford's 10R80 bulletins list it with a leaking clutch cylinder.

causes.label: Shift spool or proportional valve sticking in the applied position
Clutch not releasing (stuck or burnt)
Solenoid stuck open or leaking
Control wire shorted to ground (permanently powered)

P0763.title: Shift Solenoid C Electrical
P0763.description: A shift solenoid is an electrically switched valve in the valve body. Manufacturers use these codes differently: Ford reports an open circuit with the base code and shorts separately, and the letter is not tied to a valve number (Saab's Aisin 9-5: C = valve S4, D = valve S5). Ford does not use P0763.

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning lamp

P0764.title: Shift Solenoid C Intermittent

Manufacturers use these codes differently: Ford reports an open circuit with the base code and shorts separately, and the letter is not tied to a valve number (Saab's Aisin 9-5: C = valve S4, D = valve S5). P0765.title: Shift Solenoid D
P0765.description: A shift solenoid is an electrically switched valve in the valve body. P0766.title: Shift Solenoid D Performance/Stuck Off

Shift spool or proportional valve sticking (dirt, debris)
Fluid level or quality
Pressure switch faulty (Allison, Aisin)

symptoms: Upper gears (4th–6th) missing, or no reverse or engine braking in first (Ford)
Slip or engine flare on shifts

P076A.title: Shift Solenoid H
P076A.description: Shift solenoid H exists only on transmissions with eight or more solenoids. Ford's 10R80 ends at F, GM's 9- and 10-speeds report clutch pressure valve codes; the only documented user of the H block is the 2017–18 Genesis G80/G90 with shift-by-wire, where it concerns the on/off solenoid of the park lock rather than a shift valve. Connector or wiring
Transmission module

symptoms: Park lock or range selection fault, shift-by-wire warning

P076B.title: Shift Solenoid H Performance/Stuck Off
P076B.description: Shift solenoid H exists only on transmissions with eight or more solenoids. Ford's 10R80 ends at F, GM's 9- and 10-speeds report clutch pressure valve codes; the only documented user of the H block is the 2017–18 Genesis G80/G90 with shift-by-wire, where it concerns the on/off solenoid of the park lock rather than a shift valve. Ford's 10R80 ends at F, GM's 9- and 10-speeds report clutch pressure valve codes; the only documented user of the H block is the 2017–18 Genesis G80/G90 with shift-by-wire, where it concerns the on/off solenoid of the park lock rather than a shift valve. causes.label: Loose contact or corrosion at the transmission connector

P076F.title: Gear 7 Incorrect Ratio
P076F.description: P076F means the ratio in seventh gear is wrong: input speed divided by output speed does not match the commanded gear, so a clutch slips or another gear is engaged. It only exists on transmissions with seven or more gears. Ford's 10-speed 10R80 and 10R140 list it in bulletins together with the other ratio codes and the check engine light – causes include a migrating sleeve on a clutch cylinder causing hydraulic leaks and sticking valve body valves. Ford's ratio check elsewhere flags more than 30 rpm off for 1.8 s three times. On GM's Corvette with seven-speed manual gearbox, P076F is a plausibility check of the gear position sensor instead (ratio window 0.41–0.50), after one trip.

Sticking valves in the valve body or solenoid
Fluid level or condition
Gear position sensor implausible or not learned (GM manual only)
Turbine or output speed sensor

symptoms: Slipping or flaring engine speed in seventh gear
Check engine light, transmission warning, possibly limp mode

P0770.title: Shift Solenoid E
P0770.description: What shift solenoid E does depends on the transmission. On Ford's 6R80 and 6F35/6F55 it is an on/off valve that moves a multiplex valve, so solenoid D feeds either the low/reverse brake or the 4-5-6 clutch; on the 6R140 and 5R110W it is a proportional clutch valve with separate short codes (P0985/P0986). On Saab's Aisin 5-speed E is valve S1. P0770 is the general code for solenoid E; Ford uses it for an open circuit, detected when the smart driver feedback disagrees with the command for 0.5–5 s, and on the 6R80/6F it covers all circuit faults of the solenoid. On Ram's 6.7 L with Aisin AS69RC a 2023 bulletin traces P0770 to a leaking capacitor in the engine module, together with other circuit codes. Limp mode follows; on the 6R80/6F engine braking in first or the 4th–6th gears may be missing.

causes.label: Open or corroded wire or transmission connector
Solenoid coil faulty
Transmission module or electronic module faulty
Solenoid supply missing

symptoms: Transmission warning or check engine light
Limp mode in a fixed gear

P0771.title: Shift Solenoid E Performance/Stuck Off
P0771.description: What shift solenoid E does depends on the transmission. On Ford's 6R80 and 6F35/6F55 it is an on/off valve that moves a multiplex valve, so solenoid D feeds either the low/reverse brake or the 4-5-6 clutch; on the 6R140 and 5R110W it is a proportional clutch valve with separate short codes (P0985/P0986). On Saab's Aisin 5-speed E is valve S1. P0771 is Ford's functional check by gear ratio over 10 events (2012) or 3 (2020–23, 2023 diesel). On the 6R80/6F it means the multiplex valve stays in its rest position, so solenoid D acts on the wrong clutch; valve and spool cannot be told apart. On the 6R140 the 4-5-6 clutch does not apply. Ford counts the whole clutch system in, and its 10R80 and 8F35 bulletins list P0771 with mechanical repairs. Slipping or missing gears and limp mode follow.

P0772.title: Shift Solenoid E Stuck On
P0772.description: What shift solenoid E does depends on the transmission. On Ford's 6R80 and 6F35/6F55 it is an on/off valve that moves a multiplex valve, so solenoid D feeds either the low/reverse brake or the 4-5-6 clutch; on the 6R140 and 5R110W it is a proportional clutch valve with separate short codes (P0985/P0986). Clutch plates stuck or burnt, piston hanging

Contaminated fluid

P0775.title: Pressure Control Solenoid B
P0775.description: Pressure control solenoids are current-controlled proportional valves, and what B and C mean depends on the design: on GM's clutch-to-clutch automatics they are the pressure valves of clutches 2 and 3, on GM's CVT B is primary pulley pressure and C line pressure, on Jatco CVTs B is the secondary pressure valve, on Saab's AF40 B and C are clutch valves SLC1/SLC2. No manufacturer document available to us uses it; the trade journal MOTOR names it as a performance code of line pressure valve B on Ford's 5R55, set together with ratio codes after a broken overdrive servo. Line pressure wrong (load signal, main regulator)

P0776.title: Pressure Control Solenoid B Performance/Stuck Off
P0776.description: Pressure control solenoids are current-controlled proportional valves, and what B and C mean depends on the design: on GM's clutch-to-clutch automatics they are the pressure valves of clutches 2 and 3, on GM's CVT B is primary pulley pressure and C line pressure, on Jatco CVTs B is the secondary pressure valve, on Saab's AF40 B and C are clutch valves SLC1/SLC2. GM's 8-speed flags gear slip of 400 rpm for 1.5 s three times, the 9-speed clutch 2 slip over 200 rpm for 3 s, the CVT primary pressure below 200 kPa for 3 s – all after one trip. P0777.title: Pressure Control Solenoid B Stuck On

symptoms: Limp mode (Saab: second and reverse only)

P0779.title: Pressure Control Solenoid B Intermittent
P0779.description: Pressure control solenoids are current-controlled proportional valves, and what B and C mean depends on the design: on GM's clutch-to-clutch automatics they are the pressure valves of clutches 2 and 3, on GM's CVT B is primary pulley pressure and C line pressure, on Jatco CVTs B is the secondary pressure valve, on Saab's AF40 B and C are clutch valves SLC1/SLC2. In J2012 P0779 is an intermittent fault of valve B. The only manufacturer use found differs: Mitsubishi's 2022 Jatco CVT sets P0779 for an open circuit or short to positive in the secondary pressure valve circuit after 1 s (short to ground is P0778). The transmission then engages harshly, accelerates weakly and does not lock up.

causes.label: Connector or wire open or loose contact
Short to positive in the harness
Valve coil faulty

P077A.title: Output Shaft Speed Sensor Circuit Loss of Direction Signal
P077A.description: Some transmissions use an output shaft speed sensor that also reports direction of rotation: in a GM patent two offset Hall elements send one pulse per tooth whose width encodes forward or reverse. The direction is needed to detect rolling back on a hill (a Hyundai patent raises idle speed then), for hill hold, stop-start and the forward/reverse change. P077A means the sensor still delivers speed pulses but no usable direction information – the pulse width stays outside the direction windows or one Hall element has failed. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; GM checks direction coherence under P0721. Hill hold, auto hold or stop-start may then be disabled and the forward/reverse change runs in a substitute mode.

causes.label: Output speed sensor faulty (one Hall element or direction channel failed)
Contact resistance in connector or wiring distorts the pulse
Wrong replacement sensor without direction function
Reluctor wheel damaged or air gap too large

symptoms: Transmission warning or check engine light depending on manufacturer
Hill hold, auto hold or stop-start unavailable
Rolling back on a hill not caught

P077B.title: Output Shaft Speed Sensor Circuit Direction Error
P077B.description: Some transmissions use an output shaft speed sensor that also reports direction of rotation: in a GM patent two offset Hall elements send one pulse per tooth whose width encodes forward or reverse. The direction is needed to detect rolling back on a hill (a Hyundai patent raises idle speed then), for hill hold, stop-start and the forward/reverse change. P077B means the sensor reports a direction that does not fit – for example reverse while a forward gear is engaged and the input and intermediate shaft sensors confirm forward motion. GM's transmission modules list P077B as a blocking condition for other checks, but run the actual check under their own codes: direction contradicts the gear for 2.5 s above 500 rpm, after one trip. Speed and direction are then unreliable: hill hold and the park and reverse logic fall back to substitute modes.

causes.label: Output speed sensor faulty (direction evaluation disturbed)
Wrong or incorrectly fitted sensor (orientation to the wheel)
Reluctor wheel damaged, metal debris on the sensor
Faulty reference (input or intermediate shaft sensor)

symptoms: Check engine light or transmission warning

P077C.title: Output Shaft Speed Sensor Circuit Low
P077C.description: GM's transmission modules from 2019 to 2025 (9- and 10-speeds) also read the active output speed sensor's line voltage as an analog value. P077C means this voltage is below 0.25 V – a short to ground of under about 0.5 Ω between signal and module ground – for more than 0.05 s with the system above 10 V; GM rates it after one trip. GM then blocks the no-signal and ratio checks so that P0722 is not set instead of the actual short. Without output speed the transmission enters limp mode and road speed may be missing. On GM's 10-speed input and output sensors share a supply.

causes.label: Signal or supply wire shorted to ground (chafing at the case)
Sensor shorted internally
Oil or moisture in the connector, corrosion
Module input faulty

P077D.title: Output Shaft Speed Sensor Circuit High
P077D.description: GM's transmission modules from 2019 to 2025 (9- and 10-speeds) also read the active output speed sensor's line voltage as an analog value. P077D is the mirror of P077C: the voltage is above 4.75 V – a short to the module supply of under about 0.5 Ω – for more than 0.05 s, after one trip. GM then blocks the no-signal and ratio checks; a GM hybrid also blocks its idle diagnosis. Without usable output speed the transmission enters limp mode, and speedometer or cruise control may fail.

causes.label: Signal wire shorted to sensor supply or battery voltage
Sensor faulty internally
Ground fault at the sensor, corroded connector
Module input

P077E.title: Transmission Fluid Temperature Measurement System Multiple Sensor Correlation
P077E.description: P077E is a plausibility check between several fluid temperature readings – for example sensors A and B, sump and valve body, or the module's internal temperature. If they differ by more than allowed after a settling time, such as a long stop, the code sets, without being able to blame a single sensor. No manufacturer document available to us uses it: GM checks each sensor alone (P0711, with the module temperature on the 6T70), and Ford has no multi-sensor check. A substitute value then limits converter clutch and shift adaption.

causes.label: One temperature sensor drifting (aged NTC)
Contact resistance at a sensor connector or wire
Fluid level too low (sensor not wetted)
Module or software

symptoms: Transmission warning, possibly check engine light
Converter clutch applies late or not at all

P077F.title: Reverse 2 Incorrect Ratio
P077F.description: P077F checks the ratio in a second reverse gear: input speed divided by output speed lies outside the tolerance band around the target ratio – a slipping clutch, a wrong gear or a sensor fault. Only transmissions with two reverse ratios need it, such as Mercedes' 7G-Tronic (−3.42 and −2.23, with the second reverse kept in limp mode) and its 5G-Tronic predecessor; GM's 9- and 10-speeds, Ford's 10R and ZF's 8HP have one. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; the check works like the other ratio codes such as P0736.

causes.label: Slipping clutch or brake in the second reverse power path
Fluid level low or fluid worn
Solenoid or pressure regulator sticking
Faulty input or output speed sensor

symptoms: Transmission warning or check engine light

P0780.title: Shift Error
P0780.description: Shift codes are a functional check of the gear change itself: the module compares the commanded shift with the speed trace and flags a shift that takes too long, is too short or abrupt, does not happen, flares or ties up. Ford does not use P0780–P0784 (its shift completion check feeds the solenoid codes), nor do GM's 2018–2025 tables. P0780 is the collective code when the faulty shift is not assigned to a gear. GM's 2006 Aisin-type five-speed counts five shifts that are too long, too short or tied up with fluid above 60 °C and lights the MIL at once; GM's Honda-built unit flags a 3–4 shift that stays in the lower ratio after two trips; Saab's 2010 Aisin six-speed counts ten faulty shifts without MIL, limits torque and keeps second and reverse. Nissan fixed P0780 on the 2021 Rogue CVT with new software.

causes.label: Fluid level wrong, fluid worn or contaminated
Valve body, shift or pressure valve sticking
Worn clutches or bands (mechanical damage)
Module software or shift adaption
Faulty speed sensor signal

symptoms: Limp mode with fixed gear, reduced power

P0781.title: 1-2 Shift
P0781.description: Shift codes are a functional check of the gear change itself: the module compares the commanded shift with the speed trace and flags a shift that takes too long, is too short or abrupt, does not happen, flares or ties up. Ford does not use P0780–P0784 (its shift completion check feeds the solenoid codes), nor do GM's 2018–2025 tables. P0781 names the 1–2 shift as the faulty one, up or down; slip in a steady gear is reported by the ratio codes instead. Lexus' AB60F six-speed (LX 570, 2008–11) lists P0781 among its transmission performance codes; the bulletin first checks fluid level, then installs new software and, if needed, a new transmission. No manufacturer publishes thresholds for P0781.

causes.label: Fluid level wrong, fluid worn or contaminated
Valve body, shift or pressure valve sticking
Worn clutches or bands
Module software or shift adaption
Faulty speed sensor signal

P0782.title: 2-3 Shift
P0782.description: Shift codes are a functional check of the gear change itself: the module compares the commanded shift with the speed trace and flags a shift that takes too long, is too short or abrupt, does not happen, flares or ties up. Ford does not use P0780–P0784 (its shift completion check feeds the solenoid codes), nor do GM's 2018–2025 tables. P0782 names the 2–3 shift as the faulty one, up or down; slip in a steady gear is reported by the ratio codes instead. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; GM's 2006 Aisin-type tables run the same shift time check under P0780, Ford's under the solenoid codes.

causes.label: Fluid level wrong, fluid worn or contaminated
Valve body, shift or pressure valve sticking
Worn clutches or bands
Module software or shift adaption
Faulty speed sensor signal

P0783.title: 3-4 Shift
P0783.description: Shift codes are a functional check of the gear change itself: the module compares the commanded shift with the speed trace and flags a shift that takes too long, is too short or abrupt, does not happen, flares or ties up. Ford does not use P0780–P0784 (its shift completion check feeds the solenoid codes), nor do GM's 2018–2025 tables. P0783 names the 3–4 shift as the faulty one, up or down; slip in a steady gear is reported by the ratio codes instead. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; GM's Honda-built five-speed checks exactly the 3–4 change, but reports it as P0780. Missing or late fourth gear and flare on the 3–4 shift are typical.

causes.label: Fluid level wrong, fluid worn or contaminated
Valve body, shift or pressure valve sticking
Worn clutches or bands
Module software or shift adaption
Faulty speed sensor signal

P0784.title: 4-5 Shift
P0784.description: Shift codes are a functional check of the gear change itself: the module compares the commanded shift with the speed trace and flags a shift that takes too long, is too short or abrupt, does not happen, flares or ties up. Ford does not use P0780–P0784 (its shift completion check feeds the solenoid codes), nor do GM's 2018–2025 tables. P0784 names the 4–5 shift as the faulty one, up or down; slip in a steady gear is reported by the ratio codes instead. It only exists on transmissions with five or more gears. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; GM's 2006 five-speed tables run the shift time check under P0780. High engine speed on the motorway from a missing fifth gear is typical.

causes.label: Fluid level wrong, fluid worn or contaminated
Valve body, shift or pressure valve sticking
Worn clutches or bands
Module software or shift adaption
Faulty speed sensor signal

P0785.title: Shift Timing Solenoid A
P0785.description: 'Shift timing solenoid' means different parts: on GM's 4L60-E the 3-2 downshift solenoid that times the band apply on that downshift, on Aisin five-speeds (GM, Saab) the linear valve SLS that sets clutch pressure during the shift, and on the 2017–18 Genesis G80/G90 with shift-by-wire the on/off solenoids that engage drive (A) and reverse (B). P0785 is the general circuit code for solenoid A. GM's 2006 tables use it for the 3-2 downshift solenoid circuit (more than 43 of 50 failed counts, after one trip); Saab's 2002 Aisin box for an open or short in the SLS circuit with warning lamp and limp mode; Hyundai's Genesis bulletins for the drive solenoid, replacing valve and electronic module and then the module if it returns. Limp mode, harsh 3-2 downshifts or – on the Genesis – no drive follow.

causes.label: Solenoid coil open or shorted
Connector or wire at the transmission (oil, corrosion)
Electronic module or transmission module driver

symptoms: Genesis shift-by-wire: drive cannot be engaged

P0786.title: Shift Timing Solenoid A Range/Performance
P0786.description: 'Shift timing solenoid' means different parts: on GM's 4L60-E the 3-2 downshift solenoid that times the band apply on that downshift, on Aisin five-speeds (GM, Saab) the linear valve SLS that sets clutch pressure during the shift, and on the 2017–18 Genesis G80/G90 with shift-by-wire the on/off solenoids that engage drive (A) and reverse (B). P0786 means the circuit is intact but the solenoid does not reach its target current. GM's 2006 Aisin-type five-speed flags a deviation of more than 80 mA for 2.75 s at a steady commanded current above 835 mA, with 11–16 V and fluid above 20 °C, and lights the MIL at once. Rough shifts and limp mode follow; low and high circuit faults are P0787/P0788.

causes.label: Valve worn or coil resistance drifting
Contact resistance at the connector
Unstable system voltage

P0787.title: Shift Timing Solenoid A Low
P0787.description: 'Shift timing solenoid' means different parts: on GM's 4L60-E the 3-2 downshift solenoid that times the band apply on that downshift, on Aisin five-speeds (GM, Saab) the linear valve SLS that sets clutch pressure during the shift, and on the 2017–18 Genesis G80/G90 with shift-by-wire the on/off solenoids that engage drive (A) and reverse (B). P0787 means current or voltage in the circuit is too low – an open circuit or short to ground. GM's 4L60-E checks the 3-2 downshift solenoid output (more than 43 of 50 counts) after one trip and then sets maximum line pressure, holds third gear and disables the converter clutch; GM's Aisin-type five-speed flags SLS current below 92 mA for 12.5 s. The opposite is P0788.

causes.label: Wire open or shorted to ground
Solenoid coil open
Module driver stage

P0788.title: Shift Timing Solenoid A High
P0788.description: 'Shift timing solenoid' means different parts: on GM's 4L60-E the 3-2 downshift solenoid that times the band apply on that downshift, on Aisin five-speeds (GM, Saab) the linear valve SLS that sets clutch pressure during the shift, and on the 2017–18 Genesis G80/G90 with shift-by-wire the on/off solenoids that engage drive (A) and reverse (B). P0788 means the circuit is shorted to positive or draws overcurrent. GM's 4L60-E checks the 3-2 downshift solenoid output for an invalid state at more than 43 of 50 counts; GM's Aisin-type five-speed flags SLS current above 1356 mA for 2 s and lights the MIL at once. Limp mode and shift jolts follow; the opposite is P0787.

causes.label: Short to positive in the harness
Winding short in the solenoid
Module driver stage

P0789.title: Shift Timing Solenoid A Intermittent
P0789.description: 'Shift timing solenoid' means different parts: on GM's 4L60-E the 3-2 downshift solenoid that times the band apply on that downshift, on Aisin five-speeds (GM, Saab) the linear valve SLS that sets clutch pressure during the shift, and on the 2017–18 Genesis G80/G90 with shift-by-wire the on/off solenoids that engage drive (A) and reverse (B). P0789 is an intermittent fault in the circuit of solenoid A. No manufacturer document available to us uses it; manufacturers report the circuit under the base, low and high codes. A loose contact or a coil with heat-dependent dropouts is the likely cause; shift jolts and the warning lamp appear at times.

causes.label: Loose contact at connector or harness
Coil with thermal dropouts

P078A.title: Shift Timing Solenoid B
P078A.description: 'Shift timing solenoid' means different parts: on GM's 4L60-E the 3-2 downshift solenoid that times the band apply on that downshift, on Aisin five-speeds (GM, Saab) the linear valve SLS that sets clutch pressure during the shift, and on the 2017–18 Genesis G80/G90 with shift-by-wire the on/off solenoids that engage drive (A) and reverse (B). P078A is the general circuit code for solenoid B. The only documented user is Hyundai/Genesis: on the 2017–18 G80/G90 with shift-by-wire it is the on/off solenoid that engages reverse. The bulletins replace valve and electronic module, then the transmission module if the code returns. Reverse may not engage, with warning lamp and limp mode.

causes.label: Solenoid faulty
Electronic module or transmission module
Connector or wire

P078B.title: Shift Timing Solenoid B Range/Performance
P078B.description: 'Shift timing solenoid' means different parts: on GM's 4L60-E the 3-2 downshift solenoid that times the band apply on that downshift, on Aisin five-speeds (GM, Saab) the linear valve SLS that sets clutch pressure during the shift, and on the 2017–18 Genesis G80/G90 with shift-by-wire the on/off solenoids that engage drive (A) and reverse (B). Only Hyundai/Genesis is documented using solenoid B, and only with the base code P078A. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; the description follows solenoid A (P0786: current deviation with the circuit intact, on GM's Aisin-type unit more than 80 mA for 2.75 s). Rough shifts and the warning lamp follow.

causes.label: Valve or coil faulty
Connector

P078C.title: Shift Timing Solenoid B Low
P078C.description: 'Shift timing solenoid' means different parts: on GM's 4L60-E the 3-2 downshift solenoid that times the band apply on that downshift, on Aisin five-speeds (GM, Saab) the linear valve SLS that sets clutch pressure during the shift, and on the 2017–18 Genesis G80/G90 with shift-by-wire the on/off solenoids that engage drive (A) and reverse (B). Only Hyundai/Genesis is documented using solenoid B, and only with the base code P078A. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; the description follows solenoid A (P0787: open circuit or short to ground, on GM's 4L60-E more than 43 of 50 failed counts). Warning lamp and limp mode follow; the opposite is P078D.

causes.label: Wire open or shorted to ground
Coil open

P078D.title: Shift Timing Solenoid B High
P078D.description: 'Shift timing solenoid' means different parts: on GM's 4L60-E the 3-2 downshift solenoid that times the band apply on that downshift, on Aisin five-speeds (GM, Saab) the linear valve SLS that sets clutch pressure during the shift, and on the 2017–18 Genesis G80/G90 with shift-by-wire the on/off solenoids that engage drive (A) and reverse (B). Only Hyundai/Genesis is documented using solenoid B, and only with the base code P078A. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; the description follows solenoid A (P0788: short to positive or overcurrent, on GM's Aisin-type unit above 1356 mA for 2 s). Warning lamp and limp mode follow; the opposite is P078C.

causes.label: Short to positive
Winding short

P078E.title: Shift Timing Solenoid B Intermittent
P078E.description: 'Shift timing solenoid' means different parts: on GM's 4L60-E the 3-2 downshift solenoid that times the band apply on that downshift, on Aisin five-speeds (GM, Saab) the linear valve SLS that sets clutch pressure during the shift, and on the 2017–18 Genesis G80/G90 with shift-by-wire the on/off solenoids that engage drive (A) and reverse (B). Only Hyundai/Genesis is documented using solenoid B, and only with the base code P078A. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; the description follows solenoid A (P0789: an intermittent circuit fault). A loose contact is the likely cause; the warning lamp comes and goes.

causes.label: Loose contact
Coil with thermal dropouts

P078F.title: Transmission Mode Switch C Circuit
P078F.description: P078F is the circuit fault of a third transmission mode switch (C), after A (P071A–P071C) and B (P071D–P071F): its state is invalid or implausible. GM's transmission modules of 2023 and 2025 list the number only as a blocking condition for another check, without a description of their own; GM reports its drive mode selector today under P05D0–P05D3 (8-step resistor ladder, two trips). No manufacturer document available to us describes P078F itself. The mode then cannot be selected and the transmission stays on its normal schedule.

causes.label: Switch or button faulty or sticking
Wire or connector open or shorted
Moisture or dirt in the centre console
Control module

symptoms: Drive mode (sport, winter, tow) cannot be selected
Transmission stays on the normal program

P0790.title: Normal/Performance Switch Circuit
P0790.description: P0790 is the circuit fault of the normal/performance (sport or power program) selector of an automatic transmission – the older single code that preceded the mode switch codes P071A ff; the early J2012 list still called it 'circuit malfunction'. The switch is usually a button to ground or a resistor ladder; a fault is an invalid level, a permanently pressed button or an open circuit. No manufacturer document available to us describes it; GM uses P05D0–P05D3 for its drive mode selector today. The sport program is then unavailable or permanently on.

causes.label: Button faulty or sticking
Wire or connector open or shorted
Liquid in the console
Control module

symptoms: Sport or performance program unavailable or always on

P0791.title: Intermediate Shaft Speed Sensor A Circuit
P0791.description: The intermediate shaft speed sensor measures a shaft between input and output – a countershaft on Toyota's U760 six-speed, the intermediate shaft behind the overdrive set on Ford's 5R110W. Together with turbine and output speed it lets the module check each gear stage and control clutch slip. Ford uses P0791 as its only intermediate shaft code, for 'no or too little signal': while the vehicle drives under power (turbine at least 1500 rpm, output at least 650 rpm or 15 mph), the sensor reports below 250 rpm for 5 s – in the 2012 and 2020–23 summaries, with MIL. A Toyota bulletin for the U760 (Highlander, Venza, Camry 2009–10) replaces the countershaft sensor for P0791/P0793. GM's 10-speed has two such sensors but uses its own codes. Limp mode and harsh shifts follow.

causes.label: Intermediate shaft speed sensor faulty
Connector or wire at the transmission (oil, corrosion, chafing)
Reluctor wheel damaged or debris on the sensor
Control module

P0792.title: Intermediate Shaft Speed Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P0792.description: The intermediate shaft speed sensor measures a shaft between input and output – a countershaft on Toyota's U760 six-speed, the intermediate shaft behind the overdrive set on Ford's 5R110W. Together with turbine and output speed it lets the module check each gear stage and control clutch slip. P0792 means a signal is present but implausible: intermediate shaft speed does not match turbine or output speed for the detected gear stage, exceeds a maximum or jumps unrealistically. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code – Ford uses only P0791, Toyota's bulletin P0791/P0793, GM its own codes; the logic follows GM's range checks for input and output sensors (P0716/P0721). Ratio codes, by contrast, point to clutch slip rather than a sensor fault.

causes.label: Sensor delivering faulty pulses (air gap, reluctor wheel)
Interference or loose contact
Mechanical slip interpreted as a sensor fault
Wrong sensor fitted

symptoms: Check engine light or transmission warning

P0793.title: Intermediate Shaft Speed Sensor A Circuit No Signal
P0793.description: The intermediate shaft speed sensor measures a shaft between input and output – a countershaft on Toyota's U760 six-speed, the intermediate shaft behind the overdrive set on Ford's 5R110W. Together with turbine and output speed it lets the module check each gear stage and control clutch slip. P0793 means there is no pulse signal from the intermediate shaft sensor although the vehicle is moving according to other speeds. Toyota's bulletin for the U760 six-speed lists P0793 with P0717 and P0791 and replaces the countershaft sensor with a revised part. Ford reports the same fault under P0791 (below 250 rpm for 5 s). Note that a 2007 Allison table's 'P0793' for shift solenoid 1 low is a typo for P0973. Limp mode and check engine light follow.

causes.label: Sensor faulty (internal open circuit)
Wire open or connector loose
Reluctor wheel or air gap
Transmission module

P0794.title: Intermediate Shaft Speed Sensor A Circuit Intermittent
P0794.description: The intermediate shaft speed sensor measures a shaft between input and output – a countershaft on Toyota's U760 six-speed, the intermediate shaft behind the overdrive set on Ford's 5R110W. Together with turbine and output speed it lets the module check each gear stage and control clutch slip. P0794 means the intermediate shaft signal drops out or jumps briefly – not long enough for P0793 – typically a loose contact or a wire breaking under movement. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; the expected logic counts unrealistic jumps like Ford's P0718 for the turbine sensor (200 spikes within 1.5 s each). Occasional harsh shifts follow, and limp mode after several events.

causes.label: Loose contact at the connector or broken wire
Sensor thermally unstable
Interference (ground, shielding)

P0795.title: Pressure Control Solenoid C
P0795.description: Pressure control solenoids are current-controlled proportional valves, and what B and C mean depends on the design: on GM's clutch-to-clutch automatics they are the pressure valves of clutches 2 and 3, on GM's CVT B is primary pulley pressure and C line pressure, on Jatco CVTs B is the secondary pressure valve, on Saab's AF40 B and C are clutch valves SLC1/SLC2. P0795 is the general code for valve C. No manufacturer document available to us uses it; GM's 8-speed uses only P0796/P0797 for its clutch 3 valve, Saab's AF40 only P0798 for valve SLC2. Sub-codes for performance, stuck on, electrical and intermittent follow (P0796–P0799).

causes.label: Valve body or pressure valve C
Fluid or line pressure
Circuit or coil

P0796.title: Pressure Control Solenoid C Performance/Stuck Off
P0796.description: Pressure control solenoids are current-controlled proportional valves, and what B and C mean depends on the design: on GM's clutch-to-clutch automatics they are the pressure valves of clutches 2 and 3, on GM's CVT B is primary pulley pressure and C line pressure, on Jatco CVTs B is the secondary pressure valve, on Saab's AF40 B and C are clutch valves SLC1/SLC2. P0796 means valve C is electrically fine but pressure stays too low. GM's 6-speed flags 400 rpm slip in steady fourth gear with an intrusive test (4-5-6 clutch), the 8-speed 400 rpm for 1.5 s three times (clutch 3), the 9-speed clutch 3 slip over 200 rpm for 3 s, the CVT a line pressure deviation – all after one trip. GM noted false settings on 2017 8-speeds; a 9-speed bulletin calls for clutch inspection and a new valve body. Slipping, missing upper gears and limp mode follow.

causes.label: Clutch, return spring or piston seal of the assigned clutch faulty
Valve body or pressure valve dirty or worn
Fluid level low, fluid worn, filter clogged
Software false setting

P0797.title: Pressure Control Solenoid C Stuck On
P0797.description: Pressure control solenoids are current-controlled proportional valves, and what B and C mean depends on the design: on GM's clutch-to-clutch automatics they are the pressure valves of clutches 2 and 3, on GM's CVT B is primary pulley pressure and C line pressure, on Jatco CVTs B is the secondary pressure valve, on Saab's AF40 B and C are clutch valves SLC1/SLC2. P0797 means valve C is electrically fine but pressure stays applied – the off-going clutch does not release. GM's 9-speed flags clutch 3 slip below 50 rpm for 0.8 s (0.15 s in other cases), the 8-speed uses a torque and inertia phase test, both after one trip; GM's 9-speed bulletin and Maserati's MC20 dual-clutch sheet list the code too. Harsh shift jolts and a default gear follow.

causes.label: Spool or pressure valve sticking
Clutch stuck or piston hanging
Contaminated fluid (debris after clutch damage)
Software or false setting

symptoms: Harsh shift jolt, transmission ties up
Limp mode in a fixed gear

P0798.title: Pressure Control Solenoid C Electrical
P0798.description: Pressure control solenoids are current-controlled proportional valves, and what B and C mean depends on the design: on GM's clutch-to-clutch automatics they are the pressure valves of clutches 2 and 3, on GM's CVT B is primary pulley pressure and C line pressure, on Jatco CVTs B is the secondary pressure valve, on Saab's AF40 B and C are clutch valves SLC1/SLC2. P0798 is the electrical code for valve C. Only Saab's 9-5 (2010–11) with Aisin AF40 uses it: a deviation between commanded and feedback current of clutch valve SLC2 (normal range 0.1–1.1 A), with the circuit codes P0969–P0971 alongside, rated after two trips. The module switches all solenoids off and keeps only second gear and reverse, without adaption. GM and Ford use the circuit codes P0968–P0971 instead.

causes.label: Clutch valve SLC2 coil faulty
Wire or connector open or shorted
Transmission module damaged (e.g. after a short)

symptoms: Limp mode (second gear and reverse only)
Transmission warning or check engine light

P0799.title: Pressure Control Solenoid C Intermittent
P0799.description: Pressure control solenoids are current-controlled proportional valves, and what B and C mean depends on the design: on GM's clutch-to-clutch automatics they are the pressure valves of clutches 2 and 3, on GM's CVT B is primary pulley pressure and C line pressure, on Jatco CVTs B is the secondary pressure valve, on Saab's AF40 B and C are clutch valves SLC1/SLC2. P0799 is an intermittent electrical fault of valve C. No manufacturer document available to us uses it; Saab's AF40 catches short dropouts within its circuit codes (five times in 100 ms). A loose contact or chafed harness is the likely cause; harsh shifts or limp mode appear at times.

causes.label: Loose contact or corroded connector
Chafed harness
Coil with heat-dependent winding fault

symptoms: Limp mode or harsh shifts at times

P079A.title: Transmission Friction Element A Slip Detected
P079A.description: The 'friction element slip' codes monitor a clutch that is commanded locked in a power-split hybrid transmission: the module calculates its slip from electric motor, engine and output speeds (target 0 rpm) and flags slip above a threshold for a minimum time, with sufficient line pressure and clutch torque; from 2016 GM also flags a calculated friction energy threshold at once. P07B2.title: Transmission Park Position Sensor/Switch A Circuit/Open
P07B2.description: With electronic gear selection the park position sensor/switch reports the park request or position. On GM's shift-by-wire selectors (2017 LaCrosse, XT4/XT5, Bolt EV, later SUVs and pickups) it is the P button, read by two redundant analog sensors A and B with separate 'released' and 'pressed' voltage zones. P07B2 means the circuit of sensor A is open: the module sees a missing or undefined signal. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; GM covers an open analog circuit under its low and high codes (P07B3/P07B4), which CARB allows when an open cannot be told apart from an out-of-range value. P07CB.title: Transmission Fluid Thermostat Performance

P07D7.title: Stuck in Gear 8
P07D7.description: P07D7 means gear 8 cannot be disengaged: the module commands a shift out of 8th, but the transmission stays in it. It is the counterpart to P07D8, where gear 8 cannot be engaged. The only documented user is Maserati's eight-speed dual-clutch gearbox in the MC20 (from model year 2023), whose bulletin lists it next to the other 'Stuck in Gear' codes: hydraulic actuators move the shift forks, and a fork that does not reach neutral is reported. The repair path there first runs a service fast-learn with valve flushing and new adaptation, then records system pressure – it should hold 20–30 bar; drops below 5 bar point to the mechatronic unit, a stable pressure to the gearbox itself. No thresholds or trip counts are published.

causes.label: Shift fork actuator or shift valve sticking (contamination)

Fluid or filter contaminated

symptoms: Transmission stays in gear 8 and will not downshift

P07D8.title: Unable to Engage Gear 8
P07D8.description: 'Unable to Engage' means the transmission does not reach the commanded gear – here 8th. Documented users are eight-speed dual-clutch gearboxes with hydraulically moved, position-monitored shift forks. A GM bulletin for the 2020–23 Corvette lists it with the MIL on, caused by a solenoid or internal switch sticking from debris: valve cleaning is only advised when system pressure codes are present as well, otherwise a service fast-learn; if that fails, the mechanics are damaged. Maserati's MC20 lists it with a pressure check of 20–30 bar. On a dual-clutch box the half carrying the even gears may be locked out. No published thresholds or trip counts.

P07D9.title: Gear 8 Incorrect Ratio
P07D9.description: A ratio code compares input or turbine speed divided by output speed with the ratio of the commanded gear; a slipping clutch or the wrong gear trips it. Ford's summaries describe the check (over 30 rpm off for more than 1.8 s, three times) for gears 1–6 only; its 10-speed bulletins show gears 7–10 as P076F, P07D9, P07F6 and P07F7. P07D9 covers 8th gear. Ford's 10R80 (F-150, Mustang, Ranger, Expedition and others) and 10R140 (2020 Super Duty) list it in bulletins on harsh or delayed shifts, caused by adaptive learning, sticking valve-body valves or a migrating sleeve in a clutch cylinder. Nissan's nine-speed Frontier and Titan set it with the MIL on; a Stellantis bulletin pairs it with P0731 on low-mileage vehicles with wrong factory adaptives. Hyundai's eight-speeds and GM's 10-speed do not use it.

causes.label: Clutch slipping or hydraulic leak (Ford 10R: migrating sleeve in the CDF clutch cylinder)
Shift adaptives wrong or not learned
Sticking valve in the valve body
Fluid level low or fluid degraded
Turbine or output speed sensor signal wrong

symptoms: Slipping or flaring engine speed in gear 8
Check engine or transmission warning lamp
Gear 8 locked out, higher rpm at cruise

P07DA.title: 6-7 Shift
P07DA.description: Shift codes check the gear change itself: the module compares the commanded change with the speed trace and flags a shift that takes too long, does not happen, flares or binds up two clutches. They continue the series P0781 '1-2 Shift' to P0784 '4-5 Shift'. No manufacturer document available to us uses P07DA or P07DB: Ford's Diesel summary checks shift completion (speed must drop by more than 30 rpm on an upshift, flare above 300 rpm) without a gear-specific code, Ford's 10R80 feeds the solenoid function codes and GM the clutch valve codes. P07DA names the change between 6th and 7th gear, in either direction, as faulty; it exists only on transmissions with seven or more gears. Flags and thresholds follow the manufacturer's own logic.

causes.label: Shift or clutch valve sticking
Worn clutch or hydraulic leak on the clutches involved
Shift adaptives wrong
Fluid level or condition

symptoms: Engine speed flares during the shift

P07DB.title: 7-8 Shift
P07DB.description: Shift codes check the gear change itself: the module compares the commanded change with the speed trace and flags a shift that takes too long, does not happen, flares or binds up two clutches.
